So currently, you'll see a lot of crude remarks and "reviews" about Just Cause 3 in the community hub. A lot of them have to do with them believing the game isnt fun or does not function correctly which I'm ok with, that was their experience, but I feel like it's starting to cloud the judgement of people who have a high probabillity of enjoying this great game that Avalanche studios and Square Enix have made for us.
I'm here to put out my opinion on the game and I'll start with straight off saying HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.
I'm totally for this game, bugs and all.
So I won't do a Pros vs. Cons lists because it's a bit annoying imo to see a list of things someone doesnt like, but I will tell you what I do like.
The most important feature in the game is the wingsuit now: The wingsuit is fairly easy to master and can be really fun if you know when to time your grapple shots. It's pretty quick and can get you to most places without using an air vehicle.
Challenges: They're rewarded throughout your gameplay (When you liberate or take a settlement) and you essentially are playing them for mods and a bit of practice using different tools. The challenges are based on many factors and the result of getting points in them is GEARS. Gears are like a currency type for your mod menu and unlock the mods as you recieve them. You can earn up to 5 gears in a challenge, 5 being fairly difficult to achieve without practice.
Mods: Modding is a new feature and is really cool! It allows you to toggle on and off certain things you want to apply to your tools such as rocket boosters to C4, a faster reel in for grappling (which applies to multiple actions like, wingsuiting, parachuting and regular grappling), and many many more. *****Do Not Confuse In-Game Modding With Workshop Mods*****
Story: Much more humor has been put into the story, and the characters have more...character to them. The story could still use work for future games in the series but you now have a much firmer grasp on ricos past and the concept the Developers are going for in this game.
Graphics: Absolutely lovely. If you played BattleFront beta on High settings, you may have noticed how amazing it looked kind of giving you a warm happy feeling. Thats what the graphics are like in Just Cause 3. Simply Beautiful.
Unlimited C4: This is also a new feature, one of many. Rather than simply being allowed to drop C4 everywhere and finish the game in 3 hours, you now can place 3 C4 on any nearby object or drop them from above in parachute mode and detonate them from far away, maybe on a high vantage point to admire your work. You can also upgrade to 5 C4 later on.
Upgraded Grappling Hook/ Multiple Tethers: The grapple hook now looks much more sleek and presents a much better feel to the player when grappling to objects. I Don't know for sure, but it also seems like the grapple distance is slightly farther. You may now upgrade to 6 Tethers throughout the game and you start off with two fairly early, say 15 minutes into the game. With these tethers you can pull objects together with the new Manual Retract Function.
Weapons: Not much to say other than ammo is much more common throughout the world and there are many more weapons presented compared to Just cause 2. These can also be modded.
Over All Gameplay: A very fun game, full of moments where you question what your true abillities really are! You may ask yourself whether or not you can accomplish a task, truth is you most likely can. The gameplay is rewarding and well worth your money (Remember it's in my opinion) and runs really smoothly....MOST OF THE TIME. This leads us to the bugs

For someone who likes collecting or taking care of creatures without much stress of them dying- which is the fun part for me, personally- this is a perfect game. You get to run around bringing home slimes and exploring a diverse alien world for various resources that can be used to farm or invent devices to make your life easier. There are simple puzzles here and there and hidden goodies spread across the map for you to hunt down, and plenty of things to do to keep you constantly busy. It is not a difficult game by any means, as there is no real combat or any hard problems to solve, but those who just like to sit back and waste time having fun will likely find it enjoyable.
However, I will say that unless you are fairly easily entertained, the current state of the game might leave some things to be desired. Exploration sort of feels like a side quest more than anything, since caring for your slimes might take some time, and exploration is something that kind of has to be prepared for rather than going on spontaneous adventures (unless you're willing to risk agitated slimes escaping!) There also simply isn't a humongous map TO explore and you learn your way around quite quickly. People who may come to the game expecting to explore this huge open world with tons of different slimes might find themselves disappointed. The game still is in early access, however, so it might broaden with time!
tldr; This is such a fun and happy game and I adore it! I bought it when it was on sale but knowing what I do now, I would have happily bought it for the full price!

It is a great game if you look at it with lots of improvements when you compare it to its predecessor.
The game is well made and plays fluently (even on a mid-range pc). There were some launch issues, I never had any problems with those but appart from that there aren't many bugs and glitches that break the game.
Dark Souls is still a hard game, atleast harder than your average game. Dark Souls II seems a bit easier than Dark Souls but when you get to Drangleic Castle you won't notice a thing! The multiplayer system has improved a lot since Dark souls I. summon signs pop up everywhere when you're playing on a busy hour. This can be of great help if you are having trouble with a boss. The new covenants are worth mentioning too, ofcourse you can join the Sunbro's again but there are also new covenants that focus more on helping those that are being invaded. Invading isn't as active as I'd expected. you can get invaded even when hollow but still I've been invaded only twice (in the same area after using a bonfire ascetic).
In my opinion it was a good idea to add a respawn-limit to areas. This way you can't farm loads of souls to make it easier in the next area. It is also a nice thing to have when you are stuck at a boss. Some bosses have a bonfire that is far away from the fog gate, eventually you can just run to the boss without defeating twenty enemies first and using all your estus. Estus Flask have been changed aswell. In a positive way, you start out with only one estus flask but as you progress you find shards of estus. These can be changed into more estus flasks.
If you start comparing Dark Souls II with Dark Souls Prepare To Die Edition you'll notice that there is indeed a nice graphic improvement and above all the 30fps lock has finally been removed! This does give a small problem (if I have to believe my sources). Due to the variable fps weapons and armor durablility will decrease faster (more fps means that your weapon has more frames inside a monster). The world is really well made but it doesn't feel as cleverly connected as the world in Dark Souls I.
Even though it might lack a few things its predeccor had, this is still a really good game
I definitely recommend it ! 9/10

Happened upon this freebie by accident, and despite something of a distaste for RPGMaker projects decided there wasn't any harm in giving it a try...turns out I stuck with it to the end, and chances are if the thing interests you enough to merit a download the same will hold true for the reader.
On a basic level the game feels something like the older Ys titles - you and the enemies move around in real time, and if you bump into them you exchange damage. There's not a heckuva lot of technique to it at first, but as you progress you add a handful of special attacks (a dash slash, a projectile, etc.) to your arsenal, which will come in handy against foes which put up a better fight when approached head-on - since your life and special attack points gradually regenerate the game never gets too difficult (hardly surprising, considering that's one of the creators' stated goals), but for the handful of hours it lasts things stay engaging enough to keep things moving. If you want to find everything you'll likely end up taking a second trip through, as I did, and do so with a closer eye on your surroundings to sniff out persnickety hidden stuff that seems stupidly obvious once you've noticed it.
Visually, Eternal Senia makes pretty good use of both stock assets and original artwork - the three sections (four, if you count the intro) of the tower you have to climb, and the baddies dwelling within, are distinct if somewhat predictable, and the music, while not particularly hum-worthy in my opinion, does its job admirably otherwise. The story tying the whole thing together is pretty boilerplate (your adoptive sis went to the tower and hasn't come back, time to head in and find her yourself), but the small handful of characters present are generally low-key and likable, not to mention that each of the three endings, while perhaps a bit melodramatic, will still likely evoke at least a little bit of "right in the feels" from many players.
As far as weaknesses go, the translation is a bit rough (albeit never enough to obfuscate things to any major extent), leveling up your gear and skills to their peak requires some grinding (though the game is still very much beatable without doing so), the only major threats to your well-being come when you're surrounded and trapped by enemies and their area-of-effect magic spells, meaning most of your deaths (especially if you attempt to bolster the challenge by turning boss fights up to "hard") will be the result of frustrating "pinball bounces" between attacks, and while you can fast-travel around each individual area you're not allowed to return to cleared zones to complete your checklist.
Other than that, I can't really fault the game for being what it is - a simple, breezy, and overall pleasant (not to mention, once again, free) little action-RPG. It isn't likely to light anyone's world on fire, but it isn't trying to, and shouldn't feel any need to. If you're ever in the mood to wander around for a bit, smack some unfriendly sprites upside the head and get strong enough for the next batch in the process, there's no reason not to spend a little time with this unassuming, but warmly genuine, production.

Where do I begin? Okay, so I now have over 110 hours on the Steam client and had somewhere between 300-550 hours on the original client. Now, I will say that there are negative aspects to the game. However these are more particular to MOBAs in general and less about Smite. Matchmaking in League, Dota, (I assume Heroes of the Storm, but never played and never heard anything about its matchmaking) and Smite is no exception. If you're trying to teach a friend to play without making a smurf account, well, it's really REALLY hard. Since a party will always play against people around the highest party member's level, it usually results in absolute domination by the opposing team because you have at least one team mate (Being your friend you are trying to teach) who barely understands the game. This is less of a problem for experienced players of other MOBAs like LoL or Dota, however not unheard of either. The grind to level 30 is also astonishing long. I should mention that even with all this time played, I am still a level 25. I've been playing since the closed beta in October 2012. Sure, I've been playing off and on in that time, however, that doesn't change the fact that I have a♥♥♥♥♥♥ton of time in the game. The only reason this is a problem is that you can't play ranked until you are level 30. If you're playing a normal game in the "premier" gamemode Conquest, expect bad plays, bad team comps, and overall bad team players. I personally recommend that if you do play conquest, play with a friend who is on or above your skill level. If you're alone, I suggest gamemodes such as Arena and 3v3 Joust. Both are shorter games which means less time commitment and usually have more laid back people who aren't gonna wine if you end up being the first blood. This is not to say the game is bad. The game is a downright amazing game that I would recommend to almost anyone. The players themselves are the bad part. This isn't even mentioning the totally awesome concept of playing as freaking GODS. "Oh, so you're saying that in this game I can murder Zeus with Thor, proving my dominance as the best god of thunder? SIGN ME UP!"
TL;DR
This is a free to play game with an awesome concept, awesome gameplay mechanics, and provides you with an awesome time. Play the game. There is actually no reason not to give it a go.

Another great game from Avalanche Studios that can make even Michael Bay feel jealous!
This time the action takes place in Medici, an archipelago with a mediterranean look where everything seems to be latinized. The voice acting of most characters is done with an italian accent and sometimes they sound funny. Even the PSAs that you hear on the radio after liberating a base are hilarious.
The game doesn't take itself too seriously. Story is generic, just as expected, but you are here for the action and to blow stuff up - and that is where the game shines. Explosions look awesome with nice particle effects and Rico Rodriguez, the one-man-army, has a lot of creative ways to make things go BOOM. You can use a wide variety of guns and vehicles, but some of your best and most fun toys unlock later in the game.
The open-world is filled with optional activities and collectibles, but there is some grinding involved if you want to unlock all the mods. Although the open-world is huge, there are a lot of useless green areas like forests or fields that make for long travelling times between objectives (until fast travel is unlocked).
Unfortunately the game is not very well optimized for PC and the physics engine acts unexpected sometimes. If you are hoping for another Mad Max then you'll be disapointed because this game requires a high-end machine to run smooth. There is an always-online component that makes the game stutter. Also, found one game breaking bug in a main story mission so I would suggest to wait for further patches that will hopefully improve optimisation and fix all issues.
Overall: I had a fun time with Just Cause 3 and I recommend it if you like open-world action games.

It's not a golf game, it's a shell of a golf game with no internals. There is no AI, no season/career options, no stats, no tournament play. You can play a round against yourself or an online opponent and that's it! Graphics are average but it does however still require serious PC juice to run. Menus are few because there are no real features that require menus. Visually the menus have a very simplistic layout and are certainly not intuitive to navigate. There are no great new features in Perfect Golf that other golf games don't have. The features it does have are nothing new and are extremely basic with many bugs/issues.
You would think the developers would do something great with one of the most important areas of any golf game, the swing meter! Well, no, it's as basic as you can get!
I like to click. You have some very basic difficulty settings you can adjust for the game difficulty and that's the end of the swing meter feature list. There is no option to change the swing meter speed to something of your liking. There is no option to add markers to the meter. The meter links to the graphics engine so if you don't have a silky smooth running game, you also won't have a silky smooth meter making it impossible to play. These are simple meter options golf games over a decade old provided. Perfect Golf gives you the most simplistic of meters with virtually no options to tailor it.
If you use the mouse method for swing, same deal, extremely basic with little to no control. There is not even a horizontal mouse swing option! There is no feedback on how well you did with your swing as in Tiger Woods games so you never know what area of your swing needs work.
Considering how little of a golf sim Perfect Golf provides, you would think the developers would nail what has been done before in golf games and improve upon those features. No such luck! Here we have first time developers and it shows in every bland detail of the game!
One final example to leave you with. The game contains a follow the ball in flight option same as a ball-cam from the Tiger Woods games. In Tiger Woods the camera follows the ball through flight and as it hits the ground the camera smoothly follows behind the ball as it bounces and comes to a stop. In Perfect Golf, as the ball hits the ground, the camera bounces along with the ball! The entire screen jumps up and down. Talk about annoying! Talk about motion sickness! Talk about the feeling you are playing arcade golf! You find youself expecting the golf ball to explode or some dude to come out from behind a tree and start shooting at you every time your shot hits the deck!
It's an early access game but it's not too difficult to see a game that no amount of time and patching will help ever become a good one. Complete waste of money and time!

Hands down the best golf simulation ever created. Things that seperates itself from other games:
-A real time physics engine combined with real ball flight data(launch angles, spin rates and ball speeds) taken from launch monitors put this game in a class of it's own. Once you experience the before mentioned there really is no going back to other golf games.
-The Motion Swing mouse mechanic is a first of it's kind that introduces D plane swing theory. What is D plane theory and how does it realate to the mouse? Well, the simplified answer is the tracking of the actual swing path plus the tracking of the clubface angle. Your swing path is determined by the direction you move the mouse and the clubface angle is determined by the tempo at which you move your mouse.
-A real time weather and lighting system allow you to input a geographic location and play in those weather and lighting conditions. Never before has a golf game recreated weather and lighting conditions like this game. The lighting and shadow effects are exceptional and really change the look and feel of a course. You can even play in a thunder and lightning storm. Even though you wouldn't do this in real life it's worth doing in PG just to see the lightning effects.
-The last thing worth mentioning, and maybe the most important is, this may be the first game to offer up realistic scores in competition. I see no way to shoot in the 50's on a consistent basis, especially with aids turned off. I see scores being very close to real life, maybe even higher. Since tempo plays such a high role in the swing, straight edging or trying to zero out the x axis on the mouse is not going to get your far. Also, since the game uses a real time physics engine to determine spin you can't put artificial spin on the ball and throw darts at every flag.
$20 for this game is a steal. Buying it now will save you $10 to $15 when it goes retail. Once the course forge is released with the retail version and courses start pouring in, there will be no reason to even talk about another golf game. The potential this game has is limitless. If done right, this could be one of the greatest sports sims ever created.

So, you wanna know if you should get this game?
Alright. Let's start with how it performs.
I have a pretty decent old rig that runs most modern games at a fair clip. Intel i7-2600 @ 3.40GHz, overclocked to something ridiculous that I can't remember. 8 gigs of ram. 2x GeForce GT 545 (not great, but fair) with 4 gigs of total memory on 'em.
Not spectacular, right? The game runs very smoothe. Seriously. There's a bit of lag when you use your motion tracker and your vision refocuses. Same thing with using the access tuner on a couple of the hacking minigames. When an alien is doing his kill animation on you or an android is steadily squeezing the life from your un-stealthy neck, there is also some lag, but not so much that you cannot fight your way free (or die, accordingly).
Aside from that, on High (or even Ultra in some cases, cept maybe near the end) the game looks SPECTACULAR. Seriously, the job they did on optimizing this thing is beyond the standard I've come to expect from a lot of game makers. So, if you meet the minimum requisites for this game, you will undoubtedly have zero problems running it.
And, if I didn't emphasize it enough, it's -so-, SO pretty. In a game like this, the environment and clutter being top-notch helps immerse you in the experience. And, throughout, the game DOES NOT "play like a movie." Cutscenes are short, to the point, and occur from the main characters point of view. They did good with the immersion.
Optimization and Visuals: 9/10
How about the gameplay?
Controls can be a bit finnicky at very stressful moments (Hold E to Hide? Really? LEMME IN NOW!), but you will undoubtedly manage with a little foresight and caution. The AI is, in general, pretty good, but you will definitely feel like the Alien is cheating at times. That's because, even though they say the alien is "unscripted," there are some encounters you will be unable to avoid. Plus, they've gotta make it follow you throughout the complex, or else what's the point. Sneak past it once, and be safe? Cheh, naw bro. Though, the humans are fairly poor. You'll have a tough time NOT killing them to get that fancy little achievement.
The weapons have all the stopping power that the best Nerf artillery can offer--they're nearly useless, except for killing humans (humans die easy). Stick with gadgets (which are awesome, and easy to come by) for taking care of bots or distracting the Alien. The game runs a bit long, but the different things you get to do during that long bit of gameplay kept me entertained; I think my finishing run-time was around 14 hours.
By the end of the game, the "scariness" has somewhat worn off, and you end up facing down your foes with more battle-hardened ferocity than any casual shooter could bring out of you. Unfortunately, that's not a great thing for horror games (unless you like feeling as if you've conquered your fear).
Overall Gameplay: 8.5/10
How about the theme of the game? Does it "stay loyal?"
We have, in the past, been disappointed by Alien-franchise games. This one won't disappoint you. Watch Alien, then play this game. Seriously. Then come back and tell us how satisfied you are. I'm not going to spoil it for you, just take a look at some screenshots.
The whole thing is pretty tasty.
Theme/Brand Loyalty: 10/10
Overall, the game delivers a fairly polished experience. I would advise you, if you like to be frightened of heavy footsteps and screeching noises (or badly modulated voices saying soothing things), and all the horrifying cutscenes that follow (you'll see a lot of them) that you snag this game. If you want to wade through the corpses of your enemies with absolute disregard for your safety, this is not the game you are looking for... but it may give you a healthy respect for the perspective of your pathetic foe. Pick it up, get some empathy, then carry on as a somewhat more enlightened Slayer of Henchmen.
Overall Score: 9.25/10 -- Get this game if you're down with the stealth horror experience.
Caveat: If you are NOT a fan of Alien(s), this game is going to lose your interest. During a certain lengthy mid-to-end game portion, you will not likely find yourself entertained. Reduce overall score to 8.25 for non-fans.

I've postponed my writing of this review for quite a while so that I could fully explore and complete the game before I wrote about it.
Alien: Isolation is certainly the best game in any Alien related franchise and it was really great to play, the aesthetics are true to Ridley Scott's Alien film and this really helped the atmosphere of the game follow suit in a way particularly remniscent of the first (which is often overlooked in Alien games for Aliens) the pace of the game felt right the entire way through and the suspense and dread were met in all the right places.
One of the things I am particularly fond of with the game is that you partake in a similar journey to Ellen Ripley in the films, when you begin the game you are helpless and completely out of your depth, but you see Amanda transform through the game in much the same way Ellen did in the films, she battles through and gains new strength and determination as the game progresses and this is something I think can really be felt as you play through the game.
The areas you are able to explore can also be revisited to find extra treats at later stages in the game which gives both nostalgic feelings to areas were you were perhaps a little more helpless with a new approach. There were also notable homages to the first film which made everything fit really nice with the overall experience for fans of the original film.
I played through the game on the hard difficulty to get the most accurate experience possible in terms of survival and scarcity of equipment to survive, although at times I do think I had more resources than I think I should have I was also met with points of dread where I had little to keep myself alive which was really great.
In terms of how the game performed I was pretty impressed and I spent almost the whole time feeling immersed in the setting, this was halted only at three points where I encountered some bugs. The first of these bugs was after I was set on fire and subsequently extinguished this fire - I remained visually still set on fire and this prevented me from progressing and I had to load from an earlier save to fix this. The second bug occured during the point in the game where Marlow explained the findings on LV-426, at this point I was able to see an artifact shadow through the ship that should not have been visible. The final bug I encountered was while I was outside in the space suit where although I should have had nothing in my hands the Molotov kept appearing in my hand at random as it was the last item I had equipped before entering the suit.
Overall I really enjoyed the game and I think this is the only must have Alien game that has ever been on the market. Alien: Isolation really is a fun game to play (or cower while playing).

Amazing game. I was worried at first because of the bad history of Alien games and because of some early reviews that were sour, but this game is even more fun than I expected. It's extremely immersive and engaging. I'm actually terrified to play it sometimes because I honestly dread having my face eaten off or getting impaled, shot, or smashed against the wall by an adroid, but I still keep coming back for more.
So here's my quick take on a few aspects of the game. The immersive experience and fun gameplay are the best part. I hate more stealth games because they seem so cheesy, simply figuring out the enemy patrol paths and then sitting in "shadows" so you can't be seen. In this game, if you are crouching two feet away from someone looking right at you, it doesn't matter how dark the room is, they are going to see you eventually. Sometimes they walk up and squint for a while, but they figure it out. You actually have to hide behind and under things, be completely silent, and yet keep moving.
Unfortunately the tools that you can craft aren't always that useful. In fact, if you use them, it's too easy to attract the alien and get yourself killed. Everything you do in the game makes noise, and every noise makes you cringe because you're afraid the alien will hear. So I like using the smoke bombs because they make me hard to see, but they make a loud bang. In the end, some tools were indispensable, but more often than not I found a way to sneak through without them.
The graphics are fantastic. I run it on the highest settings without a problem. I remember when I was hiding behind a desk and the alien was standing over it, and I looked down and saw the alien perfectly reflected in a puddle on the ground. It was spectacular. I could actually track the alien's movements by looking at his reflection. The environment also has great (and sometimes creepy) detail, adding to immersion. There's also plenty of things borrowed explicitly from the movie, which really add to the effect.
The sound is fantastic. The music is incredible. I recommend turning down the music, but not turning it off, because I found that the creepy music was often most responsible for increasing my fear. Sometimes the music was so loud and terrifying that I was afraid to do anything because I figured the alien was on to me. So it's good to turn down the music so you can hear the actual alien better. His loud footsteps and other movement sounds really allow you to track him well.
I also found the story to be engaging and interesting. It's not the most unique and surprising story ever, and it's not loaded with shocking twists, but it still really does the job. It makes me want to keep going. An early review complained about the voice acting, but honestly, I think the only bad voice acting was in some lines from Amanda Ripley at the very started of the game. Most of the time she does a fantastic job and sounds honestly scared and relatable. I like that they didn't have a silent hero. For some reason, though, at the very start when she is not yet scared, her acting isn't as good.
The sad thing is that now that I am done, I want more. Survivor Mode is there, but it's very confusing and difficult, so I'm not sure I'm really ready for it. It has limited supplies, a timer, and no map or clear guidance. It takes the difficulty of the compaign and expands upon it.
In summary, this game will be considered a classic. Buy it.

Dark Souls is still a hard game, atleast harder than your average game. Dark Souls II seems a bit easier than Dark Souls but when you get to Drangleic Castle you won't notice a thing! The multiplayer system has improved a lot since Dark souls I. summon signs pop up everywhere when you're playing on a busy hour. This can be of great help if you are having trouble with a boss. It is also a nice thing to have when you are stuck at a boss. The world is really well made but it doesn't feel as cleverly connected as the world in Dark Souls I.
Even though it might lack a few things its predeccor had, this is still a really good game

A game about death. Literally. Odds are, your first 10 minutes in the game will result in the death from stupidity of rolling off a cliff. And that won't be the end of it. Exploring a world of hollows, or undead in simpler terms, you'll find more than enough ways to stay angry at this game in the most satisfying way. How is rage satisfying?
When you tackle the challenge over and over again, trying out new methods to fight your way through zombies, giants, demons, knights, and a myriad of bosses, when you finally find something that works, this game gives you a sense of excitement and accomplishment that no other series has done.
And for people who play a game for the story more, this game is packed full of hidden lore, slowly revealed to the player by collecting items and boss souls. There's always a reason for something ridiulously crazy existing, and it's always an exciting feat to understand it; this is coming from someone who skips most of the dialouge in rpgs too. The world of Dark Souls is truly one of the most fascinating fantasy realms that I've ever come across.
In beating the game, you have the option to make it even harder, or you can simply start a new character; there's endless ways to play through the game, and so many weapons to fit different playstyles, as well as many covenants, or in-game groups, the player can join to appeal to their taste, whether it's a co-op related covenant or one set on invading those who have sinned and punishing them, or one that increases the in game difficulty even further for those who love a REAL challenge.
In short, Dark Souls is a fantastic game that kept my attention for many, many hours of my life, and I don't regret a single one invested into this game. I beckon you; to anyone reading this review, buy this game now, and prepare for the experience that you'll never forget.

I understand you can go offline to avoid PVP invasions, but it's not worth the effort to me, I'd rather the game build in more acceptable ways to avoid it.  I actually really like the way PVP works in the game, but it needs to have a simple on/off switch, as a result, in its current state I can't recommend the game.

Having played every Total War game since release I can say now I love Rome II. Are there flaws? Sure there are plenty. Is the game worth buying? Yes, absolutely yes.
*Cons*
-Public order and food management is constant and at times annoying, even if it is a good mechanic.
-Warscape engine is poorly optimized for infantry combat. Combat ends in blobs unless you micromanage.
-Pathfinding during sieges has  a 10% chance of slowing the game down making it unplayable.
-Shogun II is a much more polished and difficult game (difficult in a good way)
*Pros*
-DAT CINEMATIC CAMERA
-The loading music will get you pumped for destruction.
-Graphics that make your hardware weep. Even if you have a decent rig (some amazing, some poor optimization).
-Armies need a general, no more tiny stacks of 2-4 units.
-Garrison armies can actually do something.
-Easy to micromange agents (also no agent movies, I always skipped them anyways)
-Combined land and sea battles are beyond awesome.

Let me start by saying this. No More Room In Hell is just a half-life 2 modification and it is better (in my opinion) than other zombie survival games.
This game is unique because unlike other games, No More Room In Hell has slow moving zombies(a few can run) that attack in hordes and waves making the fearful challenge that is this game. There is also a limited number of guns and ammo given to your group of survivors. Melee weapons however come in large amounts and have different uses.
There are heavy melee weapons such as a fire axe and hammer, but there are also smaller light weapons such as a kitchen knife or a machete. The heavy weapons will often kill a zombie with one hit if you aim for the head but will make you tired and will disable you from running, pushing, etc... The light weapons will often take a number of hits to kill a zombie even if you attack the head but it won't make you as tired.
There is a large number of guns in the game and just like the melee weapons, they have their own prime reasons for use.
guns such as the pump shotgun, and uzi are great for taking out a group of zombies, and other guns such as pistols and rifles are good for single target zombies.
The game's community is large and is normally full of fun people, but it isn't uncommon to end up in a game with some guy that isn't the most fun to be around. (total ♥♥♥♥ing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥). Like some other games, if you wish you can follow No More Room In Hell on facebook, Twitter, Youtube, and Steam, so you can keep up to date with new updates and content added to the game. The game itself is full of servers that are played on the many good default maps or costom maps that you yourself can make and add to the game.
The two main game modes are Survival and Objective.
In
, you and your group of survivors must survive (duh) against waves of zombies. With each wave, the numbers of zombies grow and so does the difficulty of the zombies. Your group must protect itself and try to live till the end and get rescued by the army. This isn't an easy task and will take time and communication with your group to complete successfully in one peice. Every few waves, there will be a supply drop, In the supply drop there will be weapons (both guns and melee), ammo, tools, boards for doors and windows, and other useful stuff.
In
, you and your group must complete a bunch of tasks to continue your journey to a extraction zone for rescue. Unlike in survival mode, there are no supply drops. There are only the guns you find as you walk around and try not to die. same thing goes for the other items in the game.
To add to the whole survival feel of this game, if you are attacked by a zombie and don't die, You may end up bleeding or becoming infected. Both will end in death if you leave either one untreated for too long. If you are bleeding, you must find a bandage before you bleed to death, and maybe even a first aid kit. If you are infected, then you must find pills to stop the spred of the infection temporarily. You must find more over time, but if you die from the infection, a zombie attack, or from a fellow survivor, then you will become a zombie. (only if you were infected).
To end off this review, I'll list off everything that this game has.
I'll rate this with a 8/10

Alien: Isolation had a lot to prove to me from the beginning. I'm a huge fan of Alien/Aliens, and so far nobody has gotten it right in terms of how an Alien game should feel. Dead Space got close, but since it is merely inspired by Alien and not directly in the franchise, it didn't fill the need for a solid Alien video game experience. Alien: Isolation has nailed it. Never before have I felt so vulnerable in a game, so uncertain as to whether I really could keep it together enough to make it to the next checkpoint without mishap. From start to finish, I feared the Xenomorph and its keen, unpredictable intelligence. However, like Ripley in the first Alien film, my fear was soon balanced by the will to do what needed to be done, whatever the risk. I didn't become less afraid, but I did become more skillful at eluding it as time went on. However, when the creature outsmarted me or did something unexpected, that same vulnerable fear returned right up to the end credits. I strongly recommend this game. It's the best Alien experience created since the release of the first two films and stays true to what we love about them from start to finish.

A timeless classic! If you played Bioshock, you can clearly see from where did they take a huge chunk of it. System Shock 2 is amazing. It's difficult but not impossible, it has a great atmosphere, great story and tension runs high from start to finish. It's not  a "horror game" in it's core, but that doesn't stop it from being quite scary in a number of occasions. The only downside is the deterioration system (which is FAR TOO INTENSE) and the fact that getting the right skill points are CRUCIAL to the conclusion of the game.

System Shock 2 is everything I look for in a game. Great gameplay, great story, nice graphics, great soundtrack, great atmosphere, uncanningly amazing voice acting. The player models are a bit "ugh" but aside from that the graphics are quite good for the time it was released. The one thing I didn't really like about it was that the default controls really suck. W is forward (as usual), but A and D were turn left and right, respectivly, and S was crouch, whereas Z and C were strafe left and right, respectivly, and X was backward. Of course, this can be easily changed, so it is but a minor annoyance.
The thing that first hit me about this game was the tutorial. Most of the time, the tutorials in games are crudly done (Half-Life) or very vague (Ghost Recon) if existant at all (Day of Defeat). System Shock 2 takes tutorials to a whole new level. It's very thorough and fits into the storyline like a cute glove. And if you're on your second playthrough, you can skip the tutorial completely. However, if it is your first time playing, you really should play it. This is not just another FPS. This is unique.
So how much is this worth? More than Steam is selling it for. If you don't like RPGs, you wouldn't like this. If you only play modern games because "GWAFIXXXXX", stop it for this game. You can't just not play it.
Oh, and by the way, there is a co-op mode. Haven't tried it yet, so I'll get back to you on how well that works.
It only gets better with age. . . . :headcrab:

I've always loved this game, but I think that I appreciate System Shock 2 even more now than when I first played it. The game's tense and even frightening at times. I think this is why I can appreciate the game so much more in 2013 than I did back when it originally came out, as its juxtaposition against modern games like the Bioshocks emphasize System Shock 2's accomplishments as even more groundbreaking than they once were.
The only criticisms I have with playing it in 2013 are temporary criticisms. You'll first want to download a model replacer for npcs. The original low poly models now look a bit silly and clash with the experience the game intends to provide, so get a model replacer mod set up prior to playing. You'll also want to rebind the keys before playing, but it seems like there's an included preset that makes the game control like a modern fps, so switch to that.
Make sure to play it with the lights off and the volume up.

First, let me say that the gameplay and interface have overall left me with a very positive impression. As regards the gameplay in particular, it is indeed excellent, although even at the easiest setting the shot meter is very unforgiving. A slight miss off the center line, left or right, yields an erring shot in no man's land. So you better hone your reflexes. That caveat notwithstanding, the game is great fun. Kudos to the developers at this stage of development.
Now, on the less positive side: the graphics are nice, but a bit disappointing, if we consider that they are roughly on par with the graphics in the game Links 2003. I must say, however, that I am here comparing the best and most recent offerings of this old game, with respect to available courses, and the likes of Shardowlands in Perfect Golf. Still I find that the vegetation, especially the foliage of leafy trees, could and should be better, more polished and photo realistic. I would likewise welcome some flowers in places to add a touch of color and variety to this green fest. Also, even with the antialiasing on, there are still some noticeable jagged edges. Keep in mind that I have the graphical settings at ultra high, with max resolution of 1440 P. In short, I believe there is still work to be done on the part of the developers when it comes to graphics.
Clearly, and quite predictably at this stage, there is also a lot of work to be done when It comes to available courses, clubs, and avatars. Furthermore, I would love to see an array of AI opponents of different skill levels for off-line games.
I suggest Perfect Parallel include a store in the game to give the option of considerably expanding the content at a reasonable cost. I personally have no issue with financially rewarding the developers (like the competent course designer Mike Jones) for this most promising game. Yes, I am hooked, albeit with some reservations at the present time. I am truly burning with anticipation, thinking of what is to follow for us golf lovers.
Let us hope for the best.

First off, a big thanks to the devs on bringing us this Early Access version of Perfect Golf. I'm running the game in windowed mode 1280x768 on a 5 year old laptop with AA on and Bloom on. Trees are set at 350, shadows 200, Grass 100 and camera view distance 1500. All things considered the game runs good apart from a few stutters here and there that I can live with and haven't yet affected the playability.
Ball Physics: the team has done a wonderful job on the ball physics, especially after the latest update. I considered the ball physics in Links v1.07 to be one of the best I've seen in a golf game but in PG they've taken it to another level of realism. Sure, there is still some work to be done but having played a few different golf games this is the best I've experienced as yet .......
BUT .... while I feel that tee to green the devs have created up to now the best simulation of real golf yet seen in a computer game, I do feel an element of realism is then lost with the putting model. To help explain this I should point out I am a novice real life golfer, having only played the game for around 18 months. So it is fresh in my mind what it is like to be a beginner and having to learn the game. I feel a simulation should have the same sort of difficulties and learning curve with all aids off as the real thing. That may also mean I'll never be able to shoot under par for a round as in real life. A par on a hole should feel like an achievement. Unfortunately the putting model destroys this sense of achievement because it feels like I have too much help. Sometimes I misjudge my long putts on a real course massively - and that never seems to happen to me in PG due to the putting meter. And sometimes in real life I've putted from the fairway just off the green and given too much power and ended up off the other side of the green. I can't seem to do that in PG as my power is limited by the meter.
My suggestion - a straight swing bar that follows the movement of the mouse. The putter head placed two thirds down the bar with movement then for back swing and power and length of follow through for movement. Putting aids can be markings on the bar to help judge distance but true simulation mode with no aids would be with no markings and just from feel as in real golf. Don't know if something like this is possible. It would mean that by selecting a putter the graphic would automatically switch from an arcing swing meter to a straight putting bar. In simulation mode full back swing (of course restricted to a point) and full, fast follow through would always result in a maximum power putt.
A free roam mode would be nice, even if it was only restricted to a 20 or 30 yard zone around the golfers position, to allow for better planning of shots like in real golf when views are restricted. Of course, these restricted views should also be set to golfers eye level for realism.
Look forward to future update improvements and hopefully more courses. Great job so far and the closest to a simulation of the game I've yet to play.

I've been playing golf and computer games for about 25 years now, ever since I was about seven years old, so I feel reasonably qualified to comment on something that combines the two.
The early access of Perfect Golf is a fantastic start and the devs appear to have every motivation to bring the game to full fruition. Unlike many early access titles, the devs at Perfect Golf aren't promising heaven and earth just to get people's money but they are promising to create a great golf sim for real golfers, something I firmly believe they are very capable of delivering.
The current basic build is solid and enjoyable enough to hint at what is to come. Of course it has some bugs and it is missing many features and some areas require polish but these are all being identified and dealt with systematically and professionally as far as I can tell.
For anyone looking to buy this game in its current form, note that it does not yet have the following features which some may want to wait for:
- Computer opponents
- Career mode
- Golfer appearance customisation
- Statistics and Tracking
I would also say that, while the game looks very nice on my machine in ultra high detail at 1080p (you need a proper gaming graphics card here by the way), the golfer animation could be doing with being more fluid and the feeling more solid when the ball is struck or impacts the turf. It just feels a little floaty at this point with the golfer, terrain and ball all having a slightly disconnected feel. Additionally, the wind conditions seem to have no effect on the trees or flag; at 50mph the trees move identically to when the wind is at 10mph.
On the other hand, the in flight ball physics are awesome and the mouse control "motionswing" mechanic is brilliant and is easily the closest feel to a real golf swing that I've experienced in a PC golf game. This mechanism puts the onus on the tempo and rhythm of your swing rather than just how straight you can move the mouse back and through (anyone remember table edging?). Downswing too fast and the ball is going left, too slow and it's going right, similar to real golf. If you let the pressure get to you and you lose your tempo, you're in trouble, just like real golf.
Also, the real time weather and sky conditions make everything feel a lot more realistic and help with immersion.
At this point there are no computer opponents and no sort of career mode but these are planned. Additionally, there is no golfer or gear customisation beyond being able to select which 14 clubs you want in your bag.
If you are a new starter (or even if you're not), here are my top ten tips for bringing down your scoring and increasing your enjoyment of the game:
1) go to options and change the camera to track your shot because it's a static camera by default which is boring
2) bring up the map using the button on the top right of the screen to allow for easier aiming
3) right clicking in the power circle allows you to change club and select normal or chip shot type
4) right clicking again in the power circle allows you to alter the trajectory or add fade/draw bias
5) read the instructions and practice with motionswing. It may be tough to start with but it's worth it when it clicks!
6) The marker on the putting green has nothing to do with power, only direction. The centre point on the putting power bar is the power needed to reach the hole on a flat green. You need to go past this point if you want to putt uphill
7) activate the terrain slope graphics for normal shots as well as putts because the ball being above or below the feet will send the ball left or right respectively
8) wind seems to have smaller effects on the ball than in other golf games but once the speed goes above 20mph it starts to have more of an impact
9) go into your golfer settings and swap something out for a 64deg wedge. This is easily the most useful club in the bag behind the driver and the putter
10) if you want to chat in a multiplayer game, hit enter
As far as multiplayer goes, it is currently based on a peer to peer hosting system with the normal modes of play you would expect and a few unusual ones. Since there is no central server yet you need to ensure you have a fast and stable internet connection if you are going to host a game. Otherwise, ask someone with a better connection to be the host. My experiences have been mostly positive as both host and guest with no disconnections but perhaps I have been lucky with my opponents.
From memory I think there are 6 courses currently to choose from and new ones are being added regularly as part of the updates.
If you are a fan of golf and you are looking for a proper golf simulator you should buy this game now.
If you enjoy golf games in general but want a career mode, customisable equipment and computer opponents, check back in 6-12 months.
If you want to pretend you are a superhuman who can drive the ball 400 yards and impart spin with the power of your mind, go play Tiger Woods.

Black Mesa is definitely worth a buy. It captures the atmosphere of the original Halflife exactly as I remember. The annoying brain-hoppers, the fantastic firefights with marines and the very scary fish-monsters are all there.
The developers made some additional improvements (well at least I cannot remember them being in the original, or I just hadn’t figured it out at the time…), like you can pick up automated turrets and use them on enemies, and the option to feed those ceiling buggers a snack like a yummy steel barrel or explosive charge. The corrosive splatter and blood animations on Morgen Freeman are great. Maybe they could have taken it even further with adding damage over time (till you jump in a pool with a big hungry fish...).
On the downside, the devs made some changes (or kept stuff) that I personally don’t like that much. While the level design gives you a good immersive feel like in the original, the length of most levels overstay their welcome. After some time, I had enough of crawling through linear corridors and ride train number zillion into another electric puddle. I remember from the original that once the marines dropped in, it was an almost non-stop thrill till the weird alien world.
Also, Black Mesa recreated the big bugs that you cannot kill with small arms fire. They didn’t have to. Those scenes might be iconic, but they were, and still are, more confusing than fun. It is a bit strange to have a 20 foot tall hulk waiting patiently, like a faithful dog, for you to insert a plug to electrocute it to death.
And lastly, expect some fun-draining bugs. In particular the green blasting aliens (but also marines on some occasions) have a tendency to have broken IA (just stand still, and do nothing). This not only breaks immersion, it also reduces the difficulty of the game. Also the end-game is still missing. So, devs forget new skins for guns, I don’t care, just fix the brain-dead alien issue (which is known for over half a year) and finish the end-game!! Please ;)

Where do I begin? Okay, so I now have over 110 hours on the Steam client and had somewhere between 300-550 hours on the original client. Now, I will say that there are negative aspects to the game. However these are more particular to MOBAs in general and less about Smite. Matchmaking in League, Dota, (I assume Heroes of the Storm, but never played and never heard anything about its matchmaking) and Smite is no exception. If you're trying to teach a friend to play without making a smurf account, well, it's really REALLY hard. Since a party will always play against people around the highest party member's level, it usually results in absolute domination by the opposing team because you have at least one team mate (Being your friend you are trying to teach) who barely understands the game. This is less of a problem for experienced players of other MOBAs like LoL or Dota, however not unheard of either. The grind to level 30 is also astonishing long. I should mention that even with all this time played, I am still a level 25. I've been playing since the closed beta in October 2012. Sure, I've been playing off and on in that time, however, that doesn't change the fact that I have a♥♥♥♥♥♥ton of time in the game. The only reason this is a problem is that you can't play ranked until you are level 30. If you're playing a normal game in the "premier" gamemode Conquest, expect bad plays, bad team comps, and overall bad team players. I personally recommend that if you do play conquest, play with a friend who is on or above your skill level. If you're alone, I suggest gamemodes such as Arena and 3v3 Joust. Both are shorter games which means less time commitment and usually have more laid back people who aren't gonna wine if you end up being the first blood. This is not to say the game is bad. The game is a downright amazing game that I would recommend to almost anyone. The players themselves are the bad part. This isn't even mentioning the totally awesome concept of playing as freaking GODS. "Oh, so you're saying that in this game I can murder Zeus with Thor, proving my dominance as the best god of thunder? SIGN ME UP!"
TL;DR
This is a free to play game with an awesome concept, awesome gameplay mechanics, and provides you with an awesome time. Play the game. There is actually no reason not to give it a go.

I don't think there's much more to add that people haven't said about the technical and game-balance successes or failures of the game.
I also want to mention, before I get to it,  that I did appreciate quite a bit the nature of the SP portion of the game.  The take on "advanced" warfare was interesting, and I actually thought it was a good piece of enjoyable enough sci-fi-ish sort of material, somethign that shows us a possible future with tech that might or might not be around in a few decades.  The exos, the portable walls, drones, etc., are probably going to be part of our future sooner rather than later, and I found that more entertaining than not.
The downside is that beyond the SP, the MP *can* possible be unfulfilling.  I think, socially speaking, the implementation of the MP portion for PC contains (and continues) traditions that are bad for PC and gaming as a whole.  These are small (or not so small) things, such as no keyboard conversing between matches, connectivity bars instead of ping values, and a pre-set 800 ping connection threshold, amongst other.  These aren't game-breaking individually or as a whole, but the fact that they made it in either without or in defiance of protest, is somewhat alarming and depressing.
In some ways, and to refer to what CheckForAPulse_ wrote, my experiences and my eyes don't match up.  The game can be telling me that I while we all have fantastic, 4-bar connectivity, but there's no crispness, no consistency in how hits register, while at times a 3 or 2-bar connection results in a more consistent and agreeable play experience.   I've seen someone with 4 bars warping laggedly around the map, and I daresay he's not experiencing great a great connection... although to him, perhaps we are all playing in slow motion.
In any event, add to that no numerical ping values, and you basically have cencorship of the worst kind, where the game is telling me that my senses, my experience, my input, is all subordinate to what it defines as my experiences; that is to say, I will feel what and how it tells me to feel, and dammed be my own senses!  You feel like something is wrong?  Nope, you are wrong, and so accept it.  Thus, the game forces me to censor myself, if only so the dissonance between what the game tells me and what my mind and body tells me, can be reduced.  That process becomes more difficult as time goes on.
Furthermore, there are no player/third-party run servers, so I cannot find someone running a server closer to my physical location, or not running one on a Doritos Chip processor.  Once again, if my experiences and the feedback from the game matched up, then I have less to complain about.  But, despite that disconnect, I cannot actively work to try to better my own play experience, as I could in a less restrictive (or less console-centric) design.
In the end, such things can add up to an unattractive play experience.  I had a good time in SP, but MP less so.  If it's just repetetive weapons, so be it.  Poor server performance (if they're servers at all), so be it.  Punishing lag compensation?  Well, okay.  Great game but highly opaque mechanisms finding and regulating my games?  Well, better than nothing.  But, in my opinion, CoD:AW falls short in too many aspects, and as game time accrues, my play experiences is not better for those lackings.
But it on a big sale if you really want, but to me, the game's sins are not as much technical as they are the type which should make PC gamers say, "this is why we can't have nice things."

When one has truly experienced a good story they are left with a sense of emptiness upon finally reaching the end. Throughout the story, you've come to know the characters. You've gone on an adventure with them, only to be violently ripped back into reality. It's as if they, as well as the time you spent with them, never existed in the first place. It's really saying something when a 2-3 hour long game is immersive and memorable enough to do something like this.
-Story 9/10-
My only complaint is how short/lacking in content it is. The entirety of it takes place in the Tower of Eternity where the protagonist, Senia, is looking for her sister who ventured into it. The Tower of Eternity is supposedly very dangerous after all. As far as the setting of it goes, there just isn't much. We don't even know anything about the outside world.
Okay that aside, how about that sisterly love? Seriously, this is some tear-jerking♥♥♥♥♥♥ The story between Senia and her sister Magaleta is probably what got me so hooked. It's tragic but beautiful at the same time.
-Combat 9/10-
For a classic-style RPG, the combat is quite nice albeit repetitive and beyond easy. It's a nice change of pace from turn-based encounters in most other games. Unfortunately, there are only 4 skills in the game, two of which are actually useful. You'll mostly be using Q to do damage and R when it's up to nuke bosses. That's about it. There's not much diversity, but then again there isn't enough game to really justify going further in depth in this department.
-Music 10/10-
Some really beautiful stuff here. The only BGM that I felt didn't fit was right at the start of the game. Everything else was perfect. On top of that, all the sound files are sitting loose in the game folder. Free music too! :D
-Art 9/10-
For an indie RPG of this caliber, the sprites are quite well made. The larger bosses had a lot of effort put into their art. The only con I can think of is how some of the bosses attacks kinda seem like the don't link up very well to the sprites. An example would be the giant lasers on s few of them.
Seriously, just get it. Knock it out in a few hours. You've got nothing to lose!

First off the game is addictive. The music track is complimentary to the landscapes, both are outstanding.  You are competing with other players who are running around trying to accomplish the same tasks you are. There definitely are times when a partner comes in handy, but you are all attempting to accomplish the same goals. Non player charcters often add to the comic relief with witty (and some so not witty) comments.
The good things about the game: First, the gaming controls are simple and easy to learn. Those who are familar with Elder Scrolls wil feel comfortable, those like me who are new to the series will make many mistakes and smack your head for making dumb mistakes. Secondly, the charcter you build develops skills and gains abilities through the game.
Bad things:  None really. It took several hours to downlaod and setup.  After that no real problems.  Had the server drop out of the game once so far, no biggie.  I would like to see more development and personal interaction between your charcter and the charcters you meet in your journey, but that would be a programming nightmare I imagine.

Alien: Isolation had a lot to prove to me from the beginning. I'm a huge fan of Alien/Aliens, and so far nobody has gotten it right in terms of how an Alien game should feel. Dead Space got close, but since it is merely inspired by Alien and not directly in the franchise, it didn't fill the need for a solid Alien video game experience. Alien: Isolation has nailed it. Never before have I felt so vulnerable in a game, so uncertain as to whether I really could keep it together enough to make it to the next checkpoint without mishap. From start to finish, I feared the Xenomorph and its keen, unpredictable intelligence. However, like Ripley in the first Alien film, my fear was soon balanced by the will to do what needed to be done, whatever the risk. I didn't become less afraid, but I did become more skillful at eluding it as time went on. However, when the creature outsmarted me or did something unexpected, that same vulnerable fear returned right up to the end credits. I strongly recommend this game. It's the best Alien experience created since the release of the first two films and stays true to what we love about them from start to finish.

I'm a major fan of the Aliens franchise ever since i was young, my mother told me that when i was 3 or 6 i can't remeber that i watched the entire movie of Aliens. Come back to now I truely appreciated the concept and story for the movies. AVP 2008 was a so so game but it definently better than Aliens Colonial Marines. It was a bomb shell of a game.
But when Alien Isolation was first shown, i was excited. When I got the game I thrilled at the same time scared beyond comepare. The game is everything that the Movie deserved in a game.
The game has a good story, being Ellen Ripely's daughter Amanda, who is looking for answers 20 years after the events of Alien.  The location couldn't of been better chossen on a Space station, which is a first for the franchise. Because if you think about it Alien was on the Nostomo a  Commericial cargo ship, which was a small ship with a small crew . For Isolation your on a much larger Station the Sevastopol with a sizable skeleton crew of  150+ people.
The situation in the game went to♥♥♥♥♥♥in favor of the crew aboard the station, and you as you relise what you have on your hands. Hands down this game is scary, to many jump scares, either from the xeno or the random face hugger. In the begining alone my heart was pounding listening on everything i could to make sure the xeno didnt get the jump on me.
Once the xenomorth became more frequent in its apperances I had to adapt quickly to them so I could continue the story. I found everything perfect. The graphics are just gorgous its like being in a interactive Alien movie. Creative Assembly did a perfect job with this game.
This game was well worth its price with its great story line, and it was long which to some is bad but to me it was perfect for me. So much to play and learn in the story. All in all this game should be nominated for game of the year the best game for this year.

This is my first time ever leaving a review for a game but I feel almost obligated. Slime Rancher is such a delight! It's such a laid-back, fun way to spend some time. I've found myself playing it a lot whenever I'm stressed or not feeling great- it just plain makes me happy. It's hard not to be, when you're staring at a bunch of smiling little slimes!
I would absolutely recommend this game to anyone who plays games casually, or even people brand new to video games.
For someone who likes collecting or taking care of creatures without much stress of them dying- which is the fun part for me, personally- this is a perfect game. You get to run around bringing home slimes and exploring a diverse alien world for various resources that can be used to farm or invent devices to make your life easier. There are simple puzzles here and there and hidden goodies spread across the map for you to hunt down, and plenty of things to do to keep you constantly busy. It is not a difficult game by any means, as there is no real combat or any hard problems to solve, but those who just like to sit back and waste time having fun will likely find it enjoyable.
However, I will say that unless you are fairly easily entertained, the current state of the game might leave some things to be desired. Exploration sort of feels like a side quest more than anything, since caring for your slimes might take some time, and exploration is something that kind of has to be prepared for rather than going on spontaneous adventures (unless you're willing to risk agitated slimes escaping!) There also simply isn't a humongous map TO explore and you learn your way around quite quickly. People who may come to the game expecting to explore this huge open world with tons of different slimes might find themselves disappointed. The game still is in early access, however, so it might broaden with time!
tldr; This is such a fun and happy game and I adore it! I bought it when it was on sale but knowing what I do now, I would have happily bought it for the full price!

Very uninteresting tower defense - no towers that play interestingly off each other, a 'slow' tower confusingly named poison that has no discernible effect and is more expensive than the basic damage tower. A ground-only damage tower that seems to be identical in effect to the ground-and-air basic damage tower, apart from not hitting airborne creatures. No upgrade trees, just straight upgrades, which seem to be 100% not worth it (they cost more than half a tower and don't increase the damage by that much [or at all? hard to be sure], though they do slightly increase range); the stats aren't visible so it's hard to tell. Seems like all you really need is lots of splash damage (I think it's still better against one unit than the basic damage towers, per cost) and beacons when invisibles come in.
The graphics are pleasant, but in my opinion that's all this has going for it over any other tower defense game. (And there are others prettier too.)

In fact, it's not a bad game, but a td finished in less than 4 hours with all achievements is a bit sad.
All I can tell you is that I enjoyed it, but, again, for 4 hours.
So, from my point of view, I can make a positive review because I got what I expected nevertheless if you are hoping to find a very good td in that game go away.

I found the difficulty to ramp up to "grind map until you figure out the "one way" to beat it". Not particularly fond of not being told what things are or what things do or otherwise notify me of what is happening by way of tooltips billboards and other informative cues. By the time you get to level 5 you better have memorized what towers do and where they are best placed and partnered with through repetitive behavior or you might get too frustrated to keep playing. Once you figure out what the towers are and what creeps they are powerful against the game gets a lot more fun. Which by the way, can take up to several hours to the "new to tower defense genre" player. This is a grinder TD game similar to Prime World: Defenders and Ancient Planet or even Defense Grid. If you are a hard core TD nut you'll like the challenge of learning the game through tens if not hundreds of hours of trial and error. But to those who like to have a strategy that is derived from data and information given to you by the game, will not play this game much at all and might get 10 hours out of it in total. At the time of writing I have 2.1 hours of play time and plan to give it at least another 25 before I give it a solid judgement.
How much range or power or whatever a tower has is not known to you in the game other than the 'info' tab on the front page.﻿ I have yet to find out what the enemies are and what they do other than memorizing their cute little sprite and alocating -> thats a land unit, or that's a land unit with armor, that's a flyer...etc...
Pros-
Love the music and color scheme
Beautiful backdrops
Creative comic book load and cutscenes
Fast Action
Not overwhelmed with zillions of towers/upgrades/creeps and other choices given to the player
Cons-
Take any run of the mill tower defense game and change the theme and you have this game.
Does not properly inform the player about the game or the units in the game
User Interface lacks style and creativity
Game difficulty over time can become impossible to the casual player early on
Game maps seem to be 'one way' solutions or at best minimal types of tower pattern(partners) solutions

There's been plenty of gripes with this game, and i'm in complete understanding of all of those gripes, but this is a good game (In my honest opinion). If you have the money to buy the game, and are willing to spend the money, it's certainly a good buy. Rome II is best to buy when on sale, however, because some people don't appreciate the streamlining they have put in place. I'm unsure of how this effects the overall quality of the game compared to other total wars, because i've only ever played this one, but the game is entertaining if you're choosing one of the harder factions to start with. If you plan on playing as rome, or carthage, or whatever other power with more than 2 cities in the beginning of the game, give it up. It loses it's entertainment value rapidly if you're picking a well off faction. Hell, any faction with Easy as a start difficulty WILL BE BORING. But the battles will certainly be interesting. If you're a formation attuned commander (Like me) you're♥♥♥♥♥♥outta luck. The units absolutely REFUSE to remain in formation if you attempt to work with a formation in a battle. They seldom remain in formations to begin with, unless you use the lock function, which ♥♥♥♥s your control over them 80% of the time. The public order is comprable to a sexually distressed teenage girl, and is always on some sort of mood swing, and rebellions are generally inevetable, ESPECIALLY if you enslave enemies often. You'll have to dedicate a good bit of your attention to keeping military contigients in cities to ensure rebels either don't rise up, or don't take the cities. The balance of power meter really only serves to discourage you in some places if you've any real tactical genius in you, and auto-resolving always gets more troops killed the necissary, and it takes away the fulfillment of winning an actual battle with your mind. DON'T USE AUTO RESOLVE, Elephants are intensely overpowered, and most units suck at the start of the game (But this is familiar to any RTS player), and Thracians are all OP. 7.5/10 For some of it's falling short in places that should be important (Like politics, which I STILL don't understand) But as with any RTS, the win is the game. Winning is so pleasing (When not using auto-resolve) And spikes pride in your units. There's PLENTY of good features, like how you can rename armies and give them traditions, but it's largely restricted in terms of customization (Which urks me). This game is a good buy when it's on sale, and isn't being sold at some ungodly price that's going to leave your wallet as barren as Caesar himself, and leaves you with a game that can get really boring, really fast.

I don't know how to start this. But maybe I should start by saying that this game is the latest Total War game in a universe of 7 to 9 games if you consider Napoleon and "Last Samurai" as StandAlones.
If I were to review this regardless of the previous games I would say it is worth buying, it is a solid game, has some bugs but none game breaking at the moment, the devs update the game once in a while, the battles are epic, the campaign in early and mid game is engaging kind of feels like Civilization and then mixing that with the accomplishments of your RTS battles it's a pretty solid rewarding experience. And I'd have to give it at least a 7/10 in the game's current state. Shame that the developers decided to go with all those DLC things with factions and units. But the game is there and it's good. I already spent 460h on it and most of the time it was great.
Now reviewing this taking into consideration the earlier games... This game was very, very disapointing. It is a little better now with the patches but it's still disappointing. Family trees, the building system of Rome I, the inability to have smaller defending armies to complement the garrissons that are led by captains instead of generals, the AI which isn't better and at times is worse, the agent system is rather dumb, all the mini clips that would pop out throughout the game are gone, the field battles are quicker and have arcady goals and sometimes it looks like arcade games. So... There's a lot of thing that were dumbed down, others totally removed. When I first started playing I thought "Oh my god, the graphics are nice, not as good as I thought they'd be but nice, gameplay is nice... oh but where is the family tree? but... I can't have armies without generals? what?"  Well I got used to it.  But the emersion is just not there. You play because you want to win. And in late game it just feels like a Grind. It's painful. The Civil War system is completely broken as well. How is that? I would have made it as one army goes rogue or all the armies controled by the family who rebeled and those would go take your capital. If they took it they'd be in charge. You could either give up command or lose your territory and try to re-capture the capital to gain control of the empire. That'd be awesome but no. You just get a random number of armies spawn around one of your cities and that's the civil war. Plain dum and stupid.
The only reason I kept playing Rome II is because I made a mod to make the battles exponentially better. Plus there are features I can't live without and with other mods the game is pretty nice to play. Considering all this and the earlier games I'd rate the game a 4/10 due to the huge let down, with mods I'd give it 6/10.
It's worth trying. But wait for it to go on sales. Below 35 ~ 40 euros/dollars it is worth to pick and try.

At first, when I saw this game I told my self:"It's just another MOBA, no need to waste my time trying it", hell I was wrong.
Game feels more like Action RPG than MOBA actually, yes there are builds for each character and yes this game has same mechanics as Dota and LoL, but it's made differently.
While Dota being more noob hostile at the time I was trying too play it, this game has much more explanation for what is what and who is who. Item shop has "Recomended" pre-set for you too buy, but you always can go wild by opening "All-Items" folder. Also the fact that you cant buy stuff that's not compatable with your character (No Swords or Hammers for Mages and no Magical Staffs for Physichal characters) makes it even better.
You can buy 6 items like in Dota or LoL, but you also have 4 additional slots for your active items and consumables (2 for each).
So far the biggest struggle for me are voice commands, but It's nice that they are there, along with Pings on mini-map, this can save your time if you know the right key-combo to say something to your teammates.
The game gets updates frequently, getting more Gods and balance changes along with some sick skins for Gods.
One thing I don't like about skins is that there are Golden and Diamond ones, they simply look stupid and unoriginal,
I see how devs wanted to go for CoD-like(I'm very funny) experience, but they simply look aesthetically ugly.
There are also rewards for playing game every day and for reffering friend who told you about this game.
So yeah, try it, if you liked MOBAs but hated their strategyish look than you will love this game, for sure.
