Purchased it five days ago, and have played non-stop since. I know this is a fact everyone knows, but it is a Rust clone, and to be honest, I'm fine with that. The game does some things better than Rust, some things worse. It's cartoonish appearance makes it interesting. Vivid colors and clear contrast is half it's charm. The hardcore factor is not really true though. There is nothing in this game that is hardcore. Within an hour of playing, you will know the game mechanics and how most necessities work.
-Beautiful graphics
As I said earlier, the graphics are amazing. They need more polishing, but they are pretty nonetheless. Gun textures are pretty dull though. I would choose this game over Rust when it comes to graphics.
-A sense of achievement
This is something the game nailed. When it's so easy to lose your resources, building a huge fortress feels amazing. The fact that the whole world is working against you makes every little upgrade worthwhile, and pretty satisfying. The simple upgrade from an Iron Hatchet to a Gold one is pure bliss.
-Nice building model
The building in this game is actually pretty stellar. You shape your house as you please, and that's something we didn't have in Rust. (More in Cons)
-Cars
Amazing for transportation, really cool models aswell. (More on this in the cons)
-Great open map
They really did a good job on the map. The hill areas need polishing, but the overall map is epic. Making a base in each biome is a must-do task.
-The Servers
Oh my God. I realize that we are currently in the Alpha Stage, but the servers are garbage. With the rumor of new servers, I hope that I can one day edit this part out. You'll often find yourself shooting at a boar, just to find out it has teleporting abilities with will literally be a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥
-Cars
I know I put ''Cars'' in the Pros aswell, and this is why; The chances of you ever getting a car in this game are so slim you would have more luck getting a car in Minecraft. The drop rates for car parts are garbage, and after 55hours of play with a whole clan of people, we have managed to get three wheels. Not to mention the sheer amount of bugs with vehicles. Sounds glitching, clipping through the map, randomly getting thrown out... If you are buying this game for the cars, don't bother.
-''Infamous'' System
I realize that this is here to make the game a bit more unique, but in my opinion it is one of this game's worst features. A rich individual can go to spawn and go bananas on some fresh-spawns without much consequence. This game's whole thing is it's hardcore factor, and this is where the hardcore factor goes away. Tools are harder to make, but you will always keep them as long as you don't kill anyone.
-Community
This doesn't really go under the CONS area, because the Devs can't change this; but it is worth mentioning nonetheless. If you have never played games like DayZ, Rust, and like like, be prepared to be KOS'd. There doesn't need to be a reason behind your death, as long as the Russian behind the scope is trigger happy. The Infamous system counteracts this to a certain degree.
-Bugs and Glitches
I know this is completely normal in an Early-Access game, but nonetheless worth mentioning. The game is plagued with game-breaking glitches and annoyances. The whole Survive-bar is annoying as all hell. The Wetness factor and Temperature need so much fixing it shouldn't be in the game yet.
-Party System / Friends
Even though you can share your house with your teammates, there is no way to identify them. No way of adding them on a friendlist, or mark them some way. Forget playing together if you don't use TS3 or the like. (You should do this anyway) This should be implied as soon as possible.
-Drop Rates
Some fixing needs to be done with this. At the moment, they are completely horrendeous and need fixing.
-Map
This game is in desperate need of some type of map. We currently have a ''compass'' which shows the user it's homes/bases, but no real way of knowing the area. Combining the Beacon and a map function would make this game a lot easier and more enjoyable to play.
All in all, this is a game worth trying. If you are a fan of Rust or DayZ, it's a truly refreshing. Even though there are a lot of Cons, I still love this game for what it is, and I hope they will fix some of these.
Edit; 2. Jan 2015: Suggestions, Maps

You better be, becouse this game is not your average MOBA, it might look like MOBA, but trust me, it's something more than your basic top-down strategy-like point and clicker.
At first, when I saw this game I told my self:"It's just another MOBA, no need to waste my time trying it", hell I was wrong.
Game feels more like Action RPG than MOBA actually, yes there are builds for each character and yes this game has same mechanics as Dota and LoL, but it's made differently.
While Dota being more noob hostile at the time I was trying too play it, this game has much more explanation for what is what and who is who. Item shop has "Recomended" pre-set for you too buy, but you always can go wild by opening "All-Items" folder. Also the fact that you cant buy stuff that's not compatable with your character (No Swords or Hammers for Mages and no Magical Staffs for Physichal characters) makes it even better.
You can buy 6 items like in Dota or LoL, but you also have 4 additional slots for your active items and consumables (2 for each).
So far the biggest struggle for me are voice commands, but It's nice that they are there, along with Pings on mini-map, this can save your time if you know the right key-combo to say something to your teammates.
The game gets updates frequently, getting more Gods and balance changes along with some sick skins for Gods.
One thing I don't like about skins is that there are Golden and Diamond ones, they simply look stupid and unoriginal,
I see how devs wanted to go for CoD-like(I'm very funny) experience, but they simply look aesthetically ugly.
There are also rewards for playing game every day and for reffering friend who told you about this game.
So yeah, try it, if you liked MOBAs but hated their strategyish look than you will love this game, for sure.

Dark Souls 2, like its daddy, is a fantastic game. Challenging, yet ultimately fair, it rewards patience and attention. Much of what can be said of Dark Souls 1 can be applied to Dark Souls 2: Difficulty, beautiful environments, open-ended exploration, epic boss fights, vague but intriguing story, and lots and lots of dying. That doesn't diminish at all from the game itself. Dark Souls 2 isn't trying to shake up the series standard, it's an overall refinement of it. More fluid combat, more choices, more lands... Overall, the game is bigger than Dark Souls 1.
The framerate is smooth, the controls...while much better than the first game, still leave room for improvement. With practice, the mouse and keyboard can be doable (I used them), but instead of being able to fully customize your layout, you can only select from pre-selected options. The game plays much better with a controller, I'm sure.
In conclusion, Dark Souls 2 is Dark Souls 1, but even better.

I'll start off by saying that this is a great game and if you are a fan of the souls games you should buy it right now. However the game falls short in a couple categories that I would like to point out.
1) Recycled bosses/enemies - The game uses bosses/enemies from the original dark souls way too much. Making the game feel cheap and making those boss fights easy because you know most of all the tricks.
2) Fast Travel Issues - In Dark Souls II you can fast travel from the get go which seems amazing. But ultimately what this does is seperate the world into bits and makes everything feel disconnected. The introduction of fast travel should be a little down the line so the player can learn the enviorment and feel a sence of direction and placement of areas on the map.
3) Newcomer problems - Dark Souls II was said to have been streamlined for new players while keeping that punishing difficulty at the same time. The game makes almost zero improvements on streamlining the game for new players. The controls are still tough to learn and the tutorial area serves almost no purpose but to let the player read messages about how to preform certain actions and attacks. The main problem with why the game is harder for new comers is the new system of losing health when you die. In Dark Souls II you lose a bit of your health every time you die decreasing until your at 50%. At the begging of the game this is really punishing because to get your health back to full you have to use a human effigy (humanity) which is a rare for new players that die a lot and use a lot.
Other than these three main points the game is really fun and introduces players to a wide varity of weapons, magic, and playstyles to choose from. Wanna be a light weight with a dagger and fire magic? No one is stopping you. The addition of a rare item that lets you reset your skill points allows players to change play styles late game while maintaining that character. It may seem like I dogged on the game pretty hard but it is a true sequel to the original and if your up for a challenge dive right in, it will frustrate you at times but when you overcome those challenges nothing feels better.

UPDATED 2-20-16
To potential buyers, be warned that the developrs have askd for poeple to post reviews. So the flood of recent reviews stem from that request.
Even with the latest updates this game still has a long way too go. The RTS mouse swing isn't as good as PGA2k, TW series or CPG/WGC. It just has no feel, you have no idea what went wrong when the swing motion that just worked fine now sends your shot shanked off into the woods or a hazard. Ball physics are still unrealistic. This game is more frustrating to play than real golf a lot of the time.
I would love to say yeah buy it. But if you do just know there is still a ways to go yet.
Recommend this game? yes with a caveat. It is FAR from "Perfect" Golf. ball physics are terrible, putting is unrealistic, motion swing isn't real-time or tied to the golfer, wind has no effect, multiplayer has issues. Graphics are good (not as good as The Golf Club, better than World Golf Challenge 2011, the other 2 golf games I play).
The other caveat is to play this (and most new games) you'll need CPU and video card horsepower to run  it at high graphic settings.
Basically this is Links 2003 updated to a 2009-ish game. If you like Links 2003 you'll really like PG. For those of us who like a golf game with a real-time mouse swing buy this early access release and see if the improvements over time make it better. $20 isn't a deal breaker. Right now I've stopped playing it and will try it again in a month or so to see if any improvements have been made.
UPDATE 8-13-16
many patches later this game still has issues. Latest patch introduces some "anti-cheat" into the software. So if you make a number of good swings the game says "must be cheating, using some outside swing aid on the mouse" and then will cause a mis-hit resulting in an errant shot. So you get penalized for honing a swing?!?
Ball physics still not realistic. Lob Wedge  shot lands, kicks forward?? no back spin? Yet out of the rough or sand ball checks up and spins back.
They really need to bring back the original programmers who initially did the game so the code that keeps getting broken with every patch can be fixed. but given so many have now worked on the code, it's probably really messed up for good and needs a complete rewrite.
So still can't recommend this game, just be aware of all the faults if you do decide to buy

Before I start:  I am one of those people that think Dark Souls is one of the most brilliantly designed games I have ever played.  In this review I will occasionally draw a comparison between the two games.
Dark Souls 2 is more of a revision of what was done in the original than a sequel in regards to combat.  Any veterans of the original will notice that many of the same bosses are in the sequel (i'm looking at YOU Gargoyles).  This isn't a bad thing, as they changed the encounters, but there are many points that deja vu that are disorienting.  I'm not going to go into too much detail, as half the fun of the game is learning how to handle the multitudes of baddies throughout the game.
The combat feels like it is lacking the same weight as the first game.  A big deal is made about the dual-wielding, but I have not tried that (as of yet).  It still feels like a Souls game still, though more like Demon than Dark.
My major complaint is with the world design.  Don't get me wrong, the world is beautiful, but it is lacking the polish and thought-out design that the orginal had.  In the original Dark Souls, every area that you go to fits together perfectly.  No disconnect between areas, in fact you can see many areas that you will eventually go to from other areas.  There is no "overlap" to the levels.  Dark Souls 2 lacks this major feature.  There is a point that you beat a boss at the top of a tower, and to get to the next area you have to take a long elevator up... To a castle that has sank into the ground...  I looked around before going into the tower, and there was nothing but sky around it.  You will find nothing like that in the original, and is a major negative in my view.
Enough rambling.  Should you get this game?  Yes, if you like Dark Souls.  Just don't expect it to be as brilliantly done.

Bosses aren't too terribly hard, but they're not challenging either.

Overall, it's become an easier game to get into, but retains most of the aspects of Dark Souls, the grueling environment, huge bosses, many enemies to slay, and the countless times you will die.
So have fun, and Prepare To Die, a lot.

Having already read a few reviews here I was a bit afraid of how the game would look. But, as a huge fan who preorderd the game, I decided to just see, I could always try to go on low. I posted a review when I first installed it but, frankly, had to just rewrite it after two entire playthroughs. So here we go.
It's a brilliant game. The feel from Dishonored is still there, all the things I loved are just as they were. I still have some minor issuses, like getting used to the fact that while my mouse sensitivity seems to work just fine for playing, it doesn't perform as well when I try to acces weapon wheel.
As far as perfomance goes the games goes on my computer just fine, without hiccups on high - it did so even without patches so I cannot really say how useful they were.
First - level desing.There are a couple of amazingly designed levels that, one you get a hang of them, are quite uniqe. Though I've noticed there are less ways o move around rooftops. Karnaca is more vertical than Dunwall and there is a challenge of getting to some balconies, but there is rarely a way to go through a level almost not touching the ground (what I usually did). In my secon playthrough I got more comfortable with that and managed to stay in the air for way longer - that might be also becuase I feel that Emily's Far Reach has a bigger reach than Corvo's Blink (expecially without upgrades). Also getting ghost will be much, much haredr - there are civilians everywhere and in some locations there are very difficult areas (expacially in the more creative levels).
I feel that making your own charms is somwhat uneccesary - after a while most of your slots will be filled with Black Charms anyway and you won't be willing to throw them away most of the time.
The plot is not an overly complicated one, but it manages to keep you interested not by not revealing what will the ending be (you can guess that even before you start playing) - but the levels have seperate twists, which overall make a riveting story.
Game is really just fun to play, there are ton's of places to find, diffrent approches and opportunities to play with powers. I would definitely say that Domino is a must-have in case of Emily, amount of saved ammo is immense. Although, diffrently to Dishonored first game, I found myself almost ignoring passive skills - only around three I found useful at all, and even than, I preferred to upgrade other abilities.
Generally speaking it's a game I'll play at least four times (High and Low on both characters) with many things I still haven't found in two playthrous. I will recommend it with all my heart (but if you haven't plyes the first one, go and do that before, it's much more fun this way).

Lots of things to say about this game good and bad
First im a huge fan of the series on top of this game in general, i really enjoy most of what it brings to the table.
First with the buy once idea. originally worried about pay2win, not at all 90% of it is cosmetic stuff. As well as their equivelent to R-A-F in WoW, which are pledges of Mara which is awesome but not perfect (ill get into my issues with this later though).
factions in this are big, just like in WoW. They represent the story of the time and division among the races and lust for power. the overall story of the two factions i have played are good however, AD was a bit dull for a while however it was also very full of lore.
Soloing- Great, tons of fun if you get into the ES series a lot, while it is a bit more on train tracks as far as when you go where, you can still spend quite a few hours exploring zones. i spent almost a day and a half in Auridon just exploring. however, some of the enemies in the first few areas are a little too weak, which can make the first few hours annoying.
Duo-ing- Ring of mara with a friend! Xp bonuses together and all that good stuff. as well as the ability to grind dungeon trash and grind in the zones. HOWEVER, this is one of my main issues with the game and is a warning to new players. I DO NOT reccomend questing with a friend if you are a ONE character person, if you dont mind making a second go for it, because in a duo you will not really do too much story and as i said with the starter zones being too easy, this has made literally EVERYTHING ive fought while questing easy, with the exception to world bosses.
Group Content-All i can speak for so far, are dungeons in the PvE perspective, and while i havent done the hard modes of them yet (Veteran dungeons) I can say that these were what made me finally get REALLY into this game as an MMO, instead of other MMOs where the tank has 10000000 people hitting him and no one else is getting hit except for an occasional shot here and there, this feels like a realistic swordfight (minus magic lol), the tanks only hold the strongest few enemies (otherwise you drop) and everyone else is kind of in a big chaotic fight, it really brings a great enviornment to the group content, it adds so much depth and makes you feel like youre in more of a battle with avoiding aoe and killing the guy thats hitting you then helping others. it brings a depth to combat that most other MMOs only have in late game raiding with one or two adds hitting you. If you do get this game and you arent sure about it just yet, at least get to a point to try Dungeons.
PVP- This is where i start to fall off, i dont know as much about this as it is extremely complex with what can be done. However destroying the walls and storming a keep with groups of people is a ton of fun, defending your keep under a giant attack is great and even when youre not in combat but running with a massive group of people as you take an elder scroll to your temple or another keep of yours that is further inside your territory is a ton of fun. On top of this the PvP is very balanced so far for what ive seen, its rarely one side domination (it does happen every once in a while) and so far in the non veteran campaign ive seen all 3 factions hold a majority of the territory at least once.
All this plus a play your way style of game makes for a fun time given you get past the first few hours that are pretty slow and kinda boring, on top of mount leveling, crafting and tons of unique quests. this game really does bring a lot to the table, especially now that the devs have put so much time and effort into it.
Oh and a fun bonus, if you sub (which you dont have to) you get a 10% xp boost, all DLC, and almost your entire moneys worth of the in game paid currency (crowns). Keep killing it devs !

For many PC gamers, this is the one, that illusive perfect game that will never be topped. Years ago when I played it, I certainly agreed. Today, it doesn't hold up quite as well. That said, I believe SS2 should be a required play for anyone with even a passing interest in gaming. The Steam and GoG versions of SS2 are easily modded to upscale the graphics and sound, which is good, because let's face it, early 3D games will probably make your eyes bleed. The depth of gameplay is amazing for its time, and it's a damn shame that the Bioshock games toned down that complexity. Atmosphere wise SS2 is still top notch, SHODAN especially will haunt you long after you've beaten it. The real strength of SS2, and the reason I believe it should be required gaming material, is its legacy. It's plain to see that many of the games we know and love today owe their everything to this masterpiece. After watching the first movie "Alien" from 1979, I promptly proceeded to play this game. The story happens 15 years or so after the events shown in the movie. If you watch "Aliens" from 1986 (if you haven't) before playing the game, you'll get a spoiler of the fate of Ellen Ripley's daughter, Amanda. So the order of enjoying the series would be: Alien (1979), Alien: Isolation (the game in question), Aliens (1986), Alien 3 (1992) and Alien: Ressurection (1997). My critical opinion about the game is:
Graphics: 90/100 - Superb, they really captured the atmosphere and tones present in the movies, the lightning work is excellent and the attention to deatils is really worth noticing. A few minor aesthetic differences from the movies exist and were noticed by other reviewers. Personally, I felt that, on the big picture, if you are not actively looking for those extremly minor differences, you won't notice them.
Gameplay: 85/100 - Excellent, the controls are responsive and you have to actually work your way through the game, not just rushing torwards an objective and shooting anything that moves, that is extremely discouraged. You'll feel powerless against the Xenomorph, even with a futuristic .357 magnum revolver. The AI work is so well done that the enemies can actually hear your tracking device and respiration (if they are near your hiding spot), you can also explore this feature to set traps, create diversions and even "use" the xenomorph against other threats. Some minor glitches can happen (personally, I experienced one that the Alien almost didn't get me, while firing my revolver at him until it got past the hitbox/detection bug and finally got me, but it happened just once).
Sound: 95/100 - Superb, if you are playing alone, in complete darkness and has some kind of 3D audio system like a surround home theater or really good headphones, get ready to feel the shivers and tensions that come with the noises that the Xenomorph produces, also, the soundtrack will get you extremly tense, worried and scared, but not in a bad way, after all this is just a game!
I will not provide any further details about the plot, as I'd like to avoid providing spoilers. My recommendation is that you don't even look at the achievements, as they can hint you torwards what will happen next.
Overall: 90/100 - Superb, SEGA has really scored an excellent grade for a game that follows the path where many failed. The games that capture the universe of a movie, either trying to reproduce the movie's plot or adding to it, usually are rushed and end up as a massive glitch fest, with no replayability value at all. That is not the case for this game. Try to play it on the hardest difficulty as I have done, despair is ensured when in a tight situation!

A complete breath of fresh air. Alien Isolation is tense, stressfull, horrifying game that tightly keeps in sink with the original 1979 Alien.  The protaganist Amanda Ripley is right in line with its original epic character.  Tough,  experianced spacer who may not be a call of duty hero with military experiance, but can think on her feet and use a variety of componants to make makeshift weapons and survive.
The Alien is a terrifying opponant who you cannot directly confront and survive. You must avoid, hide, sneak and distract it.  To this end Ripley is armed with a variety of schematics (which you must find by exploring) to craft noisemakers, flashbangs, smoke bombs, emp grenades, etc to distract, conceal and avoid direct confrontations. The Alien itself can often be used as a weapon to clear out hostile human opponants or synthetic(yes crazy robotic psychopaths are on the station.).
Later in the game you will have weapons and items that can temporarily drive the Alien off, but you must balance thier ammo against usefullness. Making inventory manegement more then a chore but the difference between life and death.
These componants use many similiar resources, so you must decide weather to make a pipe bomb to kill multiple humans, emps to kill synthetics, med kits to heal or noicemakes and flashbangs to distract the Alien.
With the exceptian of a few very minor bugs the game is about perfect.

For any familiar with the Total War franchise, this, their latest title is probably one of their best games thus far.  I can honestly say that the games of this series are quite unlike many other turn-based strategy games that have to do with world conquering.  While debatably focused on the war aspect of a growing empire, there is still a great balance, as ever with this company's titles, between diplomacy, trade, and domestic barriers to overcome.  Historically speaking, starting conditions are more or less accurate, but because of player decisions, historical accuracy is quickly thrown out the window.  Rome, in my current game, was taken over by Athens and Sparta, for instance.  It is truly a great joy to be able to take some of these ancient cultures and rewrite history, at least on a computer screen, and with the additions to the game's content, even more lesser-known factions can be explored, both in gameplay and in vague history.  All in all, this is one title that I highly recommend, especially to those unfamiliar with Total War as a franchise who are also interested in a good world-domination strategy game.

Overall however I found Rome 2 to be pretty enjoyable though not nearly as polished as Shogun. My comparisions will be between these two as they are the most recent. My opinion may be invalidated due to the fact that I didn't play Rome 1 so I'm ready for your rage.
Of course what you want in a Total War game is here. Strategy, economy, city building, diplomacy etc. But everything just seems so barbones with corners cut and what was added doesnt feel good at all.
All of the hallmarks are here, tactics like flanking, hammer and anvil, elevation, ambushing, etc. Units are varied, can be faction specific and have unique looks from the different regions in the game, though most will say they are reskins. Unit type is also varied as most types will also have sub types and so on. An example would be Cavalry, there are subtypes like Shock Cavalry, Heavy Cavalry, and Light Cavalry that are used for a specific purpose, not using them for that purpose is somewhat wasteful. Naval combat is pretty good when it is working right, having the ability to embark land units on their own without naval specific units is a poor design decision however.
Now if you like quick tactics and have the attention span of a goldfish you will like the combat in this game. Battles end WAY to fast. Unit morale is the ♥♥♥♥ing worse I have seen in one of these games.  I am one of those guys that like to zoom right in when the action starts but in Rome 2 by the time I zoom in one of the two units fighting rout. While I'm on the topic of zooming in why the ♥♥♥♥ does the camera level out if I zoom in/out? I want to stay at the angle my camera was facing thank you very much.
Anyways a usual fight will last you anywhere between 5-15 minutes, anything longer then that is due to either not engaging or waiting out the clock. To a newcomer this may still sound like a while but trust me 1/2 to 3/4 of the time is setting up your army properly and the remaining time is chasing down routing units. This part here is a big issue and ♥♥♥♥ing stupid design choice. So as in other Total War games your units can level up and the way to gain experience is by killing units, this means there is not a better time to gain experience then when the enemy is routing as they cannot attack back. Whoever decided to make it so that routing units arent shown on the map should be fired, you literally have to scour the map to find units to find the straglers.
You also cant field an army without having a general which leads to limited armies, no ability to garrison effectivly and frontlines that spread troops too thin. I hope this changes in future Total Wars.
On the topic of leveling up I think the system for leveling in Rome 2 is stupid, choosing what you want to level up is just a toss up as you dont know what you are working towards. In Shogun 2 the skill tree was set up so you could see what you could get and work towards how you wanted to build your general. Rome 2's Zeal, Cunning and Authority is a system that would be good if it was laid out properly akin to Shogun 2 but due to the fact that you dont know what the ♥♥♥♥ your skilling the general ends up being a jack of all trades and a master of none.
Competition in the early game is not too bad but it only gets easier, at around 5 villages you will probably be the biggest faction in the game and from then on is just a slaughter fest as you go for the 100% conquer. In Shogun 2 there would always be factions rivalling you in size and military strength the entire game. In Rome 2 once you get your first region everyone else just bends over and spreads their♥♥♥♥♥as you make them your ♥♥♥♥♥ by autoresolving and the once in a blue moon real-time battles.
UI is kind of ♥♥♥♥♥♥, but I'm not smart enough to think of a way to fix it. I just feel like it could be more informative while showing less.
City building in this game is a ♥♥♥♥ing tragedy, there always this balance between unhappiness and happiness which has always been there but I dont understand why getting the best of a building would cause unhappiness, why are people upset when they get such a large amount of food, income, etc? I'm not sure if they have kept in the mechanic where you can just build one super happiness city in a region and just take a♥♥♥♥♥♥on the other villages and still be in the green but if they havent taken it out then this game is beyond help.
Money is never something you will have too little of, very easy to aquire and maintain upkeep if you are paying even the slightest bit of attention to the budget tabs.
Muliplayer works but that should'nt be praise worthy, it should be expected that things work. I also understand the reason they took out the avatar conquest in Rome 2 but I do wish that they could have kept the armor customization.
Game looks good but so does Ryse, gameplay is more important here. The action cam or whatever they call it is a nice addition and much better to look at than the first person they had in previous games. I wish we could move the camera around the unit though.
Diplomacy is paper thin usually only used to declare war or trade, alliances and what not are more for connon fodder and I do like the ability to walk over other factions territories without having to declare. Also seems like RNG to get a proposal accepted.
DLC is whatever, it's not going away. Thankfully some of them are more than a couple factions and units.
Lot of mods in workshop to cater to most of your needs and will add quite a while to the games life.
Not much else as I'm sure many other reviews have touched on thing more in depth then I have. The patches have brought the game to a pretty good state and if you wanted to ever try a Total War game then pick this one up and then buy the next one, that way it will look like such a huge step forward in the series to you.

I've played golf for over 25 years. Also, I've been playing the best golf-sim till now, the RTS swing in Links 2003. I thought it would be impossible to better that. Other games, like Tiger Woods, WGT or The Golf Club have lot's of glitch 'n glossy of course, but they don't have that 1 definitive thing: a true golf swing. It's just not there. And that is what a lot of people have been waiting for: the true dynamics that go with immersing yourself in a virtual golfing environment. Swing plane, swing tempo, clubface angles, it's all there. And more. Much more.
But it's here now! For the very first time, we now have 'The Motion Swing' (now updated to the 'Real Time Swing') in Jack Nicklaus Perfect Golf. A true masterpiece of computer engineering. After spending a couple of hours on the driving range in PG, I've started mastering this great simulation. Everything is there, albeit in embryonic phase, not polished and glitchy yet, but it's there! AND it works beautifully. For every golfer out there, real or otherwise, 'JNPG' is going to be your game, I can almost garantee it.
Once you get past the learning curve (3-click and other options are also on board) you'll discover courses and other options to keep you happy for ever. Not right now of course, the game is being build as I write this, but in the coming months PG is going to become the new standard in simulation golf. A big reason for this, is because it has 2 guys on board who have been at the forefront of computer golfgaming and -course design: Mike and Andrew Jones (no relation). Mike, a one time golfpro himself, started dabbling in PC golf years ago, and ultimately became a major force is this departement for the Links series. It helps if you KNOW what the real game is all about.
A sublime golf swing, real weather simulation, all kinds of gameplay, on- and offline, a multiplayer lobby to meet up with other players, courses come to life with moving objects like trees, water, birds, even cars, ships! etc, Jack Nicklaus Perfect Golf is going to be everything golfing adepts have been waiting for. All we now have to do is wait for it's completion...

Let me start this by saying that SMITE is my first MOBA. I was, and still am, completely turned off by the types of games. If I have to be honest, it all just looks like a more advanced Put-Put-you point, you click, you win (You dont even get a song like in Put-Put D:) However, SMITE isnt like other MOBAS. There are still, and bear with me, "Lanes" and "Ganks" and "Jungles" and other MOBA crap like that. What SMITE does differently is it's all in the 3rd person. Now, you may be asking, why is this that big of a deal? If you had to ask me, it engages the player more. Instead of just being a pawn that you click and they move, you use the WASD keys. Movement feels fluid and slik-it feels...nice.
Now that thats out of the way, SMITES reeeeealy good. There are "classes"-those being Mage, Hunter, Guardian, Warrior, and Assassian-and everyone has a role. A team full of Guardians may work, but it wont work as well as a team with a Guardian, a Mage, 2 hunters, ect. Oh, as for WHO you play, it's all gods. Y'know, like Zues and Thor? Gods and monsters; stuff like that (Scylla2good4you). Granted, every god isnt free. You'll start with a hand full, and can buy more via Favor/gems/or microtransactions. Gameplay wise,  You can play between a multiple of game types. Don't like a lot of team work and lanes? Joust is for you. Want a more competitve game? Go Conquest. Want to just look out for yourself and inevitably start feeding? Go Loki Arena. There are so many options!
Okay, okay, enough of me fanboying. I recomend this game to people who are afraid to get into MOBAS: it'll teach you some basics while not being as hard as League or Dota. I also would say that, if you like Mythology and sterff, then get this. Listening to Tyr call out Fenrir is really cool. Just give it a try, it is free afterall. .

This game is surprisingly addictive, and has quite a lot of content considering it's still Early Access.
The game mixes the repetitive goal-seeking fun of Harvest Moon, or Stardew Valley with a huge sense of adventure and discovery, and really lets the player choose what mix of the 2 they want. Despite having no "objectives" the game evokes a constant desire to explore further lands, unlocking new areas, and offering new, more lucrative slimes and other resources. It does a good job introducing more and more mechanics as it goes along, although somtimes it seems arbitrary when you can unlock them.
The game is still in Early Access, and eventually you will actually run into a sign indicating where the game has literally not been finished, but that is totally fine because there is already tons of gameplay before that point. I can't wait for the game to get its next update, but I don't want to discourage people from buying it early access. There is still plenty of excellent game to be had!

This is an excellent horror game and an excellent Alien game. After several flawed releases, its nice to see something that does the Alien franchise justice. The attention to detail here is astounding, from the retro-futuristic sci-fi aesthetic of all the environments to each sound, even the littlest beeps and hums, that bring the world to life. The graphics in general are fantastic, I was surprised the game could maintain a constant framerate with such high detail. The alien itself is suitably terrifying and intellegent as the main attraction of the game. While you confront other enemies in the game at times, none of them compare to the alien. The threat of its presence (or the possibility of its presence) its a constant and relentless assault on your senses, which is largely why the game succeeds so well at being a horror game I feel. You do get some gadgets and weapons that destract and ward off the alien, but it does little to ease the overall tension. You have to be smart about what you do and where you go to survive against it.
While theres a lot of great things to say about the game, its not without its flaws. While the alien AI is great, the other enemies in the game suffer from a very predictable AI. With very simple pathing and a tendancy to lose you easily, the other enemies are very easy to maneuver around and just end up being underwhelming. The save system is both a blessing and a curse. On the one hand, save points instead of a checkpoint system add to the tension, and make finding one a very rewarding experience. However, some save points are generously spaced apart and having to continuously redo a long segment when you die can get quite frustrating. The dynamic music also caused some issues, there were some tense moments in the game where the music got so loud it got difficult to hear where the alien was.
Overall, I didn't find these issues very detrimental to the experience, and the good definitely outweighs the bad. I Highly recommend this, especially for fans of horror games. There hasn't been a horror game quite this good in a long time.

It's free, which is always nice for a game. This game isn't perfect by a long shot, but it's definetly worth looking at (even if you do eventualy uninstall it).
Pros:
-Free, without any of the pay to win idiocy usualy in this type of game
-Decent story
-Battles can be brute forced through with high levels, but on harder difficulties or lower levels it is possible to beat every fight without grinding if you play it smart.
-Music is good, and unlike many games, the soundtrack doesn't get irritating after playing for a while.
-Structured so that you don't have to devote all your focus to it at all times, making it good for picking up and playing for a few minutes here and there.
-Multiple save files (seriously, not enough games do this anymore).
Cons:
-The grammer and writing both read like a poor dub out of the 60's.
-Short, with alternative paths taking at most an hour to finish.
-Cutscenes are unskipable, and take way to long to go through sometimes.
-Story doesn't really feel like it gets a proper resolution.
-Crafting system is way more limited than it could be.
-Unable to visit past areas after completing them, making it difficult to see everything on a first playthrough without clever use of save files.
Even if you don't end up liking it, it's free, so at the very least you should try it for a little bit. You may love it, or you may uninstall it instantly, but you won't lose anything from trying.

Arkane, man. I knew after playing the first Dishonored and its fantastic expansions that second game was only a matter of time, and it was going to be another masterpiece of gameplay design, mission design and audiovisual artistry. And that prediction proved true. Having just finished my first playthrough as Corvo, completely nonlethal, I am again amazed by the experience. Arkane just know how to build fascinating places. From the streets of Karnaca, through abandoned solarium, Rubik's cubish Clockwork Mansion, the beautifully moody observatory, to gloriously handled time travel..Dishonored 2 kept surprising me. The things that make me reconsider my recommendation: The story feels forced, the tie-ins to the original seem very weak, and the character design as a whole feels pretty flat. This is partially due to the writing, and partially due to the delivery by the voice cast. The default controls on a PC keyboard are awkward and kind of painful. It's clearly a game that was designed for consoles first and PCs second.
If you like a good sneaky-stabby, then you'll probably enjoy this. That said, it's not my favorite in the genre. Go play Thief 2.

I heard a lot of good things about this game from some pretty unreliable sources around the time it came out, but I never played it.  I suppose it's not fair to give it an earnest review now that the game is so old, but I'm going to do it anyway.
I sort of knew what I was getting into with this one, but I was bored and curious and it was on sale.  Playing this game was sort of like going back and watching Blade Runner for the first time because you heard everyone talking about what an inspiration it was to later science fiction movies.  You could see all of the influences System Shock had on the genre.  You could see the amorphous, rudimentary blobs of creation that would eventually evolve into enjoyable gameplay mechanics in later titles.  You can also see the cancerous growths of an unforgiving and largely cryptic leveling system that punishes you later on if you didn't happen to level the way the game never told you you should.
System Shock 2 is a relic of an earlier era.  I would not argue with people who claim that the game was revolutionary for its time, or that it was the progenitor of many of the modern games that I love -- assuredly these assertions are true.  However, I am forced to ask simply, "Is the game still fun to play?", and sadly I must answer "No."  Ignoring the draconian advancement system, the game feels sluggish and poorly optimized, and the interface is a complicated counter-intuitive mess.  Also, I hate to say it, but the dated graphics seriously hurt the ambiance the game attempts to create.  I've been told that the game can be made less unpleasant through the use of mods, but I simply can't be bothered.  The game is old.  It was probably good for its time, but it's old now.  Let us give it the respect it deserves and allow it to fade into a pleasant, nostalgia-laced cocoon of obscurity.

Before there was Bioshock there was System Shock 2, a classic horror FPS-RPG.
The game takes place thirty years after the events of Citadel Station in the first game where you play as a soldier of the UNN who joined the expedition on the Von Braun; The first starship built by humanity that is able to travel faster-than-light and is accompanied by the UNN Rickenbacker which is literally connected to the ship. After going into cryosleep, you wake up to find that everything has gone to hell with most if not all of the crew dead, missing, or worse...turned into twisted monstrosities by parasitic creatures from the surface of Tau Ceti V and the only one who can stop them from reaching Earth is you.
Gameplay wise, its a First Person-Shooter with an inventory, in-game currency, and of course a variety of upgrades for your character such as increasing certain states such as Strength, increasing your ability to hack certain devices, and/or even utilize psionic powers that weren't available in the first game. You start out with a Wrench as a melee weapon but there are other weapons you can pick up (depending on your skillset, that is) ranging from firearms, to energy, and even weapons made out of alien tissue.
The graphics of the game are dated by today's standards but there is a large range of fan-made High-Definition mods that improve the quality of the textures, models, and interface. Speaking of mods, there are also some custom campaigns that can be found online for download if you get bored of the standard campaign.
I would highly recommend this game for anyone whose played the first System Shock game and/or anyone whose played any of the BioShock and/or Dead Space because this game is not only its spiritual predecessor to both games but is also a cult classic from the golden age of gaming.

At first glance, Hurtworld appears to be another cheap addition to Steam's already massive collection of Early Access survival games. Initially, I didn't pay it much mind, assuming that it would be quickly abandoned, like many other similar titles. However, after watching a few gameplay videos, Hurtworld caught my interest.
While I'll agree that Hurtworld's lack of originality is somewhat offputting, I believe it is fair to say that it is borrowing from the right places. It plays very similarly to Rust, another great survival game, but with tighter controls and combat mechanics. To put it simply, it feels like a refined first person shooter with major survival elements, whereas games like Rust are focused primarily on survival with the addition of slightly loose gun-based combat.
Moving to Hurtworld's surprisingly large roster of features, all the action takes place on a relatively small map. Those who have played the Legacy version of Rust will feel right at home in the derelict setting of Hurtworld. The map is host to several varied biomes, each of which holds a multitude of resources and threats, meaning that select points on the map become highly contested hot spots. When you begin playing Hurtworld, you find yourself in a dry and dusty area, with a scattering of trees and rocks. Through the gathering of materials from resource nodes, you will be able to craft tools which will aid you in your journey. Unlike Rust, Hurtworld's equipment system is split more precisely into item tiers, similar to those find in other games such as Minecraft and Terraria. Whether this is good or bad is up to you, however, I tend to prefer a more vague approach in survival titles. I could ramble on and on about Hurtworld's features, including their merits and flaws, so I will focus more on what is perhaps the game's most unique aspect, the infamy system. This system is designed to deter players, mainly those with guns and powerful gear, from killing newly spawned or truly friendly players. Killing players temporarily adds to your infamy bar. The more people you slay, the more your infamy status increases. Reaching certain levels of infamy will cause you to drop some of your valuable gear on death, something which normally does not happen. However, if you by some chance end up gaining infamy, all hope is not lost, as it will decay over time. While the infamy system is certainly an interesting mechanic which creates more player interaction and makes early game life easier, I feel it also has some serious negative impact. The most glaring problem is that killing players for their guns and clothing, among other valuable gear, is entirely pointless if they have no infamy. Further more, it will add to your infamy bar, putting you at a temporary disadvantage. Admittedly, it's kind of odd that a system which removes much of the risk from dying is in place in a game that advertises itself as being hardcore, but I digress. The infamy system, along with a diverse cast of dangerous creatures which roam the map, puts the environment at a similar threat level as other players. While it's refreshing to see PvE at full strength in a PvP game, I feel this is partially due to an absurd amount of animal spawns, and would love to see some sort of change to the infamy system which would allow for more combat between survivors.
Aesthetically, Hurtworld is a decent looking game, though I can't say I'm a particularly big fan of the game's graphical style. The simplified art works wonders for optimization, putting it miles ahead of many Early Access survival titles in that regard. There is no music to be found, however, there are plenty of sound effects, most of which are crunchy and satisfying.
If you didn't already see this coming, I legitimately feel that Hurtworld is a diamond in the rough. While the game has not been in development for very long, and has its fair share of bugs and issues, there is plenty of fun to be had. If you are a fan of survival games and do not mind the Early Access program, I would certainly recommend picking up Hurtworld.

Now, you may be asking, why is this that big of a deal? If you had to ask me, it engages the player more. Instead of just being a pawn that you click and they move, you use the WASD keys. Movement feels fluid and slik-it feels...nice.
Now that thats out of the way, SMITES reeeeealy good. There are "classes"-those being Mage, Hunter, Guardian, Warrior, and Assassian-and everyone has a role. Gods and monsters; stuff like that (Scylla2good4you). Granted, every god isnt free. You'll start with a hand full, and can buy more via Favor/gems/or microtransactions. Gameplay wise,  You can play between a multiple of game types. Don't like a lot of team work and lanes? Joust is for you. Want a more competitve game? Go Conquest. Want to just look out for yourself and inevitably start feeding? Go Loki Arena. There are so many options!
Okay, okay, enough of me fanboying. I recomend this game to people who are afraid to get into MOBAS: it'll teach you some basics while not being as hard as League or Dota. I do not think it is fair to judge slime rancher any different because it is an early access title. The game costs 20 dollars and I have (so far) gotten almost 15 hours of positive playtime out of it although I am already near the endgame content. I have enjoyed Slime Rancher, and apart from my own frustration with its genre it has not had a moment where I regret purchasing it.
The game has a wonderful aesthetic and the modelling and texturing is beautiful. Fun thing: go up close to any in game screen and it has a rgb look that makes it look like a real screen. Such small detail make games like this shine with the faux simplistic design. The lighting effects are good and there's a fair amount of variety in the scenery.
Genre and gameplay wise this game is strong. It is quite literally a cute exploration/management game. The world is expansive and adorable while still being potentially dangerous. I think in terms of criticism to the world I would point out the NEED for a map. Please.
The gameplay is a smooth 60fps joyride, but my biggest issue is that there seems to be an odd stutter/delay. I can run games like titanfall 2 and BF1 at max settings fine, so this should NOT be happening. Its minor and you don't notice it after playing a bit but I will still complain as I am entitled to.
I have my own quips with games like this when it comes to management/sim games. I am just not very good at them. The only thing I was frustrated with because of an actual design flaw was the lack of automation. You do everything and anything on the farm. The closest to automation is the collectors and feeders. I believe endgame should have a big focus on automation and way to really lock slimes in place. I know the point is to have bouncy slimes but endgame I just want to sit and admire my hard work. I don't think seeds should disappear after a few harvests and I believe there should be more spots to build. I felt like I was constantly running around and there was no exponential increase to my earnings or rewards.

I initially gave this a positive review but I feel compelled to start over. I love the game, it is probably my favourite TES game (if you ignore the arm-twisting to group up), but I find it increasingly difficult to defend the developer/publisher. I strongly suggest people read the Terms of Service before buying and don't give the dev the benefit of the doubt when you realise how one-sided it is. I don't think I've encountered an MMO dev who treat their players with so much open contempt.
A bunch of players just had their accounts 'cancelled' (including their support accounts, making appeals a nightmare) because they supposedly input the wrong codes for the Morrowind expansion, whatever that means. It appears that ZOS messed up the codes for physical copies of Morrowind and, rather than giving players the benefit of the doubt or merely suspending access to the expansion, they're banning long-time customers from the entire game. You can find more details about this on reddit and possibly the official forums, although they usually delete all trace of appeals threads on the forums, as they've straight up made questioning staff decisions against the rules.
A few months ago, a large group of players on PS4 suffered a similar fate. For the sin of dressing in white robes and using the /torch emote, with a few inappropriate comments in chat, a whole guild of dungeon runners had their accounts 'cancelled' - including, supposedly, several guild members who weren't even present during the klan role-play. One of their group was a notable youtuber and you can find more details there. This is apparently not the first time something like this has happened. This is not intended to be a political point, merely a warning that ZOS don't give paying customers much leeway when it comes to jokes/politics/conduct and will revoke access to the game.
Also, this game's whole business model is increasingly seedy. They charge you for the game, charge you for an almost-obligatory subscription (you do not want to be a crafter without a sub - the inventory system is practically broken), and have an in-game store that sells not only cosmetics and crates but all kinds of experience boosters (you can buy crafting progress, mount-riding progress, XP boosters, and near-exclusive skill lines). On top of this, despite being roughly the same size as other DLC packs, they decided to reclassify Morrowind as a 'chapter' to avoid including it with a subscription, and have tried to pass Morrowind off as a full-price game, despite having maybe 1/10th the content of the whole base game and DLC usually only costing $20-$30. I wouldn't call the game 'pay to win' but Jim Sterling's 'fee to pay' label does seem appropriate: you pay money for the opportunity to pay more money.
Also, as in my original review, I need to point out the game's technical problems: ZOS don't ship patches via Steam and include a very old build with the Steam download. You have to download about 50GB via Steam just to launch a 100MB updater that then redownloads the entire game, another 50GB, from ZOS' servers. If you are going to buy this game, buy it from the official website, not Steam, if you have a slow connection or restrictive data caps. Also, they only have two servers: one in the US and one in continental Europe. While the netcode is pretty robust for PvE at higher latencies, PvP is ridiculous and people not in those countries should be aware that latency will be an issue. You also need a good CPU to play this game, as it bottlenecks on a single CPU core, hard. Even with an overclocked Skylake CPU, a barely-utilised GTX 1070, and the draw distance below 50, you can't maintain 60FPS in most cities.
I love this game, continue to play it, but I dread the day I have to deal with their support staff and you should be aware of what kind of company you'll be doing business with.

Eternal Senia...well, it's a free game, so trying it out is probably the best option regardless of what reviews say.
But for me, well, I had fun with the game. I thought it was definitely worth the few hours I put into it, and I admire the developer's dedication and thought put into the game (the crafting system is a good example, being easy to follow while still adding flavor). The soundtrack has its fair share of standout moments, too (personal favorites include "Inner Forest" and "Passage of Bravery"). A few minor issues exist here and there (e.g. iffy translations from Chinese, lack of exit game option), but nothing major.
What keeps me from showering this game with praise, though, is that I could never get into the story, or its characters. A quick glance at the reviews suggests that I'm in the minority here, but for me, the story felt unoriginal and uninspiring to the fullest, never deviating from the tired "love conquers all" theme, never even trying to explore minor intricacies like the mysterious "Eternity" substance.
So, ultimately, I end up viewing this game as the developer's tribute to eastern RPGs - a soft, quick encapsulation of the genre, but nothing of substance on its own. Do I recommend it? For free, it'd be hard not to. But neither do I think you're missing out if you don't bother.

A nice little aRPG-lite with some fun gameplay and a neat little story.
Gameplay:
A barebones combat system that is very similar to rogue-lites where you attack by bumping into things, and along with the default attack you get 4 special moves that are equally useful. For a game made using what I can only assume is RPG maker  (or something similar) I'm really impressed with the non-standard gameplay. The bosses also make great use of the aRPG-lite gameplay, but all bosses except the final one are pretty much a pushover sadly. The level design on the other hand feels very stale and generic, but there are a few places in which the game mixes it up or tries to do something different and for the most part it succeeds.
Story:
I nice, if not cliche, story with the only fault being poor translation. The overall story is nice and the endings are well done, but unfortunately poor grammar and awkward sentences ruin a lot of the scenes that attempt to develop the characters.
Overall:
In the end it is a free game with some fun gameplay, a nice soundtrack, and decent story. If you have time to kill one evening this game would not be a bad choice by any means. 7/10.

Alright, alright. Seriously. This game is FREE.
If that, plus the extremely high ratings from the reviewers isn't enough to convince you to try it, I'll just add my review as well. I suck at reviews so I don't write them often, but some games just deserve my recognition.
To begin with, it is worth mentioning that this game was built with RPG Maker, such as multiple other games released on Steam (and which accidentally, are overpriced and atrocious in the majority).
Well, don't let that mislead you - Eternal Senia is in NO WAY even close to being considered a bad game.
Here are the reasons:
No, it's not using the usual boring turned-based combat system from RPG Maker. Yesss.
Instead, the developer designed his very own ARPG battle system, which means that the combat happens on-screen, directly on the map as you encounter enemies. No button mashing either. You just walk into an enemy to fight it.
"But wait, doesn't that get very boring very quickly?"
Nope. The developer didn't forget to add diversity to the combat system either. Firstly, different enemies you encounter will have different combat skills. Secondly, YOU will unlock skills as well. The combination of perfectly balanced skills and enemy difficulty makes this game's combat system extremely appealing and fluent.
Did any of you ever play a game which, although being fairly short, took you on a ride on a wave of emotions? Because this is an approximately accurate description of this game's story.
I won't be lingering on talking about the story - after all, I'm not here to spoil anything.
All I'll say for now is that the game has a total of 3 endings, all
slightly different. However, remain reassured that luckily, all three endings will not require you to replay the entire game; saving the game when prompted is recommended if you want to go back and get all the other endings (which I HIGHLY recommend, by the way).
The only thing which may turn off a few of you grammar nazs is the fact that
words may be spelled incorrectly, and
grammar mistakes can be found in the text. But give the developer a break here - this is translated, you should be happy that you can have it in English language at all, right? Besides, it's not God-awfully bad, in fact it barely even annoyed me, a grammar freak.
Wait, you're still reading? You probably would have had the time to download the game already.
Seriously though, give it a try. Come on! It's free for fu... For the love of video games. What have you got to lose except a few minutes, which is what you've just wasted reading my longer-than-was-supposed-to-be review.
TL;DR: Definitely worth playing. And IT'S FU... It's FREE dammit.

Neutral:
=Not as many vehicles/settlements as JC2 (can be seen as a positive or negative)
=Need for flares and beacons for fast travel and weapon drop (adds extra game time, but can get repetitive)
Negatives:
-Occasional crashes/FPS drops (has improved a lot since release)
-Most cities feature nearly identical police stations

Even while being mindful of this being an Early Access release, this is still disappointing. And I wasn't even expecting a lot to begin with. When it works, the overall gameplay may be decribed as passable or rudimentary at best. When it doesn't, you will be struggling with all manner of bugs, glitches, and inconsistencies. From frequent crashes, to graphical glitches, to loss of chat features/interface. Admittedly, I am running the game on a near minimum requirements spec PC, so others may have a technically superiour experience, but I am, for example, literally unable to play two rounds in a row as the game crashes to desktop every single time I try to load a second round.
Motion swing controls are either broken or the developers simply don't understand what the whole point of being able to play by using your mouse as a club is. (It is to give the player the feel of actually swinging a club, in real time, and therefore requires 1:1 motion controls and respective visual representation. Another game achieved this perfectly, in 2001.)
Underwhelming at best. Every chance it will improve down the road, but impossible to recommend at this stage, particularly to those with lower specced PCs.

I don't usually write reviews,  that's because I wish I had more time to come up with an in depth look into the game I'm playing to actually give it a worthy review. This game is great in my opinion, sure it has a few problems none of which are gamplay or graphic-wise (my biggest problem is with the change in the Outsider's voice but I can look past that and view the masterpiece in wake of that one flaw). The visuals are stunning to look at, the gameplay is hours of fun and the story is decent. The problem is in the game's optimizing apparently, and that's not something to look passed and say "If it worked this would be a great game!" then give it a positive review based on what you hoped the gae would be. I personally have had no performance issues, so I guess I'm one of the lucky ones. So based on my experience of the game, the game is great! I'd recommend it for sure if there was a way of knowing for sure the game worked with your computer.
Corvo's back! That's great (I haven't played as him yet), and his voice is perfect for him. The character didn't have a voice in the first game, and giving a beloved character who didn't speak in the first game a voice is always going to be risky, but I think by giving the role to the voice of Garrett from the 'Thief' series is a bonus, especially when you consider the thief games and their influence on the development of Dishonored. Our dear Emily has all grown up and you can play as her. Her abilities are interesting and differ greatly to Corvo's while still at times feeling reminicent as to make sure you're not unable to reach places as one character that you couldn't reach as the other.
There's so much negativity in these reviews, and what I personally believe to be unnecessary negativity. I haven't had a single problem with the game not working, crashing or having low frame-rates and I know I'm one of the lucky ones who hasn't had issues. I feel like I need to dilute this negativity with my own positivity to some extent. So this is a place-holder for now in hopes that one day I'll actually be able to do this game justice but there needs to be more positive out there so I'm doing my part.
If you're interested in purchasing the game... I'd have to say wait, but that doesn't mean I'm saying not to purchase. Definitely come back to this once it's been polished up a bit so you can live this experience the same way I've been fortunate enough to be able to.

Dishonored 2 improves on Dishonored 1 in every aspect.
Even though the PC performance is a bit lacking, it can be worked on with updates and honestly, at least with my current system of an i7-6700k and GTX 960 4GB I had no real issues. No stuttering or scenes that made the game unenjoyable.
With that aside, even though this game offers you the choice to play either as Emily or as Corvo, in the end those two characters don't do much of a difference storywise. What's more important is the choice between powers or no-powers mode, low chaos or high chaos run and of course the pacifist options. I had a blast playing this game twice and some missions even multiple times like the Clockwork Mansion. There is so much to see and to explore, especially when taking in ghost routes to not be detected. And even after 2 playthroughs, I stil l want to go back at least one more time to do more achievements which practically are more like rewards for challenges. If that is something that can motivate you even more, even if it is just a challenge to play the game in a more different, difficult way, you can get a lot of playtime out of this game. Replayability is the key word. Look at my current playtime, I have put in 30 hours already without feeling drained or exhausted and if I wasn't going to play the next game on my list for a review, I would just continue playing it for above listed reasons.
Recommendation: GIVEN!

There are probably a million system shock 2 reviews. It's an old, classic "retro" game. Screw that♥♥♥♥♥♥ I was 4 when ss2 came out. nostalgia is not why I like this game. I like system shock 2 because of it's a amazing video game, with some of the best artificial videogame characters and it's videogame systems. A videogame human character does not have the depth or complexity of a real person, and system shock 2 understands it. The best video game characters are the ones that aren't human at all. You are human however, and that makes you special in system shock 2. It also makes you lonely. The feeling is very similar to playing as Chell in the Portal games, where again, the characters are all artificial. The other amazing thing about system shock 2 is the game systems. It is mechanically a first person shooter, but relying only on your abilities to avoid damage and kill things will not be enough. You must master the cybernetic enhancements systems, learning to spend your cybernetic modules intelligently, and learning to master stealth, hacking, research, and resource conservation.

This is my first review. Feedback is appreciated.
I've played this game for a long time, and I still play it weekly with my friends.
It's also to go at it alone.
Graphically, the game looks pretty neat, and the sounds of the zombies are good. You can hear a zombie approaching you from behind (footsteps) and such.
There are plenty of zombies to go around.
You have your
, some slightly faster than others, with different walking animations, your slightly rarer
, and of course, something you'd rarely see in a game and that I LOVE for the added realism,
. Children only scratch you, they don't bite and they also run.
Recently the developers have also added soldier zombie. They have a helmet that decreases head damage. They might also drop supplies.
, however, when a player dies, he can become a runner controlled by AI and attack other survivors. By observing a player's death, one can usually tell whether the corpse will raise or not.
The variety of weaponry is nice, and it still increases every now and then when updates are released.
You have melee weapons, firearms, explosives, and others, such as the bow.
All of the weapons have different weights.
Melee weapons have different damage outputs and stamina usage, and some are efficiently used in a certain way than others. For example, the fireaxe is very good if you charge the attack before striking the head of a zombie, usually resulting in an instant-showering-pop for a reasonable stamina drain, while a sledgehammer or a fubar is very efficient against multiple enemies standing next to each other if you use a 'quick' swing towards the head, usually killing several zombies at once, costing you however a colossal amount of stamina.
Oh crap, did I mention there's a chainsaw that consumes fuel?
You have lots of firearms: pistols, sniper-rifles, rifles, submachine-guns, shotguns.
The only automatic weapons so far are the MP5A4 and the Ingram Mac-10, both submachine-guns.
Firearms use different kinds of ammo.
Not all of the firearms instantly kill on headshots (unless realism is activated).
You can check how much ammo your current gun has by holding your reload button.
You can kill yourself with your gun.
There are throwable explosives, such as the grenade, the TNT (huge range, keep away from it, seriously) and the molotov.
The molotov will lit zombies on fire. Zombies on fire can sometimes begin to sprint towards you, so yeah, you've been warned. Usually, bashing them away or simply walking (yes walking, not walking backwards though) away will be enough to let them die off.
There's also a flare gun! Zombies become darker and darker as they burn.
Finally, you also have a bow... and you can pickup the arrows. Even if they are stuck on a zombie as they walk. :)
You cannot see how much health you have
, however, another player can tell you your name's color so you can have an idea. I believe 70+ hp is green, and it gets worse and worse until it goes red.
The stamina I speak of cannot be seen in the game, there's nothing on your screen that tells you how much of it is left, you can only know your stamina by hearing your breathing.
Pressing 1, 2 or 3 shows your weapons, ammo, and voice-commands respectively.
Affects how many items you can have in your inventory and how quickly you run out of stamina while running. Although I don't usually pay much attention to this, and correct me if I'm wrong, I've also noticed an increase in overall movement speed if the player has less weight.
When you suffer damage, there is a chance for you to start bleeding. This includes fall-damage as well, my friend fell from a vent and started bleeding on the FEMA map, luckily, there was a bandage under the bed.
While bleeding, you start to lose 1 HP every few seconds. Bleeding can be cured with bandages or a first-aid kit.
Well you got bit... and suddenly some veins begin to surround your field of view. A few minutes later, you are completely blind, and within seconds, you collapse, only to raise and begin to feast on the other survivors (controlled by AI).
If you are infected, the best thing you can do is to shoot yourself in the head with a gun, yes, kill yourself, that way you won't ♥♥♥♥ people over.
Or you can just become a pill hog and rely on them until the end of the round... Yes, you have to take pills every few minutes, because they start to wear off. Oh, and be careful around infected players, you can kill them, and they can't kill you (unless friendly fire is already on the server).
Recently they have also added a rare item that is very small and possibly hard for some to see called Gene Therapy, permanently curing your infection and making you immune. There is a chance for you to be partially blinded for 10 seconds or something around that though.
There are lots of maps, that's for sure. They can be split into two big groups. You have your survival maps where you hold down somewhere for a certain amount of waves of zombies, with supply drops every few, and then you have your objective map, in which you do... objectives.
Some maps also change objectives, which adds for replayability.
Being a realistic survival horror game, where zombies are actually dangerous, specially in large groups, teamwork is essential. A single zombie can screw you, simply due to the fact that you can get infected.
But the community... oh the community...
Lots of players that don't even speak english, so teamwork there is usually a no-no.
Others are newbies and don't listen to veterans, ending up dead and wasting a great amount of resources (ammo, medical items, ...).
Then there's also mic-spammers.
All of the above are even more common in unlimited ammo servers, you've been warned.
In Realism mode + FF on servers for example, communication is extremely important, mainly because if there's no communication, players will just try to melee the zombies while pushing eachother / teamkilling by accident, or throw an explosive somewhere, killing others because there was no pre-warning ("Throwing a grenade!" -- The character says, but too late :P)
In other games I've always been slightly disappointed at the lack of children in the middle of an apocalypse. Well, immersion = fun for me. In an occasion, I've found a player who didn't want to shoot the children, saying it was too much for him. That was enjoyable to watch...
"THEY AREN'T ♥♥♥♥ING CHILDREN, THEY'RE MONSTERS!"
Updates, although not frequent, are very nice. They recently revamped the medical system and I must say it turned out pretty good!
The zombie hitboxes need some more work. I've had occasions (and so have my friends) where I've shot the head several times but the bullet didn't insta-kill when it should have, sometimes even twice or more. This is slightly rare though.
Feel free to add me, maybe we can play sometime!

Finally a game who deserves the name "Alien" in its title.
What you should now before you buy this game:
- No it's not a pure action game or shooter like you would expect
- Yes this game is a survival horror game and it does everything right
Read here why:
I pre purchased although I had sworn I wouldn't pre purchase any Alien game any more after the disaster of its predecessor. So they game got released and I started to play. During pre-load and the first launch I just told to myself every minute: "Please don't suck again!". With that I meant the game not my gaming skill but during the intro and after my first steps on the Sevastopol station I was blown away. Here is why:
This game has an awesome atmosphere. The level design is very good, The sound effects fit perfectly to the overall level design and game situation and support the already awesome atmosphere. The options which way to take, where to hide or in general how to handle a situation are not endless but sufficient enough to allow the player to take the choice. The path of the Alien is not always the same but somehow random which gives every situation a more realistic touch since studying the alien path doesn't always help you getting past the alien. Goodies and pickups are well placed. The player is punished for every little mistake. And the game is still fun.
So all the important points for delivering a good/very good survival horror game are set. Only thing I was partly disappointed was the fact that here and there the hide and seek game with the alien gets somehow repetitive until the story is continued to suck you into the game and the happenings on the Sevastopol.
As I said before: this is a survival horror game.
Yes it is hard.
Yes you will die very often.
Yes you will think it is unfair because being spotted by the Alien usually means instant death.
No it is never frustrating and that's what's all about. Finding the thin line between unfair and frustrating makes the difference and this game is the best proof for that.
This game is for you if you:
- love the Alien franchise
- are looking for the best Alien game released until today
- are looking for an awesome survival horror game with tight atmosphere
- you love challenging games
- would love to destroy an android with a maintenance jack
This game is not for you:
- if you expect a fps or pure action game
- if you hate to die often or cannot handle challenging situations.
- if you think that "Nostromo" is the new cocktail which is only served in the lunchroom of a nuclear power plant near Sevastopol a small region in Siberia :)
