An absolutely fantastic experience, I myself am not a fan of horror or stealth games but I love sci-fi and the alien universe, so this was a must pick up for me.
The graphics are absolutely stunning, there is so much attention to detail its hard to take it all in at times and I spent the first part of the game just examining every little part of the place. The particle effects that puff when every door opens, the incredible lighting and the particles even had shadows on them, I cannot fault the aesthetics of the game which perfectly recreate and expand upon the films universe. I only ever encountered a few minor visual glitches and some I only picked up on as I am a level designer myself, like a few visible seams and clipping issues but they were so minor and rare its barely worth noting.
The atmosphere is incredible, you never feel safe ever, even in your hiding spaces you can be caught, the sound design truly helps with this. The foley work and sound effects throughout the entire game are just incredible, every last creak and groan of air ducts really adds to the unease and tension. That's not to say you never get a break, cooldown chapters are interspersed to stop it becoming too stressful, particularly after very tense missions, where you dont have too much danger to deal with. The sound also plays just as important a role as your motion tracker in letting you know where enemies are and when the alien is in the vents.
The music again is great and the dynamic score can actually aid you as it gets steadily more dramatic as you get closer to being detected. It also helps keep the tension up during the dramatic parts and to spur you on when you are caught and have to either run away or defend yourself.
The game tutorialises each new enemy really well, they each tend to get their own dedicated chapter which starts of pretty hard until you learn how to avoid each enemy type. You also get new tools along the way and with regards to the backtracking I didnt have any problems as different paths are open or closed, there are different enemies and with your new tools you can find different ways around. There are multiple solutions for getting through the rooms and it was interesting to see the completely different approaches my friends took when playing the game.
Storywise it was pretty good with a few plot twists and turns, some predictable, some not, i thought the ending was ok but not as great as it could have been.
Overall, 10 out of 10 from me, a must play for sci-fi and Alien fans, stunning locations and some fantastic set pieces, with incredible sound design, cannot recommend enough, fantastic.

I first heard about System Shock 2 and its supposed greatness about 10 years ago. Since then, every now and then the title would cross my mind and I would think how I wanted to play it. That's why I jumped at the opportunity to purchase it on Steam when it recently arrived. I was not disappointed. System Shock 2 is nothing short of a masterpiece.  I can only describe System Shock 2 as a hybrid of the original Deus Ex and Half-life. It is also the spiritual predecessor to Bioshock.  With comparisons to legendary titles like that, what can go wrong?  System Shock 2 is immensely fun and extremely addictive. Its strongest attribute is its chilling atmosphere and sheer level of depth.  For a 1999 game, this kind of FPS and RPG fusion, combined with an engaging story and horror elements, was revolutionary.  The level of quality is still remarkable even by today's standards.  As I expected, the late 90's gameplay mechanics can be clunky and frustrating. Combat is rigid and takes time to get adapted with. The learning curve is fast, steep, and unforgiving, and I found myself saving and reloading frequently, which at times took me out of the experience. Eventually I got used to it.  Do yourself a favor and visit this piece of classic cult gaming.

To call System Shock 2 just a great game, or even an amazing game would still be a understatement, so I'm just going to come out and say it, System Shock 2 is probably be fare one of the greatess games every made... PERIOD!!!
Forget the Bioshocks, especially Bioshock Infinate's dumbed down for the Halo/COD kids gameplay, they fail in comparison to the shear genious of this under-rated classic.
To vast magority of gamers around 1999 Half-Life was still considered king of the FPS games, but Half-life was, is and always will be over-rated.  And once you play and experience this game for yourself you will see why.
Back then I was still very much the standered FPS fan I liked my shooters, loud, dumb and funny, then I played this game, and it opened my eyes to a whole other world and forever changed my perseption on gaming, and to this day I find most FPS games nowadays just lack the overall complexity, satifaction and depth that System Shock 2 offered me.
Fair warning to ye oh HALO and COD children for this game is not for the fait of heart or weak of mind. I pre-ordered this game with high expectations, and like many loyal followers of the series, I was greatly disappointed. Having put this game aside for several months, I am pleased to say that at least some of the teething problems have been corrected by succeeding patches and new DLC. I am currently enjoying my new campaign. The map and graphics are stunning. Critics, myself included, have bewailed the loss of some of the earlier content of Rome: family tree, unlimeted unit recruitment, etc., but the game plays well now, and each legion can be varied and personalized. The game forces you, the player, to do more with less, and there are a variety of mods to be explored. In this game, it is very important to prioritize your goals; spread yourself too thin, and you will lose legions. To my mind, a successful corp is two legions AND a supporting fleet. Save frequently, and rembember: mass not driblets. Local superiority is the name of the game. Good luck!

It's a bimbo of a game; so much beauty but no brains. CA has gone wildly astray with both Shogun and now Rome II. The game has a massive map, beautifully rendered cities, but it doesn't use them to create a compelling strategy game. The tech tree is dumbed down, the diplomacy system leaves much to be desired and the urban and infrastructure development is very shallow. Developments to eg public order and dynasties have potential to make a difference but are poorly executed.
The result is that you go from one stunning battle to another, but that is all there is and you can get pretty bored of that. If CA would use the beautiful citiscapes to create a new interface on civic managmenet with a detailed political, economic, tech and social/dynasty systems the game would be much more immersive and enjoyable. As it is don't bother with the campaign, just enjoy the battles straight from the start menu as that is all the campaign has to offer anyway.

Overall with all the patches it's one of the best total wars to date.

Altough this is not the best game in the Total war series in my opinion ( i'm still very loyal too Rome: Total war ) this game had been on my watch for years. As you can see i have played the game thoroughly and i have a few things to ssay about it.
Notes before buying
- Make sure you have updated your system well, an old cpu will result into random crashes due too system overload.
- This game has stunning visuals but if you are planning on upgrading for this game start with CPU.
Pros
- Even almost a year after its release it is still being patched and dlcs are still coming out.
- You can play this game for ever because of the diverse campaigns, playeble factions and the multiplayer.
- The community is amazing. Everyday mods are being released to improve and extend the gaming experience.
- It is definitly the most evolved and diverse Total War yet.
- The DLC offer a lot of new scenarios that we didnt see that much in other Total War games.
- CA did an fantastic job at listning to the community and making the game for the people instead for money.
Cons
- If you have a weak system your game may crash.
- If you are running to much mods you may experience them clashing and thus crashing your game.
- On a high end system the graphics could have been somewhat more ''organic''
- DLCs are paid for and are around 8,- in every country.
- AI diplomacy does not reflect anything about your economic or millatary power, on a higher difficulty it will only be more unreasonable. There is a mod that has a fix for this.
- It maybe relies on mods to much for it to be exciting or diverse.
In my opinion this game is totally worth buying ( maybe wait for a sale if you come in short ) it is beautifully disigned, it has a great community and a die hard Total War fan this is just an absolute dream because i have been waiting for 10 odd years!

A few friends have already asked for my opinion on this gam-MOD, IT'S A MOD. So, I decided to make a review about it instead of talking about it over and over. As usual, I'll talk first about the bad things, however there's not that many:
First and foremost; the controversy. I've waited for a long time to buy it because I was seriously against what the devs did. You see, time ago, this was a Mod. For free. The Devs had not yet finished it, but left it there for people to test it out. When they did that, they promised that Black Mesa would NEVER cost money, as it was a mod they created with passion to revive a game they love. Well that's kind of bullsh#t because soon after the game arrived in Steam Greenlight, and after a few months it was released in Early Access, still unfinished, and FOR 20€. A lot of people did NOT take this lightly, as it was a God-damn lie which they tried to hide from the Internet. In the end, I waited long for a sale, and I got it on the Autumm sale of 2015.
The second bad point of the game, is that after so many years in development, it's still unfinished. From the start to the Lambda complex, you'll get to see an insanely beautifull recreation of Half-Life, to then get hit in the face with a "to be continued", as the Xen chapters have been in development for a ton of time. To this point it's still not there, but that's not the only thing missing, as there's also a lot of maps missing on the multiplayer. Crossfire, for example, has been my most favorite HL map ever. It's a chaotic mess that I love, and it's yet to be added (devs said it's the next map to arrive). The multiplayer is also kind of abandoned as I rarely found servers with people, although I won't blame the devs for that.
That being said, what we have left is a game so good, it almost looks like Valve made it. The engine has been pushed to it's limits, and it clearly shows. Textures, animations, models; they all look insanely beautiful. Infact, I've only found a few bugs so far, one of them with a strange hitbox of a door, and another about an elevator that gave me ammunition for no reason at all everytime I went into it. The only bug that really annoyed me was the Hive-gun not appearing on my first playthrough. It was nowhere to be found where it was on the original HL and original Black Mesa, and I couldn't find it anywhere else. I was never a fan of that gun, but it seems that it got buffed and wanted to give it a try...
Weapons have been balanced and/or remade to keep them from over-shadowing others. They also can appear in different areas than in the original game (remember the guard you can safe from a zombie early on? He now lets you take a revolver instead of a shotgun, which appears much later on, when the military shows up). The game also gives you a fair amount of challenge along the game, just as it gives you a fair amount of health, armor and ammo pick ups. Exploration is important, as there are a lot of said pickup items hidden in hard to reach areas. NPC's are helpful on it's own, and also have more personality and character than in the original HL game. You actually feel like they are someone who also got screwed because of the aliens, people who are trying to survive as hard as you.
If you haven't yet (for some dumb reason) played the original Half-Life, I'm gonna tell you to play this instead. However, seeing as it's still unfinished, and the price they ask might be too high for some, you should seriously wait for a sale. 10€ would be a fair price, further down would be a must-have.
Oh and, nice job putting the damn hat at the beggining of the game. It's the Gnome Achievement from HL2EP2 all over again.

I don't usually write reviews,  that's because I wish I had more time to come up with an in depth look into the game I'm playing to actually give it a worthy review. This game is great in my opinion, sure it has a few problems none of which are gamplay or graphic-wise (my biggest problem is with the change in the Outsider's voice but I can look past that and view the masterpiece in wake of that one flaw). The visuals are stunning to look at, the gameplay is hours of fun and the story is decent. The problem is in the game's optimizing apparently, and that's not something to look passed and say "If it worked this would be a great game!" then give it a positive review based on what you hoped the gae would be. I personally have had no performance issues, so I guess I'm one of the lucky ones. So based on my experience of the game, the game is great! I'd recommend it for sure if there was a way of knowing for sure the game worked with your computer.
Corvo's back! That's great (I haven't played as him yet), and his voice is perfect for him. The character didn't have a voice in the first game, and giving a beloved character who didn't speak in the first game a voice is always going to be risky, but I think by giving the role to the voice of Garrett from the 'Thief' series is a bonus, especially when you consider the thief games and their influence on the development of Dishonored. Our dear Emily has all grown up and you can play as her. Her abilities are interesting and differ greatly to Corvo's while still at times feeling reminicent as to make sure you're not unable to reach places as one character that you couldn't reach as the other.
There's so much negativity in these reviews, and what I personally believe to be unnecessary negativity. I haven't had a single problem with the game not working, crashing or having low frame-rates and I know I'm one of the lucky ones who hasn't had issues. I feel like I need to dilute this negativity with my own positivity to some extent. So this is a place-holder for now in hopes that one day I'll actually be able to do this game justice but there needs to be more positive out there so I'm doing my part.
If you're interested in purchasing the game... I'd have to say wait, but that doesn't mean I'm saying not to purchase. Definitely come back to this once it's been polished up a bit so you can live this experience the same way I've been fortunate enough to be able to.

Yes, very recommended but...only for those who played Demon's Souls or Dark Souls and want some more without high expectations about the story.
In general terms I really loved Dark Souls II. First Souls game with native HD and beyond resolutions for PC. Also the 60 FPS was a very important "must". The plot and lore are not that great as Dark Souls PTDE but it has his own good moments.
This new entry is full of new items and some other little interesting mechanics like the coffin of Things Betwixt, the life gems and some new covenants. It was fun to discover them through the game.
The humanity thing remains but this time is easier to handle. In general Dark Souls II has a lot of things to make the difficulty of newcomers easier (wich I recommend you don't abuse if you played a Souls before).
About Souls and leveling this time you do it between Emerald Gerald in Majula. Similar to the Maiden in Black from Demon's Souls Nexus.
About visual and sound...mmm... Visually is not mind blowing but is an step forward from PC Dark Souls with DS Fix. The art looks fantastic in lighting terms. Maybe is different in it's style in terms of environments and enemies design. A lot more cliche but enjoyable. Oh! rag doll is off in this game...and the lighting and assets from it's first gameplay shown to the world ¬¬

The sound design (foley etc) is good. But the music score is something I recommend you didn't expect to be better than previous games. But is good!...Take listen to Demon's Souls for instance. It has some interesting flutes and leitmotifs wich are missing on the next game. I find the Intro, Phalanx or the adjudicator one the most memorable ones. In Dark Souls there's a great variety of styles and there's even more memorable songs. And unfortunate for those who love the music of this games Dark Souls II is kind of flat...epic but flat. That doesn't mean i doesn't have it's moments ;)
About the important thing...Gameplay. It's almost the same but more responsive and smooth. The kick was replaced for the shoulder push. But there's a lot more weapon styles even bare hands styles. I find my self on PvP with players with very strange setups xD and of course two hackers in a few months (I'm not very expect on the PvP thing). The only downside here is that "Soul Memory System" wich is not optional.
The co-op. Now you can summon two players the NPC of the area you're (if it's available) and an internet player. This can make the game much easier. I don't recommend this much. I find myself solving some bosses with this method and then feeling horrible haha. But never again!
Mmmm Boss Fights...they're not that interesting as the areas they're on. But there are some of this friends wich you'll hate at the same level as before.
I think Dark Souls II is not a bad entry at all (BTW Hidetaka Miyazaki just supervised it but it wasn't it's director). We can't say is a bad game. Maybe a transition. I think it's better than have a hole until Bloodborne is released and of course it deserves it's price ;)

Alien Isolation is by far the best Alien game to date, and had me on my toes through the whole game.  The game has you play Ripley's daughter Amanda, as she boards an old space station called Sevastapol, when it is discovered that they have the flight recorder from the Nostromo.  Not surprisingly, she soon finds out that the station has gone to heck, and there is an alien creature wandering the station, brutally killing anyone it finds.  To add insult to injury, there is also a legion of 'malfunctioned' androids, called Working Joes.  Amanda must use her wits, and her ingenuity to evade the alien, the Joes, and even some unfriendly humans to find the answers she seeks, and to get off the station.
This game was so epic in scope, and provided everything you could ask for in an Alien game.  The level design was inspired by the set pieces from the original Alien film, and when you couple that with volumetric lighting, and eerie steam and particle effects, the result was unnerving, to say the least.
The DLC features characters from the film, and is voiced by the original actors.  You can't put a price on that, but they did anyway, and that prize was 4 dollars.  Wow.
The only negative thing I would say about the game, is that the story required that you backtrack a few times.  But even with this minor flaw in the game, it was an amazing and terrifying journey that I would recommend to anyone who likes first person shooters, survival horror games, and expecially fans of the Alien franchise.

No matter what, this game is, and will always be, fun to play. I have hundreds of hours playing this game on console before i came to pc gaming and i still get the itch to play through it all these years later.
Pro's:
-Although the story is not ground breaking in my opinion, It still captivating enough to play through. Its a slight follow up on the games predecessor, Borderlands but dont worry although it would make the experience better if you have played the first borderland its not in any way required to know what is happening in this game.
-The gun play feels really nice aswell the aiming feels nice and smooth and there is little input lag, the weapons are well designed and, well, one of the selling points of the game is its vast variety of weapons.
-New game plus, Or as its called in this game True vault hunter mode. Once you have beaten the final boss this is unlocked, like most new game plus type game mode you just start the game again but all the enemy's are stronger and you keep your level, weapons and abilities. If like me you enjoyed the game the first time around this is a huge plus side because you get to go blow up, shoot and massacre more bad guys all over again.
-The DLC, I feel like the DLC expansions for the borderlands are spot on and well worth the money aswell. Each one adds more great charecters have there own playfull storys and have thier own atmosphere, although most of the enemys in the DLC's are just Re-skinned and named enemys from the normal game there are still new and challenging foes and theres alot of extra content in them.
-Skill trees, Although a action FPS game the borderlands is also a RPG, The base game has you chose from 4 characters each with 3 original skill tree's (there are also 2 extra charecters aswell
in the psycho and mechromancer packs) Each skill tree focus' on a different style of play and this is also true for the characters themselves, for example one day as zer0 you could be a head hunting sniper and the next you could re-spec into a melee monster, slashing everyone to pieces.
-Comedic side, This is simple really, The game is funny. Well all comedy is subjective but the game dose try its best to be humorous and light hearted.
The cons
-Honestly i might be biased due to how much i truely love this game but i cant think of any bad points at all, given how old the game is, its aged fantastically well. Its fun to just go around and kill things. the few times the game wants to be serious or have a moment its showed perfectly and all the major charatcers are designed extraordinarily well. AND you can do it all with friends! In my opinion this game is a absolute masterpiece and deserves at least a chance, even more so if its on sale.

Altough this is not the best game in the Total war series in my opinion ( i'm still very loyal too Rome: Total war ) this game had been on my watch for years. As you can see i have played the game thoroughly and i have a few things to ssay about it.
Notes before buying
- Make sure you have updated your system well, an old cpu will result into random crashes due too system overload.
- This game has stunning visuals but if you are planning on upgrading for this game start with CPU.
Pros
- Even almost a year after its release it is still being patched and dlcs are still coming out.
- You can play this game for ever because of the diverse campaigns, playeble factions and the multiplayer.
- The community is amazing. Everyday mods are being released to improve and extend the gaming experience.
- It is definitly the most evolved and diverse Total War yet.
- The DLC offer a lot of new scenarios that we didnt see that much in other Total War games.
- CA did an fantastic job at listning to the community and making the game for the people instead for money.
Cons
- If you have a weak system your game may crash.
- If you are running to much mods you may experience them clashing and thus crashing your game.
- On a high end system the graphics could have been somewhat more ''organic''
- DLCs are paid for and are around 8,- in every country.
- AI diplomacy does not reflect anything about your economic or millatary power, on a higher difficulty it will only be more unreasonable. There is a mod that has a fix for this.
- It maybe relies on mods to much for it to be exciting or diverse.
In my opinion this game is totally worth buying ( maybe wait for a sale if you come in short ) it is beautifully disigned, it has a great community and a die hard Total War fan this is just an absolute dream because i have been waiting for 10 odd years!

Warning there will be a set of spoilers at the very end of this review which I will indicate where they begin. I am including these for those who do not care about spoilers as well as I believe they had a big impact on my opinion of the game.
Overall I would definitely recommend playing this game. If you have played the original then it is definitely worth it. Whether you want to pay $60 is up to you. I am going to avoid talking too much about the glitches,frame rate drops and so on. The only thing I have to say is I am running a medium quality pc and I didn't have any problems that made the game feel unplayable due to the improper port. I experienced one freeze throughout the entire game. I did however experience multiple noticeable frame rate drops down into the 20-25 fps but nothing that made the game unplayable.
The positive points of the game:
The biggest improvement from the original game is the level design. I cannot stress how well these are done. Like they were incredible and just so fun for me. This is the games strongest point which you may be thinking "really the level design is the best thing?" The other aspects such as combat and stealth are also done very well but the level design is just so great that it surpasses everything else. The levels are well thought out, offering more verticallity, more possible routes, clever location and interactive environments, and overall an immersive layout that always felt exciting and encouraged exploration. Without giving any spoilers I always wanted to keep exploring each area and there was always another path hidden path waiting to be found.
The new powers are also very well done. I played as Emily in my first play through. The new set of powers keep the game feeling fresh and make the game feel like a different game than the original. It is also very neat that if you play as Corvo you used all the powers from the original. Thee difference in the two is quite nice and offers a ton of replayability. The introduction of expansions on the powers is also a nice addition. Because I have to play without killing anybody or being seen I wasn't able to use all of the powers to their full extent but they did still offer a ton of variety and blended well with level design which I can not stress enough was on point.
Because of the poor port I did not play this game to what my pc should be able to run yet the graphics were still decent. The art style is unique enough that it is pleasant but still keeps a serious tone. This combined with the steampunk world from the first brings out a lot of life in each level. The nightime streets and houses are aestically pleasing and well thought out. My only complaint with the art design is (perhaps its just me) that everyones eyes look a little too far apart. Perhaps this was on purpose but it seems a little off like everyone is a quater whale. This kinda makes the main antagonist a little less intimidating but that is just me.
Combat and stealth are good. The new powers just add to everything from the original. It never really felt unfair or op and it was pretty obvious when I would get caught it would be my mistake rather than poor stealth mechanics. With the exception of the teleport power being a little hard to aim. I can't say too much about combat cause I only ever used it when I was seen and just wanted to kill everybody real quick to vent out my raging sexual frustration before reloading to before I was seen. Without going into too much detail the stealth mechanics are better than most stealth based games. Also one can play the game pretty much any way they want which is nice.
My biggest complaint about this game is the story. Its just kinda bland. Its not necessarily bad but its not great either. I didn't really care about what was happening throughout the entire game. There were a few cool parts but mostly it was just not all that great. There were also parts that weren't explained or seemed like plot holes but I really wasn't all that engaged in the games lackluster, more watered down than the flooded district politics. Also nothing felt super satisfying in the games resolution.
Another down side to the game was the voice acting. At times it sounds as though lines were recorded on two separate days for just one sentence. Sometimes the dialogue was too over done with emotions while at other times didn't have any when it felt like it should. This is a personal opinion here but I really liked the silent protagonist of the first game and idk what it is with Bethesda giving main characters voices but it is included in this game. My biggest problem with this is it makes it much harder to project onto the character and the dialogue interjections in the story are off. For some people a vocal playable character is a good thing but I personally don't like it. The new outsider sucks btw.
Even with its downsides the replayablity, stealth/combat, and of course level design make up for any short comings. I really enjoyed this game and did't mind paying full price for it. I would probably rate it at about 79/100. The story and voice acting could've been much better but it didn't ruin the game at all. Level design though phew that was, that was just more on point than timberlake on some chopped trees in a creek.
SPOILERS

Clearly the premise of this game is idiotic and ridiculous. Yet for some reason it's strangely compelling. The complexity can be surprising and overwhelming at times. But it is strangely endearing and pretty challenging. It works with my Logitech GT wheel (on Linux no less) and with that it can be quite immersive.
It would be nice to have a normal car mode to lower the difficulty a bit but an unloaded truck isn't too bad.
Missed turns are a nightmare. When I get to a crossroad the freeway exit which I could use to turn around and which the nav computer says to take is blocked with Xs! Brutal.
I do not like the reverse controls. I don't want a full manual transmission but I want the brake to always be a brake; never a throttle in reverse.
Not being able to set sleep time is annoying. On one hand, you have to plan carefully; that's fine. On the other hand if I can't specify how long to sleep, I can't execute a careful plan.
No motorcycles? Also no bicycles? Even in Holland?
Driving onto the ferry to Calais is awesome. Tunnel train is cool too.
Overall the scenery matches my recollection of Europe from Scotland to Switzerland. I'm quite impressed at how the spirit of the countryside is beautifully captured. An impressive game with great attention to detail and a premise that turns out to be a lot less stupid than I first thought! Gute Reise!

This is going to go down as one of my all-time favourite games and it's not just because i loved the first two Alien franchise films but because it's a damn good survival horror game and i hope that this well and truly breaks the ice on a genre that i really hope to see come back.
If you are a fan of the franchise and want to play a game in the spirit of the first film with an excellent amount of effort put into recreating the Alien universe whilst still making it fully believable in the modern world then this is a game for you. It's also a game for you if like or love a good survival horror  game because it does an excellent job and i rank this alongside the Resident Evil remake that came out over a decadse ago and is now available on the PC as well.
The Storyline:
This, unfortunately is nothing special and i have to say that it does end on a crappy cliffhanger. there's nothing particuarly amazing about it or any part of it.
Performance and Graphics:
This game is an excellent PC game. It runs very, very well and looks great. Have no concerns about PC technical issues i haven't had any since the first month of release and while they certainly annoyed me now that they have been thoroughly ironed out i have been able to enjoy the game in peace.

Finally a game that justifies the Alien series, it really manages to capture the horror of being hunted by something you can't fight. To keep this review short:
The good:
-The game is styled to the way they saw the future when making the first Alien movie, which means computers are massive and nothing really feels modern, even though it takes place in space
-The alien is unpredictable, the AI of the Xeno is fantastic besides some minor things. Like one time it ran past me while i was in the middle of his path, now don't think you can just run around, because there isn't much you can do when he sees you.
-Ammo is hard to get, there are guns which can only kill people and the androids, not aliens. Each shot has to be justified as you can't allow to waste a lot of ammo
-You're hunted, this game does this better than anything I've ever played. Hiding in a closet while hearing humans being brutally murdered one by one. You will die a lot in this game, but it always feels like it was your mistake
-Graphics are great, the lightning especially is really well done
The bad:
-The interactions feel robotic, it's stupid that there are about 4 seconds in between exiting a computer and being able to walk. Anyone can see and kill you during this period. Does capture the horror element quite well, but it just feels unnecessary
-Not being able to jump over small obstacles, i get the horror element, but do i really need to be stuck to the ground if i can take a shortcut over that small barrier?
-Story isn't all that interesting, i didn't find any character to be interesting
Definitely a game I'd recommend, get some surround headphones and this game won't be like anything you've ever played.

This game is not terrible, but there are certainly issues with it.  I haven't bought a CoD game since MW2.  I got burned with MW2 with no dedicated servers, no numerical pings, lag, hackers, horrible weapons and perks, and an overall downgrade in game quality.  Hell, I reinstalled CoD4 for about the 6th time this past year and still find that the most enjoyable in spite of all these new releases clearly aimed at promising the community what they want just to sham them because another will release in a year.  Not to mention a 110 price tag if you incldue the DLC to play CoD every year.  After getting burned a second time with this game, I doubt I will buy into this company anymore.  Unfortunately there is no other shooter like it and I bought it to play with online friends, but it is seriously time for the PC community to give the finger back to Activision.  I'll be on the lookout for new FPS games for me and my friends to participate in where features and functionality that PC gamers need exists, while still remaining enjoyable.
Overall, the game can be fun, but it can also be frustrating.  Exo abilities are cool but often feel like over powered bunny hops.  There is practically no cover, and nowhere you can go to play strategically with these abilities unless you are inside.  The game only feels truly tactical in hardcore mode.  Lastly, we cant remove hackers as we spot them, nor host our own servers.  I made it through 3 prestiges and don't really have any inkling to launch this game back up.  I'd rather play Skyrim and CoD4 until something better blows Activision out of the water.  It is good quick fun if you enjoy lag, hackers, overpowered lasers, noob tubes, hackers, extreme bunny hopping, and not playing tactically at all.

Highly entertaining game to be played both alone and with friends. I played through the entirety of the main campaign with my girlbro and we enjoyed every second of the explosive gameplay. Platforming is superb. You have to carefully plan every move you make. The environment is almost completely destructible, creating some funny situations. There are dozens of characters to unlock based on stereotypical action movie stars like Terminator, Rambo, and Neo from the Matrix. I won't ruin all of them for you, but it's very rewarding and satisfying to use their new weapons and special attacks. This is definitely a game you can go into and play at any time. Just fire it up and start blowing enemies to pieces! Here's girlbro's two cents: " It's fun. The characters are cute & funny. I like that it's not the end of the world when you die, you're back in the action pretty quick. That's a big plus because it's easy to die in that game. I just feel like there are some bugs to work through, & without those it would be a solid 8 or even a 9. I enjoyed it a lot." The game does have some bugs to work out, but I only experienced them in the multiplayer. Sometimes it will require a restart, and that can be frustrating because you'll have to begin your "world" again. When I say that, I mean Mario-style worlds. 1-1, 1-2, etc. There are probably about 3 or 4 levels per world, with bosses. We beat the game in probably about 5 or 6 hours. Recommended.

Right, let’s get the negatives out of the way first:
- Issues at launch with bad fps, which made the game unplayable for the first week.
- Some issues with bugs like people being killed when I knocked them out and were linked via domino power.
- Adaptive resolution, I hate it! and what made it worse was the fact that I had to turn it off every time I loaded up the game.

BUT after the first patch sorted out the fps issues the game opened up into what Dishonored should be.
Positives:
+ STORY: Obvious, but enjoyable with great returning characters and references to the first game.
+ LEVEL DESIGN: Is back and is great with so many different ways of completing a level. (Clockwork mansion and Dust district mansion being standout levels).
+ ABILATIES: So many different ways of using the powers you're given to neutralise targets and traverse the environment. (I love Domino, such a great idea).
+ CHOICE: the choice to play as Corvo or Emily, the choice to build the powers how you want to match your own playstyle and the choice to go lethal or non-lethal.
+ GRAPHICS: I can see some people not liking the graphics or the art style, but for me I think they suit the world perfectly.
All-in-all despite the initial bad launch with bad fps (which was sorted out for me in the first patch) Dishonored 2 has built on the very strong foundations that Dishonored put in place with a unique world, great level design and multiple paths of completion. When I think of what I wanted in a sequel from the first game I wanted one that: continued the story of the characters, visited new parts of the empire and retained the best gameplay elements.
If you loved the first game then you will find all you need in Dishonored 2, but be prepared that your machine has to be a bit beefy and accept that you will still get frame rate drops in certain areas.
Better version of the first game in every aspect.

Dishonored 2 is, much like the original, one of my instant favourites. The world is rich and alive, the characters lively and detailed, the gameplay swift and smooth. It is easy for me to recommend such a game, and I do so wholeheartedly. Note, that I've only done a single playthrough as Corvo and intend to update this review, if necessary, after doing so with Emily.
In the end, though, even I have to admit that Dishonored 2 does suffer from a few issues compared to the first game. The voice acting has suffered in some areas, and something about the game engine causes voice lines to trigger a bit too fast, making many conversations seem hasty and twisted as the characters seemingly try to cut one another off mid-sentence. The story, as well, seems to pick up a bit too hastily compared to the first game, and the whats and the why's, the motivations that drive many of the characters, are a bit too obscure.
All in all, while not perfect and not quite up to par with the first game, Dishonored 2 is a great game to put a few evenings into and it serves well both for those garnering for stealth-oriented gameplay or bloodthirsty and imaginative murder-fests.

This time around, the PVE seems to be a lot more focused in co-op, there are a lot of battles with two bosses at same time and groups of enemies capable of one-shooting you, which is not bad (co-op is really fun), but it seems like a lazy design to make the game appear harder, something that I didn't feel while playing the other games in the series.
The summoning system for co-op is really innovative and well thought... until you want to play with a friend. I think at least a third of the time I spent playing was waiting on the summoning signs. Seriously, they should have made it easier to play with a friend.
Say what you want: that I suck at PVP (I do), that I'm playing it wrong, whatever... But the PVP in the series is broken and don't think I can be convinced otherwise. Why? Because of the lag, that's why. My first impressions was that the PVP mechanics were very cool... and then I was lagstabbed in three consecutive invasions. On the next fight, I was able to hit the enemy player (the game even played the sound for when you successfuly connect), but his HP was unchanged, it's like he rolled, but my weapon was clearly clipping his head at the time. Then I stopped doing PVP altogether, only to be invaded while my friend and I are co-opping, we die, because of the reasons above and we have to spend the next ten minutes waiting on the summoning signs again. I got mixed feelings about this, on one hand, I don't like the idea of being forced do do PVP. On the other hand, I like that the game gives you the idea that every player's world is connected.
I really liked the level design. Every area is unique on it's own way, everywhere I look there's something worth looking at. I found myself more than once looking at statues, enemys and structures analizing it for a piece of lore or stopping and admiring how beautiful some of the areas in the game are.
The character models have improved considerably and the voice acting is incredible. I liked every single one of the NPCs that I met.
If you played any of the Souls games you probably already know about the difficulty of the series. Well, that's true, you'll probably die... a lot. Every death is costly, enemies will respawn and you'll lose a little bit of your life every time, but that's the fun part, in Dark Souls, losing is the best way to evaluate if your strategy is working or not. If it's working, you'll know and every death will only serve to refine your skills and timing, if not, you'll fell you are doing something wrong, and you will adjust accordingly. Observe your surroundings, always look out for traps and analyze every movement of your enemies and learn how to fight from them. If you do that, I guarantee you won't find this game so hard. It's chess, not checkers. And that's what I love the most about this game.

As a stand alone game, Dark Souls 2 offers a challenging experience making you feel rewarded for remaining alert, and learning and adapting to the situation. If you're a Dark Souls 1 fanatic as myself having put 600+ hours on PC and an additional 40+ on Xbox360, prepare to be disappointed.
The ability to remain hollow to avoid PVP doesn't work anymore, having new players and PVE players alike forced into PVP in unavoidable locations. Other players ( and NPC phantoms ), may invade you while you're hollow, as well as be forced into invading another player, but you may only summon other players while human. Not all is lost however, as you can join a covenant and be under the protection of friendly players.
Poise as we know it has been removed from players, but remains on enemies as the developers way of setting and ramping up PVE difficulty throughout the game.  This causes the smallest attack such as an empty fist to stun the player, but large weapons are needed to stun enemies. The change in poise ( in respect to melee players ), makes PVE ruled by those who use the largest weapons available, and PVP ruled by the player to hit first with their 1 handed rapier and stun lock you.
The NPCs provide little in the aspect of lore, depth, or connectivity. At no point did I feel anything for them. You wont find the equivilant back stories of such Knight Lautrec, Solaire, Siegmeyer, Paladin Leeroy, or why Gwyndoline is in Anor Londo, or Big Hat Logan's history in Lordran. No, the NPCs here are not as great, but this can be overlooked.
Each death decreases your maximum health by 5%, up to a cap of 50%. A good idea for PVE as it rewards avoiding frequent deaths, and is a representation of hollowing. This however works agaisnt Dark Souls 1's memorable multi hour long PVP sessions in hotspots as each death has you weaker for the next fight.
The open concept world map may have been taken too far this time, as I found myself lost for direction of where I should be going, or why I was going that way. In closing, Dark Souls 2 is a fine game for those with no Dark Souls 1 experience or attachment. If I had not pre-orded and bought Dark Souls 2, I would not have spent the time finishing the game. Not recommended as a substitute for Dark Souls 1. On its own, I believe its still a good game with its own memorable moments.

First, let me say something:
I play this on a relatively new laptop, with a nVidia Geforce 980 or something, 8 gigs of ram, 500GB SSD and a fairly crappy i5. The only time I got any significant framerate loss was either using one of the F.O.W.s and causing a chain reaction or if id left my laptop on for more than a day or two (cause I got s**t to do).
TL;DR: Get the game. It is Just Cause 2 with all sorts of sprinkles, and its always fun to grapple a jet into a carrier plane, jump off and watch the dance of explodey goodness. The entire game can be summed up in one line by one of the characters:
"You need a more positive outlook on life son! You've got an infinite parachute for Pete's sake."
This game, as Yahtzee (ZeroPunctuation) puts it, is something that AAA gaming should do more often, because it is one of the few things thy're good at anymore.
This game is exclusively about running around blowing stuff up. Don't let the opening cutscene fool you into thinking it has any sort of rigidly defined storyline. I did the first 3 missions then went and messed around freeing settlements and irritating the local police by hurling myself headlong into them. The beauty if there are so many ways to blow stuff up - you can shoot them with guns (if you're boring), or you can fire the "oh♥♥♥♥♥♥quot; missile launcher that splits into 8 and zooms off towards whatever its locked onto, or the F.O.W.s (or "♥♥♥♥ Off Weapons") you get for freeing central commands in regions, or plant an explosive (did I mention infinite plantable explosives?) on an unsuspecting guard then tethering him to the thing you want to go bye-bye, or....
You get the point.
I also didn't really have the problem that everyone else does with the loading times. This is probably because of the SSD, but the longest loading time I had was 30 seconds. This may be a long time, but when the vast majority of the loading times are around 10 seconds, its entirely livable with - besides, the loading screens only happen when you die (so no break in the action that wasn't your fault), after cutscenes (no real break in the action) or between attempts of challenges - I found that far more livable with than games that have to load something after what seems like every single room.
I will admit, there are faults with the game. The aforesaid lack of any urgency with the plot does occasionally come back to bug me, and there are occasional framerate stutters (though as I said they were more from me not paying attention and leaving my laptop on for days). There is practically no point to the vehicle challenges, unless you're using it to spawn like 5 dump trucks to attatch sticky bombs to and then tether together. The wingsuit (while absolutely amazing, and probably one of the main reasons I will still be playing it for a long time) is very easy to ♥♥♥♥ up if you're trying to be cool and skim the ground, or even just the top of the trees (there is almost no visual distinction between tops of trees you can glide through and ones you can't).
And then there is the big problem.
In this age of "Always on" consoles, it was but a short step to "Always online". I may have a better internet connection than most, as I have only wound up getting dropped from the servers (which you are forced to enter upon starting the game and cannot stay out of) maybe 5 times so far, but each time it did have reconnection times of up to 2 minutes. I don't really mind about the ranking scores taking up part of the screen, as it does make me more competitive, but this is the kind of game that really needs to be either 100% singleplayer or have a mode that is 100% multiplayer - unless you can see the feats being performed, there isn't much point to telling us it has happened.
One final, and incredibly minor, complaint. There are challenges that are possible to exploit to get really high scores on, without actually doing the challenge possibly. Case in point - a challenger on a course I was doing got a score of 600,000 or thereabouts. On this wingsuit course, on each track, there was a maximum of about 18 rings with a variance of about 2, and the score for 5 starring that challenge was around 60,000. This means the guy must have just flown around in circles for nearly an hour. This is more of a complaint to the developers, but that sort of thing is incredibly irritating when youve spent a while trying to get perfect on every ring to find out you could have been flying in circles the whole time. So, Developers, please make it so that that sort of thing is at least harder to do.
But yes. Overall, I reccomend the game; its explosions and ways of causing carnage are glorious, and the wingsuit is one of the most fun things I have ever done in a game (particularly when you get it right and are just soaring through the are for tens of minutes at a time).

Finally a game that justifies the Alien series, it really manages to capture the horror of being hunted by something you can't fight. To keep this review short:
The good:
-The game is styled to the way they saw the future when making the first Alien movie, which means computers are massive and nothing really feels modern, even though it takes place in space
-The alien is unpredictable, the AI of the Xeno is fantastic besides some minor things. Like one time it ran past me while i was in the middle of his path, now don't think you can just run around, because there isn't much you can do when he sees you.
-Ammo is hard to get, there are guns which can only kill people and the androids, not aliens. Each shot has to be justified as you can't allow to waste a lot of ammo
-You're hunted, this game does this better than anything I've ever played. Hiding in a closet while hearing humans being brutally murdered one by one. You will die a lot in this game, but it always feels like it was your mistake

The bad:

I really wanted to like this game.  I have an unhealthy love for building spaceships that blow each other up.  The conceit, that the end boss of each level is your previous ship, is an awesome idea.
Ultimately, though, I can't recommend it.
First and foremost, you're continually fighting with the camera to see anything.  The game automatically zooms in and out with the range to what it thinks is your target.  Missions regularly zoom way out and away from the ship to show you new ships entering the mission, while sometimes also blinding you with a giant white "warp drive" flash- without pausing the game or restoring the camera to where it was when done.
Secondly, the missions aren't very fun.  They're constantly filled with very tightly-timed insta-fail conditions.  Get used to restarting because something you were escorting got blown up or something you were chasing escaped.  Combine this with the hostile camera and fidgity controls, and expect a lot of frustration.  I assume this mission design is an attempt to help mix up the combat, which is somewhat limiting because the AI mostly seems to be limited to doing jousting-style weapon passes at you, but it's no fun at all.
It also sometimes feels like completing mission objectives too promptly can render later mission objectives much harder by causing enemies to spawn near something you're defending sooner and closer.  Finding the sweet spot between instant failure and failing the next objective because I succeeded too quickly isn't particularly fun- some events seem like they ought to occur at fixed times and distances instead of relative to the player's progress and position.
Controls aren't great.  Imagine steering a car with a keyboard where you can only turn the wheel as hard left or right as possible with nothing in between.  Now imagine you're doing this while trying to shoot at targets under a tight time limit using a gun bolted to the front of your vehicle.  Also, although a tractor beam mitigates this, you're trying to fly around and pick up items on the ground.  All while also being under the constraints of the first two complaints: you're fighting the camera and racing instant-fail mission conditions.
Another control issue is that the game also emphasizes using "manual control" to boost and repair components, but does a very bad job of making this manageable for all but the smallest ships, given that you've got the number keys and a relatively short scrollable list on the right side of the screen to select what you want to boost but a lot more than ten components and very little free time with which to micromanage.  I see what they're trying to do, but a more classic guns/engines/shields/repair ship-wide boost probably would have been far more manageable.  At a minimum, though, it needs better ways to display and select the components you can be boosting.
The ship design itself is OK, although the game does a very poor job of explaining the mechanics.  What's that green +125% aura parts get and under what circumstances do you get it?  How is damage distributed when your ship gets shot?  What's stability?  Is there any reason not to just stack all of your parts that aren't armor on a block safely in the middle of your ship and then build a framework of armor around it?  How can I tell if a weapon has any sort of firing arc, and how big that arc is?  I've got figured out partial answers to most of these, but the game doesn't tell you much about the core bit of the game: ship building.
The final fight mechanic is a bit undermined by bad controls and limited AI, but I still appreciate it because it forces you to design against two constraints- the requirements of the mission and the ship you last designed.  This helps encourage you to avoid settling into a single design you use over and over a bit.
Overall, this feels fix-able, but at the moment it's just not enjoyable.  The camera, the controls, and the mission design all serve to undermine the core awesomeness of building and fighting with spaceships and against your own designs.
I'm sad to be not recommending this game, because the concept is great, the genre is one I love, it's not terrible and irreparably flawed by any means, and the developer seems interested in soliciting feedback and making the game a better game.  In its current state, however, I just can't recommend it.

This game has some good mechanics. I really enjoy the ability to create your own spacecraft and load it out with your own weapons.
But it got old very quickly.
If you’re not aware, the main principle of this game is to build a ship and control it though a mission, at the end of the mission you fight your own ship from the previous mission, only controlled by AI. Once you beat the mission, you lose your ship and the cycle begins anew for the next mission.
This is the premise that caught my attention, I love ship building games, and the ship construction part of Defect is good fun.
It seemed like a neat and novel idea to fight your own ship designs.
The campaign is hard.
I found myself failing the missions (very early game), over and over. I would try again with a different strategy only to have the same thing happen and to have to watch the same cut-scene repeatedly before once again ending in failure. It began to grind on me. Out of the 6 or 7 missions available, I was completely unable to finish any of them. I would try again and again and again, trying out different strategies and ship designs. It’s very frustrating, and makes it glaringly apparent how repetitive the game is.
When I finally managed to complete one of the missions available, my ship was taken away I was presented with another two missions. The cycle started anew.
“Unprecedented freedom of creation - Create the most powerful ship in the galaxy piece by piece, with more than 180 components available and many more to come.”
Even if you try and unlock new ship parts by going back over previously completely levels, the same thing happens. You complete a mission you have already completed, and bam, ships gone, start over. As someone who likes building ships, the combination of repeated failures and completing old missions meant I was building ship after ship after ship, and boy did it get stale fast. Pieces unlock chronically slowly, meaning you’re using the same handful of pieces for the majority of missions.
“Exploit your designs - Create the perfect design to complete the mission, but remember to build in a weakness you can exploit later when your crew inevitably turns against you.”
The loss of your ship after every mission doesn’t add anything to the game, it’s just a gimmick. You can load up exactly the same ship design for the next mission. Considering how the game requires you to switch up your strategy so often, you would likely never be able to use the same ship twice anyway. I never found fighting my own ship designs difficult, the AI just drives straight towards your guns blazing at the end of each mission. The idea that you can build a ship to complete a mission, defeat the previous ship you built and still have room to adjust your design to make it easier for yourself next time is utterly laughable. I found I didn't have enough components or power early on to have the luxury of choice in the way I designed my ship.
"Epic scale - Unlimited combinations available from tiny fighters up to battle stations the size of a small moon."
I had so much trouble I actually went ahead and watched a video on shipyard construction made by the developer. It showed him making a goliath ship with masses of power available, which is what I wanted from this game, but to me, it would take another 10-30 hours of gameplay just to get to that stage.
Despite all that, this game has a lot of potential. If parts unlocked much faster, you would have more choice in your ship designs and that, hopefully, would make things easier, more diverse and theoretically make it easier to make progress and have fun. At the moment though, for me, it's an exercise in futility.

The single-player only game features a branching campaign of repetitive missions where you must design a ship to defeat a series of enemies followed by the last ship you designed. Components for the energy core, crew, hull, engine, wings, weapons, and other accessories can be freely attached, scaled, or rotated in 2-D. Controlling the ship is performed using the WASD keys. While the crew automatically fires weapons, camera control is very inconsistent and it is difficult to aim precisely. You can take direct control of a component to repair it or improve the stats, but this usually leaves the ship vulnerable in other aspects. Scrap dropped by defeated vessels can be used to repair. AI ships is good enough to act as capable adversaries. Although Defect has a very novel concept, monotonous mission design and a cumbersome control scheme reduce enjoyment.

I took a 6 months hiatus from the game and I decided to try the game once again.
The storyline proves the main strength in the game.  You start out an unnamed hero wearing rags with no reputation.  As you progress through out the quest, your hero gets better gear and you start to build up a reputation.  The progression that you make out in the game does affect the world.    If you save a village, you can see the villagers returning back to their homes.  NPCs around town will start to talk about the deeds that you have done.  Your deeds do build up to an epic quest that involves saving Nirn.  The only downside is once you have finished the quest, the other quest that you do does not feel grand in nature.
Inventory management still provides to an issue at the beginning.  You have limited space and you find yourself with a lot of items to carry.  I find that inventory management does become easier once you have enough in-game money to buy a larger back pack.  I recommend not get into crafting until you are able to upgrade your back pack first.
When I initially played the game, the loot drops were awful.  I either get nothing or just few coins.  The loot drops have improved where I get weapons or clothes from the monsters that I killed.
I originally did not recommend this game, but I can see that developers are working to improve on game play.  There are some flaws as listed in my original review, but I now like this game enough to recommend it.

Playing the first six hours into the Elder Scrolls Online: Tamriel Unlimited, I was immersed in the deep Elder Scrolls lore that was infused into this game.  It was breath-taking to travel across the scenic lands of Tamriel.  As I do more and more quests in the game, flaws in the online experience becomes apparent in this game.
The rich storylines and quests found in the Elder Scrolls series like Skyrim is a strength and weakness in this game.  It is weakness because the quests are designed with the solo player in mind.  While you see many players in the city, none of them are interacting with each other.  If I wanted to play a solo experience, I would have played Skyrim.
There is an illusion that you can go anywhere and do whatever quest you like.  This is not true.  Each area has a specific level that a player can fight the mobs in.  The game leads you along and disguised the linear destination with a dozen of quests to take.
One of the things I liked about Skyrim or Oblivion is you can learn any skills you like.  If you want to be a melee fighter that shoots out lightning, it can be done.  ESO is more restrictive in the skills you can use.
There is a lot of focus on the solo quests, but there are no timed events held in the game.  There is no incentive for players to gather together to work towards a common goal.  Unless you know friends outside the game, gathering a group together to go into a dungeon is non-existence.
There is no viable system in place to sell items to other players in the game.  You cannot setup your own stand and sell your wares.  If you are not part of a guild, you are locked out of selling your goods.
I spend a good time in the game managing my inventory.  If you decide to take a craft in the game, your inventory space runs out fast.  You can buy more inventory space in-game, but it cost a lot of gold.  My routine in the game is to finish a quest, manage inventory, do a quest and repeat.
I feel that ESO is work-in-progress game.  The developers have the cake, but not the icing that makes a good polished game.
I am going to stop playing ESO for awhile to see how the game develops.

The game has received a lot of bad reviews talking about how it's a WoW clone and it's really buggy, (most of these reviewers played before the Tamriel Unlimited update went live) but I don't think it's true.
Bear in mind, I haven't got to endgame yet so I won't talk about it until I have, if I ever do.
First of all, it's not buggy, I haven't played too much (around 30-40 hours at the time) and haven't found any bugs (unlike in Skyrim or any Bethesda game).
Now, about it being a WoW clone, I don't think it's true (and I do play WoW quite frequently), and it feels way more similar to Everquest 2, mainly because it's very open (at least while leveling). When leveling up, you can walk in a direction and you'll probably find quests there, but it's also really good that it's almost impossible to get lost; in EQ2 I played through the tutorial and everything is cool, but then they take me to the city (Qeynos I think) and you're on your own, so I think "well, I guess I can just start picking up quests outside the city", and while it's true, I always ended up taking quests that were 5 levels higher than me, which resulted in awful grinding because I didn't know where to go. In ESO, by the time you get to the higher level quests, you'll be ready to do it, because they put the harder quests far from the starting zones.
Also, the quests can feel sometimes like they are the classic "kill X until Y drops" or "go to X, take Y and come back to me", because they are (just like in Skyrim or any other game) but they know how to hide it, and also you will sometimes get a choice and sometimes it is either the evil way or the good way, but sometimes it's not; the last one I did was about getting a crown for a noble woman and at the end, a ghost that has been helping you, tells you to release him by making the princess touch a cursed crown instead of the real crown, so basically you can give her the real crown or the cursed crown.
Combat is kinda action based and kinda targeted, if you've played DC Universe Online, it's pretty much the same without combos, (but way more customizable thanks to the skills being based on your guilds, weapons, class and so on) if you haven't played it, you don't have an auto attack button like in all tab targeting games, but your regular attack is triggered by the mouse button, you can block and dodge, and you can charge your attack, but you also have the hotkey skills.
Crafting is also a pretty big part of the game and it's actually pretty ok. I like it but it's not really innovative in any way. You get styles that change the look of the items, but not their stats (so you won't see everyone walking around in the same armor just because it's the most powerful one), and to change their stats you can:
1) increase the ingots (or leather or whatever) that will go into the creation of the item, increasing it's level.
2) use better materials, which will increase it's level even more, and change the look a little bit, but keep the same style.
3) improve the item's quality using rare items, but the upgrade's success is based on how many of this items you use, and if you fail, the item will be destroyed. But this is also the only way to improve items without increasing it's level, which is useful because you can't equip items that outlevel you.
And resource gathering isn't bad because there aren't too many mineral deposits, but you can destroy items you have to create materials.
I've only been in one dungeon and it was really fun, and it's also a bit more social due to the fact that there's no group finder so you actually have to form a group, I don't really have much more to say.
Imperial City PvP is also really big but I haven't played much of it, and if you're into PvP it could be really fun. It also doesn't feel forced into the experience, so if you like PvE you don't actually need to play it.
Also, the graphics were criticized because they're stylized or "cartoony" but I really like them and you can play on potato PCs without any problem, I could run it in a non gaming netbook as long as I kept the graphics low.
It's also really good that there's no monthly sub so you never feel like you need to play and you can pick it up whenever you want.
All that being said, the game has it's flaws, but they don't ruin the experience (for me, at least), just hold it back.
First of all is the community, specially in Daggerfall's (Daggerfall Covenant's starting zone) General Chat, it's basically Barrens' Chat. Mostly filled with ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s.  And then there's the people you'll find during your leveling experience, that will probably never respond to you and if you invite them to a group, they'll reject even though (s)he knows you're doing the same quest. But, of course, you'll also find some really cool people.
The mega server is awful, mostly because there are no "special ruleset" servers, so no world PvP and it's also a shame for roleplayers because the only way you'll find roleplay is in a roleplay guild. And it also doesn't serve it's purpose of making zones feel more alive and having friends play with you because it has some really weird phasing thing going on.
There are only 4 classes, and even though they're kind of customizable, having more would be great.
Also, for the first 16 levels, your gear will look the same way except for the racial styles.
There are not too many dyes and most of the easy ones to get aren't really good.
One of the most important ones is that you do get that feel of "I'm the One, but I still see 10 "the Ones" walking around".
And the loading screens, I don't think they are that bad for everyone, but if you have a low end PC, you will have some really long loading screens.
TL;DR (kind of).
After all, I think it's a great game but don't go expecting Elder Scrolls 6, which was most people's mistake, but it's also not an ES themed WoW clone, it actually feels way more open and closer to the ES experience. Also, a little advice, don't rush to endgame, just like in any ES game, you don't rush through it, and now that there's no sub, there's no excuse to rush it.
I'll probably update this review once I get to endgame, and I'll also check out the RPing community and overall experience.

While it comes from the likes of the RPGmaker and classic Ragnarok Online, Eternal Senia is a game that believes in one principle, and that is impact through simplicity and emotions. This is a gaming experience that wouldn't work as well if its mechanics or story were any more complicated or difficult to go through.
For a free game, it reminds me of some amazing things that can happen with indie RPGs from eastern developers, like in the case of Ib. Though a short and simple RPG, Eternal Senia invokes emotions and investment pretty easily, all with said simplicity. The art and music do well in orchestrating the mood, though some assets may be repetitive if one cannot bear that with patience.
It's also an easy game too, with a progression system of a similar slant. Again, this is a compliment rather than a slight against it; the experience and pacing would be terrible if it wasn't easy or relaxing.
Do yourself a favor, and don't spoil yourself of anything before playing this game. Not its heartfelt story, nor its childlike discovery. Just step towards eternity.

Despite releasing in a absolutely horrid state, Total War Rome 2 is now a good game.  There are dozens of factions to choose from which offer unique playstyles.  The graphics are very good, and with a little help from the Workshop they are great.  The gamemap is very big which gives good replay value.  The real time battles are a lot of fun with thousands of units engaged at any given time.
My biggest complaint is with the Campaign AI.  It gets very predicable past the early stages.  It doesn't feel like you are one nation among many, but more like the world revolves around you.  I also feel the game doesn't bring enough originality compared to previous Total War games.  There are a lot of small features (prisoners, politics, and diplomatic reputation to name a few) that are not fully fleshed out and feel gamey.  I think veterans of Total War will notice these flaws more than newcomers.
So if you have been considering giving the Total War series a try Rome 2 is a great place to start.  If you are a veteran of the series I will say that the game has been in a good state since roughly Patch 8 (current version is Patch 13).

First, let me say something:
I play this on a relatively new laptop, with a nVidia Geforce 980 or something, 8 gigs of ram, 500GB SSD and a fairly crappy i5. The only time I got any significant framerate loss was either using one of the F.O.W.s and causing a chain reaction or if id left my laptop on for more than a day or two (cause I got s**t to do).
TL;DR: Get the game. It is Just Cause 2 with all sorts of sprinkles, and its always fun to grapple a jet into a carrier plane, jump off and watch the dance of explodey goodness. The entire game can be summed up in one line by one of the characters:
"You need a more positive outlook on life son! You've got an infinite parachute for Pete's sake."
This game, as Yahtzee (ZeroPunctuation) puts it, is something that AAA gaming should do more often, because it is one of the few things thy're good at anymore.
This game is exclusively about running around blowing stuff up. Don't let the opening cutscene fool you into thinking it has any sort of rigidly defined storyline. I did the first 3 missions then went and messed around freeing settlements and irritating the local police by hurling myself headlong into them. The beauty if there are so many ways to blow stuff up - you can shoot them with guns (if you're boring), or you can fire the "oh♥♥♥♥♥♥quot; missile launcher that splits into 8 and zooms off towards whatever its locked onto, or the F.O.W.s (or "♥♥♥♥ Off Weapons") you get for freeing central commands in regions, or plant an explosive (did I mention infinite plantable explosives?) on an unsuspecting guard then tethering him to the thing you want to go bye-bye, or....
You get the point.
I also didn't really have the problem that everyone else does with the loading times. This is probably because of the SSD, but the longest loading time I had was 30 seconds. This may be a long time, but when the vast majority of the loading times are around 10 seconds, its entirely livable with - besides, the loading screens only happen when you die (so no break in the action that wasn't your fault), after cutscenes (no real break in the action) or between attempts of challenges - I found that far more livable with than games that have to load something after what seems like every single room.
I will admit, there are faults with the game. The aforesaid lack of any urgency with the plot does occasionally come back to bug me, and there are occasional framerate stutters (though as I said they were more from me not paying attention and leaving my laptop on for days). There is practically no point to the vehicle challenges, unless you're using it to spawn like 5 dump trucks to attatch sticky bombs to and then tether together. The wingsuit (while absolutely amazing, and probably one of the main reasons I will still be playing it for a long time) is very easy to ♥♥♥♥ up if you're trying to be cool and skim the ground, or even just the top of the trees (there is almost no visual distinction between tops of trees you can glide through and ones you can't).
And then there is the big problem.
In this age of "Always on" consoles, it was but a short step to "Always online". I may have a better internet connection than most, as I have only wound up getting dropped from the servers (which you are forced to enter upon starting the game and cannot stay out of) maybe 5 times so far, but each time it did have reconnection times of up to 2 minutes. I don't really mind about the ranking scores taking up part of the screen, as it does make me more competitive, but this is the kind of game that really needs to be either 100% singleplayer or have a mode that is 100% multiplayer - unless you can see the feats being performed, there isn't much point to telling us it has happened.
One final, and incredibly minor, complaint. There are challenges that are possible to exploit to get really high scores on, without actually doing the challenge possibly. Case in point - a challenger on a course I was doing got a score of 600,000 or thereabouts. On this wingsuit course, on each track, there was a maximum of about 18 rings with a variance of about 2, and the score for 5 starring that challenge was around 60,000. This means the guy must have just flown around in circles for nearly an hour. This is more of a complaint to the developers, but that sort of thing is incredibly irritating when youve spent a while trying to get perfect on every ring to find out you could have been flying in circles the whole time. So, Developers, please make it so that that sort of thing is at least harder to do.
But yes. Overall, I reccomend the game; its explosions and ways of causing carnage are glorious, and the wingsuit is one of the most fun things I have ever done in a game (particularly when you get it right and are just soaring through the are for tens of minutes at a time).

Bit of a parody on the whole "'Murrica the Eagleland!" trope, but something of an affectionate one.  This game is F. U. N.  That's right, fun!  No pretentious story, no attempts to be art, no moving emotional cinematics here.  This is just pure, bloody-minded (and pretty bloody!) fun!
You play as a number of "Bros", each one based on various movie characters, most of which come from the action movie genre.  The real trick of the game is that each Bro is a Glass Cannon of sorts.  You can rip and shred and shoot and explode your way through swarms of enemies... and then die in one hit when some low-level mook gets in a lucky shot.  You earn lives by finding more Bros in cages, each one tied up with a bag on their head.  You rescue them with a mere touch, but then the game's most tricky mechanic kicks in.  When you rescue a Bro or die with lives in reserve, the game gives you a random Bro to play with.  There is no way to know who you're going to get (like a box of deadly, angry chocolates), and with each rescue you get closer to unlocking more Bros to use.  Their abilities and weapons vary widely (though all of them can jump and have a melee attack), so you have to adapt your tactics according to who you're playing.  For example, you might be fighting a boss with a Bro who's just really good at tearing through the boss' health bar.  Then you slip up and die.  And that's when you find out your respawn (who might be your last life!) is armed with a whip and a gun with six shots.
It's about then that you start praying to whatever gods you might believe can save your sorry behind.
And you know what?  I wouldn't change it for the world!  Sure, it sucks to get a Bro I don't like or can't use well, or that's completely unsuited to the situation at hand!  But it's part of the challenge, and it never really feels like the game is cheating me out of a great experience.  Heck, it's still in early access, and I reset all my unlocks and all the levels just so I could play it all over again!  And the Aliens expansion has only added to the fun!  The devs could stop here and let Steam workshop take over, and it'd still be a damn good game!  I hope they don't, of course, because I want more!  But they'd have to work really hard to screw this game up.  With near-fully destructable environments, gameplay elements that encourage creative problem solving (you can skip an entire level by *riding a dead pig!!*), and new levels and enemies that constantly challenge your ability to assess the situation and blaze through it, you'd have to be a particular kind of person to not have fun with this game!
Oh... and did I mention... multiplayer?
I'll be buying this very soon for a few friends.  It's worth the expense, and I know they'll love it.  And if they don't, hey!  Free game!
If any of the devs are reading this, please, keep making new stuff!  I love this game and I'm excited to see what crazy nonsense you come up with next!
