This is a tale of brutal revenge, as you cut a bloody swath through your enemies enroute to reclaim family and throne. Or maybe this is a tale of someone looking to right those same wrongs not through violence, but by correcting injustices through other passive or less aggressive means. Perhaps it's a mixture of both, where you listen to the voice of someone you're close to and use that as a guiding point on who gets shanked and who gets to live another day. Dishonored 2 is a game that can weave many different tales depending on the mood of the player.
Look, it's no secret that Dishonored 2 has had a rocky PC launch. Technical issues abound for many, leaving those afflicted with framerate issues on one end of the spectrum, and rampant crashes on the less fortunate end. Within those confines, people are also experiencing sound bugs, glitches, graphical infidelity and a slew of other issues. On the outside and just glancing at the forum, most users would be like -
And it is, for many. There are some serious problems in the underbelly of Dishonored 2's game engine and to ignore them or pretend they don't exist is a disservice to both the gaming and development community. Accountability is the great redeemer, and for their part, Arkane Studios seems to be aware and are working on addressing the issues that some gamers are having. We can argue the finer points of releasing games with issues in the first place, but those type of discussions can be found quite easily on the steam forums. I hope soon that most of the major issues some users are having gets resolved, so that other Dishonored fans can dive into this incredible game.
The art and graphical style of the Dishonored series has always appealed to me, and it's no different here; textures are sharper (bugs aside), the abundance of detail seemingly present in almost every corner of every map is astounding, and the way it all blends with the art style of the game world is really impressive. There's so much going on within the environment of the game all at once that it's hard for me to find something to ♥♥♥♥♥ about without sounding like pretentious nitpicking. They really nailed atmosphere here, crafting a unique world for gamers to kick back and get absorbed into.
Same goes for sound. The music really fits the mood and overall tone of the game, and the random songs sung by NPC's are, at their worst mildly funny, and at best, quite beautiful. The ambient sounds serve to ramp up tension and a feeling of helplessness within the kingdom, whether it be over zealous overseers, or ever increasing bloodfly populations terrorizing the populace. The magic of sound direction works best when it's allowed to fade in and out of the background, never overstaying its welcome, but never underperforming either. It's a shame that sometimes sound glitches can cut the immersion, but overall, really solid sound design.
And gameplay is obviously no slouch. The first Dishonored game gave us a sort of magical assassin's toolbox of naughty toys, and this game gives us two, in the form of either Corvo or Emily. Since two is almost always better than one, this just means more powers and options for playing through the story. Combat is visceral, stealth kills are satisfying, powers are fun. It's more of Dishonored with new stuff and it's damn fun.
So ... what then? The game is amazing and it pisses me off that people are having trouble playing it, because I feel like I'm one of the few who are able to truly appreciate the game for all its fantastic qualities. I recommend it solely on my experiences; it's been my favorite game of 2016 up to this point, and I'm looking forward to playing through it again. If you're looking to buy, I'd maybe advise waiting until another patch if the steam forums put the fear into you, but my issues have been minimal on an i5-2500k/GTX 1060/16 GB RAM on a standard HD.

This game is absolutely wonderful. I don't think I have words to describe how happy it makes me, but I will try to do so in this review.
This is a game in which you drive a truck. You pick up some cargo and then drive it to its destination. Sounds a bit boring? To some people it might be. But for people like me, this game scratches that itch that can only be scratched by, what I would call a "Zen game".
What I mean by this is that I sit and play ETS2 to just relax. In this game, I just have my truck, a long road and maybe even some nice music if I decided to turn on the internet radio. Or sometimes I just like to listen to the engine purring in the background and just let go of all my thoughts.
I'm not saying that this game can't get exciting. You can definitely have some of that too, if you try to transport some difficult, high value cargo. Or you take a delivery that you have to complete in only a few hours, so you have to rush a bit always watching for police cars and speed cameras so you don't pay a fine. Or maybe rushing towards a rest stop because you need to sleep. But in most cases, this is a very chill game and that's the way I like it.
The gameplay itself is what I would call "just right". I play on the keyboard and the simulation is challenging enough. You can tweak a lot of options to fine tune it to your taste though. This game can be adjusted to fit almost any playstyle which is great.
What's great is that you can also manage a company. Soon you will have a giant fleet of drivers getting you a lot of money. Buying new garages and trucks and then hiring new drivers is the best feeling ever. As is leveling yourself up with new skills. Skills allow you to take new types of cargo and increase rewards for completing deliveries. You can also train your drivers with those same skill so they can bring in more money into your company.
The customization is absolutely amazing. You have a lot of trucks to chose from and then you can pick parts to make the truck run better. With paintjobs and other cosmetic parts like wheel rims, lights, mirrors and so on you can customize the look of your truck to your own liking.
And here is a nice little bonus to the gameplay aspect. When is the last time you had meaningful achievements in a game? ETS2 is a game that has those. While the game doesn't have a story or real missions, you can look at achievements if you want a challenge.
The graphics are very nice. Not the best, but they are great considering that this in an indie game. You will have plenty of pretty things to look at and at some points the game can look gorgeous. Sunrises and sunsets are my most favorite times to drive around.
Sound and music is great and on point. I already mentioned that the engine sound is my most favorite, but the environment also sounds great. It's really immersive to drive during a rainstorm, listening to rain drops tap all around you with occasional flashes of thunder. The music that plays in the menus is a bit generic, but you won't hear it when you have the internet radio on. You can also have the game play your locally stored music as well.
And my biggest reason for writing this review is this games developer. SCS Software. I've been following the development of ETS2 for many years and I was super excited for it. I don't usually follow developments of games, but I was excited for this one because I wanted a good trucking sim ever since the amazing 18 Wheels of Steel series which was also made by SCS and is how I got introduced into the whole genre. I think that 18 WoS: Across America was the first simulator I played in my life.
Anyway, ETS2 finally released and I bought the game in retail. Later, I voted for it to be released on Steam through the Greenlight program. The game that shipped almost 4 years ago was the game I was hoping it would be. And much more. I was blown away by it. But then something amazing happened. Something I didn't even dare dream would happen.
SCS continued to update the game. At the time of writing this review, the game has seen almost 30 major updates over these past 4 years. And all these updates were completely free. New trucks, major improvements to the lightning engine that made the game look stunning, better looking world, new awesome gameplay improvements, tons of bugs fixes and so much more. All this and so much more was added to this game for free by these wonderful devs.
And they continue to expand this game. With new updates and DLCs that continue to grow Europe with new places to visit. The work that SCS has done on these map expanding DLCs is amazing and I’m seriously excited for each new one that gets released.
In conclusion, I only have positive things to say about ETS2 and I can wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone who has an even remote interest in trying a trucking simulator. There is a demo available on Steam, but I’m not sure if its updated so take care when judging the game from the demo if you decide to try it.

Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare is at best a mediocre FPS game in an already crowded closet of Michael Bay-esque  action shooters. I have been a long-time fan of the Franchise, but the two most recent installments, Ghosts and Advanced Warfare, have only perpetuated the clichéd joke that Activsion is recycling ideas in every installment since COD4.  While the Sledgehammer Games has implemented a new movement system in the game to encourage faster-paced game play and fierce engagements,  the upgrades did not translate well onto the PC port of the game. We are left with sometimes glitchy, unbalanced, and lackluster gameplay.
The PC version of COD:AW is a port. The actual game was originally developed for the XBOX ONE and PS4 and then adapted to run on a PC, XBOX360, and PS3. The single player campaign is relatively unaffected by these changes. The textures, animations,  and background effects all look detailed and vivid. While these are not the best graphics in gaming I have seen, they are certainly the best in the franchise to date. However, the multi-player graphics are dramatically different on the PC compared to the singleplayer campaign. Textures appear blurry, fine details are unrecognizable, and some maps cause frame-rate issues. I am running the game with current (as of 2014) hardware, and have tried downloading patches from Steam and graphics updates from Nvidia to fix the issue.
Graphics are not the only issue on the PC port. Since this game was made for the console, most guns will not fire the way they were intended. The clearest example of this is the an laser rifle that projects a constant beam of energy. A player can effortlessly move their mouse  to quickly dispatch foes even without aiming down sights. It is much harder to do this with a controller on a console. Recoil is also pretty much non-existent on most assault rifles and sub machines  on the PC port. Weapons aside, the new mechanic which allows players to quickly dodge, dash and straddle can be erratic at times when attempting to predict when a player will land. Player animations seem jagged and abrupt sometime leading to frustration when trying to gun-down a fast moving enemy.
The single player campaign was almost negligible  had it of not been for Kevin Spacey's voice acting. Spacey's performance in the game was very strong and perfectly personifies a morally ambiguous corporate CEO that players almost sympathize with. All the other characters, including the protagonist, are bland, lifeless, and forgettable. The single player follows the "go to A, then B" objective system, with certain missions almost directly reminiscing older Call of Duty single player moments.  There were a few non linear levels. For example, in one mission the player must use a few of stealthy takedowns to eliminate soldiers in a large environment without getting caught. Also, this game STILL uses quick-time events and slow-motion sequences, which feel very clichéd and overused by this franchise at this point.
My other major complaint with this game is that it seemed to crash 5-8 times a week. I again tried to upgrade my graphics card, but the problem still persisted.  After checking in with the online community, this is just an inherit problem with the port. At other times, I cannot seem to connect to the game's server's for online play. I have tried disabling my firewall and opening ports on my router and PC, but the occasional problem persists. There are hackers who use aim-bot and map hacks, but no more than the amount of hackers in Battlefield 4 or Titanfall.
All in all, if you want the proper COD:AW experience, buy the PS4 or XBOX ONE version. The PC port will leave you frustrated with glitches, hackers, and unbalanced gameplay. The new movement scheme is fun for awhile, but quickly feels old and some annoying.  The single-player campaign is only seven hours long and does not have much replay value unless you are a die-hard Kevin Spacey fan. PC Gamers can only hope for the almost non-existent day when Activsion announces a dedicated PC COD game.

First things first, The Elder Scrolls Online is truely a fun game to play with an increadible amount of amazing content in the form of quests, interactions and locations. At certain times, this game can give you a sense of wonder when looking at a gigantic metroplis of a city, and at other it can make you cry with a very sad story line. That said, the game has a completely different feeling to it than any Elder Scrolls game before it, which can potentially ruin the experience of many fans.
Lets just get this out of the way with: The Elder Scrolls Online feels more like World of Warcraft than like Skyrim or Oblivion. While there are many great quests in the game, there is an equal amount of "go here, kill these guys, collect a bunch of stuff of their corpses, wait for them to respawn, repeat" types of quests. Whearas in Skyrim or Oblivion, each quest felt like it was designed for hours if not days, quite a few quests in Online are, well, very forgettable to say the least.
The combat also feels much more like other MMORPGs than like other TES games. When fighting an enemy, that enemy is highlighted in bold red, all attacks hit, and you have a bunch of random attacks or magical boosts that you activate using number keys. This is what dissapointed me the most. In Skyrim or Oblivion, each enemy encounter felt personal, engaging, and clearing an entire fort of bandits felt like an epic achievement. In Online, enemies just respawn a minute or so after you kill them, and there is barely a memorbale fight. The combat is very much MMORPG, and not enough TES, in my opinion.
What makes the game great though is its beautiful and diverse locations, as well as the increadible amount of content. You have to chose one starter faction to play though. Each faction has 6 or so regions to go through. I'm 180+ hours into the game and I have only finished playing one faction. And I'm not even that slow. That means that if you take it easy and dont rush the game, playing every area without any replay or different character can give you 500+ hours of gameplay. That is simply uncanny in many modern day games. The quests themselves are also pretty damn fun. Each region has a specific story which the Vestige (The main character, the player) has to go through. In one region I had to attempt to save a Werewolf-infested town (Which turned into pretty much all-out human vs werewolf war) and in another I had to investigate politcal disturbanses and strange goings-on in a certain region (Spoilers: Vampires were involved).
To be honest, I haven't played much on the giant multiplayer map of Cyrodiil. If you really want to play it properly you need to be a higher level. Overall, from what I've seen, it is a really cool concept and is a lot of fun when a lot of players are on, but when alone the whole country seems a bit empty and lifeless.
Let me just finish up here. It is a great game with waaaaaay too many microtransactions and a not-too-perfect combat system, but that is otherwise perfectally playable. I even temporaraly played it on my mac for a week or two (as my PC broke and I had to build a new one), on which it worked pretty well for a 80+ GB game. Overall, it seems The Elder Scrolls Online cant figure out if it wants to be TES but then online, or a TES-themed World of Warcraft. Basically, is it another MMORPG or is it the next TES. It is both, but it does neither perfectly.
Thanks for taking the time to read this, enjoy the game if you buy it.

Does the highly anticipated sequel of one of the best loved and niche games of the genration lives up to it's expectations? Well, that does in a way depends on what your expectations were. Dark Souls was well known for being tough, unforgiving yet extremely rewarding game. And while DS2 should be reviewed as a separate game, comparisons with Dark Souls cannot/should not be avoided as per my opinion, for such is the fate of any sequel (a fair trade off I would say for re-using the old IP).
The best part of Dark Souls for me was not that it was tough. It was tough, yes, but the combat system made it extremely rewarding. In fact, the difficulty was never the final goal, more like the game had to have certain difficulty to make sure you pay attention and learn rules the world plays by. The intricate and lovingly crafted combat challenges would have been lost if it was allowed to just R1 spam one's way to the finish line, but if you master it, you shall have the evental pleasure of leaving the once tough foes in your wake of mayhem and destruction. With Dark Souls 2, the basic priniciple remains same. Yes, the combat is challenging, and yes it needs to be mastered and understood well to make progress.
However, I could not help notice, and you are welcome to suspect my ineptitude in playing it, that the combat seemed a little off. Whether it is nerfed backstab, parry timings changed so that the only parries I was able to make looked more like lucky strikes rather than planned strategy (my DS1 parry percentage was almost close to 70%, here it was more like 10) or the guard break move which replaces the kick, but for some reason was not as consistent in execution as kick, I never really felt I have mastered the combat. I did finish the game, but didn't really get the end-game feeling of having progressed from being a noob to someone who has finally learned and mastered the rules of this game. In DS1, I still remembered the only death in my last two hours of playing was a bad jump in the catacombs. Giant skeletons, black knights etc were all dispatched with ease as I pushed on inexorably towards my final goal. But as mentioned before, in all probability, it could be just me, but this is my review after all.
The level design of the game lacks the interconnected loopbacks of it's predecessor. Don't expect the epic aha moment when you took the elevator from undead parish to the firelink shrine. THe game map is like a series of dead ends starting from the hub area.
Let me give you my take on the difficulty now, since that is what the the franchise is most well known for, unfortunately so in my opinion. In fact, there is a prominent structure in the hub world which keeps tabs on number of deaths world wide, like From Software is compelled to remind you in every step of the way, "you wanted difficult game right? Well, there you go!!"
The learning curve according to me is steeper. You have multiple foes who get aggroed and can inflict considerable damage, archers with unerring accuracy who keep chipping at your health bar, and to top it off, you start with only one estus flask (you upgrade it to maximum of 12 as you gather estus shards throughout the map), with a consumable known as lifegem to keep you alive till the next bonfire. The bosses are the usual mixed bag very easy, tough till you figure out and really tough. Then there is a re-hashed fight with 5,6 or was it 10 belfry gargoyles, yeah, while not the toughest, is definitely the most annoying.
Multiplayer remains insane fun. And yes, you can be invaded even when you are hollow, but you can summon only when you are human. Humanity is restored through human effigy, a rare (I managed to have about 60 on me when I finished the game) resource. Also, you can keep your humanity and souls on dying, provided you have a ring on which breaks on your death. But since the hub blacksmith is only a warp away from any bonfire, you can just repair it, and thus get to be human for a majority of your playthrough.
Finally despite pointing out the flaws and looking like I did not enjoy the game, it remains a soul game at heart. If you have enjoyed the previous iterations of this hallowed franchise, well, I guess you already have this game. Flaws not withstanding, this remains an extremely fun game, which will push you to your limits, and you will feel a better man (or just a better gamer) when you have finished the journey, before going out to punish yourself a second time, either NG+ or a new character. This gets my full recommendation.

I bought this game within a few days of its release. Yes it was very broken in most respects but it still functioned from day 1 in single player, multiplayer, Steam Workshop & game replays/saves which is more than can be said about a lot of other games that had way more money spent upon them and still don't work to this day (Battlefield 4 prime example).
Since its release there have been 13 big patches which have fixed and rebalanced the game. The main problem I have is that a lot of the DLC is just faction packs or the 'Blood & Gore pack' which were already built into the game and were clearly used to just get more money. I don't mind having the Ceasar in Gaul as DLC because it actually adds to the game with new campaign, units and abilites that were not there before.
The gameplay at the core is basically the same as most other Total War games with army formations, units that counter others, economy for the campaign map, city building etc. The differences being how they are all set up in this particular game. Cities are now grouped into provinces of 1-3 small towns and 1 walled city that acts as a sort of capital for the area, whoever came up with that did a great job as managing the economy is so much smoother and easier. Armies are built and maintained in the same way as before with agents being able to support them. Naval warfare can be a bit hit or miss but it can actually be played unlike when the game was first released.
The battles between your army and another have a clear distinction between single and multiplayer. This is to be expected but not to the degree it still is. The game AI is very predictable and usually ends up doing the same thing over and over with each battle, charging cavalry into pike/spear formations in a bad attempt to get at your ranged units for example. Plus I have noticed the AI will keep building armies of basic troops (1 general, 10 basic spears/swords, 2/3 light horse and the rest slingers is usually the template) so the only time you have a true challenge is when there are 2/3 of these armies attacking you at once or when a Civil War happens as the AI get high quality troops (only because they are pre made not recruited). The battles themselves though are very fun and using the cinematic camera during the heat of battle is one of my favourite things to do.
The community support helps out the game with peoples own designed units and maps. There are even a few total conversions which have made the game more historic, given bigger unit sizes or changed how the whole economy works. There are plenty of smaller things such as unit re-skins or stats changes.
Overall the game, now it has been patched, is highly recommended if you are a fan of the Total War games. If it is your first game of the series don't think it will be too much to handle as it set out in a very easy to understand way and the built in adviser does help out a lot.

This review is mostly for those who know and love the Total War Series.
I have played quite a few over the past years, and I was very excited about the new Rome installment...
...And it was a letdown. Mind you, it's not a bad game in the slightest, but it just doesn't add anything when you compare it to Medieval II or Shogun II. It's like I bought the same game with a new map and different unit names. Otherwise, it's just about identical.
So if that's what you're looking for, a copy of Shogun II, themed to ancient Mare Nostrum, then consider this review void. But if you're looking for an enhanced or next-gen Realtime/Turn Based Strategy game, this isn't it.
The AI hasn't been improved whatsoever, running around in circles occasionally, or just refusing to take the initiative and flank you. Furthermore, the Grand Campaign is hard to navigate, as allies and "client states" are terrible to work with, and completely untrustworthy. In effect, the diplomacy screen has become almost obsolete. You'll only ever be disappointed by the help your comrades provide you with, as they prefer hiding out in their holds to protect their own cities from rebellions.
And with good reason, since Rome II introduced a ridiculous system for Public Order, making it nigh impossible to keep your empire from falling apart when you reach a certain number of provinces, even in times of peace.
In short: Don't buy this, unless you are either looking for a Roman TW: Shogun II, or you haven't played any Total War Games yet, and would very much like to try one out. After all, it IS the newest and perhaps best installment, even though it did not care to flaunt it too much.

I am not a fan of horror genre, and i played Alien Isolation first of all because its an "alien game", rather then horror. It is definitly not a perfect game, there are some issues with temp (i hate backtracking) and narrative (some story twists are out of place or feel forced for sake of longevity), but i can say for sure, that all its faults are surplus compensated by its atmosphere and core gameplay around Alien. Former makes it an excellent "alien game", and latter makes its one of the best adventure games i ever played.
Unscripted Alien with complex yet intuitive and logical behavior creates a permanent suspense. You rarely see Creature itself, but tension is even more intense when it is not around, because you know that it is  actually HERE. Noise in walls is not just a scripted event to scare you, it is actaully produced by Alien, and you know that he will always react to your actions: he will hear you running, will notice your motion tracker sound, will react to machinery you activate, and he will come, thats for sure. He doesnt have any programmed routes, you never know where or when he will drop down from vent to check corridor and rooms, if he will simply pass that wall shelf you are currently hiding in, or decide to take a closer look, forcing you to hold breath. There are no patterns of survival here, you just need to think over and measure your every action, and adapt.

I don't know if the Ragnarok references in this game were intentional or mere coincidence (which I doubt) but the moment I saw High Priest Magaleta, I knew I'm gonna love this. It was basically the reason why I got addicted.
The game starts off really slow. It comes off as a generic RPG made with VX Ace. The story doesn't begin until the player has gone through the basic controls. Honestly, I was bored to death in the beginning but it didn't take long until the game picked up. There's more to the game than just playing it and I'd like to mention a few. First and foremost would be the nicely written story. It has a lot of emotions in it and it was constructed well to go with the game's mapping design, before you know it, you'd be sucked into the fantasy setting of the game, which is something that modern RPGs lack. The art style is worth complimenting as well as it is amazing. From the menu CG, to the character sprites, to the game objects. The characters have their distinct personalities that amplifies the fun. There's the ever-so-stubborn protagonist, Senia; the composed and caring "big sister" figure, Magaleta (best girl, by the way); the not-so-annoying fairy guide unlike other RPGs; and a few more.
I might've spoiled myself of the ending by reading other reviews but I tried not to read too much. From what I've seen, it looks like I'm going to love the game even more when I actually finish it!
Overall, the game is really fun and entertaining. On one hand, I'm really grateful that this game is free so that I can actually play it (because I'm poor), but on the other hand, I feel that the game is too good to be free. The developers definitely deserve to get profit off of making such a great game. I give it 10 gold stars.

So I play worms hotseat local multiplayer with my friends, and I bought this game on sale for £7.99 (or there abouts). This means I don't feel I can comment on the state of the multiplayer features or even the single player campaign. The game was also significantly discounted and I wouldn't have paid full price (£19.99) considering I really only play it with friends. Anyway, my initial impressions are that the crafting and vechicle turret mechanics are fun and probably fit the game better than previous deviations in the worms formula.
The crafting is simple enough to pick up quickly. It makes what you do with your inventory a lot more interesting, sacrificing a powerful weapon to give you just enough resources to make a concrete donkey for example. The vehicles and turrets are pretty fun too, although the mech suit seems over powered.
On the hole, the way they experimented with the mechanics in WMD are a lot more fun than say the 3D itterations or the 2 1/2D Clan Wars. 3D made using basic weapons such as the bazooka or grenade difficult to use because you'd have a hard time judging range. While the mechanics of Clan Wars were not obfuscating to basic gameplay, neither the 'dynamic water' or worm classes were really implemented well. Dynamic water in my experience got over used and the classes didn't really change gameplay that much. With the science worm being almost irrelevant. WMD on the otherhand refreshes the experience of playing worms, with mechanics which add to the basic gameplay, not re-invent them. Crafting is not great leap from having an inventory mechanic, therefore its inclusion doesn't seem ham-fisted like previous attempts at change.
The backgrounds are also once again pretty, unlike Clan Wars, where in certain themes it was difficult to distinguish backround and foregroud. Also there are plenty more themes. Some good workshop stuff to customize worms , although lack of any soundbanks is dissapointing. The default ones are okay, but there's nothing like having your worms shout Macho Man Randy Savage quotes. Its also possible to have more than four full teams on WMD which for me and my friends is a really handy.
So overall my impression is the game is good, the mechanics are solid, and the game returns to aesthetic that actually works for it. Especially considering I didn't pay even half price for this and for what I get out of it as a casual player, I'd say its worth it. I'd certainly not pay full price, and from what I've read from those who do play multiplayer, the community is pretty dead. Still its a really fun local multiplayer game, and if you wait for a sale I don't think you'll be dissapointed with your purchace.

I don't quite get why people are bashing APB.
There are only 1-2 hackers total at one given time across all servers.
But even then, they can be easily killed when you have a teammate with you.
The major hackers of APB were already perma-banned.
ALSO: This is not Pay2Win. The only way you can increase your damage and other stats is by playing, earning money, ranking up, then buying Modifications for your character or guns. ALL MODS ARE LOCKED UP UNTIL YOU REACH A CERTAIN RANK. This makes it impossible to make the server "Pay2Win" in the sense that you can't just sell items from the premium shop for in-game cash from a veteran player. You wouldn't be able to use any of the Mods that you could buy.
The only things you can purchase are cosmetic items such as clothing, different types of guns, or vehicles.
Even then, I've seen pros go on 5+ killsteaks using the default gun that everyone gets when they start. You just need to practice your aim and you're all good to go.
The reason for the reskins of guns is because... they're guns. Guns only shoot bullets. They ALL do the same thing. The difference is that each gun has different sounds and specs. What did you expect? CoD Laser Guns? The guns, in addition to what I said, actually has many choices for gun skins. There are country flag skins for every gun, casino themed ones, and dozens upon dozens of other cool skins.
There are plenty of weapons that you can choose from: LMG's, SMG's, SG's, secondaries, AR's, Misc (like LAW's [named osmaw or Volcano]), SR's, grenades, stun guns, stun assault rifles + shotguns, etc.
Plus the customization aspect of the game is absolutely fantastic. You can literally customize all the cars and clothing you own (i.e: actually create symbols which you can paste onto either of them).
Additionally, you can create your own music and kill screen theme songs in the Social District world. There are many amazing song artists that use an in-game music UI for making it. The UI is basically like Synthesia/Studio7 but less decorative in a sense.
As for character customization, you can literally change your character's face to anything as much as the limiters go up to. Eye size, eye shape, eye tilt level, eye position, eye color, iris color, eye size, iris size, iris contact lens, hair style, hair color, hair length editing, body mass, body muscularity, skin color, body hip resizing, tallness/shortness, ETC.
Disclaimer: the only "bad" part of the character customization system is that you need to be fairly decent/inter-advanced with it, since it's EXTREMELY flexfible and anything can be changed around. Btw, you can put any Symbol onto your character's skin as a tattoo.
I hope this clears things up and that the negative reviews below don't deter you from playing this amazing game. Have fun!

The sieging system is so fun, you can use catapults, trebuchets, ballista, burning oil, and a few other weapons to attack your enemies, and destroy their castles in the process. It is a brilliant side to PVP where you get that 'Feel good' moment when you ride with 24 of your friends/allies through the battlefield.
As for the game, I haven't reached a veteran level, but at times it can be a little grindy, but overall a fun game, you can share your quests with your party members, so they don't miss out and everyone is caught up. Also - If you're in the same room as your teammate, when they pick up items for a quest, you do as well. Which is very nice when it comes to how long it takes to complete a quest.
I would definitely, without a doubt, recommend this game. As for the lore side, people have given some bad reviews on the link to ES, but... with a game that by level 10, i've come across 90+ books, it can't be that bad, can it?

Before you read this review here are a few things that I'd like to get out of the way. This review was done after completing my first run of the game using Corvo and trying to accomplish a non-lethal stealth playthrough. I will also be reviewing the game from a personal perspective, That being said lets get into the review!
After finishing my first playthrough this morning I can see why people have mixed feelings towards this game, but I feel as though most of the negative or "thumbs down" reviews are due to the poor pc performance that came with this game after launch. (they still have yet to fix this at the time of posting this review) I've looked past most of the pc performance so I'll be reviewing this without making a big deal about the performance.
I think the only other negative thing that can be said about this game is that it is very similar to Dishonored 1 in terms of gameplay, characters, and maps. I however enjoy this more than I think I would had they made a more different world than they did for the second game. Some of the similarities include, using a boat to get to the beginning of missions, another genius and his highly guarded house, (Sokolov in the first game and Jindosh in the second game) Delilah and the Brigmore witches, someone who turns into a horde of rats when they're killed, (Granny rags in the first game and Paolo in the second game) being able to play as Corvo with the same powers and abilities, and another plague. (rats in the first game and bloodflies in the second game) A lo of people might look at these simililarities and think that the dev is lazy or they're recycling the first game to make some easy money, but when you think about the world that Dishonored 1 and 2 are set in it makes lots of sense. Corvo is going to have the same powers from the first game, there's going to be more genius' that advance mankind, there's ways to make charms that do amazing things (looking at you Paolo), and theres going to be more plague's before mankind reaches a point where they have vaccines and medicine to combat most sickness. I think a big reason that I enjoyed the second game so much is becuase it was easy and comfortable to take control of Corvo again; his abilites feel like second nature now.
While we're on the subject of Corvo let's take a moment to talk about his abilities and more specifically, the ones I chose to use throughout my playthrought. I played about 85% of the game just using blink and dark visions, these two abilities are really the only ones needed when doing a non-lethal stealth playthrough as you can blink past people and use dark visions to detect enemies to avoid and items to pick up. I find that the rest of Corvo's abilities are more easily used for lethal takedowns like devowering swarm. That being said I spent a fair amount of hours trying to knock most people out instead of just avoiding them to continue with the mission. This made the game a fair but harder but it was totally worth it.
The story of the game is extremely solid and carries on from the first game but the entire story isn't told to the player without effort on the players side. Theres plenty of optional lore to collect and read that's dispersed throughout the game. This optional lore adds plenty of extra layers and detail to the well crafted world of Dishonored 2, and not all of the optional reading is directly related to major events or details. There is plenty of small details about characters lives, emotions, and situations and the play can't even participate in. Even something small like squeezing the heart will give you extra details about characters and the world around you.
Overall this sequel to the tremendous hit, Dishonored, was excactly what I wanted in a second game that carried over the story, it brought me back to characters and places that I learned to love in the first game and seeing them once more only reinforced how much I enjoy the world that's shared between Dishonored 1 and 2. Sure a lot of details, maps, characters, powers, quests, and items are the same but this only made the game more enjoyable for me. After I finished the game the only complaint I was left with was the performance which will be fixed eventually. This leads me to give the game a 9.5/10 with no complaints otherwise. Arkane and Bethesda Studios did a tremendous job with this one and I truly cannot wait to see more from the Dishonored universe.
If you've read this far then thank you for taking the time to read this lengthy review and I hope you enjoyed the game just as much as I did.

For the people with short attention spans read this part. Get the game if you have a love for alien, or horror. Don't get this game if you expect the second coming of jesus, or like shooters, this is not a shooter..
Graphics: This game is gorgeous. I don't have an amazing computer. But i can run this at ultra easy.. this game just oozes atmosphere, from the steam coming off pipes, to the dripping of the alien saliva from a ceiling vent, to the excellent use of lighting. As for the bad, the npc's look a tad fake, and the way they move doesn't help.. The alien looks incredible, sometimes his movements are a little jerky especially if you are watching him for a min or two.. All in all though this is a stunner
Sound: The sound in this game is some of the best i've ever heard. The original remixed alien score,  the different noises the ship makes, to the alien itself and the many sounds it can make, rustling in the vents the clicking of its heels, it's nervewracking stuff.. but the sound also plays a part in the gameplay as well. You can tell where the alien is or where it's going just by listening. he only bad i've seen is a few glitches where the sound would constantly make sounds like  the alien is in the vents or something.. The first few times i heard this i thought it was the aien coming to get me but after waiting for 10 min i realized it wa sa glitch lol.
Gameplay: This is different then any other Alien game you have played.. The Story is well written and makes you want to finish the game. Walking slowly through the halls with steam billowing and hearing the alien off in the distance is intense.. The gameplay is slow but not too slow.. The first time you see the Alien in the flesh your heart beats a million times.  Before that its a little slow going, but once the alien is introduced all bets are off and you gotta pretty much crawl everywhere and be alert. I loved the gameplay as it was  afresh take on both the alien franchise and the horror genre. the alien is unpredictable and can do anythign at anytime..the missions start to get a wee bit tedious after a while though, but the alien stalking you makes up for it.. There were a few points in the game i wanted to tear my hair out because the alien seemed to smell my perfume or somethign and caught me all the time. The tethering in the game is way too cloe. i wish he went further away.
Lasting appeal: This game is super long. I think it's a bout 15 hrs, I have not finished it yet, but i'm within the last hour.. I don't know how many people will want to play through it again except maybe on hard difficulty, but there are challenge maps called survival. You have a few objectives but your main one is just to finish the map. Only one map is available at launch wihth more to follow..You compete with other players for the fastest time on that map.. I would say lasting appeal is moderate..
Final thoughts: The game is not quite the masterpiece it was claimed to be, there are a few bugs, and sometimes the alien does odd things,You will want to throw your controller across the room when the alien nows exactly where you are for the 4th time in a row, when other times he could be a foot away from you and not see you, though that is rare.. but overall this game is amazing and well worth the price if you ask me..

If you liked the original Half-life, then you'll like Black Mesa.
While there are some minor changes from the original, I feel that all of them only improve the game, and while some level design is slightly different, it's close enough that I can use my knowledge of the original to figure out the puzzles or mazes, but different enough that I still have to look, I just know what I'm looking for.
While there are some minor gameplay changes, most are almost unnoticeable and the game still feels like Half-Life, with the changes been ones that came with the source engine used to it's best.
The enemies are smarter than they used to be, with human enemies often flanking or taking cover, and alien enemies different shapes and means of attacks requiring you to fight defensively more than I remember, though some of that may be due to playing on a higher difficulty than I ever did the original.
To anyone not familiar with the original Half-life, I'd still recommend this game both as a good recreation of a very historic game, been one of the first FPS games to offer a story to go with it, and a good one at that, as well as a good modern game in general, that breaks a lot of the modern trends in FPS gaming that I'm sick of.
TL:DR
In short, I'd highly recommend this game to anyone fond FPS games, and anyone who liked the original Half-life
Forget Half-life: Source - THIS is the true remake of the classic FPS.

I don't quite get why people are bashing APB.
There are only 1-2 hackers total at one given time across all servers.
But even then, they can be easily killed when you have a teammate with you.
The major hackers of APB were already perma-banned.
ALSO: This is not Pay2Win. The only way you can increase your damage and other stats is by playing, earning money, ranking up, then buying Modifications for your character or guns. ALL MODS ARE LOCKED UP UNTIL YOU REACH A CERTAIN RANK. This makes it impossible to make the server "Pay2Win" in the sense that you can't just sell items from the premium shop for in-game cash from a veteran player. You wouldn't be able to use any of the Mods that you could buy.
The only things you can purchase are cosmetic items such as clothing, different types of guns, or vehicles.
Even then, I've seen pros go on 5+ killsteaks using the default gun that everyone gets when they start. You just need to practice your aim and you're all good to go.
The reason for the reskins of guns is because... they're guns. Guns only shoot bullets. They ALL do the same thing. The difference is that each gun has different sounds and specs. What did you expect? CoD Laser Guns? The guns, in addition to what I said, actually has many choices for gun skins. There are country flag skins for every gun, casino themed ones, and dozens upon dozens of other cool skins.
There are plenty of weapons that you can choose from: LMG's, SMG's, SG's, secondaries, AR's, Misc (like LAW's [named osmaw or Volcano]), SR's, grenades, stun guns, stun assault rifles + shotguns, etc.
Plus the customization aspect of the game is absolutely fantastic. You can literally customize all the cars and clothing you own (i.e: actually create symbols which you can paste onto either of them).
Additionally, you can create your own music and kill screen theme songs in the Social District world. There are many amazing song artists that use an in-game music UI for making it. The UI is basically like Synthesia/Studio7 but less decorative in a sense.
As for character customization, you can literally change your character's face to anything as much as the limiters go up to. Eye size, eye shape, eye tilt level, eye position, eye color, iris color, eye size, iris size, iris contact lens, hair style, hair color, hair length editing, body mass, body muscularity, skin color, body hip resizing, tallness/shortness, ETC.
Disclaimer: the only "bad" part of the character customization system is that you need to be fairly decent/inter-advanced with it, since it's EXTREMELY flexfible and anything can be changed around. Btw, you can put any Symbol onto your character's skin as a tattoo.
I hope this clears things up and that the negative reviews below don't deter you from playing this amazing game. Have fun!

For the people with short attention spans read this part. Get the game if you have a love for alien, or horror. Don't get this game if you expect the second coming of jesus, or like shooters, this is not a shooter..
Graphics: This game is gorgeous. I don't have an amazing computer. But i can run this at ultra easy.. this game just oozes atmosphere, from the steam coming off pipes, to the dripping of the alien saliva from a ceiling vent, to the excellent use of lighting. As for the bad, the npc's look a tad fake, and the way they move doesn't help.. The alien looks incredible, sometimes his movements are a little jerky especially if you are watching him for a min or two.. All in all though this is a stunner
Sound: The sound in this game is some of the best i've ever heard. The original remixed alien score,  the different noises the ship makes, to the alien itself and the many sounds it can make, rustling in the vents the clicking of its heels, it's nervewracking stuff.. but the sound also plays a part in the gameplay as well. You can tell where the alien is or where it's going just by listening. he only bad i've seen is a few glitches where the sound would constantly make sounds like  the alien is in the vents or something.. The first few times i heard this i thought it was the aien coming to get me but after waiting for 10 min i realized it wa sa glitch lol.
Gameplay: This is different then any other Alien game you have played.. The Story is well written and makes you want to finish the game. Walking slowly through the halls with steam billowing and hearing the alien off in the distance is intense.. The gameplay is slow but not too slow.. The first time you see the Alien in the flesh your heart beats a million times.  Before that its a little slow going, but once the alien is introduced all bets are off and you gotta pretty much crawl everywhere and be alert. I loved the gameplay as it was  afresh take on both the alien franchise and the horror genre. the alien is unpredictable and can do anythign at anytime..the missions start to get a wee bit tedious after a while though, but the alien stalking you makes up for it.. There were a few points in the game i wanted to tear my hair out because the alien seemed to smell my perfume or somethign and caught me all the time. The tethering in the game is way too cloe. i wish he went further away.
Lasting appeal: This game is super long. I think it's a bout 15 hrs, I have not finished it yet, but i'm within the last hour.. I don't know how many people will want to play through it again except maybe on hard difficulty, but there are challenge maps called survival. You have a few objectives but your main one is just to finish the map. Only one map is available at launch wihth more to follow..You compete with other players for the fastest time on that map.. I would say lasting appeal is moderate..
Final thoughts: The game is not quite the masterpiece it was claimed to be, there are a few bugs, and sometimes the alien does odd things,You will want to throw your controller across the room when the alien nows exactly where you are for the 4th time in a row, when other times he could be a foot away from you and not see you, though that is rare.. but overall this game is amazing and well worth the price if you ask me..

Hurtworld. One of the best survival games I have played in a while. This game is basically a much better virison of Rust. It's a great game to play with friends, and even solo it's a blast. I am about 100 hours in, and still having a great time. There is a decent amount of content, but once you get to end game there is not much else to do besides PVP and wait for new content and maybe expand your base.
I would reccomend this to anyone who likes online survival sandboxs.

Hurtworld:
~~~~~~~~

You probably remember this famous movie scene where a robot (played by Mr Universe) was sent from the future and he appeared totally naked in the middle of a street in Los Angeles! Well, we need to change a couple of things here. First of all, your appearance is…. Shall we say a little bit frail and you will appear practically naked, not in Los Angeles but in the outback of HURTWORLD!!
Hurtworld is a multiplayer survival FPS game with a large open world. As you spawn for the first time in your birthday suit, you will need to gather and hunt for very important resources straight away.  Collect wood and stone by picking them up or by mining (different types of stones/rocks) and make sure you accumulate enough foods to survive another day. You might be lucky enough to find seeds and become a farmer (that depends of your life spend)! The days can be sweet, hunting animals, making friends and developing your arsenal, from spears to machine guns. The days can go sour, you can still be running around with nothing on and the weather can change from beautiful sunshine to rain and you are going to get soaked; plus night time is just around the corner and you will feel the cold to the point of dying of hypothermia!
The servers can hold up to 50 players and most players seem to be friendly. I have a particular recollection of being at a fire pit trying to keep warm when this guy was coming towards me and saying over his microphone that he was friendly and he did not mean any harm. He even invited me to be part of his group. “Great,” I thought. So I went through the menu to find out which key I was supposed to use to respond but…. I received a strange gift from him… it was an arrow straight to my poor and frail body. Then he scavenged from my dead body and his next words were, ”Wow, plenty of goodies here!” What a little bugger, I thought! Anyway, his offer of joining was genuine but I could not find where he was squatting!
This game is all about the evolution of your character and you really have to be on the ball to be able to survive to the next day. Find a workbench (or create one) and you will be able to craft plenty of items; materials - weapons - tools – gears - machines and more. If you fancy a spot at the edge of a cliff, just take ownership of the land and build your shelter there!
Graphically the game looks great and runs very well. From the control point of view you will use the keyboard and mouse in this game.
Positive:
~~~~~~~
-	Big open world
-	Plenty of ting to craft and build
-	Changeable weather
-	Servers hold up to 50 players
-	Hardcore survival game
Negatives:
~~~~~~~~
-	Occasional animals glitches (you see them from a distance but as you get closer their disappear
-	No achievements / trading cards
This is a great survival game with plenty of crafting to do! If you are a fan of this type of game, you must come and visit Hurtworld. I know you will love it!

Hurt world is like a cartoon version of Rust, (so people can run it) with a few nice adjustments...
Karma system (kill people and you have a chance of dropping your gear for some time. With this system you can be legitimately friendly and make friends doing so not losing any gear if backstabbed, though I haven't been backstabbed or matter of fact been friendly (:< )
Farming (you can farm fruit also resources like coolent and sun cream)
More ores (there is the standard iron ore then more ores in different biomes and different ways to obtain it and have different melting temperatures)
Crystals/Ambers (these are a rare resource that is used for allot adding more of the difficulty in the game)
Different types of rocks (the different types of rock offer different types of resources, I won't go into too much detail because it is self explanatory)
Some science (here and there you will see some science about the ores and resources, showing what chemicals are present in the substance)
Biomes (I know rust has some biomes but these are varied, they offer different resources and amass more survival difficulties)
Cars (who thought I would miss out the cars? The cars parts are not too hard to find except the tires they are very difficult to find, forcing you to raid and I think this is all good)
Upgrading (in the game you can upgrade your pick or axe a fair bit with the uncommon, rare or legendary ore you find, making it do more damage and be more effective)
More tools (the compass is very useful device where it shows you how far away you are from your claim pole, a.k.a your base)
Some bad things...
Glitches (it is new so it is to be expected, there is a rock glitch where you can prop glitch yourself inside to raid bases who have built up against the rock without using c4 also there is the glitchy fall damage system that I have experienced where some little jump can almost kill you... Don't know if it's intended but I will say it anyway, the drills you can get in the game can sometimes placed on foundations and can be placed and giant rocks)
You can expect these to be fixed at a later date as they are updating the game frequently with new stuff.

If you liked the original Half-life, then you'll like Black Mesa.
While there are some minor changes from the original, I feel that all of them only improve the game, and while some level design is slightly different, it's close enough that I can use my knowledge of the original to figure out the puzzles or mazes, but different enough that I still have to look, I just know what I'm looking for.
While there are some minor gameplay changes, most are almost unnoticeable and the game still feels like Half-Life, with the changes been ones that came with the source engine used to it's best.
The enemies are smarter than they used to be, with human enemies often flanking or taking cover, and alien enemies different shapes and means of attacks requiring you to fight defensively more than I remember, though some of that may be due to playing on a higher difficulty than I ever did the original.
To anyone not familiar with the original Half-life, I'd still recommend this game both as a good recreation of a very historic game, been one of the first FPS games to offer a story to go with it, and a good one at that, as well as a good modern game in general, that breaks a lot of the modern trends in FPS gaming that I'm sick of.
TL:DR
In short, I'd highly recommend this game to anyone fond FPS games, and anyone who liked the original Half-life

My background: I've played past Worms games, and I've always thought of them as a great shared screen game for fun competition between friends and family. I've never felt the need to master the physics or "meta" of one of these games or otherwise try hard against strangers online in one of these games, so I couldn't even begin to go into comparisons on physics, weapon balance, etc., because I really don't care that much.
Pros:
-Shared screen works great as always.
-Controller layout is good... my 10 year old picked up on it instantly.
-Tons of customization thanks to schemes and editors... i.e. if you don't like new features like vehicles and mounted weapons you can take them out.
-Ability to customize Worms adds to the fun.
Neutral:
-There is a good amount of single-player content in the game. Playing these scenarios can be fun and can help you learn the game a bit, but like the campaign in an RTS, they aren't really the main draw.
Cons:
-Keyboard layout takes a little getting used to but is advisable over remapping (other reviews have detailed explanations of the problems there).
-Normal price of $29.99 is quite high unless you see yourself wanting to play online against others a lot.
I definitely recommend Worms WMD for shared screen at it's current sale price of $10.19.

Many gamers ask how Alien Isloation actually is, good or bad?
The answer isnt easy, if you tell it is very good the expectations are too high,
and the gamers review tends to be bad.
The game itself sticks very close to the Alien Universe,
no mix with Predators or other circus attractions.
Genuine actors, like Ripley, found all their way into this game.
Creative Assembly has recreated the whole atmosphere very carefully and accurately,
in order to make this game a worthwhile experience.
For a video game Alien Isolation is absolutely awesome,
it took me 30 hours to complete the main campaign on hard.
And still, for a true Alien fan it is a two edged sword.
Gameplay is sometimes very tense, the AI works in most cases as expected,
but...there is always something to improve.
I had the impression there have been missing about 10 people in every staff,
animation, meshers, texturing, effects, etc. to make this game look like perfect,
through the whole missions, from the beginning to the end.
But still the animation doesnt allow those movements you'd like to expect from the Alien.
Indeed, the animation technique used in this game is very good.
But yet it still cant maintain the impression of a 'real, AI driven' Alien. Why?
For instance, It is not possible to burn parts of the Alien,
it doesnt jump over tables, all those quirky things.
After a while you have seen all of its animations/behavior, they repeat.
Nothing new, nothing surprising, nothing that reminds of a 'real' breed.
You start to sense the automation, and then, in most cases,
the Alien becomes the well known computer enemy dude.
I lost some of the fascination I had at the very beginning.
And not because I was annoyed by hiding in a locker too often.
But, to be honest, I do not know any technique in animation yet,
which would allow a much better, physics based animation giving the Alien
much more diverse and surprising movements/behavior.
We might have to wait awile for this to happen in computer games.
All in all, I would rate this game a 9.5 out of 10.

This is so difficult. I initially loved this game, and yet I hate it. I got about 4 hours in, and I decided to sacrifice my save point to show my "Alien"-loving friend the game from the beginning. "I don't care! Not only am I happy to do this to show you the game from the start and not spoil anything, I'll enjoy playing those hours again." That's how much I liked it, and there's so much to like for any fans of the films. It's so lovingly made, and you can feel that the makers are fans too.
That was a big mistake. The longer you look, the more you see the cracks, and some of the cracks are chasms. I'm really fed up of replaying the same zone because of the terrible AI. Sometimes it's weirdly under-sensitive, and sometimes absurdly over-sensitive. You can't get a handle on the rules here, and I now realise that I was getting through some of those stages the first time on pure luck.
That's not even the least of the problems of unfairness. More than once, I've had the task of reaching a distant elevator. There's an android in the way. I use a smoke bomb and sneak around it, and by the time the android catches sight of me again, I'm already in the lift. I've pressed the button, and the doors close just as the android makes it to the elevator. A moment of exhilaration and relief? Yeah, nearly. The lift rises, and a couple of seconds later the android is magically in the elevator with me. On one occasion I fought off the teleporting interloper for long enough to reach the next floor, but our struggle immediately attracted his magic robot friends, and that was it for me.
And the humans. When they're not being psychic, the humans are so stupid. You'll sometimes find them walking on the spot, snagged on a vending machine or some other environment detail. On top of this, you can watch the alien exit through a vent in front and then almost immediately reappear behind you before anything else happens. That's not because of swiftness of movement, or any kind of movement at all. That's one routine ending, and another beginning. I want to forgive it, and I want the game to fool me into thinking this is me vs real thinking enemies, but I'm at a point of frustration with it where the game may remain unfinished. Or maybe I'll force myself through it, I don't know. Both possibilities are miserable, which tells you all you need to know.

I got this game gifted by a friend with whom I'm working on developing a game. It was meant as taking a break from development and maybe get inspired by.
At first I wasn't sure if my computer could run it, but here came the first surprise:
The game runs incredibly smooth whilst looking amazing. I haven't actually checked the my fps, but it felt like a solid 60 all the time, even at times with lots of particles, light effects and other stuff going on.
The attention to detail in the game is also amazing. The game took me about 16 hours to finish, and in that time I have taken a total of 638 screenshots. That means that on average I took one screenshot per 40 seconds.  The detail varies from smoke particles coming out of every door that opens, to lights that turn on when you enter a room.
The level design is also very clever and well done.
As a level designer when I saw this room:
I just stopped and looked in awe for about a minute. There is so much detail, but the lighting immediately shows where you have to go, the windows very nicely remind you that you're in space as well. The big sign still shows signs of a better past.
The gameplay is solid too, I'm personally not good at stealth games, but I still managed to beat the game on normal. The game is lengthy, but I feel that the pacing is pretty good. New things get brought in regularly, and generally after some very tense missions you'll have a bit of time to cool down again.
A last thing that simply must be praised in this game is the sound design. Man oh man, the sound really, really gets you on edge. The first bit of the game there's not really anything to be actually scared of, but the music really keeps you sharp and scared.
All in all an amazing game, I'm already ready to vote this game my game of the year.
This game has inspired me more than any other game I've played. There's so much good stuff here I want to learn from and use in anything I work on in the future. I will totally play this game a good bunch of times again!

This game is great... If you have a Graphics Card and Audio and Video Drivers that are compatible with this game, or else you won't even get past the Splash screen without a problem occuring. Personally, I couldn't even get past the Splash screen (The Total War: Rome II loading screen) and I tried everything that I knew and saw on the forums, but to no avail, but luckily, SEGA Customer Service, after only 2 emails, fixed my problem and I could now enjoy the game, so keep this in mind when buying the game.
Firstly, the Campaign is really nice in terms of UI (User Interface), Graphics and the display. It's really cool how you can see cities grow when you expand them and the puff of dust that appears when you build/repair something. Mostly everything is visually appeasing and the variety of factions, in my opinion, is very large. I also like the units unique to one faction as it makes you feel like this faction isn't another copy-and-paste that happens to be in a different place on the map. Even though the Spies, Dignitaries (I think) and Champions are bascially the same, they actually seem to serve more of a purpose in Rome II and can actually do visible effects on an army (I suggest not to assassinate generals, it's almost futile). What does make the game a bit less enjoyable is that the AI is way more aggressive than before Patch 1 as they declare war on you one-by-one until, next thing you know, half the known world is DoW-ing your♥♥♥♥♥for little more reason than "I like killling". That eventually does make the campaign a nearly impossible game (Check out Lionheart's Odrysian Kingdom LP for a great example of that and my Screenshots, if I ever find out how to Screen-cap since F12 doesn't seem to work).
Battles and Multiplayer battles are both really cool and are also very aesthetically pleasing and the UI is simple like usual. The morale of units may make battles frustrating since you spend good money on a unit that breaks within one minute of battle, thus making them worthless. Siege battles are mostly a bore since torching the gates is really just a suicide mission and the archer towers are way too overpowered and can wipe out a unit in no time. (Hopefully CA can nerf it to be like it was in Shogun 2, slow-firing and utterly worthless) The Objective points in Siege battles are really a Double-edged sword so to speak. They can make siege battles a breeze and make you win or they can be a royal pain-in-the♥♥♥♥♥and cause you to lose for no apparent reason. The Capture point, if held by the enemy and the countdown has finished, will cause your units to ROUT, which is dumb because in real life, this would never happen, which brings up the conversation of sacrificing realisticness for more playability. The Unit cards are a subject of controversy amongst some Rome II players since to some (including me), they look really nice, but to others, it looks like a Kindergartener collage that mimics the appearance of Greek Amphorae-People. Multiplayer is fun since you can choose whatever unit you want within the fund limit unlike in Shogun 2 where you had to capture regions to unlock certain units and the players aren't douches and you can have a challenge and not always fight against high ranking players. 3v3's and 4v4's are a bit laggy and very often I notice many players leaving because of their computers incompatibility with the game (which basically brings us back to Paragraph 1, DO NOT BUY THE GAME IF YOUR GRAPHICS, AUDIO AND VIDEO DRIVERS ARE NOT UP TO DATE OR STRONG ENOUGH)
Naval battles are pretty tedious and require extreme micromanaging and skill since a simple, little ship filled with a unit of Mob can easily destroy your favourite, overpriced elite unit with a simple ramming order. Transport ships are famous for destroying elite Naval units that are specifically designed to kick♥♥♥♥♥yet don't. Navies are useful for blockading enemy ports, however and hampering the enemy greatly.
So, to sum it all up, Total War: Rome II is a great game that should not be ignored and now, thanks to the patches, the AI is less buggy and the game is fully playable and some of its more controversial features have been ripped out of the game or tweaked a bit. It has great replayability value and is worth the money during a sale so, whenever it's discounted, buy it if you can. Final Verdict: 84%-A solid game

Since this is a sequal, I'm going to compare it to the first game (which I'll abbreviate as 1).
Cons
-You've heard about the PC issues by now. I don't need to reiterate the details.
-It's beautiful, but it doesn't have the same amazing stylization as 1
-The story isn't as emotional
Pros
-Movements of the NPC character models aren't as awkward as in 1
-Four distinct play styles: Corvo low chaos, Corvo high chaos, Emily low chaos, Emily high chaos
-More variety in voices (although I'm not a fan of the Outsider's new voice)
-Power upgrades branch out and are generally awesome. A+ for heathen magic.
-The world/universe is highly detailed and well crafted. You really feel like the places and cultures are real.
Main Points
-Most significant con: less emotional story than 1
-Most significant pro: magical stealth/fighting? Count me in! Great gameplay.
All in all, it's a genuinely fun game. It's a must-have for fans of the original and I'm sure it's still fun if you haven't played 1. While 1 is certainly better, this game is a worthy sequal that I expect I will be spending maaaaany hours playing.

A review from Worms Armageddon veteran.
Another clunky cash grab from Team 17 bloated with unnecessary bells and whistles, while the game itself isn't nearly as smooth and enjoyable as Worms Armageddon.
PROS:
+ Slightly closer to WA in terms of graphics, customizability and game feel than previous entries.
+ Now you technically can play good-old custom game modes like shopper, WxW, rope race (no bow'n'arrow though), doesn't mean it will be as fun and smooth as it used to be.
+ You can customize your team's looks.
+ Runs without slightest hiccups on a modern systems, unlike WA.
+ Proper SteamWorks integration for multiplayer.
+ Big enough single player campaign, because people buy this game to play single player, right?
CONS:
- The game's physics are really bad, everything is too heavy and there are no options to tune it to your liking. Even the "Low Gravity" item isn't there anymore. Forget about efficiently roping around, bouncing grenads off terrain for cool skillshots or making something skip on water.
- Weapon category and hotkey layout is a mess. In WA it was like F7+Space+F7 and you're on a rope with parachute selected, ready to traverse the map without worrying that a slight mistake will end your turn. Here parachute is on F2, because... I guess Team17 doesn't want you to have convenient hotkey controls...
- No adjustments for weapon power or rope length, which cripples experience from barely playable classic custom modes.
- The worms are too small. As a result, you have to zoom in too much to see what you're doing and not see the bigger picture and vice-versa.
- The multiplayer is almost dead, even despite the expected influx of new players from the game being included in a recent bundle. What little playerbase it has are kids with little skill and bad manners.
- Importing custom maps isn't as easy and straightforward as it used to be, who needs that huge community-made Worms Map Database anyway? Have a useless Steam Workshop!
- No option to import custom voice-banks, flags, victory tunes or gravestones, the vanilla ones are 'meh', and there are no voice-banks that don't sound squeaky.
- Crafting and vehicles don't add any depth or fun, they just break the balance and add unnecessary complication and confusion.
- Turrets are broken no-brainer OP trash.
- Competitive preset is too limiting, which means that you don't have many tools to diversify your tactics, only your skill at throwing grenades and shooting bazooka matters.
- Team 17 haven't released any updates in months, and probably moved on to making the next low-effort cash grab.
Avoid this game, don't let the devs cash-in on your nostalgia, this game is gravely inferior to WA in everything, except performance on modern PCs and Steam integration. Isn't very fun on its own either, especially with that ridiculous price-tag.

After putting in a good amount of time into the game, I will be omitting the campaign review, as we all know that's not what we are interested in reading, but instead I will jump right into the multiplayer aspect of said game. First off, this is by far the most unplayable Call of Duty game I've had the chance to play. Initial gameplay was decent and enjoyable, but that honeymoon stage is over and the game reared it's ugly face. First off, we all know Sledgehammer lied right to our faces with the promise of dedicated servers... Of which is non existent, and because of that, hackers and cheats have pretty much over run the game at this current time. With the new update that came out recently, for pc gamers, the game is in sorts... unplayable due to the fact the the game constantly crashes/freezes after a set amount of time usually less than 30 minutes. Aside from the unplayability due to bad coding and priority issues, the player base for the game has dropped drastically within the last 2 months. To those who are thinking about purchasing the game, either wait, or clench your teeth and bear it with all the current problems plaguing the game. It may have the Call of Duty name, but by no means does it warrant a loss of funds as most will be dissapointed with that fact that they will be unable to play the game smoothly, and as a side note, the only games people will be able to get into is team deathmatch and domination if you're lucky, for the most part, all other games will not have anyone playing due to the loss of players and small player base because of ALL of the issues. At the moment, this game is not recommended unless you are able to deal with frustration and anger with the problems, especially with the multiplayer aspect of which most of us purchased the game for.
EDIT: With more time on the game, comes an update, DO NOT PURCHASE THIS GAME. The DLC's require you to only play lobbies with people either having the season pass or the separate DLC purchases. Meaning you can only play lobbies with people having the season pass and no others, same with the individual purchases. Conclusion, there are realistically ONLY two playable game modes in multiplayer being TDM and mosh pit, which being the only two game modes with an actual player population of over 20 people.

Alright, let's get into some back-story. So I am a HUGE Elder's Scrolls fan, and when ESO was announced, I was psyched.......Until they announced that you needed to pay to play, even on the PC. Since then, I pretty much avoided everything related to the game. Recently, I had to move to another country. My best friend and I wanted a game that we could both, and maybe a few more people, play. Around the same time, Zenimax announced that in a few months, the game would  be subscription-free. We decided on ESO:TU, and I must say, I am not disappointed. I have roughly 65 hours under my belt right now, level 9, and probably still considered a "noob." There are HUNDREDS of hours of gameplay. The game has it's own story-line, which I won't divulge too much into ('cause, you know, spoilers.) I must admit, me and the other 3 people I am playing with have swayed quite a bit aways from the main story line, and instead have done loads of side-quests, each of which has it's own seperate lore. Each city in the game also has it's own story, so don't worry about having nothing to do. Every week or so, there is also an update adding new quests and other locations. Soon, the game will have all the locations of Tamriel, the continent in which all of the Elder's Scrolls games (so far) have taken place in. All in all, this is an amazing game, and I would recommend this to any friend in a heartbeat.

Elder Scrolls Online Tamriel Unlimited, Where do I begin. Everything people hated in beta has been fixed majorly and changes have happened for the better. Though people still hate the game because what they expect is a skyrim clone or harbor a grudge against the game due to its beta days. (Which even I will admit were awful)
If you enjoy exploring, lore, dungeons, or elder scrolls in general you will most likely enjoy this game. There are several options on how to develop a character as in most non-mmo elder scrolls games. For now I will list some of the pros coming from a mmo aspect. As I have yet to really hate anything I will post cons when I see fit. (You should really check out some youtube videos before buying this to see if its your type of game instead of asking if its a good game or not as opinions are different)
Pros
- Graphics are amazing and feel nice for immersion while exploring.
- Variety making one faction seem like another world when out to explore like it should be.
- Siege weapons in this game are interesting as they showcase how they would normally be used.
- Reading books is sometimes fun for lore or just for a laugh.
- The leveling isn't extremely hard as some mmo's.
- Plenty of skills for originality or making a personal character.
- More sheogorath jokes
Cons
- Character creation. While there is several options to choose from while making your characters I feel they should've added more hair styles and perhaps more adornments, But its more then some mmo's so I really cant complain on this one much.
- Small learning curve. Some things are majorly different from most mmo's and will leave you guessing for a hour or so before you find yourself really catchng on to them.
This is another fantastic RPG from From Software. Don't be fooled, this is a hard but terribly rewarding game. A must buy for anyone who enjoys RPGs with a challenge.
