This is a must-buy for Worms enthusiasts who've followed the franchise for a long time & were looking for a customizable experience with weapons.
So, what does Worms WMD bring to the table?
1.) Item customization - You can customize your favorite items & build a custom arsenal.
2.) The onscreen tanks, helicopters, race cars, mounted weapons, etc. that you can use aside from your own array of weapons is a welcome upgrade that gamers will definitely love.
3.) Explosive impact - weapons in WMD feel powerful & the explosive impact & special effects of the weapons are noticeable.
4.) Worms customization is easier & allows an 8-worm team.
5.) Detailed structures & fortification - Worms can now go inside of buildings & abstracts for protection (or to engage in battle inside the building itself).
6.) Traps - Enemy worms aren't the only thing that threaten you anymore.
7.) Terrain customization is easier, giving you a more comprehensive set of tools to craft terrains that suit your interests (they can improve this, but its a good start).
8.) Great OST - The soundtrack is great work & shows how much effort was put into the game.
9.) Frustrating challenges we all love to hate - Yep, they are back. Its nothing new, but its worth mentioning.
But there are a few setbacks to consider as well.
1.) While local play would make for a great time with your friends & family, The online community is small, which can impact your experience if you're heavily reliant on finding online gamers to play with.
2.) Armageddon enthusiasts may be disappointed with the current selection of available items to use & may feel that the franchise is *too* familiar to Armageddon, which may not justify the current price tag if you're debating whether or not to make the jump to WMD.
3.) Minor glitches. There are occasional times when you lose gamepad functionality (e.g. sometimes during the Worm Select tool during your turn - which may annoy you).
Another small issue is menu size. The menu is tiny, making it more difficult for new players or players with custom screens to use it. I wish there was at least a large popup which displays the name of the weapon/item you are highlighting for a 60" 4K TV.
The game is still very new & being worked on - so who knows what surprises the developer has in store for you. If you're new to the franchise and are looking for a casual game you can enjoy with your friends, this is definitely a great choice for silly fun.

So, let me help you decide whether this game is worth your money or not.
I divided this review in pros and cons, so let's begin with the positive things. Don't be mislead by the displayed hours, I have played this game on console, since it was unplayable on the PC until yesterday.
Positive things:
The gameplay is pretty nice and smooth, just as it was in the previous title. There are some improvements, the movement doesn't feel as clunky as it did some times in the prior Dishonored.
The story is pretty ok, I guess. It definitely is not the very best storyline I have ever witnessed, but it is pretty ok and entertaining at times. I really enjoy the fact that you can choose whether you play Emily or Corvo.
The graphics are very nice, especially for people that really like the art-style of this genre. Overall textures are a lot smoother than in Dishonored which is quite nice.
They finally adressed the performance problems on PC and the game is now playable, at least on my rig. Perfect.
Negatives:
To be honest, the AI in this game is pretty stupid. It was not very hard to not get detected by the AI, which made the stealth aspect a little bit unsatisfying. I also played the campaign on normal and it was not very challenging which is unfortunate.
Overall I would not recommend paying 60 bucks for this game. I also bought it somewhere else and saved a little bit of money and it was definitely worth it.

Awesome follow up on the Souls games. Gives the player the sense that around every corner you will die. After the first dark souls this one does seem easier, however I find the bosses are harder if you don't know what you are doing and don't have a good set up. Still buggy in places, such as weapons degrade very fast, especially when you play in another players world.
Co-op is a crutial part of this game, yes the enemies get harder and the bosses get more health but without the help of the other undead players you will find that you stand little chance especially with a slow build or light wieght build. If you don't like co-op players don't worry you don't have to use it but if you do and the player is just not working out you do have an item to remove them, however, if you really don't like people you can invade another player and make their experience of the game even harder!
I highly recommend this game, gives a real challenge but if you are easily agrivated this may not be the game for you... People say that games are getting shorter... Yes this game can be speed run in around an hour IF you have the experience but if you want to play the game properly it can take anywhere from 50-150 hours and with the new game plus system the game just gets harder and harder. But this will need to be done to collect EVERYTHING.
A bad note however, is the game has no structure in the areas you visit, you go from a dark hunting ground to a posin mine to then a firey castle. However when reading up on the game there are explainations for this. This goes with the 'lack of story'. Dark Souls does have a story, it has one of the biggest and most exsiting storys out there but the player has to search for it and read all the bios for the items they pick up but build a back story, Unlike the first one there are more NPCs in this game that fill more story holes.
There is no reason to play the first game if you're worried about a story continuation. This game has little relivance to the first game as you're in a different land, different issues with the world and its around 1000 years after the first game, yes to the big DS fans (Like myself) there are a lot of easter eggs relating to the first game, but for those who are not big fans do not worry they have no impact on the experience.

I'll be honest with you, I liked the first game, but I never finished it.  I hopped on that bandwagon a little too late, and before I knew it the second game was hot off the press and on my hard drive.  Nevertheless, I played enough of the first one to get the idea, and Dark Souls II is a remarkable improvement over it's predecessor.  Everything I didn't like about the first game has been fixed, and in more ways than I expected.  I don't understand why some people say the graphics aren't that great either -- the game runs on the highest settings quite easily, and I haven't seen anything that really stood out to me as far as bad graphics go.
The only thing I don't like about the Souls series, on a big picture scale, is the PvP.  Nobody ever fights honorably when you encounter an invader.  Everyone wants to be a roguish type or a magic user, and they almost always circle around you like a noob and this is Call of Duty or something, totally negating all of the same tactics you've used to previously.  Then there's the times when you find messages on the ground and people intentially mislead you or block your ability to use whatever you need the "use" button for.  I understand it's a joke, and that it's the nature of the game, but it's those kind of things that deter me from playing the game at all.  It's bittersweet.  I accidentally killed an NPC because someone left a message saying it was a "Sniper Spot".  After aggro'ing the NPC, I was forced to murder him, and that really upset me highly.  Plus, I have never been invaded outside of an, erhm, "designated invasion area", and I'm wondering if that's a good thing or a bad thing.
Apart from its flaws, I have to recommend it because it's such an addictive and mesmerizing game.  The environments, the subtle and intuitive design, the combat....it's all so perfect.  It's loads of fun and you won't be able to put it down, especially since they took all of the flaws of the first game and flipped them around quite literally, turning them into strengths in this title.  I can't ignore the fact though that some flaws of the series are deeply rooted, and how much they matter depends on what kind of gamer you are, if an honorable one at all.

ESO is a good game. It's enjoyable, it's fairly pleasing to the eye, it's set in Tamriel for all the grandeur that brings and for the most part it really is rather immersive.
But... One cannot help but compare ESO to other games. As an MMORPG it pales in comparison to the likes of Guild Wars 2 in terms of scope, story telling, design (both visually and in terms of game mechanics) and that all important player experience.
As an Elder Scrolls game it feels really lacking. You will remember your first couple of playthroughs in Oblivion or Skyrim: you find yourself in the middle of an enormous new world and you could set off in any direction you pleased and do whatever tickled your fancy. This had a lot to do with the dynamic levelling system where the monsters around you scaled in difficulty as you increased in level and experience. This approach just doesn't work in an MMORPG (although GW2 has a good shot at it) so that classic ES freedom to roam is badly hampered by all those big scary beasts twice your level who will rip you to shreds whilst you attempt a scenic tour.
I know this sounds like I am pushing you away from this game, but in truth I am warning you that you really can't help but compare this game to others you have played, and the results won't please you. If you have played GW2 or any previous Elder Scrolls game you may be dissapointed, if you haven't then you will love it (though for the price I'd highly recommend a look at the new expansion coming out for GW2 first).
In summary: ESO is a great game, and plays well... but be aware that there are better games out there that you might want to try first!

This was one of my first mmo's and coming from Elder Scrolls where I played in the 1st person view a lot, it seemed a little off at first (you can play elder scrolls online in first person but tactically better in 3rd to see what's going on). After tweaking some of the graphic settings and .ini files I've found the eso to be eye pleasing and I got used to the 3rd person and enemy spawns. In addition to having access to PVP at character level 10 you have the opprotunity to travel to over 15 regions from the start (about 4 main regions per alliance, then also a few small starter regions). My first play through as part of the Daggerfall Covenant took me about 100-120 hours. So you're getting about 20 hours for each reagion, and you can complete them faster if you're just doing the main province quests and/or not reading the text. After playing other mmo's like Star Wars the old republic, Guild Wars 2, Black Desert Online, Eve,  it's safe to say that eso is my favorite out of all of them. I'm not forced to pay extra for anything, and the dlc that is part of the game really is extra content. DLC I feel has been reasonably priced even if initially there is a high price, it comes back down to earth. While I was a little put off by having to purchase the new expansion instead of being able to use crowns, the expansion is supposed to be bigger then just an extra region like a dlc. Time will tell if that is true but I can just not subscribe or purchase crowns for awhile and that would then essentially make it the same as a crown purchase. You don't have to subscribe nor puchase crowns, those things are purely extra perks that have a small impact on the overall game. Since I have a job and extra money, what those were offering I found worth it.... You can purchase mounts, houses, bag space, bank space for in game coin at reasonable prices. The story is decent, but don't expect to find any "special" quests that you wouldn't have had in a typical Elder Scrolls Game. That is it's your fetch, kill, talk to type quests just like Elder Scrolls, mixed in with some dungeons (delves) and dolmens (anchors that drop from sky in certain locations and spawn enemies to kill). The only bad thing I can say is with the new system world bosses can be a pain and sometimes impossible to kill solo now where as before one could solo them. Being an mmo though it's hard to complain that help isn't available... The regions are still populated with help abound

' Alien Isolation ' is a game of exploration and survival against surprisingly good A.I where evasion is usually the best tactic.  Just like the classic 1979 film ' Alien ' expect authentic sights & sounds from the fear inducing moments of a nearby Xenomorph, right down to the wailing sirens and dated computer consoles. The eerily lit corridors are reminiscent of Doom 3, just don't expect fast paced runnin' & gunnin' with BFG's, cos here, you'll need to tread lightly to survive. If you're looking for a game with bags of atmosphere & jumps galore, this maybe for you.
Who would have thought we'd get a good alien game post COD generation ? And coming from the most unexpected studio just left me a bit speechless.

While it suffers from some pacing issues, and the trial-and-error stealth can be a bit tedious at times, Alien: Isolation completely blows the doors off of any other Alien game ever made. The design, audio and gameplay are top notch and combine to deliver a horrifying experience that you won't regret playing. Vote with your wallets and buy this game so other publishers take notice of the fact that THIS is what Alien fans want from an Alien game

The best Alien game created, everything is perfect.
The game itself has an Amnesia without the puzzles feel to it, of course in Amnesia you get free time to do the puzzles, in this, the alien is constantly around you whether it be in the vents or lurking around on the ground.
The Alien's AI is also great, the biggest fear in the game is that you never know what the Alien's going to do next. Everything the Alien does is random. The Alien will often look around rooms, under tables and in lockers for you, and if it sees you, you know you're screwed from that moment as it comes sprinting towards you. In moments you are also able to use the Alien to your advantage against other enemies that oppose you in the game, like using the Noisemakers to lure it's attention towards the human AIs.
The design of the game is great, it really sticks to the looks and feel of the original Alien movie. Not a single aspect of the game feels like it wouldn't belong in the Alien universe. Obviously some have critiqued about certain things like the motion tracker's display is actually the same as the one featured in Aliens, not Alien.
The only bad thing I can say about the game is that you get to a certain point where you obtain/figure out things in the game that slightly removes the fear of the Alien.
TLDR; Awesome game, 9.5/10!

Sometimes I begin to think : "What makes a good game?"
Good Price? Replayability? Next-Gen Graphics? Advanced Complicated Story?
This game, has simple graphics. 2D with very, simple, effects, with 16bit art style.
This game, has simple plot, not many branches, even some are quite common story.
This game, has quite short time to finish, even really less replayability.
But you know, this game mixes them all very well into very nice game.
OST really synced to the art, and art really supports the gameplay. and the gameplay, really blend in to the story.
So, I decided to answer my question with :
"Good game is a game with good combination and collaboration between the assets (OST, music, story, gameplay mechanics) and they support each other, makes player feel the game."
Congrats Holy Priest, I even feel guilty now for playing this for free - I should throw some money to your coin box.

I love this game! I played it all the way through in one day. It was oddly addicting and very captivating for such a simple game, but was also very relaxing and simple to play. Here are my PROs and CONs for Eternal Senia.
PROs:
- Well paced and emotional plot
- Has a very nice game Length
- Simple mechanics for most everything
- Wonderful music!
- Pretty art!
- Effective and easy for farming and crafting
CONs:

Despite the completely rekt gen chat, this game was by far one of my favorite games. I actually grew up playing this game, and I really appreciate the concept of it, as no other game can come close to what this game achieves. The best cops and robbers style 3ps I've played, with many more specific qualities that I find unmatched in any competing game. While there are many things I've liked and enjoyed about playing this game over the years, there's also been things I couldn't stand. For instance, the grouping system, always been unbalanced, despite the devs attempts to fix it. There was always a loop hole,  or some way for people to get grouped with or against way higher skilled people. It became nearly unbearable at times, because there was a point where Trainees would get stuck fighting Gold skilled people who had bumped their skill rank to bronze just to get easy kills and rewards. As alot of people seem to admire the PvP qualities of the game, I'd much rather have enjoyed seeing less harsh gameplay for less skilled people, or even casual players who love the concept of the game but just can't stay up to par with the all intensely competitve players.
Overall, the game is amazing for what it is, but with its faults.. playing it comes with a price. Are you up for rage quitting more often than usual? Regardless, the game has always been fun to me. So if I had to rate it with 0 to 5 stars, id give it about 4 to 4.5.

I'll be honest with you, I liked the first game, but I never finished it.  I hopped on that bandwagon a little too late, and before I knew it the second game was hot off the press and on my hard drive.  Nevertheless, I played enough of the first one to get the idea, and Dark Souls II is a remarkable improvement over it's predecessor.  Everything I didn't like about the first game has been fixed, and in more ways than I expected.  I don't understand why some people say the graphics aren't that great either -- the game runs on the highest settings quite easily, and I haven't seen anything that really stood out to me as far as bad graphics go.
The only thing I don't like about the Souls series, on a big picture scale, is the PvP.  Nobody ever fights honorably when you encounter an invader.  Everyone wants to be a roguish type or a magic user, and they almost always circle around you like a noob and this is Call of Duty or something, totally negating all of the same tactics you've used to previously.  Then there's the times when you find messages on the ground and people intentially mislead you or block your ability to use whatever you need the "use" button for.  I understand it's a joke, and that it's the nature of the game, but it's those kind of things that deter me from playing the game at all.  It's bittersweet.  I accidentally killed an NPC because someone left a message saying it was a "Sniper Spot".  After aggro'ing the NPC, I was forced to murder him, and that really upset me highly.  Plus, I have never been invaded outside of an, erhm, "designated invasion area", and I'm wondering if that's a good thing or a bad thing.
Apart from its flaws, I have to recommend it because it's such an addictive and mesmerizing game.  The environments, the subtle and intuitive design, the combat....it's all so perfect.  It's loads of fun and you won't be able to put it down, especially since they took all of the flaws of the first game and flipped them around quite literally, turning them into strengths in this title.  I can't ignore the fact though that some flaws of the series are deeply rooted, and how much they matter depends on what kind of gamer you are, if an honorable one at all.

Short of it:
Gameplay has taken a vast improvement. Level design is not as intricate or complex as its predecessor. Story is pretty awesome, but sometimes it just feels like a re-hash of the predecessor.
Long of it:
I'm trying to be as unbiased as I can here.
I respect a lot of the gameplay elements within Dark Souls, the greatest example being how Dark Souls II never lets go of its metaphor. Most games would ask you under which difficulty you'd prefer to play in some tiny window before you begin your quest, but Dark Souls II provides the player with a number of ways to play, choosing whether or not to increase the difficulty bearing larger rewards, or to simply challenge one's self, and all of this happens in game in every case. Ironically, even though Dark Souls II is known for its punishing difficulty, I never feel out of control with my experience of it. That's a rare thing, and it's specific to Dark Souls. That style of play is at home here. I hope that this triumph will have a positive effect on the gaming community and the industry as a whole.
But, Dark Souls is not just gameplay alone. The series is also infamous for the puzzle pieces given to its players in service of story. It's very engaging, and promotes the community to pool their vast knowledge of Dark Souls' arcana to thread a story together. That's amazing and unique, and I can say I'm proud to be a part of that community. However, while I will maintain that I feel this game lacks the imagination within its level design and story as its previous title, I will admit that the more I hold to this idea, the more I feel as though its just a complaint and not an actual critique. They chose to make a sequel within the same world as the original and that's exactly what we got. I worry, however, that story and atmosphere will eventually, as it inevitably does in many titles, take a back seat in the series' design in favor of gameplay, or the online experience of PvP, or "jolly cooperation." Despite that shameless reference, that troubles me.
All in all, Dark Souls II is a worthy sequel: better in some ways, while bowing to its predecessor in other respects. I'm excited to see the series thrive, and I welcome any newcomers. Hopefully one day I shall be the phantom you call upon to help in... "JOLLY COOPERATION."

This is one of greatest sandbox games you can buy, even if the presentation is some-what slap dashed.
If you enjoy open world games such as Farcry and GTA, then you should definitely consider picking this game up, especially considering keys sites are selling it for around half its full steam price at the moment ♥♥♥♥♥and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ for example).
Pros:
-The Graphics are pretty good, even on the lower setting this game looks great, nothing outstanding but pretty good, arguably better than GTA, apart from the people, who look somewhat cartoony.
-Particle effects are amazing in this game. 90% of items or vehicles in game are destructible. You can pull down structures with your grapple hook and they split into seperate objects which you can interact with individually too.
-Controls, within half an hour you will have mastered how to use the grapple hook most effectively and use the wing suit to slip away, out of danger. The game plays great with a controller, I haven't tried playing it with a keyboard, but I haven't heard anyone stating they had issues with it online, so you can assume that a keyboard and mouse works ok.
-Fun, I have had some of the funniest and stupidist moments I've ever had in gaming in this game, not to be taken seriously. It's more of an over the top action movie that you can control and interact with.
-Length, I've played the game for around 25 hours and have taken over 80% of the enemy bases in the game and completed about 50% of the story missions. However there are plenty of other things to collect and gear mods to unlock to upgrade your arsenal of weapons. I can see this being a game you could easily sink 100 hours into.
-The map, the map is one of the largest in video game history (1000KM^2). This makes GTA V look small.
Cons:
-The port, this port is hit and miss. A lot of the time I was able to run the game without any hiccups. However occasionaly I would boot up the game and it would constantly drop to below 30 fps, however restarting the game fixes this issue. There are some lighting texture glitches where they sometimes flicker on and off and the game crashes without fail when you close it down.
-Repetetive, taking over lots and lots of enemy bases can be monotomous, even if the bases are all different with their own unique layouts and enemies. If you are not a completionist, you may not get as many hours from this game as you wont be interested in collecting the extras and taking over all the rebel bases.
Overall, if you are willing to overlook some of the technical glitches and problems the game has, and can find a site selling the key at around half the store price like I did, I would highly recommend picking this title up.

Call of Duty Games have always stuck to the tried and true formula: on-the-rails level design, endless enemies, and a cult of personality storyline that always ends with a Hollywood-style final fight scene.  In these respects, Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare is no different, but it manages to perform this repetition while still being fresh and fun.  The new exo-suit (while an obvious response to Titanfall) brings an exciting new dynamic that improves the gameplay experience.  Unlike Titanfall, with it's sweeping futuristic vistas, you get to use your exo-suit in familiar settings like cityscapes, and office buildings.  Everything feels possible, which I cannot oversell as a necessary element to transmitting intensity to the player.  I feel more engaged because my character is vulnerable, the scenarios are true-to-life, and the equipment makes sense.  It actually feels like a storyline that is possible in the real world (unlike the Black Ops franchise).  Fresh, fun, and innovative; I highly recommend this game.

I only play campaign, so that's what I'm reviewing.  I was really, really looking forward to this game.  CoD meets Crysis future tech?  Sounds great!  What could have been a fantastic game is merely very good due to a few flaws, though:  The story devolves from a fairly believable scenario set in the not-too-distant future into a mustache-twirling Bond-villain affair.  OK, so I can let that slide, I still liked it and the protagonist actually spoke and had a slight personality, add in some likable sidekicks, and you're good.  I had to chuckle at the idea that the soldiers in this game can literally do anything (Fly a fighter jet?  Never done it before, but sure, why not?  I'm a bas♥♥♥♥♥).  ... BUT!  The game has technical issues.  It stutters/hitches periodically.  I think I've pinned down the cause to memory management issues.  Anyway, tweaking your page file size (bigger) and changing texture detail to "high" instead of "extra" (visually almost indistinguishable, still looks good) seems to alleviate if not eliminate it for me.  The other issue is you can barely hear the great soundtrack over the sound effects, and there are no volume balancing options, so you can't fix it.  Gameplay wise, it's really great.  Plenty of variety, fun missions, great special abilities and gadgets.  Very believable near-future military tech.  Well, except maybe the tank-walkers... which you disappointingly never take on directly.  Graphics are basically on par with Crysis 3, of not a tad better.  Controls are as tight and responsive as ever with this series.  Less linear than you'd think, since it has Crysis 2/3 style areas that open up with different routes/strategies for completing large setpiece scenarios.  So, kudos to Sledghammer for making a great new vision for CoD... they just need to clean up the technical issues next time out and it will be great!  I still highly recommend the game.

ESO is a good game. It's enjoyable, it's fairly pleasing to the eye, it's set in Tamriel for all the grandeur that brings and for the most part it really is rather immersive.
But... One cannot help but compare ESO to other games. As an MMORPG it pales in comparison to the likes of Guild Wars 2 in terms of scope, story telling, design (both visually and in terms of game mechanics) and that all important player experience.
As an Elder Scrolls game it feels really lacking. You will remember your first couple of playthroughs in Oblivion or Skyrim: you find yourself in the middle of an enormous new world and you could set off in any direction you pleased and do whatever tickled your fancy. This had a lot to do with the dynamic levelling system where the monsters around you scaled in difficulty as you increased in level and experience. This approach just doesn't work in an MMORPG (although GW2 has a good shot at it) so that classic ES freedom to roam is badly hampered by all those big scary beasts twice your level who will rip you to shreds whilst you attempt a scenic tour.
I know this sounds like I am pushing you away from this game, but in truth I am warning you that you really can't help but compare this game to others you have played, and the results won't please you. If you have played GW2 or any previous Elder Scrolls game you may be dissapointed, if you haven't then you will love it (though for the price I'd highly recommend a look at the new expansion coming out for GW2 first).
In summary: ESO is a great game, and plays well... but be aware that there are better games out there that you might want to try first!

This was one of my first mmo's and coming from Elder Scrolls where I played in the 1st person view a lot, it seemed a little off at first (you can play elder scrolls online in first person but tactically better in 3rd to see what's going on). After tweaking some of the graphic settings and .ini files I've found the eso to be eye pleasing and I got used to the 3rd person and enemy spawns. In addition to having access to PVP at character level 10 you have the opprotunity to travel to over 15 regions from the start (about 4 main regions per alliance, then also a few small starter regions). My first play through as part of the Daggerfall Covenant took me about 100-120 hours. So you're getting about 20 hours for each reagion, and you can complete them faster if you're just doing the main province quests and/or not reading the text. After playing other mmo's like Star Wars the old republic, Guild Wars 2, Black Desert Online, Eve,  it's safe to say that eso is my favorite out of all of them. I'm not forced to pay extra for anything, and the dlc that is part of the game really is extra content. DLC I feel has been reasonably priced even if initially there is a high price, it comes back down to earth. While I was a little put off by having to purchase the new expansion instead of being able to use crowns, the expansion is supposed to be bigger then just an extra region like a dlc. Time will tell if that is true but I can just not subscribe or purchase crowns for awhile and that would then essentially make it the same as a crown purchase. You don't have to subscribe nor puchase crowns, those things are purely extra perks that have a small impact on the overall game. Since I have a job and extra money, what those were offering I found worth it.... You can purchase mounts, houses, bag space, bank space for in game coin at reasonable prices. The story is decent, but don't expect to find any "special" quests that you wouldn't have had in a typical Elder Scrolls Game. That is it's your fetch, kill, talk to type quests just like Elder Scrolls, mixed in with some dungeons (delves) and dolmens (anchors that drop from sky in certain locations and spawn enemies to kill). The only bad thing I can say is with the new system world bosses can be a pain and sometimes impossible to kill solo now where as before one could solo them. Being an mmo though it's hard to complain that help isn't available... The regions are still populated with help abound
It's a very good MMO, but not a very good Elder Scrolls game.

Took about 15 hours to complete and I must say this was one of the best purchases in a long time. This game is the best Alien game hands down and captures the essence of fear. Gameplay is amazing and so are the graphics. Pick this game up, you wont regret it.

Let's start with the easy part: The environments are spectacular. It's a faithful recreation of the style of this first movie, including all "old style" technologies of the time (displays, tapes, keycards, etc). The sound design is also excellent, from the originals effects to the atmosphere, an essential aspect for stealth games. If you are a fan, there's little more one could ask for.
Now for the gameplay. The alien can't be killed, so you have to always hide from it. Later on (slight spoiler)
. Direct encounters with it will almost always result in death, so it takes a while for you to learn all the "tricks" to avoid detection (hint: don't keep using the loud motion tracker while on a closet...). The other category of enemy you will encounter is less fatal and can be dealt with stealth or weapons, so there is a little more variety.
However, It's on the first type of encounter (Alien) that this game will be worth or not. On the harder difficulties in can be somewhat ruthless and the save system - sparse checkpoints or saves at manual stations at specific rooms - can make it very frustrating. There are some cheats on the AI that can be irritating as well, such as the fact that the Alien is always around your location no matter how silent you have been and how far you have traveled. It should be noted that the game does allow you to change difficulty at anytime.
If you can deal with these somewhat frustrating aspects, there is a memorable experience here. There is a lot of tension in moments like hiding from a near Alien, just listening to his steps, or being scared to use the motion tracker because it will give your position away. As with any stealth game, with time you learn the rules and it become less effective, but when it clicks... it's amazing and scaring experience.
---
If you can deal with the buggy and somewhat cheap AI and some frustrating mechanics, this is a gorgeous game, with amazing environments, that can provide some really terrifying moments.

Alien Isolation is a fantastic game and a great addition to the game library of any true Alien fan. I just finished my first playthrough, took me around 20 hours, and it was a rewarding experience. You can tell there was a lot of work put into the game, from game mechanics, level design, graphics, sounds, everything up to the smallest detail. The alien looks and behaves perfectly, every time i restarted he was in a different place which adds value to what your next move will be.
I know people have been giving this game all kinds or reviews, saying its too long and repetitive, the aliens moves being predictable etc. but i found none of those things to be entirely accurate. The missions need to create the environment where you will be alone for a while to experience the atmosphere fitting of the alien hunting you. Also the alien was everything but predictable, you can even get killed from the ceiling vent without seeing him. And certain levels will simply leave you speechless.
Positive:
- breathtaking graphics and level design
- great music and soundeffects
- inteligent alien that actually provokes the feel of insecurity and helplessness wherever you go
- the game perfectly balances tension in different parts of the game so you arent just being chased all the time
- challenging game difficulty forcing you to use different methods and think twice before you make your move
- a lot of eastereggs and awesome scenes that remind you of the original Alien film
- game lenght, yes i definitely wouldnt want this to last just 2-3 hours, dont know why people complain about this
Negative:
- disappointing ending for my taste, hopefully there will be a DLC to continue the story
- the price! (50 euro)
CONCLUSION
If you ever wondered whether there will be a game that can restore the dignity of Alien based games after that horrendous A:CM, wait no longer. This is the game for you, and if youre an Alien fan its a must have. Alien Isolation is a masterpiece and Im sure to give it a couple more playthroughs.
Absolutely recommended!

Smite has many of the things in look for in a multiplayer game, and has great value in the God Pack, which essentially unlocks all non-cosmetic content in the game, for only $30. If you don't want to pay a cent, the game has a ingame currency and a microtransaction currency, both of which you earn from logging in daily, with the "gems" at the end of a week. You can use both of these to unlock characters. Sure, you might of heard of past issues with the developer, but that shouldn't scare you off from this quality 3rd person MOBA. Smite has a growing competitive scene and has over ten million unique accounts as of August 2015 (evidenced by the Retrocles promotion,) and now, 20 million as of June 2016. Servers are on the east coast for the US, and this can cause some minor ping issues. In Wisconsin, with 10mb down/1mb up, my server experiences haven't been terrible, most, if any issues have been on my ISP. New content and balance patches are frequent, and the more players there are the higher the quality of matchmaking.
I

Well, with the largest update and last large update out of the gate, I think I might as well make a review.
Honestly as much as I wanted to really like the game and came back with each update in hopes of getting something that would make the game worthwhile, I generally just ended up disappointed. None of the updates really felt like they added anything, though admittedly in their update plans they did say that they never planned much more than we got.
So I guess in reality I got exactly what I payed for when I looked into the game, however I don't recommend the game specifically because its sorta flat. It lacks depth on a large scale, to get to the basic problem. The game never changes once you've got your first fully upgraded corale. Yes, its a cute game. I'll agree with anyone who says that for sure, but in my opinion being cute can only get you so far in anything. While you get new gadgets and upgrades to your equipment, none of them are particularly game changing aside from the jetpack, extractors, and teleporters. The jetpack honestly feels really bad to use though, as its less a jetpack and more a hoverpack, only allowing for a slight bit of upwards lift very slowly except for at the start where it arcs you downwards slightly and then upwards higher than a jump. The main problem is that it feels like when you use the jetpack you are a brick, its slow and boring and never reaches a level of fun, rather its just another method of movement.
Extractors inclusion in this game are baffling and slow the game down to a crawl if you want to do anything with the slime science mechanics. In essence, extractors are where you get most of your slime science items from, these items range from so common you'll never need them to so rare you'll never have enough unless you grind extractors. Also while the game hides items around the map that you can unlock in the form of collectible pods, you have to buy 3 seperate upgrades to be able to actually use them, so often times you'll find the pods and be unable to get the item from them. Namely this is because these upgrades are linked to how many extractor "cycles" you've ran, which means that you have to grind out extractors for awhile before you become able to actually get all of the collectibles. Grinding the rarest resources from extractors takes a painfully long time, and generally you'll use them on teleporters and warp depots if you want utility. Each extractor cycle takes somewhere around a full in-game day, which takes around 15 minutes IRL, while you can sleep out this time, its not an efficient use of your game time.
As for teleporters, they act as a fast travel system that you have to build yourself on various gadget spots, though theres a very small amount of teleporters you can get from feeding certain slimes around the map, however a few of them are one-way teleports back to your house, so they're not particularly worthwhile. Your house is going to be absolutely littered with these, because otherwise expect to walk through anywhere between 1-3 areas to get anywhere other than the coral reef. This wouldn't be that bad, however it costs rare resources to build your own teleporters and for some reason teleporters and other similar 2-part items are destroyed over just being put back in your inventory as a whole, so if you don't like where you put that teleporter or unlocked an area that requires going through 3 areas and want to just put a teleporter there so you don't have to walk through 3 areas just to check out the new area, you have to create a new one rather than just take it and switch it.
The last thing that is really sort of endgame is a "club" thing where you spend money to get various visual upgrades and upgrades that by the point you get them you probably don't need. The reason for this is because they start costing upwards of 30k. Around 30k+ you really start to have to grind out money like a madman. The amount of plorts you have to get to reach that amount is somewhere above 200, even when you manage to sell stuff at ~100, which in and of itself is rather rare. Not to mention that you can only stack items in your inventory 50 at a time, so its about 2 trips of varying length, as you can hold 4 different plorts at a time. So in total, that means you need to make about 2 trips with 2 different largos who need to be the rarer/more monetarily valuable slime mixes. That doesn't seem like much, but you have to do this repeatedly and go well past 30k. Its not like grinding plorts is a fast process either, you have to grow fruit and veggies, then pump them into auto-feeders and wait. This isn't a particularly long process, but its long enough to be annoying.
So yeah, thats about all the game depth really. Corraling slimes and making largos is so simple its not worth mentioning. I know this review doesn't really have any sort of succinct thought line, so sorry about that. I guess my main thought though is that the game is essentially a worse version of games like harvest moon, stardew valley and other such games. Go play/buy those games if you want a better calming management sim. They do it a lot better and on a more complex level. If you want a game just to be cute, then sure go for this game. Though you could probably just watch some videos of this game and some cute animal videos and get about the same effect. Its not a bad game and if you enjoy it good for you, though I wish it was something more than what it currently is. Though the devs have said theres going to be some other smaller changes, so maybe that'll be what I wanted.

Opinion:
The world is huge, the building aspect is fun, survival is engaging, looting is fun. The main reason i play this game is because of the PVP. Headshots will kill, if you're good/lucky, you can survive a 2 on 1 battle, even if they're better geared. The biggest downfall of this game is solo play. People will not trust you to allow you into their group/tribe/clan, as you can do too much damage. If you do not start the game with other people it is incredibly difficult to start out.
Game Aspects:
-Survival - (Heat, Cold, Hunger, Health) all things you must pay attention to. (Not annoying but engaging)
-Building - Very well built building system that allows every base to be different.
-PVE - Creatures at any level of progression can be dangerous, such as Yeti.
-PVP - There is no real armor, a top level player with an assault rifle can die to someone with a spear if hes good. There are Hit Boxes, a headshot is a 1 hit kill.
-Map - Huge world with different biomes, each with unique creatures and loot to be found.
-Death - If you die, you lose only the loot you've found. The equipment you have you do not lose, (unless you're on a full loot server or have infamy)
-Infamy - If you kill someone, you will gain infamy for a certain amount of time, the more you kill the longer it is. If you die with infamy you can lose a piece of equipment which others can pickup.
Cons:
1. Lag on servers occasionally.
2. Hordes of people named "我是一个混蛋" trying to kill you.
3. Very difficult to get started, incredibly difficult to get started solo.
4. Not fun if you're playing alone, starting out anyway.
5. Randomly hit with huge FPS drops (less than 1FPS) experienced on two different PCs.
Pros:
1. Runs well at maxed graphics.
2. PVP is a blast.
3. Infamy system is fantastic.
4. Tons of fun if you're playing with friends.
5. Yell Merica and people will come to your aid.
6. Hitboxes, If you shoot an arrow and hit someone in the head, they die.
7. Official Servers are wiped every 20 days - This allows people who are new to join a fresh server, additionally allows people who have been playing to keep the game interesting.

AMD 8350
GTX 970 SLI
Samsung Evo 840 SSD
16gb PNY 1333mhz.

This is one of greatest sandbox games you can buy, even if the presentation is some-what slap dashed.
If you enjoy open world games such as Farcry and GTA, then you should definitely consider picking this game up, especially considering keys sites are selling it for around half its full steam price at the moment ♥♥♥♥♥and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ for example).
Pros:
-The Graphics are pretty good, even on the lower setting this game looks great, nothing outstanding but pretty good, arguably better than GTA, apart from the people, who look somewhat cartoony.
-Particle effects are amazing in this game. 90% of items or vehicles in game are destructible. You can pull down structures with your grapple hook and they split into seperate objects which you can interact with individually too.
-Controls, within half an hour you will have mastered how to use the grapple hook most effectively and use the wing suit to slip away, out of danger. The game plays great with a controller, I haven't tried playing it with a keyboard, but I haven't heard anyone stating they had issues with it online, so you can assume that a keyboard and mouse works ok.
-Fun, I have had some of the funniest and stupidist moments I've ever had in gaming in this game, not to be taken seriously. It's more of an over the top action movie that you can control and interact with.
-Length, I've played the game for around 25 hours and have taken over 80% of the enemy bases in the game and completed about 50% of the story missions. However there are plenty of other things to collect and gear mods to unlock to upgrade your arsenal of weapons. I can see this being a game you could easily sink 100 hours into.
-The map, the map is one of the largest in video game history (1000KM^2). This makes GTA V look small.
Cons:
-The port, this port is hit and miss. A lot of the time I was able to run the game without any hiccups. However occasionaly I would boot up the game and it would constantly drop to below 30 fps, however restarting the game fixes this issue. There are some lighting texture glitches where they sometimes flicker on and off and the game crashes without fail when you close it down.
-Repetetive, taking over lots and lots of enemy bases can be monotomous, even if the bases are all different with their own unique layouts and enemies. If you are not a completionist, you may not get as many hours from this game as you wont be interested in collecting the extras and taking over all the rebel bases.
Overall, if you are willing to overlook some of the technical glitches and problems the game has, and can find a site selling the key at around half the store price like I did, I would highly recommend picking this title up.

At the time of writing this I am roughly around 180 hours in the game.
When I first got into Elder Scrolls it was with Skyrim. Playing only that and none of the other previous games I was blown away with how detailed that game was. When I heard that a MMORPG was made with the same title I was very enthusastic. When I got Elder Scrolls Online, I was told it would not be "Skyrim Online", and to an extent, those whom mentioned it were correct. However my thoughts and feelings on that statement have changed quite a bit.
After playing for as long as I have, which in comparison to many others, I have found this to be right at home with my previous experience with Skyrim. I absolutley love this game. I feel that it is totally worth the $60 price tag and I invite other open minded players to give this game a shot. There are many differences from the Single Player version of Elder Scrolls but all of the reasons I loved Skyrim are placed in this game.
The ability to customize my character in any way I see fit, the endless caves, areas and places of interest to see. Fully voiced NPC's and endless hours of lore and other content for players to experience. Not to mention that NPC's reconize your heroic feats as you walk by them, often singing your praises and sometimes even questioning some of your actions that you have made in the game. In fact, there are many circumstances where I have had to make a tough decision and have spent much time dwelling after the fact if I made the right call. Should I have helped fight at the docks or was defending the fort the better call? The result might be the same but the fact that I even had to contemplate the lives of fictional NPC's that I would never meet again shows how enriching the plot can be.
The  PvP in my opinion is very hard, but very fun. I die often, but its not frustrating. Being able to team togeather with random strangers, plan an attack and take a fort seems like it would be difficult to do but everyone is on board and ready to play the game. They want to succeed as much as you and I found the community helpful and enriching, not to mention being able to use seige weapons is so much fun and adds a level of excitment I didn't realize was part of the game.
In the non PvP side, I found most players to be felpful, friendly and very outgoing. I found a guild almost right away and in that guild was open minded Veteren players who wanted to help grow and encourage newer players. Often investing a lot of time and energy explaining various parts of the game such as Armor, Weapons, Skill's, ect. Even non guild members and complete strangers are often pretty nice. I can recall looking for a Werewolf Bite and after a few bad players asking me for a ton of gold and crafting materials in order to give me a bite, one player simple messaged me and say "don't pay them anything, I will give it to you for free." Not only that but he also gave me tips on how to complete the Werewolf single player quest.
I plan on sticking with this MMORPG for a very long time. Its fun, its first person, its 3rd person and its live action. It has its faults, all games do, but if you can take things with an open mind and a grain of salt you will find much love for this awesome game. It wont ever be "Skyrim Online" but in many ways I really feel it is. A great story, great community of players, a big wide open world to explore with choices that are unique to your character. Seems pretty close in my opinion.

Anyone who did any slight research on this game knew that Rome 2 had a shaky release - things weren't quite balanced, game and immersion-breaking glitches, and a lack of features from past games.
9 months after release, Rome 2 is in a state that is worthy of its predecessors. The campaign map is undoubtedly, the most beautiful and well-designed of the entire series. There are new features like agent, general, and army upgrades. Of course, due to only a couple turns per year, generals and agents die off pretty quickly. Battles are simply stunning - wide variety of units, great deployable defences, ambushes, terrain, everything. Field maps are vastly different according to location, and you will never fight in the same map twice.
City sieges, on the other hand, are just par. The terrain of the surrounding area of the city may be different, but it is generally the same city layouts pasted on different terrains. One of the biggest complaints is the lack of walls for about 2 out of every 3 settlements. Sure, not every settlement had large stone walls, but the lack of even a small pallisade is discouraging. Another thing, that I hope will soon be patched, is the horrid political system. There will be occassional events that allow you to decide the fate of a random family member - thing is, there is no family tree to weigh the possibly consequences of your action.
I miss the old events from games past. Like from Rome 1 all the way to Napoleon, where a popup would appear telling you of some new invention from around the world, some notable world events - I very much wish they returned. It helped make me feel like I was in the game, commanding my armies and settlements as a real person.
All in all, even with some missing campaign elements, Total War: Rome II lives up to its name in that the battles are better than ever before. I recommend this game to anyone who likes to see their units fight out battles as individuals, but I would turn it away to anyone who wants a simulation of life in the ancient world.

Yes it may miss just a few things that was from the previous generation of worms (Revolution/Clan Wars) in the way it doesn't have the water which was the best thing in those games but WMD has so much of its own merit, it is just simply a lot more fun going all the way back to Worms 2 in my opinion.
It's a back-to-basics Worms game, 2D, with back to over-the-top weaponry and with the added ability to craft the brand new weapons which are both insane, powerfull and absolutely hillarious to use. The terrain art design is incredible with lush and just really damn sharp graphics. T17 did actually do away with the worm classes from the previous 2 worms games which I both like, and kinda of miss. They really did add a lot to the tactical gameplay with the heavy worms or the scout which was really handy to get around the levels, but at the end of the day, worms is worms, you really aren't missing them not in the game to be honest. WMD also adds vehicles, which are a suprising good adition. You can fully customize worm weapon sets along with a whole HOST of other match options. The game is very customizable.
With the game being out for a couple months now, there are also now some good community made maps with really varietys, some are hillarious, and some maps are easily recognized from the old clasic games. I simply cannot stress enough just how much more fun W.M.D is compared to worms games of the last 10 years. I highly reccomend it, it runs very well, just an absolute blast!

I think it's about time I finally review this game.
I've had a history with this game. I've played this game since Isis was released, which was over 2 years ago. I remember that I was a HUGE fan of the old Sun Wukong (Hun Batz nowadays) and enjoyed the game, although I never got hooked into it. I eventually just stopped playing and went to get addicted to other games, namely Team Fortress 2. Fast foward to 2015, where SMITE is finally released on Steam. I was very curious to give this another try, so I did. Now, before I continue, I have something to say. All of my good friends know this fact well, and I HEAVILY emphasize this:
Long story with that, but I just never liked them, besides Awesomenauts. I downloaded SMITE and gave it a second chance, figuring it might be pretty cool now. Okay, this is the part where you look at the number of hours I have in the game. Just take a nice, solid look at it. To the review!
MOBAs aren't known to have god-tier graphics (heh) and SMITE is no exception. The game is just... eh. It's sort of bland, but at the same time it actually looks really nice in some places, like Siege and Conquest. Not much to say here, but this is not a game for the photographers out there like myself.
The big question to this is, "Is SMITE a good enough MOBA to compare with LoL and DOTA?" The answer to that question is, well, yes! I find it much better to BE the character your playing as, rather than telling them what to do. It's what makes SMITE stand out from the rest of the crowd, and it shines brightly in this way. I don't want to start a flame war, but although it is very simple to understand, the game is much more difficult to master because of the fact you have to actually LAND your shots. No more "clicky-clicky here's the part where 3 champions die" or whatever. Your abilities matter, and missing one could change the course of a game. Plus, of course, teamwork is important in Conquest, and I haven't actually encountered many "OP" gods, if any at all. Some items are clearly better than others *cough* bluestone pendant *cough* *cough* but most aren't too severe. Overall, SMITE delivers with the gameplay by miles.
Just like whether or not Set will be added to the game, there is no known story. This will not be counted towards the final score.
The audio isn't all that special, but the some of the voice packs you can purchase for gods are actually really funny. Some of the writing is extremely clever and gives the game a LOT of personality.
Compared to DOTA and LoL, this game is much easier to pick up and play, although still being a very competitive game. The community, although not sunshine and rainbows, is much easier to deal with and far friendlier than those other toxic wastes of "communities." The gameplay, as said earlier, is simple and it doesn't require too much experience to understand, however I would recommend staying away from Conquest in that case. There are also daily rewards, but I don't like the fact that the prizes don't get increasingly better after 7 days, because it doesn't feel right getting 75 Favor for playing 8 days of SMITE. Invest the time, however, and it'll greatly pay off. Trust me on that.
In the end, SMITE gives me a much better point of view on MOBAs, my least favorite genre of gaming. I can easily recommend this game if you don't want to go through a brutal experience like DOTA and LoL, and the fact that it brings out its differences with pride makes it one of the most enjoyable and addictive games I've played since Team Fortress 2.

Alien Isolation is a fantastic game and a great addition to the game library of any true Alien fan. I just finished my first playthrough, took me around 20 hours, and it was a rewarding experience. You can tell there was a lot of work put into the game, from game mechanics, level design, graphics, sounds, everything up to the smallest detail. The alien looks and behaves perfectly, every time i restarted he was in a different place which adds value to what your next move will be.
I know people have been giving this game all kinds or reviews, saying its too long and repetitive, the aliens moves being predictable etc. but i found none of those things to be entirely accurate. The missions need to create the environment where you will be alone for a while to experience the atmosphere fitting of the alien hunting you. Also the alien was everything but predictable, you can even get killed from the ceiling vent without seeing him. And certain levels will simply leave you speechless.
Positive:
- breathtaking graphics and level design
- great music and soundeffects
- inteligent alien that actually provokes the feel of insecurity and helplessness wherever you go
- the game perfectly balances tension in different parts of the game so you arent just being chased all the time
- challenging game difficulty forcing you to use different methods and think twice before you make your move
- a lot of eastereggs and awesome scenes that remind you of the original Alien film
- game lenght, yes i definitely wouldnt want this to last just 2-3 hours, dont know why people complain about this
Negative:
- disappointing ending for my taste, hopefully there will be a DLC to continue the story
- the price! (50 euro)
CONCLUSION
If you ever wondered whether there will be a game that can restore the dignity of Alien based games after that horrendous A:CM, wait no longer. This is the game for you, and if youre an Alien fan its a must have. Alien Isolation is a masterpiece and Im sure to give it a couple more playthroughs.
Absolutely recommended!

This is a truly unique, challenging and different experience. It is totally alien to most FPS games out there, and stands alone. While many others has mentioned how terrifying it is, the cat and mouse aspect of the game is new and unique. If you strip down the atmosphere and terror, it essentially is hide-and-seek, with an excellently crafted AI.
Might not be everyone's cup of tea though.

If you're interested in the short version:
The game captures the look and feel of the Alien universe perfectly.  Gameplay is stealth based, and incredibly tense.  Sound design is second to none, it really is that good.  Story isn't over complicated.  The game's difficulty is perfectly pitched when playing on normal, although Hard isn't excruciatingly bad...
The only problems are that the lip-synching is very poorly excecuted and there is a bizarre lack of Anti-Aliasing (it says you can use FXAA, SMAA T1x or SMAA T2x, but they don't do anything, at least with my GTX 780).  It's not a HUGE problem, but sometimes the sparkle from jaggies does look a bit... embarrassing.  Especially as the graphics on the whole are superb.
All in all it is an absolutely cracking game.  Yeah.  Get it.

Broforce is an intense celebration of the action movie genre turned into an explosive mess of mayhem on a pixelated backdrop. Every single character has bro in their name in some form of the other; Indiana Brones, Brobo Cop, Doublebro Seven to name a few. They’ve also been heavily muscilized from their already beefed up bodies in whatever movie they’re from, which Broforce lets you admire by flexing in-game, which, in my opinion, makes everything else in the game just fluff, because they’re all so STRONG.
Apart from the already perfect game play mechanic of flexing, Broforce also features intense side-scrolling action, sometimes in which you won’t be able to tell what’s going on in the screen due to the incessant amount of America happening, or explosions, or most of the time, both. Much of the time these explosions are going to be coming from you, as each bro is equipped with their own abilities and weapons to defeat and Americanize their enemies with as much violence as possible. Such enemies include many, many, multitudes of terrorists, xenomorphs, and, in the final act of the game, Satan himself along with resurrected and more powerful versions of all the terrorists you so easily defeated previously.
If I had to sum this game up in one sentence I’d have to say that it’s simply the emotion personified that every American feels when they eat a hot dog, throw a football, load a gun, or do any other thing that could be classified as purely american. A wonderfully explosive game, America/10

Let me start with the bad port first. As many negative reviewers said, this game has a abysmal console port EVER !. If you have controller, you will not have the issue. Nevertheless, if you have only keyboard + mouse, You will have to spend 1-2 hours learning how to play with keyboard. Even after you know how to do every moveset, you still have a delay. Anyway, you still can play this game with keyboard + mouse. Me too struggled at first but now totally fine.
Second, the Graphic is unacceptable if you compare to PC RPG game nowadays. So even without keyboard issue, this game cannot get perfect score. No zooming to the face when you talk to NPC, NPC mouth is shut. Character creation is bare bone. Begining cinematic is a lie. You will not see cinematic like that again in the game. The only cinematics left are seen when you fight a boss, which most of them are mediocre.
Third, there is a very little story in this game, or I could say this game has no story at all, no quest or whatever. You just have to put yourself through the end of the game, that's it. This game is pretty much like a hack&slash game if you ask me.
However, even with these very poor features, this game still has its huge merit, that is THE CHARISMA of the game. or in another word, THE CHALLENGE, which is very unique if it is compared with most RPG games in the market. EVERY TIME YOU DIE, THE GAME WILL PUNISH YOU, this concept adds the unique tense that I never had before in other games. Every death will decrease your maximum HP 5 - 10% per time and If you die again before getting to the spot that you just died, you will lose all your souls accumulated, which can be a huge loss since you have to use souls to up your lv and spend stuffs. Of course, you cannot save your game. This rule will force you focus on the game and be cautious to every corner, traps and enemy. "I must survive ! I must not die" these are what you will chanting in your mind while playing the game. There are checkpoints (bonfire) available though, however many times checkpoints are far from each other, so if you die along the way, you will have to run from the start again.
Game Mechanic is also very awesome. I blamed it in my first review but that was because of my inexperience. This game when you click attack button, it means you just committed the attack, you cannot cancel it and you will be vulnerable at that time. This force you to play more carefully. Most of enemies in the game can be defeated only by skill not by your lv or equipment. You just need to understand its attack-pattern, dodge and attack at the right time. Boss's fights are so epic and super excited. I still remember how hard when I fought will Last Giant, the first boss and Pursuer, the second boss first time. I spent more than 2 hours to beat them. I died a lot, many times I made mistakes just when I was about to finished them off ( wanna cry). I even almost gave up. However, after I defeated them, I felt very satisfied. The feeling that you conquer the game on your own perseverance will emerge.To me, there is no game giving the winning feeling as big as this one.
Multiplayer, another thing that I must mention no matter what. This game has a VERY GOOD MULTIPLAYER, which I've never expected from RPG games. PVE, you can summon your friends to help you fight or can go to help in your friend's world. Thus, if you feel like the game is too hard, you can summon help anytime. More importantly, PVP IS THE BEAST, fighting the others is very fun. A lot of weapon have its own moveset, making the fight very diverse. There is no best weapon nor best armor in the game. Moreover, you can invade the other's world forcefully by using items, ambush poor guy while he is busy with his monsters, or be invaded yourself, or even become a helper who helps newbie fight with invader. However, for me, in a high lv 200+, the game will start to be less fun in PVP since everyone will use the same style due to the stat soft cap and soul mem matching is unreasonable.
In sum, I have a lot of fun with this game but I cannot give perfect score because those bad aspects. So here is my quick brief review
IF YOU WANT THE GAME WITH AN AMAZING GRAPHIC, EXCELLENT STORY that has various of choices and memorable NPC. This game is absolutely ์NOT for you.
However, IF YOU WANT A INTENSE CHALLENGING GAMEPLAY and GREAT PVP, this game is a must try !. I hope DLC will come soon :>

i'm gonna split this review into 3 parts: general commentary, pros+cons, and suggestions for future updates.
slime rancher is a very good game.
a very, very good game.
it's a prime example of what early access should be- a throuroughly enjoyable game with periodic updates. it's currently only at patch 0.6.0b but feels like it could be a finished game on its own(besides a few bugs that the latest patch hasn't fixed yet)
pros:
-graphically it's very vivid and stylized. there's a lot to love about the look of this game.
-there's a HUGE world to explore
-good ost and great sound design
-smooth controls
-IT'S ADORABLE, SERIOUSLY JUST LOOK AT IT
-there's always something to do
-tons of goals to work for
-the devs work fast and listen to the players
-there's some lore being written into the game now(personally i don't care about lore but if that's your kinda thing then you'll probably appreciate it)
cons:
-it starts off kinda slow
-it lags more with the glass desert update
-it's very very easy to get lost, a map system of sorts would be amazing
-slimes don't exist in real life
current glitches i've noticed:
-2 of the 3 tangle slime statues in the glass desert lose their plort and have to be re-fed each time i reset the game
-the extractors, particularly the drill one, have weird sound glitches(sound doesn't play when facing away from them despite being right next to them)
-treasure pods that have been previously opened will play the opening animation again when you enter the area
-plort output is uneven with largos(from what i've noticed, might be wrong)
-not a glitch, but the taming bell is currently really clunky to ring. maybe making it so you can press e to ring it would improve the functionality of it?
with that being said, my suggestions for future updates are as follows:
-UPGRADES FOR SILOS. 100 units is not nearly enough storage. it would be nice to have more than 4 types of items max in each silo as well.
-garden plot upgrades, such as an auto-harvester. this would make it quicker to collect crops and would prevent the crops from going bad if you're not around to harvest them.
-some kind of map system. possibly as part of slime science? maybe you can build a map of an area after collecting 1 of each unique resource from the area. or maybe maps could be unlocked through the 7zee rewards program. it would also be awesome if the maps would include some kind of way to see where you've placed extractors since it's easy to forget exactly where they've been placed.
-more 7zee ranks!
-a plort collecter for the ponds and incinerators.
-more places to put slime science gadgets such as extractors, particularly in the wild
-a way to "de-upgrade" certain upgrades for plots on the ranch, such as removing the solar shield from a corral or removing a scareslime without having to demolish the whole entire plot.
-a way to rotate slime science gadgets such as warp depots without having to demolish them
-the ability to sell resources much like you'd sell plorts, possibly another kind of market?
-better range exchange offers, particularly for later in the game
-warp depots with more than one item slot
-possibly another ranch expansion for more plots/space
-a way to see the plort market from the portable plort market gadget, instead of having to run back to the main one to see the current plort values
-generally just more slime science gadgets for convenience as well as more treasure pods for more decorations/curios

At the time of writing this I am roughly around 180 hours in the game.
When I first got into Elder Scrolls it was with Skyrim. Playing only that and none of the other previous games I was blown away with how detailed that game was. When I heard that a MMORPG was made with the same title I was very enthusastic. When I got Elder Scrolls Online, I was told it would not be "Skyrim Online", and to an extent, those whom mentioned it were correct. However my thoughts and feelings on that statement have changed quite a bit.
After playing for as long as I have, which in comparison to many others, I have found this to be right at home with my previous experience with Skyrim. I absolutley love this game. I feel that it is totally worth the $60 price tag and I invite other open minded players to give this game a shot. There are many differences from the Single Player version of Elder Scrolls but all of the reasons I loved Skyrim are placed in this game.
The ability to customize my character in any way I see fit, the endless caves, areas and places of interest to see. Fully voiced NPC's and endless hours of lore and other content for players to experience. Not to mention that NPC's reconize your heroic feats as you walk by them, often singing your praises and sometimes even questioning some of your actions that you have made in the game. In fact, there are many circumstances where I have had to make a tough decision and have spent much time dwelling after the fact if I made the right call. Should I have helped fight at the docks or was defending the fort the better call? The result might be the same but the fact that I even had to contemplate the lives of fictional NPC's that I would never meet again shows how enriching the plot can be.
The  PvP in my opinion is very hard, but very fun. I die often, but its not frustrating. Being able to team togeather with random strangers, plan an attack and take a fort seems like it would be difficult to do but everyone is on board and ready to play the game. They want to succeed as much as you and I found the community helpful and enriching, not to mention being able to use seige weapons is so much fun and adds a level of excitment I didn't realize was part of the game.
In the non PvP side, I found most players to be felpful, friendly and very outgoing. I found a guild almost right away and in that guild was open minded Veteren players who wanted to help grow and encourage newer players. Often investing a lot of time and energy explaining various parts of the game such as Armor, Weapons, Skill's, ect. Even non guild members and complete strangers are often pretty nice. I can recall looking for a Werewolf Bite and after a few bad players asking me for a ton of gold and crafting materials in order to give me a bite, one player simple messaged me and say "don't pay them anything, I will give it to you for free." Not only that but he also gave me tips on how to complete the Werewolf single player quest.
I plan on sticking with this MMORPG for a very long time. Its fun, its first person, its 3rd person and its live action. It has its faults, all games do, but if you can take things with an open mind and a grain of salt you will find much love for this awesome game. It wont ever be "Skyrim Online" but in many ways I really feel it is. A great story, great community of players, a big wide open world to explore with choices that are unique to your character. Seems pretty close in my opinion.

A game I wanted to love so much but am unable to completely embrace, Total War: Rome II is largely a disappointing sequel. Being the successor to Rome: Total War, there are some pretty big shoes to fill. Yes, Rome II provides a splendid variety of units and the unique factions - an aspect which Shogun 2 lacked. Yes, it is a great leap in graphics in comparison to its predecessor. Unfortunately, the game's substance does not live up to the hype it generated prior to release, leaving much to be desired:
1. The battle AI is subpar compared to its Shogun 2 counterpart. (Campaign AI is okay)
2. The game is not well optimized unlike said Shogun 2, whose graphics are pretty comparable.
3. The political system is more an annoyance which drains resources, and merely requires you to shuffle your generals around rather than being an actual mini game which requires proper strategizing and attention.
4. The traits system for Generals are unlike Rome 1, which were honestly pretty perfect a formula with the outcome of battles directly influencing his characeristics.
5. The immersion from pre-battle speeches is watered down to a mere monologue by some unit you have to manually zoom in towards.
I wouldn't call this one a terrible game, it is pretty good without comparing to the other titles in the series - I still play it from time to time when I need my Rome fix. However, it is more style than substance, with prettier graphics masking a pretty unfinished/unpolished game that will never be able to meet its full potential. What a shame indeed.
