This is the best Worms game release yet. It plays better than Worms: Armageddon and Worms: World Party. Here is a list of reasons why:
- My favorite update: Mechs, Tanks, Helicopters ... mounted weapons like mortars and sniper rifles. These are fun.
- The sounds and music have improved above and beyond the last few games that have been released, from the sounds of the guns and the grenade bounces to the music that plays when the normal round is up.
- Worms customization is as easy as it was in prior Worms games: you can create a team of 8 worms, name them, give them their victory dance, victory music, speech style, tombstone, and outfit.
- Scheme customization is simple and efficient, though tool tips would be nice to have for new players.
- The weapons that have been added or modified are super effective and a hell of a lot of fun to use even if you can't properly aim them.
- Certain structures generated onto the map have an interior that your worms can enter for better cover or inside-warfare, plus the Worms' voices echo as they would inside a chamber -- sounds pretty cool.
This is a MUST-BUY for Worms fanatics, tactical games fans, and anyone looking for a great party game. With a little more polish -- likely from upcoming patches and updates -- this is one of the games that will have the highest replay value on your games list.

I got no problems with this game. I've played a few Worms games, from its humble beginnings up until now. I think I missed out on World Party and Forts, and honestly who played worms 3d?
It's worms. That's basically what you need to know. It's Worms. What do you expect from worms? A turn based
Earth type game but with odd looking worm characters that are mobile and can employ all sorts of weird and wonderful tools weapons and devices, all decked out in silly outfits and silly voices with silly death animations and silly victory dances.
New to this game are building interiors and a weapon crafting system, which lets you collect crafting materials from crates (or dismantling weapons and tools you don't want and are unlikely to use, which can be done during an enemy turn too, same as crafting), and use them to stock up on normal weapons or create enhanced and powered up versions of the default weapons. Whilst the weapon loadout might seem small at first, if you take into account that almost every weapon has about 3 other variants, that really increases the loadout available, and also neatly avoids high-level weapon spam early on, or never seeing high-level weapons because RNGesus is not with you when you collect weapon crates.
A feature I somewhat miss from Worms 2 (which admittedly was kind of broken as hell) is being able to tweak every weapon's stats and behaviour, but honestly I'm none too fussed about that as being able to vapourise half the landscape with a super super powered minigun is hilarious but not condusive to proper gameplay.
There are full multiplayer capabilities here including local and online, both ranked and otherwise for online gameplay, and a nicely sized single player campaign with optional mission objectives to unlock more customisation abilities. I prefer this way of doing it honestly, as opposed to having to spend in game coins to unlock them or something. It was something of a surprise to learn I unlocked more customisation.
This game does appear to lack a level editor, but honestly I feel that no level editor is ever going to quite match up to the flexibility and pure creative freedom that the original Worms 1 allowed. Dynamic water is missing from this game (seen in Worms: Revolution) but it didn't add much honestly, but they've added in vehicles like mechs and tanks, and static gun emplacements, which really add a great new dimension and challenge to gameplay.
Just like before, RNGesus can utterly screw you by seeming to favour the enemy team over yours with the placement of drops, but you're always able to choose the nuclear option and destroy the crates to deny them the chance to get them, and also maybe hurt them a bit in the process too. Your safety cannot be guaranteed if you choose that path however. Some people.... take exception....
Just like the previous Worms games you may find yourself dying as a result of your own weapons when a previously unseen tiny pixel of ground remains right in front of you, that just so happens to be juuuust the right size to block your otherwise perfectly aimed bazooka shot. which WOULD have killed four of your enemy's worms in one, but instead just embarasses you and wastes your turn... oh and allows them to chain reaction kill you and the rest of your team. :D
Other than that though, same old, but still really good fun! Tried one multiplayer match, got an opponent straight away, gave them a good fight and ultimately lost due to pixels of earth repeatedly smacking me in the face :) Good fun all around!

It really doesn't matter how good the game is; it's good, and if, like me, you are a passionate fan of the alien universe and you've been waiting decades for a good game set within it, then I am happy to report, practically with tears in my eyes, that this is the one we have been waiting for all this time.  This is the first video game to present the alien with the gravity that it deserves; not only that, it nails the atmosphere gloriously.  If you're the type who watches these movies regularly, you'll feel right at home.
And if you're not?  This is a stealth adventure game, with a little more action than something like Amnesia.  Alien actually feels more like Penumbra, except orders of magnitude better.  If you're good with your resources, it isn't difficult to take enemies out, but it is usually the better option, and encouraged, to sneak your way through the environment.  There are enough side paths and optional tricks, traps and diversions available to suit any needs, leaving you with plenty of ways to get through a map.
These sections leave you in the perfect mood for your encounters with the alien, which are the meat of the game and the experience we bought the ticket for.  The alien is terrifying, unstoppable and, least comfortingly of all, anywhere.  It is a beautiful monster, this perfect specimen.
And it is an excellent game.  Recommended if you like atmosphere and mood, tension in your games; build-up and pacing rather than prolonged intensity.  Alien is tense, but it isn't an action game.  Play it with the lights off, preferably alone.  I've waited for this, patiently and with fervor; it has not disappointed.

A game that features a plethora of immortal beings to duke it out on the battlefield seems like it would be a great idea, and for the most part it is. However, this game is flawed in many areas. Here is my honest opinion about a game that gets a lot of hype. Is it worthy of it?
Upsides to this game include a massive and evergrowing character roster from across many different mythologies. I enjoy playing characters from Norse and Greek mythology the most, and Fenrir is my main wolf-thing. It also features distinct game modes that split into two groups: Battlefield combat, consisting of Joust and Conquest mode, and also the Arena style combat. I prefer Arena, because it seems less tactical and more pure might, as this game should embody. It can be fun to play...sometimes.
My problems with the game reside with its balancing issues, the incredibly infuriating lobby issues, the lack of diversity in gameplay, and the currency balancing. I'll go over each in depth to emphasize why this game does not deserve high praise.
Many of the characters in Smite, although cool, have a definite categorization of either Ridiculously Powerful like Hades, or Sadly Weak like...a lot of the characters. A major problem arises with how the leveling process takes place as well. Leveling up means that one player has more of an advantage over another, and that is something that runs sour in my tastes.
While I praise the complexity of the gamemodes present within Smite, but as previously stated, it only has 2 major play styles, tactical combat and barbaric mortal combat. Switch ups in gameplay could be interesting as a game changer, adding in new game modes that deviate from the existing ones greatly. Maybe add something humourous in a new game mode, like having the gods play soccer, and maybe I could be a bit swayed towards more praise, but for now the gameplay disappoints me greatly.
The currency in this game is your typical run-of-the-mill game, one currency earned through putting hours into the game, and the other being the premium that you have to bleed out of your wallet for (not cool, ever). Gaining favour seems unnecessarily difficult, and makes unlocking characters a pain, and getting new skins requires me to hand over my real life earnings.
Lastly...the most aggravating of all the Smite flaws, lobby issues. Firstly, I must complain about how matches are set up. Once you connect to a lobby, EVERYONE has to accept, otherwise everyone is kicked out and have to keep waiting. This is a big no no, because someone is going to purposefully not accept the challenge just to annoy people. Instead of this, automatically force the player into the character selection regardless of whether or not you accept. You chose to be in the queue, so what were you expecting? Also, if someone decides to disconnect during a match, their avatar is just left to stand idle and do NOTHING. As if this weren't annoying enough, nothing is done to balance out the teams, so if one team loses 2 players for whatever reason, you're left with a 3-5 matchup, which is not fair. This issue MUST be resolved, and it honestly soils my fun in this game.
Overall, the concept of this game is interesting, but its gameplay is handled poorly, and its effort to even the playing field is even weaker. Please fix this, otherwise I likely will only come back once in a while for returning bonuses.
Final Mark: 3/5

This is my review without playing DS1 before . At my first time play through,because of terrible port. I almost ditched this game but on a second thought, I gave it another try by overlooking bad port and poor graphic. This time I really enjoyed the game. I  played it till the end and still want to play more so I would like you guys to read my review first, you will understand why this game has a lot of lovers and haters at the same time, and whether this game suits your taste or not.
Let me start with the bad port first. As many negative reviewers said, this game has a abysmal console port EVER !. If you have controller, you will not have the issue. Nevertheless, if you have only keyboard + mouse, You will have to spend 1-2 hours learning how to play with keyboard. Even after you know how to do every moveset, you still have a delay. Anyway, you still can play this game with keyboard + mouse. Me too struggled at first but now totally fine.
Second, the Graphic is unacceptable if you compare to PC RPG game nowadays. So even without keyboard issue, this game cannot get perfect score. No zooming to the face when you talk to NPC, NPC mouth is shut. Character creation is bare bone. Begining cinematic is a lie. You will not see cinematic like that again in the game. The only cinematics left are seen when you fight a boss, which most of them are mediocre.
Third, there is a very little story in this game, or I could say this game has no story at all, no quest or whatever. You just have to put yourself through the end of the game, that's it. This game is pretty much like a hack&slash game if you ask me.
However, even with these very poor features, this game still has its huge merit, that is THE CHARISMA of the game. or in another word, THE CHALLENGE, which is very unique if it is compared with most RPG games in the market. EVERY TIME YOU DIE, THE GAME WILL PUNISH YOU, this concept adds the unique tense that I never had before in other games. Every death will decrease your maximum HP 5 - 10% per time and If you die again before getting to the spot that you just died, you will lose all your souls accumulated, which can be a huge loss since you have to use souls to up your lv and spend stuffs. Of course, you cannot save your game. This rule will force you focus on the game and be cautious to every corner, traps and enemy. "I must survive ! I must not die" these are what you will chanting in your mind while playing the game. There are checkpoints (bonfire) available though, however many times checkpoints are far from each other, so if you die along the way, you will have to run from the start again.
Game Mechanic is also very awesome. I blamed it in my first review but that was because of my inexperience. This game when you click attack button, it means you just committed the attack, you cannot cancel it and you will be vulnerable at that time. This force you to play more carefully. Most of enemies in the game can be defeated only by skill not by your lv or equipment. You just need to understand its attack-pattern, dodge and attack at the right time. Boss's fights are so epic and super excited. I still remember how hard when I fought will Last Giant, the first boss and Pursuer, the second boss first time. I spent more than 2 hours to beat them. I died a lot, many times I made mistakes just when I was about to finished them off ( wanna cry). I even almost gave up. However, after I defeated them, I felt very satisfied. The feeling that you conquer the game on your own perseverance will emerge.To me, there is no game giving the winning feeling as big as this one.
Multiplayer, another thing that I must mention no matter what. This game has a VERY GOOD MULTIPLAYER, which I've never expected from RPG games. PVE, you can summon your friends to help you fight or can go to help in your friend's world. Thus, if you feel like the game is too hard, you can summon help anytime. More importantly, PVP IS THE BEAST, fighting the others is very fun. A lot of weapon have its own moveset, making the fight very diverse. There is no best weapon nor best armor in the game. Moreover, you can invade the other's world forcefully by using items, ambush poor guy while he is busy with his monsters, or be invaded yourself, or even become a helper who helps newbie fight with invader. However, for me, in a high lv 200+, the game will start to be less fun in PVP since everyone will use the same style due to the stat soft cap and soul mem matching is unreasonable.
In sum, I have a lot of fun with this game but I cannot give perfect score because those bad aspects. So here is my quick brief review
IF YOU WANT THE GAME WITH AN AMAZING GRAPHIC, EXCELLENT STORY that has various of choices and memorable NPC. This game is absolutely ์NOT for you.
However, IF YOU WANT A INTENSE CHALLENGING GAMEPLAY and GREAT PVP, this game is a must try !. I hope DLC will come soon :>

I really wanted to like this game - my friends and I really wanted a good coop game and something scary seemed perfect. Unfortunately, the only thing scary about this game is how unbelievably not fun it is. I'm actually a little alarmed by the all the good reviews.
The game goes something like this: you pick a character, you choose a map, and then you walk around in wide open, labyrinthine areas trying to find abnormally large recorders. Seriously, where are they putting all those recorders that are the size of backpacks? A really poorly designed monster starts getting irritable that you're not finding its recorders fast enough and starts stalking you once it thinks you're not putting in enough effort. The basic concept in how the monster works is similarish to Slender or even Amnesia, but in a bad way. If you look at it, you go insane and die; if you don't look at it then it will just follow you around and decide to kill you sooner or later. And when I say kill you, it actually just pops up in front of you and shakes its head (probably out of disappointment).
The gameplay is not fun, there's no real cooperative actions to speak of, the maps are poorly designed and sparsely populated, and indie PC horror games really need to get over the whole "find random objects attached to random trees" euphoria it seems to be stuck on. Even the description of the game is confused: "Once the thrilling game session is over, have a laugh while seeing how you kept walking in circles!" Oh, we laughed, but not at how "thrilling" our game session was.

It's almost as if someone decided to make a game, but then they got sleepy and decided to take a nap...then maybe they woke up and bonked their head on a lamp and had amnesia, figured they were done with the game and submitted as is.

1st review of a game.
Bottom line:  Great game, polished, fun, punishing and developing.
Why you should play this game:
1)  Infamy system.  Although this seems like a small addition, it makes all the difference in the world for the game.  Contrary to what others say, you aren't KOS to everyone.  In fact, on my server, you kinda learn where to go and where not to go.  Yes, there are KOSers, but I'd say 60-80% of people won't KOS you.  Why?  Because when their infamy goes up, they have a chance of dropping items that wouldn't drop otherwise.
2)  Trading.  I've played many hours of 7dtd, Rust, H1Z1 and more.  This was the first game I actually executed a trade with players I didn't know IRL.
3)  Resource gathering.  Any veteran of new Rust knows how limited the resources are.  Gathering 10,000 steel, 10,000 lumber and 10,000 stone simply wasn't fun after awhile.  This game has rare materials (amber, earth magnets) along with rare ores (red, blue and green).  The tougher mobs also drop loot needed for end-game stuff (Yetis, sasquatches).  This creates a nice progression...sorta like an MMO.
4)  Crafting has a nice progression.  Most of my previous time was spent on Rust...where the difficulty was actually finding recipes.  In this game, you know all the recipes, but you need to find the materials.  A much welcome change in my opinion.
5)  Combat progression.  Since crafting guns WILL take some time on a wiped server, the majority of early game battles will revolve around melee and bows.  Any veteran of Rust knows how a new server wipe goes...within 2-3 hours people will be running around with AK's.  Not in this game.

A game I wanted to love so much but am unable to completely embrace, Total War: Rome II is largely a disappointing sequel. Being the successor to Rome: Total War, there are some pretty big shoes to fill. Yes, Rome II provides a splendid variety of units and the unique factions - an aspect which Shogun 2 lacked. Yes, it is a great leap in graphics in comparison to its predecessor. Unfortunately, the game's substance does not live up to the hype it generated prior to release, leaving much to be desired:
1. The battle AI is subpar compared to its Shogun 2 counterpart. (Campaign AI is okay)
2. The game is not well optimized unlike said Shogun 2, whose graphics are pretty comparable.
3. The political system is more an annoyance which drains resources, and merely requires you to shuffle your generals around rather than being an actual mini game which requires proper strategizing and attention.
4. The traits system for Generals are unlike Rome 1, which were honestly pretty perfect a formula with the outcome of battles directly influencing his characeristics.
5. The immersion from pre-battle speeches is watered down to a mere monologue by some unit you have to manually zoom in towards.
I wouldn't call this one a terrible game, it is pretty good without comparing to the other titles in the series - I still play it from time to time when I need my Rome fix. However, it is more style than substance, with prettier graphics masking a pretty unfinished/unpolished game that will never be able to meet its full potential. What a shame indeed.

It's really a shame that not more people play this online. That doesn't mean there aren't games to be found, there are. It's just a niche community when it's a game that deserves much more than that.
If you're reading this review I don't need to describe the gameplay. Scorched Earth for you old timers, and for you youngin's, just think of Angry Birds but multiplayer (probably not the greatest analogy but close enough).
This franchise has had ups and downs. Some really god awful downs. This time around, it's probably a peak for the series imo. It combines all that's welcomed in the series and introduces a few new mechanics to keep things interesting.
"Indoor" areas are a fantastic new mechanic, allowing you to essentially hide from other players views when entering a building. Maps are randomly generated just as they used to be, so are the placement of these indoor areas.
Crafting is really cool but overall I think people tend to shy away from it in more competitive play.
Vehicles are a fun new concept but nothing that significant.
Overall, it keeps the "feel" of the classic worms gameplay alive. It has global multiplayer chat, so you hop in the game, and you're immediately connected to the community that's currently playing. A really important feature imo to keep the community alive, but unfortunately, it came a bit late. Should've been part of release so it could bring more people together.
I've played nearly every game in this franchise at some point. I'm no expert at this game but I'm not that bad either.
Bottom line - If you enjoy, even slightly, this sort of gameplay...then you will love this game. Truly Team17's best work to date.

In its current state, I cannot in good conscience recommend this game to most players. Do allows me to outline my issues in a nice list below:
Major Issues:
Garbage Performance -- I, like many others have had absolutely atrocious performance in this game. To clarify, I do not have an AMD processor or graphics card and have been able to run JC 2, Minecraft, CS:GO, and Far Cry 4 on full settings without any lag excluding minor and infrequent occurences. On lowest performance this game will launch and can run, however, FPS is always pretty damn low, fuel tank explosions almost stop the game from working, and sometimes certain towns and bases give random unexplained lag in addition to the random crashes and unstable exiting of game
Repetition and tedious chores -- The repetition of towns and whatnot was a major issue in JC 2, something we all thought would be addressed in "3." While this game has more variety and beauty, it is hard to enjoy with the combined lag and I am forced to complete almost the same exact missions for Dimah to disable these ♥♥♥♥ing FOWs. After the first few missions on Insula Dracon the game becomes completely repetitive. Not to mention we are forced to complete missions to get certain equipment.
Soldiers and AI: The AI is absolutely atrocious seeing as though it will drive flaming vehicles, think it can drive a tank on a cliff, and fly a heli with a minigun directly in front of a heli with missiles. The AI is absurdly bad at finding Rico and doesn't really do much but pat people down and stand around staring at Rico. The soldiers do eventually become absurd and prevent the player from really doing much with the resources they are given.

Pros of the game:
New weapons and tools: The tether, wingsuit, and variety of guns and vehicles are immensely helpful and more interesting than JC2
Potential in story: The story has a huge potential, include the Bavarium nonsense, but I still feel that it was relatively unexplored and made to be highly cookie cutter and repetitive. Something interesting could have been done with the story, but instead the devs oped for the typical "we cannot let most glorious resource into bad hands, must kill bad guy and destroy. ALL YOUR BAVARIUM ARE BELONG TO US, SO WE CAN DESTROY AND HELP HUMANITY!" Nevermind the potential benefits of such a material.
Destruction potential: With this game, we are given the tools to do absolutely amazing things and to have great fun. Unfortunately, the cons that I outlined above make this very difficult.
Better AI than JC2: Although sub-par, the AI in this game makes an effort to call reinforcements and is reasonable. In JC 2 killing any enemy or shooting anywhere got heat. Here, if you kill all enemies and prevent reinforcements calls, nobody comes and heat disappears. It is also apparent that I can shoot on a mountain now and not have the enemy airforce deciding that random trees are in need of protection.

The game appears, at first glance to be open and expansive, and it appears that the player can destroy anything, but it quickly becomes clear the player can only destroy certain bridges and chaos items. Only new items to be destroyed are fluorescent lights, speakers, billboards, and bridges. That being said, I appreciate the hard work of people at square enix, this game is a blast when it runs correctly. That being said, the performance and obvious shortcomings of the game must be addressed eventually. It performance alone were fixed, I would give a positive review, but the other minor issues combined with performance make this experience far less enjoyable than it should be. Still, I have faith that the dev team will attempt to solve many current problems and perhaps issue some updates addressing lag and perhaps adding more towns, items, destruction, and maybe even multiplayer.
EDIT: I need to make note of several things: Military bases make no ♥♥♥♥ing sense. Surely each base should have some radar system for early warning, but bases have random stuff and aren't specialized. There are no giant radar arrays, or fuel refineries, or naval bases, or even major airfields, just bases with a random AM antenna and three identical doppler radars so close to eachother that they wouldn't benefit whatsoever. In addition, it still makes no sense that random distillation towers and fuel tanks are just sitting in military bases -- nothing is specialized, just random stuff. This game also seems to lack the ability to properly handle the objects it creates as RAM usage shoots up through continued gameplay. If I wanted stuttering and slow response times I would have turned on the presidential debates.

Ok here it is. This is my first review of a game on steam and I'm doing it because I feel this game was unfairly judged upon release. When the game first came out all I could see was hate and was hesitant to buy it, so I waited for the sale. I don't understand where the hate is coming from. The game is the same COD its always been, but on steriods. The campain is great, the "press X to continue" fiasco was absolutley blown out of proportion, It was mainly used during cutscenes and didn't take anything from the experience. In fact, I actually thought it helped drive the story.
The multiplayer is flat out awesome. Hands down the best multiplayer fps out there. Titanfall? No. Desitny? Pah lease.
The exo movements are amazing and work very well during the game adding a whole new experience. Its fast, its fun, its competitive. And by the way I am saying this whilest playing with the worst lag available (internet is♥♥♥♥♥♥where i live). Even with the lag I keep coming back for more.
CONS
-Ok so the game crashes every once in a while. It really isn't that big of a deal. It literally takes less than a minute to get back into a game.
-Low player base. There arn't many players out there and its a real shame. The only multiplayer mode I can play is Team Deathmatch (Fine by me I only play TD anyways).  Its a shame because there are 15+ different game modes and i cant even try because there just isnt anyone playing.
There are weekly challeneges that give rewards that nobody can cash is because the game mode required varies...(shame)
Pros
Game is awesome, If your a fan of COD and havn't played in a while and are hesitant because of the bull***t hate out there, DO IT.
The game is fun, great, and i wish more people would play. It really does need the player base so we can experience the full potential of the game.

A game that features a plethora of immortal beings to duke it out on the battlefield seems like it would be a great idea, and for the most part it is. However, this game is flawed in many areas. Here is my honest opinion about a game that gets a lot of hype. Is it worthy of it?
Upsides to this game include a massive and evergrowing character roster from across many different mythologies. I enjoy playing characters from Norse and Greek mythology the most, and Fenrir is my main wolf-thing. It also features distinct game modes that split into two groups: Battlefield combat, consisting of Joust and Conquest mode, and also the Arena style combat. I prefer Arena, because it seems less tactical and more pure might, as this game should embody. It can be fun to play...sometimes.
My problems with the game reside with its balancing issues, the incredibly infuriating lobby issues, the lack of diversity in gameplay, and the currency balancing. I'll go over each in depth to emphasize why this game does not deserve high praise.
Many of the characters in Smite, although cool, have a definite categorization of either Ridiculously Powerful like Hades, or Sadly Weak like...a lot of the characters. A major problem arises with how the leveling process takes place as well. Leveling up means that one player has more of an advantage over another, and that is something that runs sour in my tastes.
While I praise the complexity of the gamemodes present within Smite, but as previously stated, it only has 2 major play styles, tactical combat and barbaric mortal combat. Switch ups in gameplay could be interesting as a game changer, adding in new game modes that deviate from the existing ones greatly. Maybe add something humourous in a new game mode, like having the gods play soccer, and maybe I could be a bit swayed towards more praise, but for now the gameplay disappoints me greatly.
The currency in this game is your typical run-of-the-mill game, one currency earned through putting hours into the game, and the other being the premium that you have to bleed out of your wallet for (not cool, ever). Gaining favour seems unnecessarily difficult, and makes unlocking characters a pain, and getting new skins requires me to hand over my real life earnings.
Lastly...the most aggravating of all the Smite flaws, lobby issues. Firstly, I must complain about how matches are set up. Once you connect to a lobby, EVERYONE has to accept, otherwise everyone is kicked out and have to keep waiting. This is a big no no, because someone is going to purposefully not accept the challenge just to annoy people. Instead of this, automatically force the player into the character selection regardless of whether or not you accept. You chose to be in the queue, so what were you expecting? Also, if someone decides to disconnect during a match, their avatar is just left to stand idle and do NOTHING. As if this weren't annoying enough, nothing is done to balance out the teams, so if one team loses 2 players for whatever reason, you're left with a 3-5 matchup, which is not fair. This issue MUST be resolved, and it honestly soils my fun in this game.
Overall, the concept of this game is interesting, but its gameplay is handled poorly, and its effort to even the playing field is even weaker. Please fix this, otherwise I likely will only come back once in a while for returning bonuses.
Final Mark: 3/5

When I bought the game at release, I was kind of reluctant. The setting didn't appeal to me, the graphics were bizarre, and I wasn't a shooter player. But I got it anyway. You know how it goes: Relationship went down the drain, you need some distraction, and killing stuff that screams makes for great distraction.
I can't say the game grabbed me right away. It didn't. The first few levels were tedious, I got killed (just what my damaged ego needed), I got lost, and I had no clue what I was doing. I kept playing, though, and after a couple of hours the game really opened up. Another two or three hours and I was hooked. Borderlands 2 was the only game I played for several months, and when I discovered co-op with a friend, it advanced into the top-3 of the greatest games I've played to date.
So what makes it great? The gameplay, the loot, replayability, and the characters.
The gameplay: Like I said, I'm really not a FPS player (old, slow, awareness of a potato at times), but it's all fluid and it's not particularly punishing when you start out sucking like the ex that dumped you. The various classes all have a distinct playstyle, so you're bound to find at least one that you get a good handle on and that you'll have a great time with. The game does ramp up in difficulty,  but so will your skill (and failing that, your gear will get better and you'll feel as if you got more skilled).
The loot: While shooters typically don't work out for me for long-term fun, Diablo-like ARPGs always suck me in, in absolutely no time. The main reason is the loot. They are all giant slot machine, and every mob you slay might drop something fantastic. Borderlands 2 uses the same random loot (and loot tables) system like the best ARPGs, and it's like candy for those of us who never get tired of the thrill of the treasure hunt. You can play this for years without finding every item you desire, rolled just the way you want it, but you might get your most sought after drop after your next boss run. You never know, and it never gets old.
The replayability: The game has a ton of content even in the base game, and so much more is added by the DLC. Over the years, the level cap was raised twice, and we got a gauntlet to get from OP1 to OP8 levels to really test our skill (and it's hard). There are raid bosses (that can eventually be done solo), there's co-op, there's dueling, and there are three difficulty modes, which you can even reset and re-do the quests (to farm for quest rewards). You can play this for hundreds of hours without running out of stuff to do. This also includes increasing your Badass Rank (grants passive buffs to all your characters) by completing challenges and collecting all unlockable skins (many of which are drops).
The characters: If I had to nominate the game with the best NPCs, Borderlands 2 would be my undisputed choice. No other game I played comes close. NPCs like Tiny Tina or Mr. Torque, or even Handsome Jack, are memorable -- with lines that will pop up on your mind even after years, making you wonder where you had heard them before (like Jack's "I don't even know what to call you!"), and you probably won't be able to watch the news without exclaiming "Exploooooosions!" at one point or another. Really, the characters are hilarious, inappropriate, and downright fun. Great stuff.
So if you like loot, if you want to experience some crazy stories with messed up NPCs to tell your kids about, or if you just want to kill some sh!t for fun, this is a wonderful game. It stood the test of time well, and is unquestionable one of the best games I've played. I can only highly recommend it. You won't be disappointed. Promise!

My father's favorite game is the original Half Life, so as you'd expect, I've played a lot of half life over the years. From shooting my way out of the Black Mesa research facilility, to fragging random people online in Half Lifes hectic multiplayer mode. Half Life 2 practically reinvented the shooter genre, and has yet to be dethroned. I havnt played much Half Life recently though, and when I heard about this remake of Half Life, which started out as a mod, I thought this would be a perfect way to re experience Half Life's story.
The game feels and plays like it always has. Its very much a 90's shooter, filled with fast run and gun shooting, puzzles, and an interesting and expansive back story and world. At first I was expecting nothing more than a simple graphical upgrade, and that is partly true. This game looks great, while retaining the look and feel of half life. If you've never played the original Half Life, than this is the perfect oppurtunity to do so, as this is the definitive version. The graphics may not be ground breaking, and may not look like a next gen game, but compared to the original game, it looks amazing. Everything has been polished, and painstakingly detailed.
Beyond graphics, has anything changed? Not a whole lot, but there are some noticable differences. First off, if your anything like me, you wondered why everyone in the Black Mesa facility looked the same. Well i'm glad to say they have added new faces, and even a female scientist now. Its not a lot, but it improves the variety of characters in this game. Along with the new faces, scientists and security gaurds have been given some new dialouge, and added feature that is appreciated.
There are some new sound affects, and this time around, there is music placed at certain parts in the game, adding to the experience. Guns handle like you remember, and thats a good thing, although the shooting benefits from a higher frame rate, and makes the whole game just feel a lot smoother. The last thing I've noticed is the A.I. If you played the original game, you remember how bad the A.I. could be. They always seemed to get stuck on things, and were really slow. Well thus far into my play through, the A.I. seems to have way better path finding, and they have sped up to what you'd expect a normal human being to walk at.
As of yet, I have not played multiplayer, but from videos I have seen it looks to be a faithful remake of the original deathmatch, made modernized. Now on to the bad... First off, the 1st person platforming still sucks, which couldnt really be helped by the makers of Black Mesa, as they are simply updating the original game, but its still annoying. And my biggest complaint is that the Xen levels still have yet to be added. For those of you who dont know, the Xen levels are the parts of the game where you visit the alien's homeworld. This is aggrivating to me, as the developers have had plenty of time to do them.
In conclusion this is a must have for people wanting to re experience Half Life again, and its a must buy for those who havnt played it already. My final verdict is a 8/10. Once the Xen levels are added this is an easy 9/10

With the popularity of Slender and its many clones, it was only a matter of time before some developer stepped up and attempted to add multiplayer to the formula. White Noise Online is essentially Slender with coop: wander around a map with only your flashlight for guidance, looking for the eight tape recorders while avoiding the monster stalking you. It's a notable idea to shake up a style of game that's become rather routine, but White Noise fails to realize that the addition of other players completely destroys everything the original Slender did so well, and the few things it does new aren't enough to compensate.
The most instantly apparent of these is the complete absence of any tension, with the presence of other players turning a horrific experience into a placid walking exercise. This also negatively effects the atmosphere, losing the thick dread of ever present danger and replacing it with a comically lazy monster that does little to impede your progress. This culminates in a dull, monotonous game, that sees you spending the bulk of your time walking in circles through the nondescript environments that make it near impossible to make any progress and becomes incredibly tedious as you constantly retrace your steps.
White Noise Online is a developer failing to realize what makes a genre compelling. Slender succeeds because it excels at making you feel isolated and vulnerable, and keeps you engaged by the terror of the monster hunting you. All of these aspects are lost on White Noise, which really leaves you with nothing but a shell of a game that serves no purpose but to bore and annoy the player.
Don't waste your time with White Noise, and for Pete's sake don't drag your friends in with you.

Did I mention that you're doing this at night? Who goes out to search for a serial murderer at night? Seriously!
So you're given a flashlight to illuminate your way while stumbling around in the dark. If your game is based around a light mechanic, I expect it to be decently implemented. But the shadows cast by objects aren't really cast on anything; they don't even appear to be volumetric. I mean, I get that this is an indie game that was originally released on the peasant box, and some affordances need to be made: but this is the main mechanic in the entire game!
Which brings us to the maps: the darkness limits your view (which was probably the inteded effect), but the maps themselves consist of the same objects copypastad over and over again, ensuring that you'll get lost, and be unable to form a mental map of where you are and where you came from. Is this open mouthed statue that looks just like all the other open mouthed statues on the island a new one, or am I going in circles? Now imagine being asked to find eight needles in this haystack.

On Easy mode and Normal Mode it's pretty hard to die.  Monster generally can't kill you unless you look behind yourself or he gets a cheap popup next to you.
But on hard mode, as you're on the last tape, he actually does chase you, and you will die if you don't get to the last tape within a few minutes because you'll run out of stamina.
There's really nothing to do in this game but walk around and find tapes.  The problem is that the levels are too big with not many landmarks, so you're frequently accidentally backtracking because you don't know where to go.  You wind up going through the same area 4+ times for instance.
This game would be a lot better if the maps were smaller and the monster appeared more often to make the game less boring in the early portion of each stage (he appears more often the more stuff you collect).

No matter how much you hold your breath and pull back, and don't make any movements, chances are it will rip the locker door off and poke holes in your forehead.  Don't hide in lockers!  Problem solved.  You can hide under any desk, bed, etc., and this mechanic doesn't happen.

Broforce is an intense celebration of the action movie genre turned into an explosive mess of mayhem on a pixelated backdrop. Every single character has bro in their name in some form of the other; Indiana Brones, Brobo Cop, Doublebro Seven to name a few. Apart from the already perfect game play mechanic of flexing, Broforce also features intense side-scrolling action, sometimes in which you won’t be able to tell what’s going on in the screen due to the incessant amount of America happening, or explosions, or most of the time, both. Much of the time these explosions are going to be coming from you, as each bro is equipped with their own abilities and weapons to defeat and Americanize their enemies with as much violence as possible. Such enemies include many, many, multitudes of terrorists, xenomorphs, and, in the final act of the game, Satan himself along with resurrected and more powerful versions of all the terrorists you so easily defeated previously.
If I had to sum this game up in one sentence I’d have to say that it’s simply the emotion personified that every American feels when they eat a hot dog, throw a football, load a gun, or do any other thing that could be classified as purely american. A wonderfully explosive game, America/10

It’s been 20 years…20 YEARS!!! The world now has self-driving cars, intelligent robot vacuum cleaners and a realistic cyborg named Justin Bieber. Despite this, the artificial intelligence in Worms games does not seem to have advanced at all!
I don’t think I’ve ever seen an AI worm use a ninja rope or even navigate the map by more than a few inches. However, they can somehow throw a grenade across the whole level, making it bounce off a pube of terrain that is invisible to the human eye and roll down a blowtorch hole, exploding just as the timer reaches zero.
This is a good worms game. They haven’t tried to add a story to the single player campaign but it is well rounded and has additional challenge levels which are more like puzzles that get you to think outside the box.
Let’s face it, though, single player isn’t where it’s at with a Worms game. The joy of Worms is when your opponent tries to kill you with a sheep but it gets caught on something, turns around and blows him three miles off the side of the map.
Yes, multiplayer is truly a joy in Worms WMD but this is sadly where my only real criticism lies. Due to (in my opinion) a combination of poor marketing, a high price point and no cross platform multiplayer, the online scene in Worms is usually very quiet. That being said, all of these points are fixable, so fingers crossed for a larger player base in the future.
p.s. The game also features vehicles and crafting, which you will either like or dislike, but other reviewers have already covered these topics to death.
Honestly one of the best worms games i have seen up to date, though armageddon has a special place in my heart.

Just Cause 3:
It's fun, repetive but fun but repetive but fun but repe... you get the idea!
If you're new to the JC series like I was and you're wondering what the fuss is about then imagine this; some devs and visual artists sat down in a board room played Battlefield, COD, GTA and AssCreed whilst watching Bollywood and eating a certain special recipe of brownies until one semi-bright spark piped up with "Hey, what if.... urm... we... urm combine all this like stuff and like urm... make it a game..?"
The main aim of the game is to take over the map, not an easy feat with the map being so large.
You do this by taking over towns and military bases (liberating) until you've taken over a provence and then repeat those steps until you've taken over an island and them repeat that again over the other islands.
Taking over the towns and bases is usually as simple as wiping out a few items like gas tanks and fuel tanks and maybe even a Commander... this is where it gets repetative as it's nearly always the same scenario at each base or town.
Once you've down one or two islands you may find yourself sidetracked to something else like taking a helicopter and blowing up a load of bridges.
You may find a certain type of item a huge irritation also... monitoring systems, you disable one and then you have 4-8 more to disable in a very short amount of time. Some are easy but most with have you throwing your controller/mouse at the screen.
As far as graphics are concerned, it's pretty damn good. Not just the visual aspect but the level of animated detail even down to boat propellers spinning in the right direction while moving forward and backward. Explosions aren't half arsed either!
Weather effects (mainly sun/rain) are top notch with land vehicles having less grid in the wet and the sound chances such as wet vs dry tyre noise.
Vehicle handling leaves  something to be desired but then again this isn't a simulator.
Missions, some are annoying as hell vs some your nan could do with one arm.
Bug/glitches; Yes
You will find every now and the game with crash to desktop with no real reason
Finally completing that really long and hair loss inducing mission just to have the server disconnect for a while meaning you start that mission again isn't exactly great.
Driving a car towards the next town and suddenly end up walking with no car is a little wierd
Nvidia users have flickering graphics on certain objects
AMD users 'Just Wait 3' more months/years for a fix before you buy as the graphics are just a wreck.
Value; It's worth it if you got it in a sale/discount site
7/10

This game is just very bland compared to its predecessors. This was not what I imagined a sequel would look like when I played the first Rome 10 years ago. Even if you ignore the terrible state the game was released in (and still is in many ways), it just is full of questionable design decisions.
The UI is an ugly usability nightmare. Agents are generic and are a nuisance on the campaign map. Generals die to fast because of one turn per year. Politics can be completely ignored and is utterly useless. Naval battles are just chaos. Battle AI is alright but Siege AI just isn’t there. Although faction diversity is in theory great, all factions and battles just seem to play the same.
Heck, the game doesn’t even look that good. Details of textures and models are great but shading and performance seem worse than Shogun 2. The amount of units on screen is less than the first Rome and battles turn to chaotic blobs after mere seconds. Hurray for all the fancy animations but I rather prefer organized combat.
Now I would have hoped that with almost a year of patches and dlc the game would be brought up to standard. But none of the major problems have been tackled. It feels like all dlc has been made by an unpaid intern in half a day. It’s just fluff and doesn’t introduce any features or tries to improve mechanics. I mean, you would expect something called “Pirates and raiders” to actually (re)introduce pirates on the campaign map but instead we receive a couple of copy and paste factions a no new gameplay whatsoever.
CA should take a long hard look at where they want to go with this franchise because this can’t be it. They also might want to look up “Business ethics” while they’re at it.

Alright, This game is one that requires a serious review, for once.
NMRiH is a zombie survival mod, That puts a different emphasis on survival than most others. NMRiH is about pushing until it is all over, To give it your all until you cannot. The objective levels are seemingly designed with this in mind, With narrow hallways and doors leading to horde-filled spaces. These don't work so much as a bottleneck, but more of a grinding stone to wear down you and your team when trying to push through the wall of reanimated bone and flesh shambling at you.
For a zombie game, I feel this is the best one I have seen that acctually gets that living dead feel. They're slow and dead. They mindlessly wander, almost silently.They are fairly simple to deal with, one on one. However add two, it gets a slight bit tricky. Four? Might want to go around. Eight. Your now getting into deep *Ehem*. 16? You are more than likely going to die unless you have good skill.
Now, Weapons are good in varaiety, but low in quantity. Melee isn't fluid, It isn't easy. It feels clunky and painful to do. But hey, You are playing a survivor that is just getting by, Not a master swordsman that also can use a pipe in emergencies. Guns can be a blessing and a curse. The better guns take up a good ammount of your inventory space, yet offer an amazing advantage and safety. Ammo isn't plentiful, but makes all the difference. Even the bow, With it's O.K. space requirement and reusable ammunition isn't the easiest to use and reliebly hit your mark.
A good thing that is worthy of mention is that you can be afflicted with two ailments that hamper your survivability in a lethal way. Zombies can leave a pretty nasty hole that can sometimes cause you to bleed profuesly, Or they can infect you. Bleeding is simple to deal with, A bandage or medkit fixes it. However for the infection, Your only choice is to find some pills. Yet even this dosn't stop it, you simply delay death for a few more minutes.
The game has amazing detail and asthetics. I feel the dark atmosphere and the collapsed world go together like jam on toast, and the zombies are peanut butter making a nice sandwich. In addition to the variety of voices to make comments on how much ammo you have, or how bad you hurt fit nicely. While some of the objectives feel a bit... Odd (How did I know that this person was calling from a building I can't even see?) it can be made up for in that all the levels feel unqiue and each with a variety of difficulty (From "Hard" to "Never Going to Win") adds a certain spice to it all.
Yet, with all this good, Why have I stopped playing? The answer is that the community has killed it in my eyes. With 90% of the servers being these "Unlimited respawn+items+ammo" and nobody playing on the good 10% except a few people, the game lost all I loved in it. It's a great game, So good and so wonderfully crafted, tainted by a community that made it TOO easy. Now, don't get me wrong I have played on a few of those servers for the fun of it, but getting nothing but those servers is what is wrong.
I STRONGLY reccomend this if you manage to find a game that isn't a modified server. It's make a high number on your list.

After 15 or so hours of play, with so many reviews already posted, I will be brief in my review.  If you allow yourself to be terrified by the game, you easily can be. If you don't see this, you didn't play the same game I did.  The alien will always be mostly in the area you are, constantly testing your plan to move forward and then hide more.  Sure, it hops into vents and runs off radar for 10 or 15 seconds here and there, but it always seems to come right back to the area you are in.  Run all the way back to an area far, far away?  It'll spend most of its time there.  It's obvious, and it screams artificial difficulty increaser to extend gameplay hours.
My only gripe is with the locker hiding.  No matter how much you hold your breath and pull back, and don't make any movements, chances are it will rip the locker door off and poke holes in your forehead.  Don't hide in lockers!  Problem solved.  You can hide under any desk, bed, etc., and this mechanic doesn't happen.

This game was worth it in my opinion.  It was unlike anything else I had played before.  The Alien was mostly unpredictable.   It will ambush you from the cieling and will crawl through vents after you.  I played on hard difficulty and it was very challenging (Which is a good thing).  The game looks and feels amazing to me. The sounds and audio are equally amazing. The only thing that could have been better in my opinon was the npc player lip syncing. Outside of cutscenes the npc's you interact with have puppet like mouth movement. It's not that big of a deal though since there are not many people left alive on the station for you to talk to.

I've played the game for about four hours. So far, I'm enjoying it a great deal, but I can see how it might not be for everyone. I am a long-time fan of the Alien body of fiction. So to me, wandering around a space station that has been lovimgly crafted in the style of the first Alien movie is a treat unto itself.
I don't generally enjoy stealth games (and please understand that whatever else this game may be, it is DEFINITELY a stealth game) but I enjoy this because of that constant fear that an alien will come around the corner or out of a vent. I can often hear it above or around me, and that's a really cool, spooky feeling.
However, it is a slow game and it is NOT a shooter. I'm having a great time searching for clues, avoiding enemies, and soaking in the atmosphere. Whether or not you'll enjoy it probably depends on how much you like the Alien universe and whether or not you're willing to put up with a slower-paced game for the sake of enjoying all the amazing detail the developers put into this.

It was a beautiful afternoon in the dry lands of Craglorn. This simple mage was riding his frost horse, exploring that lands, looking for materiais to a brand new armor, searching for unknown places and, who knows, for a place to drink a good cup of mead.
When, without warning, a ferocious troll appeared out of nowhere, right before me, hitting me with his huge claws. I managed to keep riding my horse, desperate and unable to even think to where I was going.

Riding my dear Beluhga (my frost horse) straight forward, trying to escape from that ruthless monsters, I couldn't see my real nemesis until it was too late: a cliff.
Without any other alternatives, I rushed my horse and jumped right into that abyss, hoping for certain death, but without being devoured by trolls and goblins.
But the Eight was on my side that day.
As I jumped into the cliff, a fire missile from a goblin mage hit me, knocking me out from Beluhga in mid air, making me hit a tree that also appeared out of nowhere and, finally, fall into a lake.
I survived.
10/10 will jump of cliffs again.

+ I love the creativity of the Worms WMD maps. Buildings are a great concept and allows for some fun moments when hiding from enemies. The graphics are georgous. The music is pretty chill too.
+- Physics have been pretty spot on, though I miss how slippery worms could be when landing with velocity. It allowed for some satisfying shots that you can't really replicate anymore.
+- Vehicles are okay but they have limited customisability options. All vehicles are set at an all around percentage chance with no way of changing the individual vehicle chances.
+- Mounted guns are okay too, though there's no way to add them to custom maps or again, choosing what types of mounted guns spawn and what types don't.
- Crafting wasn't tested enough before being implemented and a lot of the game's structure has unfortunately been built around it. I think their excuse was it gives people something to do while waiting for their turn. I enjoyed the time between turns in Armageddon as the gameplay was entertaining and it let me plan my next move without distractions.
- There is also no way to get crafted weapons inside weapons crates and there are only five slots to hold "crafted" weapons, which should just be available as standard weapons inside the regular weapons menu. The current state of the weapons system is just disappointing really.
- Some classic weapons, such as the petrol bomb, the bow and arrow and the mole bomb have not been implemented in this version. A real shame, as it removes some classic scheme playability from Armageddon.
-- Scheme editing is available but very limited. The numbers in there are not directly editable and instead come in strict amounts from a drop-down menu. There is also no way to share custom schemes with other people, other than taking screenshots and making them input each setting manually which is way too difficult.
I have a love/hate relationship with this game and I wish it could satisfy my Armageddon itch. I can't recommend it in its current state.

Pre-ordered this game since it brings back the childhood with a whole new set of upgraded functionalities. If you never played worms before, this game will last you a long time to challenge your friends and other players online (something that was not possible back in the day).

Worms W.M.D. takes what made the worms series a timeless classic, from its simple yet complex strategy elements to its visually pleasing art direction, and added a few features to build on what made it great. Unlike other iterations in the franchise, Worms W.M.D. does not rely on new mechanical gimiks that seem to take away from the pure gameplay. Instead, Worms W.M.D. starts with the adorable 2D visuals and ubiquitous combat mechanics then builds upon it with the addition of vehicles, buildings, and a crafting system. While the game feels to be lacking in overall content and a motivating progression system, especially compared to some previous entries, there is a lot of fun to be had. Worms W.M.D. really scratches that "Worms itch" with a fresh new take, however, until more features are added it will pale in comparison to some of its more explosive counterparts.

Honestly, this game is brilliant.
But it's performance is still having many issues for many people, but it is improving. Arkane / Bethesda are producing patches for this game which are working, and I do believe that over time it will function as intended. Personally I am running this on a GTX660, 16 gig rams, and a 3.4Ghz i7.
Overall, even with the dying graphics card, it still runs alright on medium. Not great though, Battlefield 1 for example suggests I am minum specs (same as this game), but runs a solid 40-50fps on ultra. Dishonored on the other hand only runs around 30-40fps on medium, and often fluctuates both up and down from that number. This effect is significantly less pronounced after the recent patches however.
The game itself however is incredible. The world is deep and rich, with an immense amount of lore, interesting conversations between background filler characters such as guards, and interesting characters. The story overall is relatively straight forward, but still enjoyable.
The gameplay is engaging and incredibly creative. You can do countless things with your powers and weapons, leading to an all encompassing feeling of satisfaction once you pull something off.
The simulation of the NPC's in the game is also notable. Enemies will move around the map along patrol paths even when you are nowhere near them, which may seem small, but in practice makes the game feel much more real and convincing. So many small touches like these, paired with the games innate quality, make Dishonored my personal game of the year, despite its performance problems.
If you are worried about performance, or simply don't want to pay full price for a noticably broken product, then I fully understand. Hold off until they fix it or it goes on sale, If you enjoyed the first game, I can assure you that you'll have an incredible experience if you do.

THE GOOD:
-Great visuals.  They did a fantastic job of bringing COD out of last-gen.
-Multiplayer has a plethora of gamemodes and endless customization, matched with well balanced gameplay and some exo abilities to spice things up.
-Pick 10 (er.. 13?) is back.
-The voice acting for everyone but Ilona was superb.  Kevin Spacey delivers a rock solid performance.
-Runs great on dated hardware.  I play with my friends who have athlon 750k and an r7 265.  They play on medium with smooth FPS.  Much better of a PC port than COD:Blowsts
THE BAD:
-The game is horribly optimized for multi-GPU systems. Unplayable.
-Singleplayer is much longer than most COD games and STILL FEELS RUSHED.  Characters are killed off without being developed and you feel nothing.  The game forces feelings on you rather than creating a connection with the player.  A huge misstep on Sledgehammer's part.  The plot often feels rushed and things happen at an unbelievably fast pace.
-The plot is probably on par with  something you'd watch on netflix that only got 3 stars and you've never head of before.  It's good, but you're not gonna remember it in a month.
-Game is gigantic.  Whats with all these huge downloads nowadays?  I'll be deleting this as soon as I get bored with it.
CONCLUSION:
A solid entry in the COD series, but still probably not worth buying unless you catch it on sale.  I'd recommend this game if you want to ask for it as a gift or if you want to get it on some really nice sale, or maybe even used at GameStop for like 10 bucks.   COD is turning into a game that is almost never worth the money.
VERDICT:
THUMBS UP... JUST DONT PAY FULL PRICE

Euro Truck Simulator 2 is that rare thing, a strong sim tethered to a strong game. Where other vehicle-obsessed devs seem to take player motivation for granted, Czech studio SCS understand that a pleasingly modelled steed needs a pleasingly modelled environment to shine.
On this occasion that environment is a swathe of Europe stretching from Plymouth in the west to Wroclaw in the east, from Aberdeen in the north to Milan in the South. The tangle of motorways and major roads is stylised and condensed, but feels massive. After a splendid week of non-stop trucking the stats screen tells me I've still only seen 50% of it.
There's satisfaction in exploring new routes, seeing new golden been-there-done-that squiggles appearing on the in-game map, but it tends to be the promise of cold, hard cash that gets you out of bed in the morning. Like Farming Simulator, ETS2 has a simple yet resonant economic sandbox at its centre.

I get why this game has so many good reviews, i also get why it should be fun:
1) Explosions.
2) Violence.
3) Contra nostalgia.
4) More explosions.
5) Even more explosions.
6) etc.
However as far as actually having fun - i had only mediocre amount of it because of how raw and bugged this game seems to be.
The worst issue for me was the camera - it doesn't follow your character and instead tries to follow everyone at once. This results in players constantly getting out of screen bounds, falling and dying. Too often i can't distinguish my character due to insane amount of explosions, fire, bullets and other particles being on screen. The camera also constantly shakes which makes it even worse and sometimes just pans to random parts of the screen for not reason. Basically playing this game involves a lot of random tries and death's, and barely any skill, safe for fighting some bosses.
It also doesn't really support controller - there is no rumble, controls are over sensitive and switching in menus is just awful. Quite often my character kept jumping, rolling or walking forward by himself with me barely touching the controller.
There are also connection issues.
To summarize - right now this game is just too chaotic for me to have any fun. I get that this is exactly the point why everyone seems to be enjoying it but its just not my cup of tea. I like destructible environments, i like explosions, i respect Contra and movie heroes references but i hate that camera too much to recommend it anyway.

Do you like slender? Of course you don't. Slender is boring. You walk around slowly, then slenderguy pops out and goes "A BLOOGY WOOGY WOO" and you die. Now, take slender, and imagine it WORSE. Instead of walking slowly, you waddle like you've just wet the bed. There's no strafing or backwards walk animations either, since your character is always the king of pop. But wait, there's more! Instead of walking at a (somewhat) reasonable pace like in slender, you now walk at a maximum of 1 mile per hour! Oh, but I hear you say, why not sprint? Because sprinting makes you go TWO MPH, and more than quintuples the chance of the monster coming out and going a bloogy woogy woo. Speaking of the monster, the devs really didn't try with this. The monster's always this fullbright hulk-with-a-no-face thing that just kind of stares at you until you look away and walk like a geriatric patient somewhere else. Oh, but the monster comes after you if you look away, just like slender! if you look at the spooky monster too long, you'll start getting really fuzzy things around your screen then the monster pops up and goes a bloogy woogy to your face, then you die. Bonus for dying: You can actually SEE what's going on. The entire game is literal pitch-black. That's not scary, that's just inconvenient, like the limited sprint and limited flashlight which is already poor as dirt. Oh, but there's multiple characters you can't unlock until you've already gotten horribly bored with this travesty, so don't worry about it. There's no real gameplay change between characters except some can run a bit longer and some can look at weird cthulu statues or the monster without going "aghhfhf" and turning into stone. Oh. And if the other points weren't enough to put you off this game, allow me to make 2 more. One. This game is a unity game, and BOY does it show. The models are decently done enough, but everything feels just slopped in. Hell, in one map you can even see the edge of the map through a gate and just stop into a black skybox. And two, if you really REALLY want this game for god knows why, you're better off just googling the original unity slender and playing that. It's the same damn game only with better gameplay and less 3.00 xbox indie game crap port. If you are a guy who enjoys poking fun at really godawful and not spooky at all games, by all means. Playing as spaghetti-noodles velma will offer you and your friends a good laugh. If you're looking for an engaging time waster, then go buy something else worthwhile. Hell, even the new slender that just came out is better than this, and it's made on the same engine. In less time!

There's plenty of biomes and the transition into them is pretty unique, it isn't just empty space either, there's landmarks, like the fortress, airfield, and aircraft carrier, which you can find loot crates at. Crafting is quite simple and far from complex, which is what makes it enjoyable and easy-to-use.
Overall I'd give this game an 8/10, just because, for now, it could use more polishing and meat on its bones in terms of content.

I was rather bored in Amnesia and annoyed in Outlast. But holy♥♥♥♥♥♥ THIS game IS scary. Atmosphere, Graphics - especially artdesign, sound - all well done. However it is true: they are overusing the dramatic music. The story is okay; nothing special, but solid and fitting the franchise. And yes, the setting brings back some feeling of System Shock - which alone is amazing enough. However more of SShock 1, which was scarier to me anyways.
There's one thing though the reviews I read haven't mentioned: the gameplay is stressful. You are under constant pressure. The Alien is unpredictable and actually scarier when you can not see, but only hear it rumbling in the vents somewhere around you - one mistake like running and you're dead. And the Alien is an actual, dynamic threat - not some script predictably triggered.
No warping, unfair Alien experienced here. Some bugs though. Once the Alien got stuck and I had to reboot the game once to get rid of an inventory bug. The save system, which does work as in Dead Space with a delay of some seconds, is fitting and you pant exhaustedly and relieved at the same time when reaching one very often.
I haven't had such a hard time deciding whether to buy a game or not as I've had with A:I. The many reviews have been highly contradictory and covered everything from downright awfull to game of the year. Well, so far the game has delivered. I was absolutely amazed in the first hour and captured from then on. So far I haven't disappointed and I hope it keeps up until the end.
And quite frankly the Sevastopol is one of the most believable, consistent, detailed environments I was ever privileged to play in all the years. From the  70s computers, the mentioned save systems using punchcards and all the other the many, many little details in harmony with the origignal Alien. It's given credit in almost every review and rightfully so. If I will ever be blessed to see A SShock 3, I hope the devs are going to use the work of Alien Isaltion as one reference.
At some point in the game it really gives you the feel of Miss Weaver being chased down in the Nostromo by an indominatible, perfect Killingbeast. Sirens yelling, the lights, the shadows and then the Alien itself emerges. I think even Giger himself might have been spooked. ;-)
Now that I have finished it, I have to admit that I do can understand some of the critizism. And all in all my experience was definetely not the 93 of PCGamer. There have been some truly weird decisions in the order and development of events. I felt like playing the finale midgame, followed by some really, REALLY annoying backtracking, that also destroyed the rythm and tone of the storytelling through gameplay. One sequence was not just annoying but upsetting to me, especially since it symbolized the fall of a game classic to a good game with some flaws you can't ignore. And it wasn't the gun fighting/combat you will encounter later on.
So for me, as an alien fan, the first half was an 8-9 out of 10 with many moments that were a definite 10/10. The third quarter fell to an 5-7 out of 10, getting a little better in the last quarter which was a 6-8 for me. However the end really disappointed me. You really could see it coming, if you've seen the first movie, it might work in a movie this way, but in a game, after so many hours of survival of the fittest, it's simply not rewarding enough to me and the last thing you do in this core game is a QTE...great...
However, all things considered, I can definitely recommend it. Just not THAT much backtracking and a little more feeling for what to do and tell how and when in the next episode, please. ;-)
And, well..., thanks for the shaking hands, nightmares and temporary paranoia, Creative Assembly. :-)

Final verdict 9/10
Pain staking effort went into the atmosphere, ambiance,  and design of the Game, to match as closely as possible Scott Ridley's Alien.
The ubiquitous buzzing Cathode Tube styled Terminals of the era, easily mistaken as a sound of a far more nefarious origin, by an already edgy player.
The original sound track eschewing muted curiosity, to the booming scores that indicate the most heart pounding circumstance.
The art, and models borrow with great enthuse from the source, while including their own subtle touch ups.
The team assembled to put this game together, went about with what appears an obsessed determination to  create a standalone story line, that feels like it was a part of the first movie.
The game abides very rigorously the rules of traditional Survival Horror, it is not about winning but surviving an un-killable threat that stalks you nearly the length of the game.
Imagine a Ninja stalking hapless fools, jumping down from roofs to murder the meek.
And
are one of those hapless meek fools (at surface level anyway).
It cannot be destroyed, it cannot be out run, your options for the majority of the game are to move with caution, to hide liberally, and avoid at all cost.
Alternately you may decide to turn your back, drop trow, and spread cheeks, because the moment it sees you there is very nearly only
conclusion, personally I like to save some time and just pause and reload from my last save.
The negatives:
The story drags on longer than it need be, with input driven cut scenes that aren't especially difficult, but just all together unnecessary.
There is some lack of diversity in the game mechanics:
items fall into one of these categories:
-Story essential keys to mechanically simulate unlocking doors, which occur to generously so as to make a helpless feeling become somewhat mundane and uneventful.
-Throwing projectiles usually meant for avoidance tactics,
-Sparse number of weapons that you'll probably use only a handful of times for specific scenarios.
Hiding from the Alien becomes a bit to predictable and even on hard difficulty I found myself taking unnecessary risks because the AI, while fairly intelligent, is regularly predictable. The encounters of the Alien could have used with more parsing. It was always evidently clear when the Alien was there, and when I could lower my inhibitions because I knew with a certainity there was no Alien to fear. Less Alien, and more uncertainity would have done better.
I can't really comment on the plot without spoilers, but I will say its rehashed, and although I can't descredit the Developers for sticking true, the actual motivations behind the driving forces at play don't make a lot of sense when looked at objectively.
In my experience I was able to complete the game on hard fairly easily and was disappointed to learn there was no higher difficulty unlocked, your mileage may very (my teeth where cut on Counter Strike and EQ, not COD and WOW). Difficulty is a component of Survival Horror, part of creating the environment for the genre, is forcing players into circumstances where they are not readily confident in their ability to survive, led alone surpass with ease.
Summary
IGN and Gamespot are doing the Franchise, and the consumer audience a disfavor with dishonest reviews, this game is a triple A production, for the few flaws that exist are completely out matched by dedication to a polished clean game that behaves exactly according to the rules of Survival Horror.
This is a game for Survival Horror fans, not Action and adventure.
When rating a game it is expected to review it based on its limitations, you don't blame an RPG for being long and dialogue oriented, you don't blame a Shooter for being frantic and relaint on reaction. Blaming the short comings of a game on it's dedication to abiding to the rules of its predetermined Genre, isn't a feasable criticism. It leads people such as myself to believe that the true motivations behind such one sided reviews are not at all related to the context of the Game, but something else entirely.

The quests feel incredibly dull and I just find myself skipping through all the dialogue so I can go kill more stuff, this is partly my own fault and it's left me completely lost with no idea what to do - but I can't be the only one.
ESO had a lot to live up to, coming from the makers of great games such as Morrowind/Oblivion/Skyrim and Fallout 3 then trying to complete with the likes of WOW/Everquest/RS; it was doomed from the start.  This is NOT Skyrim: Online, and you will likely feel disappointed (as I did) if this is what you were expecting.
That said, if you're new to MMO's and aren't currently invested in one then I recommend you give this a try, just be careful how many hours you play for if you plan to return it.
