You know those moments in every alien movie and trailer when ripley is cornered, hidding, holding her breath while the alien hangs over her, breathing... drooling... This game is that moment, from beginning to end.
Alien Isolation is not just a video game, its a horrifying experience that will change you. Unlike other games of the genre, AI is not about blood, gore, ghosts, or other cheap scares, the threat here feels real. You are being hunted, and you have hone your instincts and use everything you find to survive. The moments that scare the most; the times when you want to quit and run; are the hardest to look away from, and the most rewarding to survive.
This game isnt scary as much as it is stressful. Much like the movies, AI is more of a thriller than a horror game. That being said, it isnt for everyone, certainly not the faint of heart. Like any good scary experience, AI will test your limits, and you will discover wether your own instincts are to fight or flee.

Finally we have a game worthy of the Alien franchise.
The creators of Alien: Isolation obviously 'get it'.
Every aspect of this game is perfectly in-universe. the maps are sets built for Alien. The creature comes as close as possible to representing what was only shown in breif, dark moments in the film.
The music and sound create a thick, oily ozone-smelling atmosphere that immerses you deeply into the grim, dark, uncaring world of the Alien franchise.
Controls are spot on. The way your body moves is perfect. Level geometry is built in such a way that, even in a panic, you know where to hide the moment danger strikes.
This is NOT a survival horror game.
This is a true Alien game. It is, I dare say, the sequel to the Alien film.
The fact that it is horrifying is incidental. The fact that you feel like you are barely holding onto the next moment of survival is incidental: this is what this universe feels like. This is what a true Alien game should be.
This is a game, set after Alien, that is built from the same creative essense, and truly exists in canon. The fact that it is a 'survival horror' game is simply by nature of these ingredients it was made from.
Totally engrossing, gripping, visceral, natural.
All there is are your tools, the game world, and the incredible characters that populate it. You never thing "this is a great game I'm playing" because you are too busy playing it, feeling it, and desperately holding onto survival.
Cutscenes are prerendered, and they are at an inconsistent, sometimes choppy 30fps.
Anti aliasing forced by your control panel is unsupported. The built in antialiasing is a bit less strong than I'd like.
T2X is the best the game has, and is fine.
These little technical issues are easy to overlook. Everything else is so superb and well crafted, it doesn't matter.
Visuals are perfect. AI is perfect. Music and Sound design are more than perfect. Gameplay/body feel/minigames to operate doors and computers is wonderful.
Full marks. Buy it now.

After the debacle that was Aliens: Colonial Marines Alien: Isolation, developed by The Creative Assembly, is a lovingly crafted and brave new take on the Alien franchise in videogame form. The most important thing to understand about this new entry into the series is it's radical shift in game-play design from those of which were, by an large, iterations on the same game-play first experienced in Doom. And it was with no surprise that the franchise was going to take this well trodden path as the sequel to the original film in the series was John Carmack's main inspiration in developing Doom.
By diagnosing the main problem with one of videogame's most popular genres The Creative Assembly have opted to make the player feel as vulnerable as possible in order to instil a genuine sense of dread and tension throughout the game. The game doesn't allow players to horde backpacks full of guns and ammo but instead forces you to use any meager gadget you can concoct in order to distract your enemies as opposed to mowing them down with little cost to your resources or safety. There are guns introduced later in the game and surprise surprise here in lies one of the games strange inconsistencies with the Alien cannon and potential flaws in it's game-play.
After a slow burn introduction to the Sevastopol Station, a crumbling space port in it's last stages of being decommissioned, the game starts out incredibly reminiscent of Bioshock allowing the player to venture in at their own pace discovering computers containing personal logs by Sevastopol inhabitants and audio recordings that help to organically deliver the narrative element of the game. Once further into the Sevastopol, and the main elements have been introduced, the game-play really takes off with the Alien and other enemies all working together to create a wonderfully organic emergent gameplay style that is never scripted and always seems unique throughout repeat playthroughs. And repeat playthroughs of individual missions will become commonplace to even the most seasoned and skilled players as The Creative Assembly have done something truly amazing with the AI of it's titular enemy by designing it to work with heightened sensors that enable it to respond dynamically to sound and situations as opposed to being moved on predetermined paths with basic AI programming. In short this game is ♥♥♥♥ING HARD!
The look and feel of the game is stunning, albeit it with a minimal amount of dodgy cut-scenes, poor human facial animations and shader aliasing problems, as the lighting and graphical fidelity convinces you that you are in the world of Alien, one of cinemas most stunning and meticulously designed films. The Alien's design and animations are far beyond anything I've seen in any game and it's clear where Sega have really channeled their money opting, with minor cost to less vital parts of the game, to really bring the Alien to life.
However there are some problems with the game, although minimal, and these are down in large part to the second half of this massive game. When I say massive I can tell you it must have taken me over 25 hours to complete the game on Normal difficulty on a very exploratory play-through and once the game reached the 15 hour mark for me, which would have been an ample length for a game of this kind the Alien "goes on vacation", for the third quarter of the game, leaving you pining for it's return. Once the game finds itself without an Alien you are left to contend with the station's second most deadly entity, the Androids, who prove to be somewhat less fulfilling. The game also chooses to ignore some vital elements of the Alien's life cycle introduced by James Cameron in the second movie which I feel are to it's detriment.
On the whole Alien: Isolation is one of the most tense and claustrophobic horror stealth games I've ever experienced and I heartily recommend to it to any and all that have even the slightest interest in horror and sci-fi. Well done CA the Alien is finally back in town!

This is not a good game. I don't want to be overly dismissive - there's a lot of good content here: it's beutiful, the characters (not the quests, the characters) are well written, and the combat is engaging (even if, in the end, it doesn't affect much to go from "tab-targeting" to "location-based" in PvE). That's about all the good though: the quests invariably consist of "follow map icon to key point/person/item, press E, follow map icon..." there's absolutely no thinking, no way to mess anything up (seriously: major heists that could use cool stealth/jump mechanics just turn into talk to servant, get drug, drug guard, get item). It becomes a bit insulting after 30 minutes or so.
And then the MMO part? Not well managed becuase nothing is instanced. Turning off world-threatening devices is less awe-inspiring when 5 strangers are doing it with you. It just makes no sense and turns the game into a "lets press E here and get to the next point even more". Then add in 20-30 people doing the same thing at the same time for a super-low enemy saturation: so you rarely have to/get to fight becuase everything is killed by others.  Nothing seems epic or even notable. Quests should not feel like grinding, but ESO somehow pulled that off (though the characters are, as I said good).
Also, everyone seems super-exited about theft. Every time you go to a town you see 3-4 people stealing. Can you report them? No. Can you do anything? No. It's a fine SP mechanic transplanted to an MMO.
In short, this feels like a Diablo 2 (for really simple quests) mixed with Elder Scrolls view/combat - and the servers are overcrowded.  It would be an okay Single Player game, but the game crams too many players into zones without making anyone feel like its a joint effort.

This is a relaxing game for folks that like to cruise through hundreds of kms and slowly build a transport empire. If You liked 18 wheels of steel, this is similar, but expanded on company side (at this time my company is running 100+ trucks). The game is updated and new DLCs come out regularly, some are really worth the cash, they bring not only extra miles, but new tasty additions - landmarks etc. While obviously the places are far from exact representations, there are nonetheless nice touches that give you an impression that authors feel what are characteristic points not only in the cities, but also roads between them (cute items like location of gas stations behind borders or crossroads that are similar to actual ones, towns not on the map, but represented on the road). Countries differ in the way roads are built, what is on the sides, how are cities organized.
Pros:
+ endless hours you can spend running
+ good performance on old hardware (and I would know)
+ a few layers to the game (when you get a bit bored of running the loads there are things to achieve on company front)
+ some good DLCs
Cons:
- gfx is not so impressive (but there's a flip side - works nicely on my old PC)
- collision mechanics and generally interaction with other cars; it's pretty random whether you can pass roundabout without hitting anyone as it's not clear at all what dictates whether cars either on or joining stop or continue - probably a good space to develop further

Ive played this game countless hours before i added it to my steam and ive been playing it on and off since the end of closed beta back in 2012 i think? i might be wrong there.
Anyways, if you're like me and don't find the standard MOBA formular very interesting as in LoL and DOTA then maybe Smite is something for you.
First of all the top down view you see in basically every MOBA has been switched out with a third-person view this in my opinion makes the game a lot more exciting and engaging it also means you get to see your hero in much greater detail.
There are a lot of gamemodes to choose from many of which are blatant copies from LoL like the Assault mode which is bacically ARAM (All random all mid) but other than this they change it up everyday with what Hi-rez calls MOTD (Match of the day) which is a customized game mode that is different everyday fx Boys vs. Girls where one team can opnly play guy characters and the other only girl characters.
Creativity on new heroes or gods can get a little bland from time to time and the character design can feel a little uninspired on some but it's not all bad and it's definetly not the majority.
In short if you want to enjoy a MOBA but have a hard time having fun with LoL or DOTA then try Smite it's free also if you really like the game then consider buying the god pack, with it you buy every god in the game and automatically unlock every new god that comes after (free stuff forever), it's fairly cheap and the way i see it it's a waaaay better deal than any other MOBA.

I cannot recommend this game enough... A free to play game, that truly is ABSOLUTELY FREE!!! I have not found a SINGLE option to pay real money within the game. Just that alone is good enough to give a game a great start in my eyes. And then the game itself proves itself to be amazing as well, and here is why:
Pros:
- Fluid yet simple combat system, with many of the bosses being fairly unique, and at what I believe to be a perfect mix of difficult, but not too hard.
- AMAZING SOUNDTRACK!! I cannot emphasis how much I've fallen in love with the soundtrack, especially the main theme... It's worth downloading just to listen to the main menu.
- Great story. As to not spoil anything, you have been taken in by a young woman at a church as her younger sister, and she goes missing. You (Senia) go after her, and thus you embarck on your quest... Beware: Males who play this game may end up with several holes in their walls, as they try to feel manly again after they shed tears...
- You'll spend roughly 3-4 hours to finish the game, depending on how completed you want it.. But wait, there's more... THERE ARE MULTIPLE ENDINGS! Your choices play a part in the endings, a feature that it seems not even AAA developers can do when they charge $60 for a game... and this is a F2P
All this good doesn't come with a few flaws, sadly. However, I'd say that the flaws can be overlooked considering that it's free to play.
Cons:
- Some bosses seem to be broken. The basic combat system is a "you hit enemy, you take a hit back". With several bosses within the game, the damage you deal to them is comparable to what they will deal to you in return, but you have far less HP than them. This results in you having to use your special attacks (no hit returned) and waiting for you MP and HP to regen before engaging... The bosses don't pursue you, and this results in upwards of 10 minutes wasted on one boss, as you are constantly waiting for your stats to regen.
- No ability to change resolution. You can change screen size, but on the larger sizes the game becomes quite blurry... a major shame, because it's gorgeous when on its native resolution, but it's too small to effectively play on.
- UI could have some major improvements. It's bearable, and you'll get used to it, but by no means is it convenient, especially when it comes to crafting your upgraded items.
- Minor translation issues. Because the developer isn't a native English speaker, some of the translations aren't perfect. They are easily understandable, but you could have things like "you be angry".
Should you play it? YES!!! It is easily well worth the money I put into it. I'd even say that this game could cost $5 and still be well worth the money, for upwards of a 6 hour story if you go for full completion, or about 5 if you just wish to complete the game. The fact that this game is completely free is astounding, considering it has a longer story than some AAA $60 game campaigns. *salutes developer*

My first playthrough lasted ~30-45 minutes.
I decided to go with an almost full 28/30 server with a good ping.  After playing Rust Legacy for some time, I quickly got acquainted with the crafting / inventory system.  I started near nighttime and quickly went looking for wood and flint.  I survived my first night.
Day 1 - I gathered more resources and made a hatchet, pickaxe, and a spear which I thought was cool that I could toggle a throwing arm to throw it, and was pleased that I could retrieve the spear from the point of impact.  Once I got used to gathering nodes, I found some rabbits.  I miss most of my spear throws, but I did land a good shot on one and got it's meat and leather.  I took the meat back to the fire and cooked my first steak.  I read not to cook them too long, so that's what I did not do.  Anyways, I fed myself then met my first player.  He didn't speak, but I felt generous.  I took my spear, threw it on the ground, and walked away.  I felt good about it.  I had enough resources to make another one.   All of a sudden I hear microphone noise and 2 well equipped guys ran past with shotguns and one of them faced me.  I put my hands up, but was met with a shot to the head.  A naked guy near the event came up to my body and teabagged it.
Where I like this game over Rust is the part where I get to keep my equipment.  Not having to make new equipment, I used my knowledge thus far to kill some deer and get enough resources to make basic pants, shirt, and shoes before logging out.
My survival gaming consist of DayZ (Arma 2 mod), Rust, and GRAV before trying this out, and from what I've played so far, it's looking like it's going on top of my list here.
If you're casual like me and don't mind another survival game that launches, connects, and plays smoothly with a somewhat cartoonish feel to it, then I recommend this title.

It's extremely rare for there to be a movie to game adaptation that's actually worth a damn, but this one actually turned out to be pretty damn incredible. They nailed the atmosphere (without a doubt one of the strongest points of the game, especially later on), and you feel like you're the one being hunted, not the other way around. It's nothing like that shooting gallery, Colonial Marines. You do get weapons to defend yourself but nothing is all that effective against the alien, it's just to distract or injure it to buy you a minute or so of time, but he's always lurking and you're almost never safe. His AI is dynamic so encounters never seem scripted, except for a few story parts. Another enemy type in the game, the working joes probably made me more nervous than the alien did, even though they're technically easier to deal with. The story was handled well, doesn't do a whole lot to add to the movie story, but it does fit in and is in my opinion the best Alien has been since the second movie. Epic length too, took me almost 20 hours to beat, where other similar games are usually only 8-10.

Grab your guns, fire up the flames of Democracy, and take down the enemies of freedom in third world countries with the BROFORCE!!!!!!
In seriousness, Broforce is a 2D shoot-em up scroller in the style of Contra and Metal Slug where there is a ridiculous amount of explosions, shooting, cheesy American propaganda, more shooting, and more explosions. It is set in the design of an '80s action movie/series with a ton of "bros", or playable characters each with their own unique abilities and advantages. For instance, the first bro you get, Rambro, has a powerful semi-auto rifle with his special attack being grenades. I won't name anymore to avoid spoilers and have the joy and getting that next bro, but I have personally enjoyed every character thus far.
The gameplay is fast-paced and high octane shooting. All the terrian is destructible but be careful and not just hold down your fire button because you might accidentally blow yourself up with explosive barrels. The game offers a challenge at normal difficulty and increases significantly at harder levels (which makes it even better bro!). The learning curve is not difficult and you can jump right in and get the hang of the game really easily. The only hard part is adjusting yourself to each bro but it only takes a few moments. Even though this game is still technically in alpha, it has at least 4 hours of game time for the world campaign and much more outside that. You will definitely get your money's worth for this game I highly recommend this game and I think it should be in even one's Steam library along with Far Cry 3 Blood Dragon which is also amazing.

When I say that this game is not recommended, don't get me wrong, it's not a bad game. It's just not worth playing on the PC. I have read many other reviews and noticed that none of them really talk about the third game mode Exo Survival, which is surprising as there is a lot to talk about. Not all of it good however.
Campaign.
The campaign is good. It has a decent story, decent gameplay. Nothing new, it's the kind of story and linear gameplay you have come to expect from COD. It's not very long however, and i was done in 3-4 hours. After playing it the first time, the campaign becomes boring and is not at all interesting a second time (atleast for me). However the campaign isnt my focus here...
Multiplayer.
This is what people buy COD for, and if this gets screwed up... You'd rather not buy the game. That's the sad situation for AW on PC. No dedicated servers for PC users leads to laggy and frustrating gameplay. Most lobbies are deserted and you only have 3-4 games in TDM if you're lucky. On top of this there are often random disconnects from the servers even if my internet is running perfectly, bringing an end to an anyways frustrating game. So one day I decided to play a Private match to see how the game is without lag. I was impressed. I actually had more fun on a private match against Veteran bots than I did in the public matches. This shows that AW has the potential to be a great game (which, on the console, it already is). Its just the negligence of SHG towards the PC port that has caused this disaster...
Exo-survival.
Now in this game mode, public lobbies are far more active than in Multiplayer. Usually you'll find 40-50 games compared to the 2-3 games in MP. Also the lag (weirdly) is far less of a problem in Exo survival, you barely notice any shot delay or lag even if your ping bar is red. I dont know why this is the case, but I'm not complaining. More matches, less lag doesnt lead to a fun game however. Most lobbies are filled with people who have NO idea how to play exo-survival, this leads to failed objectives, repeated downs, and an overall irritating game. I admit that this situation may improve over time, but there's another issue, which makes exo-survival a bore. Bland maps. SHG used MP maps in exo survival, this makes the game very boring, as the maps are very small and often have nothing special about them (you play one, you've played them all). They could have done something like treyarch does with their zombie maps. Add openable doors, buildables, easter eggs etc. Hopefully the upcoming Exo zombies will have more interesting maps, but as of now. Exo-survival is a boring gameplay mode.
Overall, I would say that SHG could make this game work with a few clever patches and Dedicated servers. Until those come out however, stay away from this game! Buy Black ops 2, a 2 year old game still has more people online than a month old release. That should give you a good idea of which game is better.

Amnesia? Played through it without really blinking.
Outlast? Laughed and ran all the way through.
This game? I think I'm out of clean underwear. This is the most terrifying game I've ever played. It definitely borrows a ton from games like Amnesia and Outlast in the sense that it's a horror game where you're defenseless and all you can do is hide. The way Creative Assembly has executed this game is mind blowing. It replicates the tension found in the first film, not only that but it ups the intensity by 100. You never know when the Xenomorph is going to strike. It could be anywhere and you always have to think about places you can hide in case of it showing up. All you can do is keep moving slowly and hope for the best. Then you add in the fact that not only is the Xenomorph a threat but so are androids & even other survivors, the feeling of danger is always there. Not once in my 4 hours of playing so far have I felt safe. I've always felt like I'm danger and I haven't had a chance to breathe. This is a must play for any fan of horror games, horror films or the Alien franchise. This is one of the single greatest licensed games ever made & I'm only a third of the way through. I have no problem giving it that high of praise.
Now in terms of the port itself, it's incredible. So far I've played this game completely maxed out on a GTX670 and now a 970 @1080p. On the 670 I was getting a 130FPS average and on the 970 I'm currently enjoying 190-210. The optimization here is fantastic. You can likely max this game on something as low as a 470/560Ti and get a 60FPS experience from what I can tell. It's barely using up a gig of VRam by the looks of it too. Now with performace like that you'd think the game might not be that great visually but this is one of the better looking games I've played. The way the lighting is handled, the textures and the overall aesthetic is superb! The FoV slider even goes up to 75Vertical (which is around 120Horizontal) so those who get motion sick off of low FoV like myself there is no need to worry!
The sound design is also some of the best you'll hear. Every footstep, creak in the vents, light flicker, sound in the distance just brings this game to another level. The sound design is something that will make you paranoid and afraid moreso than the visual feedback you get. That's just how well done it is.
Overall, buy this game. It's GOTY quality for sure, unless the last half is terrible which I just don't see happening at this rate.

Quick-and-dirty opinions on the main campaign right after finishing it on the highest difficulty. Played the game during nightime only with headphones on, pitch black room, solo. Played through it in two long sittings. I'll play the rest of the content and update accordingly.
Pros
1) Incredible atmosphere
2) Stunning sound design and visuals faithfull to the source material; manage to capture the film's essence down to the core. That is due to both the impeccable art design and the astonishing gfx.
3) Tech is not only impressive but scales incredibly well on low-end machines. Managed to run the game at a respectable 40+ fps on a laptop with a gt740m, i7-3630qm, 4gb ram with most settings maxed at native res. Played through the game on my main system (gtx670 jetstream 2gb vram, 3770k, 8 gb ram @ 2133 mhz) with everything maxed out at 80+ fps at all times. The game felt very fluid while looking breathtaking.
4) Gameplay offers freedom to tackle encounters as you see fit; you can stealth and try to distract opponents, try to "muscle" your way through certain points, fight back or flee .
5) Crafting and salvaging materials manages to cement that sense of gameplay freedom allthewhile separating this title
from standard gameplay conventions found in the genre.
6) While the alien is undoubtably the main attraction, all the other hazards that you have to face manage to be
equally menacing and disturbing for their own reasons without them feeling "tacked-on" or out of place.
7) The game manages to be very intense without relying on scripted events or jumpscares.
8) Another triumph, in my book at least, was how the game made me undergo the same transformation that Ripley's character went through in the original film. From feeling terrorized and helpless to feeling empowered and determined while maintaining the predator-prey relationship all the way through. Even when i had all the right tools at my disposal due to my exploring and frugal use of equipment, i was always on my toes and facing danger always felt like playing with fire.
9) While the Alien certainly felt like it had a certain bias towards me it did not ignore other stimuli
and responded accordingly in different situations making the eco-system in the Sevastopol believable.
10) The dynamic environment adds tons to the game's thick, opressive and suffocating atmosphere with visual and aural feedback accompanying your each and every move. Unwanted noise is created with your every step; doors and vents open automatically from a believable distance. A distance that would make sense for use under normal circumstances becomes a liability and a trap under the conditions that you have to face. Your surroundings are always a factor and may prove to be either an ally or a foe. This dynamism adds perpective and manages to offer full body awareness, immersing me completely in the protaginist's role.
11) Voice over is spot on and true to the spirit of the source material.
12) Map design is incredible with complex levels strewn with shortcuts that can be accessed straightaway or
by the use of upgraded tools that you find through the game. The "metroidvania" aspect of unlocking certain
segments with upgrades is present and you are free to revisit areas, within narrative constraints,  disregarding your main objective if you choose to.
13) Exploration comes at a price. You can either focus on the main objective and do the barely minimum to advance or
choose to snoop arround searching for info or materials/equipment at the cost of putting yourself at an even greater risk.
14) The excellent design choice for your character to not be invulnerable while interacting with terminals or even when saving the game gives this constant sense of tension and dread.
Cons
1) Epilogue (ch 18) feels too conventional and in contrast to what the rest of the game manages to achieve.
2) Shadow aliasing adds "noise" to otherwise immaculately crafted visuals.
3) Cutscenes, while very detailed felt choppy.
4) Lipsync is off. Not hilariously bad but noticeable.
Neutral
The game is lengthy. Chapters 15-18 felt like the equivalent of an "extended director's cut" film.
All in all, best Alien game i've played. Undoubtedly one of the best in the Alien(s) franchise and certainly one of the GOTY for me.

its not the only enemy either however.  desperate humans may kill you (or try anyways) on sight, and failing that, the commotion they make can and usually will attract the alien.  also, androids like the ones from the movies work the station, and will kill you in unrestricted zones, their glowing red robotic eyes and inhuman nature make them terrifying as well.   the humans and the androids serve to create other sources of terror besides the alien and help keep things fresh.
as for the enviroment, the attention to detail is ABSOLUTELY STUNNING.  everything here from the smallest of details is lovingly crafted after the original's 70's style sci fi equipment/enviroment.  save stations are phone consoles in which ripley slides her card into to save the game.  computer consoles have these old flickering crt screens.  things like this bring to life the world of the film/ Perhaps the only glaring mistake i could find in this area is the fact that ripley has no shadow, despite bieng able to see her legs if you look down.  this is quicklly forgotten in lieu of the amazing atmosphere that truly captures the feel of the film.
THIS is the alien game the franchise needed
if you're a fan of the original alien, look no more.  this could easily be considered a spiritual successor to the first film.  an Alien 2 if you will.

Oh Black Mesa, how you've grown. The mod began as a literal remake of the original Half-Life, and while this is that, it's so much more. The mod that came out awhile back (I think I played it in 2012) was very good. This is absolutely incredible. The game changes up a few small things from the original, like where you got certain weapons, adds in some new areas, etc., but this is still the original Half-Life.
That last part is very important to me. I played the original Half-Life games growing up (the original, Opposing Force, Blue Shift, etc.) and I wanted to be able to recognize the original in this. You most certianly can. The areas, dialogue lines, weapons, and much of everything else are very close (in some cases identical) to the original.
I should probably talk about what makes this game great in some sort of list:
Pros:
+gameplay
+dialogue
+secrets
+multiplayer
+updated creature models
+achievements
+voice acting
+level design
+weapons
+++soundtrack (it is easily the best part of this remake; it's incredible)
Cons:
-no Xen (still a bit annoyed it's not here after these few years)
I've been playing this nonstop since I bought it and I can say with ease that it's my best purchase this year. Playing this remake brings back so many good memories, and has created so many more. I was literally in shock for the first few hours I was playing this.
To see the work these guys have done is astonishing. Even though the game isn't finished, it's a must buy! If you're a returning fan, or a new to the series, it's worth every penny. Here's to hoping we see an Opposing Force remake too :D

Certainly worth buying. It's the updated graphics, source engine and a lot of small features (like portable flares). If you're not satisfied with original HL - this remake might be just for you.
Overall: Great game, but still unfinished (what's taking so long to make a good Xen? 3 years have passed!).

Very gritty and realistic in terms of Z-appocolypse scenarios. This aint no Dead Rising, Dead Island or Left 4 Dead, kiddies, it is like George Romero with a slight twist. This time, you aim for the head ONLY (Anywhere else, you're wasting ammo) and be careful with various guns like automatics (Which are all sub-machine guns) and 'nades (Which includes, C4, molotovs, frags and dynamite).  Know the ammo for your guns as you cannot pick up any random ammo box and it somehow turns into the right caliber or ammo type, the human vultures (Which are likely to be kids or trolls) always do this by picking up everything and filling up their inventory.
Speaking of the inventory system, it's really well made as it is limited by the size of the item. This really lets you look at your priorities as you don't have some magical way to store ALL your weapons and supplies on your person like in any other game. Ammo is also quite limited and is almost always jsut a luxury depending on the server (There are some servers with infinite ammo), map, and player's skill, so a good tip is to get a melee weapon of some kind, I prefer something with a long handle if you can find it like a sledge or fire axe and time your strikes right. So, don't just get guns because if you run out of ammo, you're screwed in more ways than one as the Zeds close in to horrificly rip you to shreds. BTW the only gun you can successfully kill zombies with a melee strike is one with a bayonett (I don't remember the name of the gun) and it's not a custom attachment. Also, protip, if youre infected and still fighting, I prefer you do the sensible thing (after actually telling everyone) and save the last bullet for yourself cuz, first timers get a cheevo.
Weapons have had a nice attention to detail as you actually need specific calibers, like the Ruger needs .22 LR and the m16 (Which has been permenately set to semi auto in this game) needs 5.56 ammunition. This also throws in unconventional weapons like the very tools you carry as you do missions, you could try to brain a zombie with your flashlight or welder. Watch out for fire weapons and molotovs as well as fire could turn all walking zombies into burning runners until they literally burn out so either run for your life or actually shoot bullets to finish it off. The operation and kick of each gun shows the devs really did their homework and probably made a few trips to a shooting range. The revolvers, after each shot, you can see the player model's thumb pull the hammer back. The shotgun's reload animation is nice as well as the player adds one more shot into the chamber making that one extra shot a bit more of a difference between life and death. The ammo hud is also a good attention to detail as it would fade away until you hold the reload button (R) to take a look at the ammo you have left as your character calls out how much he has left telling the other players to support you when they can.
Survival in general is a huge thing to look at. For example, if you're attacked by a zed there's more or less a 50/50 chance you are bitten which is garunteed to infect you even more when grabbed (so push them off with V to keep you from getting any more damage). As the infection spreads through your body, veiny paterns appear on your screen and your sight starts to darken. So your options are to either ask to be put down, find some phalanx, shooting yourself, or simply die while fighting the zeds off (Looking at other reviews, you'll see stories of people just being d**ks and not telling anyone so they can turn and just ruin lives). I highly recommend playing this with friends than strangers due to trust and communication issues that will plague public online games. If in a team, KEEP TOGETHER and dont lag behind, as in any zombie appocalypse scenarios (as shown in movies) Survivors have a better chance to survive with more people in their group. Adding to that, watch each other's back as you could be attacked from behind out of nowhere, especially in objective game modes (Survival game modes depend on how well you know the map and the layout of the map istelf).
Now onto the real stars, other than your fellow survivors, the zombies. The devs really did well with the walking corpses adding not only male and female zombies, but children and runners as well. Being surrounded by them makes the atmosphere pretty intense if you're on the run in objective mode or fiercely defending an objective in Survival mode. The children zombies are a bit of a pain to kill, not just that you're killing something that was just a sweet and innocent child in a previous life, but they are shorter and would force you to try to aim down. Runners are a bit of a problem but not as much as the children in my opinion, you just have to react fast and blast them on the face with your shotgun or pistol or let your buddies take them down. The zombie moans you hear are also a nice small detail the devs pay attention to as they have varying pitches and 'voice' like a child zombie's would be higher pitch and a bit more raspy same for a zombie woman's. It's also satisfying to see a Zed's head pop when you land a solid headshot.
I HIGHLY recommend this to anyone looking for a more genuine zombie game as this makes you feel like you're in a zombie movie struggling to survive with other survivors.

Slime rancher is a beautiful game with an incredibly easy control scheme in which you ranch slimes. Yes, you’re a slime farmer who explores the world looking for rare and unique slimes for the purpose of earning a profit. You can farm these slimes free-range or you can choose to give them all easy to manage enclosures. It’s entirely up to your personal preference on how you wish to play.
It starts out as an exploration game but then quickly turns into an incredibly large grind. The exploration is amazing and the amount of variation in the landscape and critters roaming about is fantastic. For each biome you discover it feels as if there are just the right amount of different organisms roaming each biome.
There is not a dull moment during the exploration phase of your journey.. But when it turns into a grind, it turns into an absolutely huge grind. A grind so huge that it makes the game feel as if it’s a mountain that you started climbing without knowing that you were actually climbing a mountain that you don’t even wish to climb – but you may or may not choose to keep climbing anyway considering how far up you are at the end of things.
After accruing a fair amount of newbucks you purchase gear that allows for things like flight, larger backpack, and the ability to suck up water. After accruing a massive amount of plorts, or rather slime droppings, you also have the ability to create things from resources you collect. These things allow you to teleport around, decorate your ranch, or even just display your #1 slime.
Sadly, There is only so much to explore, and when you finish exploring it becomes a waiting game in which you wait for the slime stocks to get to a level in which you’re willing to sell while storing your plorts in your silos. For what? A stupid slime trophy? Yes. A stupid slime trophy. A glorious and stupid slime trophy. Also colors, ranch upgrades, and other things you may or may not want. Most of which have no actual significance to the game.
For a score I will have to give Slime Rancher an 85 out of 100. The exploration is amazing, but the grind is not. It’s a seemingly never ending struggle to reach a level few will be willing to grind to. Are you willing? I am.
Anyway, thanks for watching and I hope you enjoyed! If you did enjoy, don’t forget to like, comment, and subscribe!

Before I can say anything about Dishonored 2, if you decide to buy and play it based on any aspect of this review, do yourself a favour and make sure everything's patched and updated. At present the game patch is in beta, but it does massive improvements on (fairly modern) PC's and I cannot stress how much of a difference nvidia drivers and the beta patch have done to improve the performance, at least on my rig.
Now, with that said, I can happily say that this game DOES have a lot of strengths and some weaknesses. As with good and bad news, let's get the bad out of the way.
We have the aforementioned and widely known technical issues. We have the very familiar gameplay, the fairly mediocre story and it really doesn't tread new ground.
If you're still reading, I can happily say that it's again a great journey into the grim world of Dishonored, many issues of the first game have been addressed, and that the power combinations available in this game go extremely well with the multiple run throughs this game like the first did in regards to the chaos system.
You'll never get all powers in one run through, and there are a number of ways to handle the missions, so I'll happily still be playing this game some time down the line and likely not find all the fun ways to blend abilities to get the most out of them, even while I carve a bloody path through or subdue and cautiously infiltrate each of the games sizable missions.
The low chaos toolset has been improved to put it far more on par with the high chaos one. New darts and combat abilities lend themselves well to even an in-your-face combat style, by shooting kneecaps or deft parrying then choking your foes or stomping their faces to the marble floor. Just the same, playing a complete phantom who causes nary a whisper of suspicion in the guards is always an exercise in patience, just as you can execute everything on route to your foe in total silence.
Visually, it's an upgrade on the previous game. There's more detail without sacrificing the first games exaggerated inhabitants and detailed locales. It's not a HUGE upgrade though, which made the requirements and troubled launch all the more confusing. I certainly had to work at getting it to look halfway decent, and certain settings aren't clear in terms of what they do, with no tooltips when highlighted. It is likely worth doing some research if you're not familiar with what each thing does, because the game does still look impressive, especially for environmental detail.
Sound is currently a mixed bag at the time of this review. I found locations that enemy footsteps and chat would cut through walls and floors where others wouldn't. I found places outside where merely looking up and down would cause substantial changes in volume to nearby talking guards, but besides this, the sound design is fitting and interesting. Music features to a degree as well, whether by nearby audiograph or even bands, but it's used sparingly.
Voices for the most part are great, love to see Stephen Russell take up the formerly silent Corvo, and most characters sound the part. Disappointed to see the change for the Outsider, although the new actor does a solid, if very different approach to the character.
One character, who you meet a couple of times I found their voice grating and very hammy, I'd say more but it would likely be spoilerific. Let's just say they're formally introduced in the introduction and his bombastic tone just seems to clash with the more subdued range elsewhere.
Overall I still really recommend this game. The adventure of it, the broadness of the powers for both characters and the subtle touches based on how you handle things in missions really does work well, just like the first, only moreso. If you have a modern rig and follow my advice to tune up your drivers and either use the beta, or if you're reading this after the actual main patch, do a bit of research on how to squeeze the best performance out of the game as possible, the game is still awesome fun. Exploration is rewarded well, the stealth is actually challenging, and while once again certain powers do make the game a bit easy, self imposed challenges are not only worthwhile, but suggested! There is an option to ignore the Outsider and play the entire game with no powers at all.
If you enjoyed the first, you will likely enjoy this one. If you weren't impressed with the first for a lack of variety in abilities/tools/etc then I feel safe in saying it's worth a try due to the improvements. If you didn't like the first overall, this won't change your mind. I only hope more people update their reviews with the patches as I feel it would be a huge disappointment to see this game painted with the same brush as other titles who never bothered rectifying their games. Progress is being made, and the latest beta patch really does help tremendously.

After the abomination that was Colonial Marines, thanks Gearbox for that one, I'm really proud of The Creative Assembly for their efforts here, what a game to revitalize Alien. The amount of detail that went into this title is beautiful, they really captured the atmosphere that made Alien what it was in the movies. Toss in the Alien, some low-budget malfunctioning androids and a bunch of edgy civilians, make ammunition and high powered weaponry scarce and you've got some serious challenges ahead of you. The game itself recommends you play on hard and there's a good reason why, it's a survival horror. What you need to bare in mind here is you are mostly helpless and the sooner you realize you're not going to take everyone out head on, the sooner you're going to set yourself up to appreciate every tense moment this game throws at you and there will be alot seeing as the Alien will stalk you through every inch of the Sevastopol station. The way in which TCA made a singular alien such a huge threat this time around was a smart move, you will respect the damn thing. It's agile and incredibly aggressive, the worst thing you can possibly do while navigating is run, it's a death sentence, and just because you hid in a locker or escaped into a vent doesn't mean you're safe. Believe me when I tell you that this ♥♥♥♥er can catch you out ANYWHERE. The game paced itself perfectly, the graphics were amazing, showing off one hell of a lighting system that just made the atmosphere top notch, the music was on que with the movies, just about every aspect of this game was done right and true to the movies. It's a game that deserves the title of best game of 2014, easily.

For people wondering if they should buy the game, wait for a sale. The story is decent, the gameplay is mediocre and easily the worst part, the visuals are a very mixed bag with anti aliasing that doesn't work and some animation problems and some actual visual glitches and sound glitches.
The biggest problem with the enjoyability of this game has to do with the padding combined with the excessive use of the alien. The alien has some really rough edges in it's AI, animation, and how it functions in general. Most of the game is hiding from the alien and performing extremely mundane tasks that are more tedious than they are creative in their design. This creates a very unenjoyable experience. These "chores" you have to do to advance from story bit to story bit are extremely mundane and it all ends up repeating. There is little variation to how you can hide from the alien, and there is little variation in the objectives you are accomplishing. Simply exploring the atmosphere of the game being free to pick up logs and such and much less forced use of the alien, either in favor of quiet or androids would have worked great, as androids cause more interesting gameplay to come into play (where the involved mechanics are often dead content since you can't use them on the alien), and since they can be killed you can at least get them out of the way.
Most of the mechanics of the game go to utter waste to the point of being dead content. Survivors are no threat when the alien is around since as soon as they start shooting they doom themselves to the alien, and you are doomed if you engage the survivors while in their proximity or are downwind from the alien coming to murder them (and you). Most of the stuff you pick up becomes worthless quickly and starts piling up. The AI of the alien is sometimes painfully arbitrary or completely ambiguous, or a combination of both, which is extremely confusing. Sometimes it will go upon rigid patrol paths where it never ceases and sometimes being quiet seems to work. In all this "thumping around" the alien does you just want to explore the level and get to your next objective, and it starts to become clear that this game is going to drag on long and loud.
The combat mechanics are decent at least, and fighting androids and surivors by themselves or at least next to a much less sensitive alien would have been far more satisfying and less annoying in terms of gameplay, and in favor of preserving the horror element of the alien, which is completely lost up until the tense moments of late game where the story hits a crescendo.
Something needs to be said about QTEs, FOV, gadget minigames, and Melee. The very last section of the game should have been decided as a cinematic, or actual gameplay. Nobody digs that kind of nonsense. Decide between the two or go home. Powering generators should have been the same as opening lever doors, as that feels more satisfying and mashing E is annoying and makes less sense. Activating melee should not lock your movement and camera, and should not alter the FOV, that was extremely annoying. Gadget minigames could have been more creative, they seem really artificial. Also, unique puzzles were nowhere to be found. All objectives are extremely regurgitated gadget minigames, minor QTEs, and hide and seek.
A minor gripe is that activating electronics through the keyboard interface should have been reduced to scrolling to the right setting with the arrow keys and press y or n. This makes more sense and you could even let the player do it rather than through a cinematic. In fact, this kind of already exists, so that should have been used instead rather than the "random typing" cinematic at least, as it's obvious and annoying how generic the typing is (it's recycled key presses, or a few kinds of recycled key presses from what it looks like).
Now that I’ve played though the game here’s how I would have worked with the existing mechanics of the game to make it better.
The introduction of the game should have been more “isolated.” In an abandoned and separated part of the station ripley would be far more alone, the alien would be used much more sparingly in favor of androids, and have no access to anything remotely offensive except for that wrench and EMP.
Medium level spoiler from here
When the aliens are introduced the player gains increasing offensive means, and aliens can be interrupted, scared away, and now even wounded and killed. These means are extremely limited early on. And how about a nice assault rifle at some point as a nice throwback to aliens, and an awesome sense of empowerment? Just because you can wound or kill aliens doesn’t always mean it’s a good idea, also, they bleed acid.
This isn’t less terrifying, it’s just differently terrifying. The “horde” itself is still a terrifying threat, and so is the prospect of not being able to fend it off.
The story structure would function almost exactly the same, and then at the end you’ll lose your weapons so the very end makes sense.
So now the game would be paying homage to the original and it's sequel aliens. Even better. In the first section of the game the alien seems invincible, but offensive means aren't introduced to cast doubt. When weapons are introduced you are then able to fight back, and to make it interesting, the game won't tell you, and fighting back is difficult but at least possible to get rid of the huge gripe of canon contradiction, which is that the aliens are not invulnerable.
Perhaps they’ll apply this to the sequel. The story and atmosphere itself is great when it isn't marred by the sheer blight of the gameplay of hide and seek, and the gigantic plothole of the invulnerability applied to the alien.

Oh Black Mesa, how you've grown. The mod began as a literal remake of the original Half-Life, and while this is that, it's so much more. The mod that came out awhile back (I think I played it in 2012) was very good. This is absolutely incredible. The game changes up a few small things from the original, like where you got certain weapons, adds in some new areas, etc., but this is still the original Half-Life.
That last part is very important to me. I played the original Half-Life games growing up (the original, Opposing Force, Blue Shift, etc.) and I wanted to be able to recognize the original in this. You most certianly can. The areas, dialogue lines, weapons, and much of everything else are very close (in some cases identical) to the original.
I should probably talk about what makes this game great in some sort of list:
Pros:
+gameplay
+dialogue
+secrets
+multiplayer
+updated creature models
+achievements
+voice acting
+level design
+weapons
+++soundtrack (it is easily the best part of this remake; it's incredible)
Cons:
-no Xen (still a bit annoyed it's not here after these few years)
I've been playing this nonstop since I bought it and I can say with ease that it's my best purchase this year. Playing this remake brings back so many good memories, and has created so many more. I was literally in shock for the first few hours I was playing this.
To see the work these guys have done is astonishing. Even though the game isn't finished, it's a must buy! If you're a returning fan, or a new to the series, it's worth every penny. Here's to hoping we see an Opposing Force remake too :D

Certainly worth buying. It's the updated graphics, source engine and a lot of small features (like portable flares). If you're not satisfied with original HL - this remake might be just for you.
Overall: Great game, but still unfinished (what's taking so long to make a good Xen? 3 years have passed!).

This game is absolute quality. If the 98% positive rating (at time of writing) and big FREE button don't convince you to get this and at least try it, maybe I can give you that last little push.
Eternal Senia is incredibly simple and quick to pick up, but by no means is it boring or too easy. Combat revolves around walking into things or using Q, W, E, and R to dash, slam, and slice your enemies. On the first few mobs you fight, it's all about dealing some damage while taking some, restoring hp, and repeating. Once you fight your first boss though, and enter into the later levels, things start to get more complex with AoE hitboxes, projectiles, invincibility, stuns, etc. You'll find things to be incredibly difficult unless you go craft yourself the best armor and weapons around. Even then though, you can always bump it up to hard mode to really screw yourself over.
As for leveling, you get xp from killing things which of course levels you up, but it has less of a role in this game than it does in most other RPGs. In Eternal Senia, you get stronger by crafting better equipment and by leveling your abilities with skill points gained from killing things . Leveling alone will get you nowhere. Fear not though, as the crafting system is also incredibly simple and easy with the classic "upgrade" mechanic. Build your weapon, then gather materials to upgrade it 3 times. Same goes for the rest of your equipment.
"Great, mechanics are cool, but who cares? I'm one of those people who only cares about atmosphere!"
Well, Eternal Senia has got that covered too. The story is a real tear jerker if you can ignore the 10 or so translation errors, and the soundtrack is absolutely beautiful. There's also 3 different endings, each of which is incredibly well done. It's not like Mass Effect 3, where options A and B are for if you suck at the game and only option C is good.
Overall, for being free, this game goes above and beyond any expectations. I'm actually glad the developer took that route, because if there were a price tag I would have never given it a second glance. Now, I'm trying to figure out if there's a way to donate and I'm hoping for a sequel :)

In some ways, it even elevates it beyond the original, and for that I am grateful. Slime rancher is a beautiful game with an incredibly easy control scheme in which you ranch slimes. Yes, you’re a slime farmer who explores the world looking for rare and unique slimes for the purpose of earning a profit. You can farm these slimes free-range or you can choose to give them all easy to manage enclosures. It’s entirely up to your personal preference on how you wish to play.
It starts out as an exploration game but then quickly turns into an incredibly large grind. The exploration is amazing and the amount of variation in the landscape and critters roaming about is fantastic. For each biome you discover it feels as if there are just the right amount of different organisms roaming each biome.
There is not a dull moment during the exploration phase of your journey.. But when it turns into a grind, it turns into an absolutely huge grind. A grind so huge that it makes the game feel as if it’s a mountain that you started climbing without knowing that you were actually climbing a mountain that you don’t even wish to climb – but you may or may not choose to keep climbing anyway considering how far up you are at the end of things.
After accruing a fair amount of newbucks you purchase gear that allows for things like flight, larger backpack, and the ability to suck up water. After accruing a massive amount of plorts, or rather slime droppings, you also have the ability to create things from resources you collect. These things allow you to teleport around, decorate your ranch, or even just display your #1 slime.
Sadly, There is only so much to explore, and when you finish exploring it becomes a waiting game in which you wait for the slime stocks to get to a level in which you’re willing to sell while storing your plorts in your silos. For what? A stupid slime trophy? Yes. A stupid slime trophy. A glorious and stupid slime trophy. Also colors, ranch upgrades, and other things you may or may not want. Most of which have no actual significance to the game.
For a score I will have to give Slime Rancher an 85 out of 100. The exploration is amazing, but the grind is not. It’s a seemingly never ending struggle to reach a level few will be willing to grind to. Are you willing? I am.
Anyway, thanks for watching and I hope you enjoyed! If you did enjoy, don’t forget to like, comment, and subscribe!

Alien Isolation - Completed on Hard difficulty, don't believe me check my achievements
Alien Isolation strives to channel your inner Ellen Ripely, The game creator's "Creative Assembly" suggested we should play the game on Hard "Mode" I did just that, completed within 26 hours. Alien Isolation is the most tense adrenaline filled and frightfully jumpy sci-fi experience since Dead Space.
After playing 5 minutes of the game I was having trouble just picking up the controller, the game instantly get's under your skin,  I found this out when playing the DLC - Lone Survivor, but after half-hour, I put on my Ellen-Ripley-Cap said to myself lets do this.

I saw myself a veteran gamer I have completed many (space, horror and shoot-em-up's) on the most unforgiving veteran mode surely Alien Isolation could be no different. Only trouble is... I was unprepared just how powerless you are in the game, and just how easy it is to die, your only real strength you have in the game is to be as stealthy as you can and avoid making any noise and move undetected.
Normally this does the trick you can get through the game with ease but  I was playing the game on hard difficulty. The slightest sound foot-step or gun-shot and you will have a terrifying "Xenomorph" dropping out of the vent's or chasing you down the corridor screaming, if It see's you and sometimes you might not here it all while it creeps up on you sticks you with it's tail from behind.

How  to survive Exenomorph!
The deciding factor's when the alien comes stomping your way and the option's you have available should you hide, run or escape the area or should you use an item to distract it?
Pro-tip from me: NEVER EVER RUN IN THIS GAME, you are basically walking silver platter with  if you run.
When you decide to hide and considering your options: Should you hide under a desk or should you hide in a locker?
Think you are safe in the lockers think again...
The alien will stalk the area your in and if you come out too early and feel you need to re-enter the same locker or another locker, I would not advice it. The alien listen's for you and adapt's to the situation, what may have worked a few times may not always work 3rd, 4th, or 5th time, stay on the move and use lockers and cabinets sparingly.

Save Station
I cannot stress enough how important it is to save while playing Alien Isolation, doesn't matter what difficulty you are playing on, no matter what you will die at some point, that I guarantee, before you start thinking:
I am not going to play this there no auto save!
Keep in mind this adds to the tension and fun of the game and every save is a reward in-itself.
I found this out more so on Dr Morely Section of the Game, I know this might sound counter productive but if you get objective done and the alien is near by, this is what I do if I can see the alien on the scanner and it's behind me sometimes it's ok to run, but only run if you need to save, atleast this way you stand less chance of the alien coming stalking your way and you would have saved yourself another trip if you got killed taking too safely and slowly.
The scanner
Use the scanner wisely and try not to use it too much on hard difficulty, the alien can here the scanner beep noise, especially if you are hiding in a locker, the alien might just stay in the area longer.

Deaths
I will not lie, I died many times, so much so that I got achievement out of it, the game will punish you at every turn, every area is designed to make your journey as difficult to complete as possible like true horror game. The game will brutally satisfyingly want to work against  you at all times, this is no "Call of Duty Action Game", this is "Survival Horror" remember that when you start playing otherwise you might not make it to the credits-end.

Objectives
Are done in such way you will end up having to do multiple things in one area and might end up finding yourself back tracking allot when a door is down due to a faulty power generator or a password is needed from access terminal or you might need to hack into something and complete a mini-game, this add's so much tension to the game, the last thing you want to do is back track when Exenomorph hiding in the vents or stomping around.
Weapons and Items
You have limited amount of weapon's and tool's at your disposal which can be upgraded and obtained throughout Sevastopol and you will have to use each and everyone one of them sparingly.
I stayed away from using as many item's as possible because they attracted the beast even though you can use the item's to lore the alien and kill  humans or use item's as a distraction by doing so the alien will stay in the vicinity and it will take longer to complete that section of the game most of the time the Alien will scan the area until it think it's ok to go back in the vents, because of this I try and avoid using as many item's as possible and just stick with being stealthy.
On hard difficulty, the alien can be just as unpredictable and sometimes avoiding the alien can be impossible at times, so always have a few Molotov-cocktail's ready and the flamethrower to fend the alien off, but remember if you do manage to scare the alien off move out that area as soon as possible the alien might  come back to check if you are still there do not rely on the flamethrower, as your main defense but as a last-resort.
Ammo and items are scarce on hard difficulty and the alien at times can be relentless so be resourceful as much as possible stay hidden.
Humans
When you come across a group of humans or just one, most of the time they will be hostile toward's you and try and shoot you if they can, If they do choose to shoot you and  the alien is near by the alien will here the gun-shots and go straight for the human, think about using this as a tactic while playing as I did when escaping the Medical Facility.
Droids not your average Joe's
The droids in the game can be just as dangerous and bothersome and take quite a beating to put one out of action, as I found out when I fired 9 Revolver bullets into head of a droid before it went down. What I found worked best was to craft  EMP device and use this on the droid and then use your wench while it was temporary disabled to kill it. The stun-rode is some what effective against them but best to use it when they are unaware of your presence and from behind, once you got the droid going berserk with the stun rod this is your moment to kill it with the wench.
The exenomorph
On hard difficulty the Exenomorph is allot like an overly attached girlfriend....
It will not be that far away and it will pop-out the vents when it feel's like it and sometimes I have witnessed it falling back out of the vents, only to go back in again. When I thought it was going to be game-over for me.
The alien on hard mode is unpredictable put it this way.
Stay invisible from start to finish only way survive! and move all the time never linger the alien will detect you hunt you down if you stay to long in one area, always stay on the move.
Move undetected don't let anyone see or hear you and you will complete the game more quickly, as this was my main strategy.
As you progress through the game you are going to come up against some scripted Alien area's where it's going to be impossible to avoid the alien, I found this to happen allot in the Gemini area of the game while I was trying to complete a task: That had me logging in to the access terminal twice!!! and pulling two lever's while having a droid and exenomorph on the look out.

Steam is showing a lot more play time than I have actually invested so far, but I am still at least half way through the game. At this point, it feels safe to write a review.
This game is glorious on many levels. It is such an amazing tribute to the world of the original film that its not hard to believe you are actually visiting that beautiful and terrifying retro-tech world. The visuals are superb; the ambience is perfect. The dialog is well written and well delivered. The cut scenes are excellent, and the story is better than I had been lead to expect by other sources. As a long time fan of the Alien franchise, I have none the less felt deeply disappointed by much of its material. I was never a fan of Alien: Resurrection. I have read many of the comics and novels, but have enjoyed few. I have played all of the previous games except Colonial Marines, and while they were fun, the spirit simply wasn't there.
It is here.
The Alien itself is restored to its respectible and awe-inspiring place as the greatest of movie monsters. Being stalked by it is nerve wracking, stressful. The game creates a tense, fearful environment where every decision feels crucial, but helplessness pervades. No matter how stealthy you are, no matter how closely you attend to the music and the sounds of the Alien creeping about around you, you know that sooner or later, your luck will run out. And it does. Again, and again. Still, I have not found the fear lessened by repetition. I have not found myself truly frustrated, either. When I survive a mission, when I reach a save point, I always feel... accomplished. I have survived an encounter with a formidable enemy.
There are minor technical quibbles. I have seen the Alien slaughter NPCs one at a time while others stood around and watched as if nothing was happening. This is rare, but it does tend to break the immersion. I have also found that, occasionally a terminal will not work properly, and I will be stuck and have to force quit the game to escape. Neither issue has caused me enough grief to want to quit playing. The game is simply amazing, and despite being exhausting at times, it draws you in, dares you to turn the next corner, to try one more time to cheat fate and outsmart the monster that hunts you.
If you love the films and love a truly frightening and challenging game, then, by all means, jump in. You won't regret it.

Short review:  Smite is a good MOBA for anyone who wants to try one and for experienced players alike.
Long review:  Smite is a MOBA that is somewhat different from others.  It has a third person perspective that I personally like.  There are a wide range of characters to choose from, 70 at the time of this review.  Along with the wide range of characters is 6 different game modes.
There are 5 different character types to choose.  Assassians, which stick and move, securing a kill.  Warrior, who are constantly in the fight.  Hunters, long range specialists for ranged attack.  Mages, who deal a variety of magical attacks.  And lastly there are guardians, who play support but can also deal a lot of damage.
The 6 different game modes differ quite a bit.
-There is arena, which is just a 5v5 deathmatch where your team tries to kill the other and escort minions into the enemies portal.  Reducing the enemies score to 0 wins this game.
-Joust is a 3 on 3 mode that uses teamwork to advance to your enemies titan to destroy it to win.  Of course you must get through the enemy teams tower and phoenix.  This is a one lane mode with buffs for each team to pick up on either side,
-Assault is 5v5 one lane fighting where you are randomly given a god and you and your team work your way to the enemies titan to destroy it.  Similar to joust, but you cannot go back and buy equipment or items until you are dead.
-Seige is a 4v4 2 lane fight to destroy the opposing enemy titan.  This is more strategic than the other modes.  Teamwork is almost always nescessary here.
-Conquest is the main game mode of Smite.  It is a 5v5 3 lane strategy game.  The goal is to destroy the enemy teams titan once again.  But teamwork and playing your role are a nescessity in this mode.  Conquest relies heavily on strategy.
Overall Smite is a fun game for me, and I personally don't play many MOBAs.  There are a few minor issues I have.  Some gods play too similar.  The community can be toxic at times, and the servers can get overloaded at times as well.  But those are my biggest gripes.  I do recommend this game to anyone wanting to try a MOBA.

seems like an interesting villain, and not everything about her is black and white.

Initial performance aside (their latest patch did a lot to improve it) and focusing on the gameplay, I'm very satisfied with Dishonored 2.
-The story is captivating from beginning to end, no matter what path you choose. I chose to go the harder route of not killing anyone, even main targets, and it provides the same satisfying challenge as it did in the first game. There's also a rich side-story, told through books and some by talking to people.
-The world is beautiful and detailed. It's visually apparent that designing the world was really a labor of love. I couldn't find any bits of it that seemed unpolished.
-The controls felt fluid and easy to use and master. Didn't change much from the first game, but there wasn't anything to improve on.
-As far as game length is concerned, it took me just about 21 hours from beginning to end. That was with a generous amount of checkpoint reloading due to my obsession with not killing anyone along the way and trying my best to never be seen. I'm guessing if you were to choose a more...expiditious way of dealing with your enemies, the game would probably take a good 4 or 5 hours less.
-Keep in mind that part of Dishonored's charm is that I get to go back and play it again with a completely different approach. I can also choose to play as Corvo, which adds more dimension to my available choices. Could result in a lot of replay value, which helps justify the price tag.
Overall I'm inclined to give it a solid 9/10. The only thing it lost 10/10 on was:
-Occasionally I would be killed by closing or opening a door on myself. Anytime I was meant to be pushed out of the way, but collided with an object, I would instantly die.
-Emily's grappling ability would sometimes short itself repeatedly, causing a bit of frustration. The marker would clearly have me landing on top of my target, but I'd pretty much end up smashing face into it, and either falling to my death, or at the very least making a racket when I landed on something.
Runs a bit low res on my 290X but with 1.2 runs ok. The game can get annoying when trying to do a stealth and merciful run but its growing on me. Still think Dishonored 1 >> 2.

Slime rancher is a beautiful game with an incredibly easy control scheme in which you ranch slimes. Yes, you’re a slime farmer who explores the world looking for rare and unique slimes for the purpose of earning a profit. You can farm these slimes free-range or you can choose to give them all easy to manage enclosures. It’s entirely up to your personal preference on how you wish to play.
It starts out as an exploration game but then quickly turns into an incredibly large grind. The exploration is amazing and the amount of variation in the landscape and critters roaming about is fantastic. For each biome you discover it feels as if there are just the right amount of different organisms roaming each biome.
There is not a dull moment during the exploration phase of your journey.. But when it turns into a grind, it turns into an absolutely huge grind. A grind so huge that it makes the game feel as if it’s a mountain that you started climbing without knowing that you were actually climbing a mountain that you don’t even wish to climb – but you may or may not choose to keep climbing anyway considering how far up you are at the end of things.
After accruing a fair amount of newbucks you purchase gear that allows for things like flight, larger backpack, and the ability to suck up water. After accruing a massive amount of plorts, or rather slime droppings, you also have the ability to create things from resources you collect. These things allow you to teleport around, decorate your ranch, or even just display your #1 slime.
Sadly, There is only so much to explore, and when you finish exploring it becomes a waiting game in which you wait for the slime stocks to get to a level in which you’re willing to sell while storing your plorts in your silos. For what? A stupid slime trophy? Yes. A stupid slime trophy. A glorious and stupid slime trophy. Also colors, ranch upgrades, and other things you may or may not want. Most of which have no actual significance to the game.
For a score I will have to give Slime Rancher an 85 out of 100. The exploration is amazing, but the grind is not. It’s a seemingly never ending struggle to reach a level few will be willing to grind to. Are you willing? I am.
Anyway, thanks for watching and I hope you enjoyed! If you did enjoy, don’t forget to like, comment, and subscribe!

After Colonial Marines I kinda gave up hope that there will be a single decent game of the Alien franchise coming out, ever. But... After the first few trailers rose, and the focus on developing a game in a way so it carries the spirit of the first (and my favourite) Alien (1979) movie inside, proving it to be a terrifying experience aboard a space station, where no one can hear you scream.
And indeed, SEGA, or Creative Assembly, to be more precise, delivered. Alien: Isolation takes the formula of current Indie-Horror games, mostly referred to as Closet Simulators, as there is no way to defend yourself other than to run away and hide, and turns it into a diverse gameplaysetting, set in one of the oldest Sci-Fi Franchises there is. At first, I thought this would become like Amnesia, only with an Alien, but instead, it actually had more gameplay than just puzzle solving and hiding.
In AI, you can craft utilities that you can use to distract the alien, humans, or synthetics in order to progress. You even get 4 Weapons + Melee weapon to use against your foes, while fighting the alien is a bad idea in general, but blowing some hostile survivors or pesky synthetics a big load of lead into their head is actually quite fun. Especially when you use the utilities to first distract them, then get from behind and smash their skull.
Combat is really diverse in this game, as there are 3 types of enemies. The humans and synthetics are pretty alike, whereas the humans use long-range guns and pumpguns, and the working Joes rather get up close and personal. Often you need to change tactics when battling one, after fighting the others, as an upfront smash to the head will do nothing against synthetics, except for you getting killed.
The alien on the other hand... You CAN shoot it, but only the pumpgun has some sort of effect, which makes the alien hesitate for a moment before charging at you. Using the flame thrower, or a molotov though makes the alien retreat into an air duct for a short period of time, enough for you to escape and find a safe place to hide.
The story is okay, it sure has some twists and turns you could've predicted beforehand, but it lives up to it's movie counterpart, the original Alien movie, but I don't like to spoil anything here.
Visually this game is impressive. It runs smooth, has lots of lighting effects, very crystal clear textures and models, as well as decent shaders. The only thing you might criticise is the lack of proper Anti-Aliasing. It features FXAA and SMAA up to SMAA 2TX, but it really only does mostly nothing. You might want to use forced AA, or even try Downsampling for this game instead.
The Sound design is really good! Awesome so to say, most of the sounds at terminals, ships or similar stations are close to the soundsets of the original Alien, especially using a terminal gives you this good ol' classy 70s Style vibe. Especially the sounds of the Alien impressed me. Hearing it stomp around near you really terrifies you, when you can't see it right there, or the way it hisses when it's stalking you, waiting for a chance to grab you from above.
Same goes for the Soundtrack. I even recognized Tracks, or parts of ambient tracks that were taken from the Original movie (or remade for this game), which really emphasized the passion the devs had for the first Alien movie.
In conclusion: Alien Isolation is the Alien game I wished for so lang. It takes the terror and desperation of the original movie, puts modern survival horror and stealth into the mix and stirs it right up, adding fan-service here and there and presents itself in front of you, terrifying, yet irresistable and addicting. This game is the best Horror-Survival I've played since two generations. Great Job CA, you exceeded my expectations.
